title: Expose exact merge-candidate lineage and CI freshness in Cara status
description:
Operator-requested observability gap found during Cacophony native merger operation. `cara status` reported the caravan graph and aggregate health, but the merger still had to call GitHub directly to learn each active PR's exact current base/head, synthetic merge-candidate SHA and parents, auto-merge owner, check-run generation, and whether visible required checks belonged to the current candidate or a stale head/base generation.

Concrete evidence: Cacophony PR #1991 was head `affacaba74132a4642c6aa06021bb8fa5e381097` on main `251d04e9be9742cbf9a9d2cfa0a194601e5a2561`, while its failed workflow selected stale synthetic merge ref `ff68423484b0be2ffe0a2dd70999c8d518c0887b` whose second parent was prior head `329c42e2a22db8146dada382811927e38ee80e50`. Cara status showed a healthy six-member graph but not this generation mismatch.

Extend stable JSON/MCP status and show output for each active member with: provider-updated timestamp; exact base ref/OID; exact head ref/OID; current synthetic merge-candidate SHA/tree/parents when available; native auto-merge enabled/method/actor; required check names and latest check/run IDs with head/candidate association; and an explicit fresh/stale/unknown classification. Bound output and preserve secret-free receipts. Acceptance: a merger can prove current PR identity, candidate lineage, sole auto-merge ownership, and check freshness from Cara alone without `gh pr view`, `gh api commits/refs/pull/.../merge`, or direct check-runs calls.

## Additional operator gap: default-branch movement provenance

The operator asked who, besides Cara/caco-merger, was advancing `main` and invalidating the caravan. Cara status exposed only current default-branch OID `251d04e9...`; answering required an external git-history inspection. Extend the same bounded provider snapshot with recent default-branch movements: commit/merge SHA, timestamp, author/provider actor when available, source PR or Cara operation receipt, and an explicit Cara-owned versus external classification. Include previous observed default OID so an agent can distinguish actual main motion from a stale GitHub synthetic merge-ref race. Acceptance: Cara alone can report which actors advanced main since the prior sync and which active caravan candidates became stale as a result.
creator: helsinki:cacophony:helsinki-cacophony-caco-merger

title: Require an explicit auth mode before activating the App broker
description:
Follow-up to bd-03d863/bd-c586b8 under bd-b15483. GitHub App mode currently activates when `CARA_GITHUB_APP_CREDENTIAL_COMMAND` is present. A broker path is credential-provider plumbing, not an explicit repository/deployment identity decision; inherited environment must not silently replace ambient/stored `gh` behavior.

Require an independent explicit mode selector, initially `CARA_GITHUB_AUTH_MODE=app_installation`, before any broker execution, App API token injection, Git helper injection, principal binding, or App-mode refusal. Without the selector, preserve exact ambient behavior even when broker-related variables are present. With the selector but missing/invalid broker command, expected slug/installation, or exact repository, fail closed before provider/Git mutation and never fall back ambient.

Unknown mode values fail closed on authenticated GitHub/API or remote Git operations with a typed secret-free diagnostic. Require non-secret expected App slug and installation ID in explicit mode so broker refresh cannot establish an unintended first principal. Document eventual repository config mapping; environment mode is deployment-level and must remain explicit until config propagation is added.

Tests: broker-only environment does not activate (child-process hermetic); explicit App mode executes broker; explicit mode missing broker/identity refuses; invalid mode refuses; no secret rendering; ambient mode parity.

title: Trust the devshell cara and drop binary-path defensive checks
description:
Operator posture change 2026-07-27. Cara is now pinned solely by flake.lock and obtained from devshells; nix flake update is the upgrade path. Cara Sync CI is disabled; sync is driven manually for now, and later by a caco cron running cara sync with hooks that dispatch pi agents to repair caravans as they break.

Under that model the defensive machinery around binary LOCATION is dead weight and actively obstructive. Remove or scope down:
- is_package_manager_binary and the self_update_package_managed refusal, which today blocks self-update outright whenever the running binary lives in a Nix store or Homebrew cellar. That refusal is what has to go: a store-managed binary is a reason to install ELSEWHERE, not a reason to refuse.
- require_first_path_executable and related PATH-precedence checks that exist to stop self-update writing a binary PATH would not resolve.

Operator correction 2026-07-27: forced self-update REMAINS useful in general, for deliberately pulling a GitHub release regardless of how the current binary was installed. So this bead does NOT supersede caravan/bd-bd58cd or updatable-cli/bd-e195f5; those stay open and are the intended replacement for the removed refusal. The relationship is: drop the blanket refusal here, and let bd-bd58cd own the safe forced path (never write into a Nix store or Homebrew cellar, install into a user-owned directory, and report clearly when the result shadows a package-managed binary).

Keep the runtime provenance surface added for bd-0629ce: version, resolved executable, sha256, and nix_store on every status receipt. That is how a version-skewed actor is proven rather than inferred; today it is the only reason we could tell one node was answering from a stale debug build while its nix profile sat six releases back. Provenance is diagnosis, not defence, and becomes more valuable under manual and cron-driven sync where a skewed actor otherwise looks like a quiet queue.

Also record the doc change: release/backfill recipes and self-update docs should state that flake.lock is the pin of record for this deployment, and that forced self-update is a deliberate override rather than the normal upgrade path.

title: Reject current-main no-op candidates instead of replaying trunk advances onto the caravan tail
description:
Operator-reproduced Cara join bug in `harryaskham/cacophony` on 2026-07-21. Harry was on branch `fix-cara-timeouts` and attempted to join what was an empty/no-op candidate relative to current default branch. Instead of refusing the empty candidate, Cara created PR #2080 and inferred the already-landed default-branch advance as candidate work, rebasing that unrelated release commit onto the active caravan tail.

Exact graph/evidence:

- Active predecessor PR #2079: head `fix-slackiq-nodes` at `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, parent/default fork `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`.
- True GitHub `main` had already advanced from `80bf4eacae` to release commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7` (`release: v1.2.1562`). The authoritative annotated tag v1.2.1562 also peels to `d9fad17e`.
- Cara created PR #2080 with base `fix-slackiq-nodes`, head `fix-cara-timeouts`, initially containing `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680`.
- `ac701198` has parent `c059bf15`, author `Cacophony Daemon`, committer `Caravan`, and exactly the same release message/patch as already-main commit `d9fad17e`; it is the default-branch release change replayed onto the caravan tail.
- PR #2080 body identifies the unrelated update-helper source (`agent/ms-dev-2/.../update-helper`, source head `e3026e0461`, mode `direct`) even though the provider head branch is Harry's `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- PR #2080 was created at 23:06:39Z. The timeline later records a head force-push at 23:08:19Z and Harry's actual `fix cara timeoutes` commit `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633` only afterwards; current PR files therefore mix the unintended release bump with the intended `.caravan/config.yaml` edit.

This proves the join/rebase delta was derived against the stale caravan/root fork (`80bf4eacae`) rather than the live provider default tip (`d9fad17e`) / candidate's intended patch. As a result, a branch with no intended delta from current main can silently acquire every trunk commit landed since the caravan fork, and Cara can force-update an operator branch with unrelated duplicated commits.

Expected contract:

1. Under the join lock, re-read the live provider default tip and candidate head.
2. Compute candidate intent relative to that live default/fork-point contract, not relative to the active predecessor's old main base.
3. If candidate has no delta from live default, refuse with a typed `empty_diff`/no-op result and do not create/reuse a PR, mutate/force-push its head branch, append membership, or schedule CI.
4. If candidate has one real change X atop newer default M1 while the caravan tail descends from older M0, rebase only X onto the locked tail; never replay M0..M1 as candidate work.

Required regression test graph: create M0 and a caravan tail T from M0; advance default to M1; (a) join candidate C=M1 and assert a typed no-op with zero provider/membership mutations; (b) join C=M1+X and assert the joined result is T+X only, with M1's already-main patch excluded. Also assert an unrelated existing/current operator branch name cannot be selected or force-pushed as the head of another source generation.

## Live automatic-admission no-op blocker — Cacophony PR #2104

After first caravan #2111 merged, operator-prioritized exact-clean #2104 became canonical. Sync source analysis proved its sole source commit 27815c9a6f13fb2618b6c0cae83ac1ab52183022 already landed in current main79a9d38; effective patch is empty, mutated=false. Cara returned join_empty_source_noop with wake_class=retry_tick and left the PR open/priority-labelled, so unchanged retries block all later candidates forever.

Extend this bead acceptance: sync-owned admission must classify exact already-landed source as terminal/advisory retirement, not retry. Under exact ancestry/tree proof, remove queue control priority/skip intent as appropriate, emit a typed already_landed/noop receipt, and continue to later candidates in the same bounded tick or provide an explicit safe PR-close/Caco-return continuation. Never replay main or report success as a new caravan. Cover root/tail admission, squash-equivalent distinct OID, mixed source where only some commits landed, and concurrent main movement.

title: Add refreshable GitHub App installation auth to local Cara
description:
First shippable child of bd-b15483: add opt-in GitHub App installation authentication to the existing local Cara process. No hosted worker/webhook service in this slice, and ambient/stored `gh` remains the unchanged default.

SCOPE

- Public config selects `github_auth.mode: local_gh | app_installation`, default `local_gh`.
- App mode binds public app slug/ID and exact installation/repository identity. Private key material is provided only through a protected file/credential command/KMS adapter outside repository config.
- Introduce a refreshable credential-provider abstraction. Generate a bounded App JWT, exchange it for a repository-scoped installation access token, cache until a safety margin before expiry, and single-flight refresh.
- Use explicit GitHub REST endpoints through the existing bounded command runner or a narrowly reviewed HTTP client. No token in argv, plans, errors, receipts, checkpoints, logs, or shell history.
- Inject the token into every `gh` command as secret `GH_TOKEN` while preserving request budgets and telemetry.
- Add telemetry/receipt identity: auth mode, app slug, installation ID, expiration, expected provider actor. Never include token/key.
- On 401/expiration, refresh once within the same request/deadline budget; no unbounded retry.
- Exact repository access is verified before any mutation. App installation for another owner/repository fails closed.

OUT OF SCOPE / FOLLOW-UPS

- Git transport credentials for direct fetch/push are a separate child. Until that child lands, App API mode is read-only or refuses branch-mutating operations before write; never mix App API identity with ambient-user git push identity.
- Hosted webhook workers and remote writer leases are separate children.
- Do not change local_gh behavior or silently infer App mode from environment.

TESTS

- local_gh default makes zero App JWT/token calls.
- App token exchange is exact-installation/repository scoped and expiry bounded.
- Concurrent requests share one refresh.
- Expired token refreshes once; repeated 401 fails closed.
- Secret values never appear in Debug, JSON/MCP, command diagnostics, checkpoints, or telemetry.
- Any branch mutation refuses while API and git transport identities are not both the same App installation.

IMPLEMENTATION SLICE DECISION

The first landing uses an explicit deployment credential broker rather than embedding private-key/JWT crypto or repository config:

    CARA_GITHUB_APP_CREDENTIAL_COMMAND=/absolute/path/to/broker

The executable receives exact host/repository in environment and returns bounded JSON `{token, app_slug, installation_id, repository, expires_unix_secs}`. Optional expected slug/installation environment values pin identity. This supports local key files, KMS, or a future hosted broker without secrets in `.caravan/config.yaml` and without adding a crypto/HTTP dependency to Cara.

This slice is intentionally API/read capable but branch-write disabled: any `git push` while App broker mode is active returns `GithubAppGitTransportUnavailable` before spawning git. That is the acceptance criterion's required refusal while API and git transport identities cannot yet be the same App installation. The separate transport child will make mutation mode usable.

title: Add idempotent Cara repository initialization for required labels
description:
## Operator expectation

While integrating Cara into Cacophony, Harry asked whether first use correctly initializes a repository by creating the `caravan`, `caravan-evicted`, and `caravan-force` labels.

Current behavior does not initialize them. `cara status` can inventory an unlabelled repository, but mutation paths call `require_labels` and fail before provider mutation with `required_labels_missing`, instructing the operator to create all three labels manually and rerun. There is no `cara init` command.

The Cacophony repository currently has all three labels, verified through GitHub, but they were provisioned externally rather than by Cara first-use initialization.

## Acceptance

- Add an explicit, idempotent first-party initialization surface such as `cara init` (CLI/MCP), or an equally clear reviewed first-use path.
- Create exactly the required labels with documented names, descriptions, and colors:
  - `caravan`
  - `caravan-evicted`
  - `caravan-force`
- Preserve compatible existing labels without mutation; fail closed on incompatible definitions unless an explicit repair option is chosen.
- Return stable receipts distinguishing created, already-present, incompatible, and provider-failed labels.
- `cara status` should report repository initialization readiness and the exact next command when labels are missing.
- `new`, `join`, `renew`, and `rejoin` continue to fail before graph mutation if initialization has not completed.
- Add provider fixtures for empty repo, partial labels, compatible existing labels, incompatible metadata, retry after partial provider failure, and idempotent replay.
- Document whether automatic initialization is ever allowed; avoid hidden label mutation from a read-only `status` call.

Filed from the first Cacophony Cara cutover. This belongs in the Caravan project, not Cacophony.

title: Ship a portable Linux release artifact and expose runtime provenance
description: Root cause from the ms-dev-2 update-helper crash (Cacophony evidence, Cara-owned deliverables). The published x86_64-linux release asset is a glibc-dynamic build (ELF ET_DYN, glibc 2.40 loader). On NixOS with nix-ld the loader resolves through glibc 2.42 plus /run/current-system/sw/share/nix-ld/lib, and the same byte-identical binary (sha256 95dd721d9dace6a23ccdde29443a6e3935f8d48ac6a951905752514901d0509a, 14613392 bytes) reproducibly exits 139 with empty stdout and stderr for status/next-candidate/log while --help still works. The identical bytes run healthy on ms-dev and on ms-dev-2 when invoked through the store binary, so this is packaging/loader divergence rather than a Cara logic defect. Deliverables owned here: (1) build the Linux release assets so they are safe on NixOS, preferring a static musl target for x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux, or otherwise proving nix-ld compatibility, and smoke the packaged artifact on a NixOS host before publish; (2) make cara expose resolved binary path, version, and artifact hash in a typed diagnostics surface so queue-sync receipts can record exactly which build answered; (3) document that a cargo-installed ~/.cargo/bin/cara must never shadow a reviewed store binary on queue nodes, since PATH order alone selected the crashing build. Signal-exit classification in callers and PATH hygiene on production nodes are Cacophony-owned (their items 2 and 3) but must be cross-referenced. Targets a 0.0.11 release once landed.

title: [broken-on-main] Cara repair start segfaults under canonical nix run
description:
## Live failure

After Caravan bd-dbb5bb fixed the hermetic Git identity tests, caco-merger retried the first-party PR #1962 repair path with the newly landed canonical binary.

- Authoritative Caravan daemon checkout was verified clean with local `HEAD == origin/main == 157ebd32f00334a4645b0aac4026eaf707d464d5`.
- `nix run <checkout> -- --version` succeeds and reports Cara 0.0.2.
- Exact `nix run <checkout> -- repair start --pr 1962` terminates with signal/exit 139, zero stdout, and zero stderr.
- One bounded repeat was made only to capture bytes and exit status; it reproduced identically.
- No repair-workspace manifest was created under the Cacophony Git common directory.
- No provider mutation, raw Git fallback, or PR branch update occurred. PR #1962 remains at exact head `05fe82fe` with auto-merge disabled.

This is a distinct runtime blocker after the test/package build fix: the supported repair command now builds but crashes before it can return a typed decision or create durable recovery state.

## Required outcome

- Reproduce the packaged `nix run ... -- repair start` crash in a clean fixture without relying on user/global Git configuration.
- Identify and remove the signal-139 root cause, including any unsafe/FFI, allocator, subprocess, Git-library, or Nix runtime-library mismatch involved. Record a bounded diagnostic/backtrace or equivalent root-cause receipt.
- Add a regression that executes the packaged repair-start binary, not only direct Rust library tests, and proves it never terminates by signal with empty diagnostics.
- On all preflight/provider/config failures, return the stable structured Cara error envelope and nonzero ordinary exit code; never crash.
- Preserve atomicity: either no repair manifest/workspace/provider mutation occurs, or a complete receipt-bound manifest is durably written. Partial crash state must remain detectable and recoverable.
- Prove `nix run <clean current checkout> -- --version` and `nix run ... -- repair --help` succeed, then exercise repair start/status/abort against a deterministic fixture through the same packaged binary.
- Publish a canonical landed SHA/version receipt before caco-merger retries live PR #1962 at exact head `05fe82fe`. No raw Git/worktree workaround is allowed.

Root-cause redirect: nonmutating clean-environment control (`env -i HOME PATH XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) makes the exact packaged binary return a normal typed error instead of SIGSEGV. Existing Cacophony bead `bd-d7d543` already contains the exact mixed-glibc proof: inherited `NIX_LD`, `NIX_LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, and foreign `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` combine glibc 2.40 loader with glibc 2.42 libc and fault in `dlsym` during `std::Thread::new`. It owns `scripts/cara-runtime.sh`, provenance/pin checks, sanitized invocation, PR #2011, and deployment acceptance. No Caravan domain/runtime change is warranted; an exploratory uncommitted Nix wrapper was discarded. Duplicate is cross-project `cacophony:bd-d7d543`.

title: A no-write plan reports a read failure as a mutation failure
description:
`cara plan sync --all` failed against the live fleet with:

    github_mutation_failed
    `gh api repos/harryaskham/cacophony` failed with status 1: TLS handshake timeout

The underlying event was a transient network failure on a REPOSITORY PREFLIGHT READ, and the plan correctly performed nothing: `operation_receipt.changed: false`, `provider_receipts: []`, `resumable: true`. Everything about the handling is right except what it is CALLED.

WHY THE NAME MATTERS MORE HERE THAN ELSEWHERE. `plan sync` exists to answer one question, "what would a tick do, without writing anything", and its headline output is `NO PROVIDER WRITES`. An operator deciding whether to authorise a real tick runs it precisely because they do not trust the tick yet. Telling that operator `github_mutation_failed` says a mutation was attempted and failed, which is the single most alarming thing a dry-run could say, and it is false. The reader must then dig into `provider_receipts` to discover that nothing was attempted.

I hit this myself while verifying that the queue had re-evaluated after PR2296 merged outside the caravan, and my first reaction was to check whether the plan had written something.

The error path is shared with real `sync`, where `github_mutation_failed` is accurate. `plan_sync` reuses it because it reuses the machinery, which is the right engineering and the wrong label: the shared helper names the operation it was written for, not the operation calling it.

Corrected at the `plan_sync` boundary, which is exactly the scope where no write is possible, leaving the real `sync` path untouched. Same class as the rest of today's findings, and notable for being in the one surface whose entire purpose is to be trusted about writes.

title: Lifecycle doc omits every CI admission rule
description:
`docs/lifecycle.md` predated the CI-admission work and had zero coverage of it: no mention of failing checks, `CandidateIncompatible`, or the forge verdict. A lifecycle document that omits the rules an operator will actually hit is worse than none, because it reads as complete.

Adds:

- §1.3 gains the CI rows: a FAILED required check skips and the queue advances; a RUNNING check does not bar admission; a forge `BLOCKED` verdict is irrelevant to admission.
- §1.4, new: why red bars admission (queueing behind red is guaranteed rework, since fixing it rewrites the head and rebases everything behind), why pending does not (it would stall every candidate for the length of its own CI), why `Unknown` groups with failure (an absent result is not a passing one), and why `mergeStateStatus` is measured rather than assumed — a clean, correctly-elected candidate reported `BLOCKED` identically to a red one on live data.
- §3.1 gains the forge cross-check as merge condition 4, typed `forge_refuses_merge`, and says explicitly that this is the only place the field is consulted.
- Also records that a hold not expressed as PR state is not a hold: draft and `caravan-join-skipped` are visible to Cara, an intention is not. An operator hit this by holding a PR socially while it remained fully admissible.

Plus a new subsection recording the failure mode itself, because six defects here were one mistake repeated: a rule applied at one site and not its siblings, tests green because each site was tested alone against inputs it constructed itself. The three things that actually caught them — test the composition not the unit, make the compiler ask the question (and note a `_ =>` wildcard is the compiler being told not to help), and verify the mechanism in situ rather than in isolation — plus the measurement lesson that a number from a degraded machine describes the machine, not the platform.

title: [broken-on-main] CI gate loses the nix devShell PATH: cargo: command not found
description:
Caravan CI build-test fails on main and on every open PR, 12-13s in, before any compilation:

  bash: line 3: cargo: command not found
  ##[error]Process completed with exit code 127

Observed red on main at 57639f4 (11:50 BST), 137a914 v0.0.12 (11:58) and c30540d (12:29), and on PR #10 twice including an explicit rerun. No repository change correlates with the onset, which points at a profile/image change on the self-hosted nix runner fleet.

Cause: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the gate as

  nix develop --command bash -lc '...'

The -l makes it a LOGIN shell, so the runner's profile files are sourced AFTER nix develop has established the devShell environment, and they replace PATH rather than extend it. cargo, rustc, clippy and rustfmt disappear even though flake.nix devShells.default still provides all of them. Line 3 of the inner script is the first command that needs cargo, which matches the error exactly.

Fix: drop the login shell.

  nix develop --command bash -c '...'

No login semantics are required by the gate, and this makes CI immune to runner profile drift instead of depending on the runner's profile files being PATH-preserving.

If the runner-side profile change was deliberate, the repo-side fix is still correct and strictly more robust; the two are not in conflict.

Impact while unfixed: every caravan PR is BLOCKED, including the bd-f8cf99 backward-compatibility follow-up (PR #10).

title: Park terminal-red caravans outside active capacity so green PRs advance
description:
A terminal-red caravan currently occupies active queue capacity and wedges independent green candidates. Live example: cacophony caravan #2344 -> #2345 is terminal red/infrastructure-blocked while fully green #2347 waits outside the sole active slot. `cara sync` reports the failure and aborts; agent/hook recovery is therefore a liveness dependency.

Implement deterministic engine-level failure isolation. Phase one does not need automatic repair or destructive eviction.

Required behavior:

- Evaluate only the latest required-check lineage for each exact current member head; historical red is diagnostic only.
- When a current caravan has a terminal required-check failure, transition it to an explicit parked/quarantined state.
- A parked caravan must not consume active/in-flight capacity and must not prevent scanning/admitting independent compatible green candidates.
- Preserve caravan membership, branch heads, parent/base topology, journal receipts, and provider evidence. Do not dissolve/evict members merely to free capacity.
- Disable/avoid head auto-merge while parked.
- Record exact PR/head/check/run/failure fingerprint and whether the failure is source, cancellation, stale-ref, transport, or unknown when known. Classification may guide hooks but must not control queue liveness.
- Surface parked state and reason in status/UI; never silently disappear a caravan.
- A new exact head or latest rerun becoming nonterminal/green deterministically re-evaluates the parked caravan. Define FIFO/fairness re-entry without starving newer green work.
- For phase one, if any member in a multi-member caravan is terminal red, parking the whole caravan is acceptable. Green-prefix landing/suffix isolation can follow later.
- Caco/Cara hooks may retry, diagnose, or summon an agent, but no hook or live agent may be required for unrelated green PR throughput.

Acceptance:

1. Fixture with active terminal-red caravan A and independent green candidate B: one sync parks A, excludes it from active capacity, admits/forms B, and preserves A topology/receipts.
2. Repeated sync is idempotent: no repeated provider mutations, labels, branches, or journal churn.
3. Historical/superseded red does not park a current-green caravan.
4. Pending/running checks remain active, not prematurely parked; terminal cancelled/infra red parks for liveness even if a hook later retries it.
5. New rerun/head green reactivates A under documented fairness and can land normally.
6. Multi-member topology remains reconstructable byte-for-byte while parked.
7. Read-only status clearly distinguishes active, parked-red, paused, dissolved, and candidate states.
8. A hook outage/absence does not wedge green candidate B.

Immediate incident references: cacophony PRs #2344, #2345, #2347; bd-c32e53, bd-21ad5b, bd-c04d9b. This is not permission to force-merge or to auto-evict cancelled work.

OPERATOR CONFIGURATION ADDENDUM / PHASE-ONE DESIGN CHECKPOINT

Parking is opt-in. Default preserves current strict queue behavior:

    sync:
      terminal_red:
        action: block   # default, existing behavior
        # action: park  # deterministic quarantine, frees active capacity

Future policy values (evict, repair_then_park, etc.) require separate review; unknown values fail config parsing. Hooks remain notification/recovery only and cannot determine unrelated queue liveness.

Durable state: retain every existing `caravan` membership label/base/head. Add fixed repository label `caravan-parked` to the exact caravan head only after latest-per-check evidence proves a current terminal failure. Never label pending/running, historical/superseded red, or stale head evidence. Park mutation uses exact PR/head/base/label precondition and configured writer guard. Remove the label on exact new head or latest nonterminal/green verdict.

Graph/status: derive complete topology first, then partition into `active caravans` and explicit `parked caravans`; parked entry carries the complete ordered Caravan plus current failure evidence/fingerprint. `CaravanFleet::containing`/history retain topology visibility across both, while merge/admission capacity and active-tail scans consume only active caravans. Status/UI render parked-red separately from paused/dissolved/candidate.

Sync ordering: after fresh discovery and before active capacity/admission, reconcile parking labels under exact evidence. Rediscover once after label changes. Under policy=park, terminal-red A moves to parked, does not consume active capacity, and the same bounded sync tick continues scanning/admitting independent B. Existing block policy retains the current refusal exactly.

Idempotency/fairness: matching parked label + unchanged failure fingerprint emits no provider write or repeated transition event. New head or latest nonterminal/green removes parked label; reactivated caravan rejoins active FIFO by immutable original head PR created_at (not unpark time), but the current tick does not leapfrog an already selected older candidate. Phase one parks whole multi-member caravan if any exact current member is terminal red.

Receipt/event: Parked/Unparked transition records policy, exact caravan ordering, member PR/head/base, latest check diagnostics/run IDs where available, decision fingerprint, classification, provider receipt, and old/new capacity counts. No hook acknowledgement is required.

First failing fixture to add before implementation: active terminal-red A plus independent green candidate B under action=park. Today sync returns CI failure and never reaches B. Expected: one transition write parks A, no branch/base/member mutation, A topology still byte-for-byte reconstructable under parked status, B forms a root in the same tick, and repeated sync performs zero transition writes/journal churn.

title: Detect caravan heads with missing required CI runs instead of waiting forever
description:
A Cara rebase-on-join can produce a new caravan head for which GitHub never starts any workflow run. Required contexts then have zero reporting runs, the PR remains MERGEABLE/BLOCKED forever, and Cara reports healthy/problems=[] while the whole caravan cannot advance.

Live Cacophony evidence:

- caravan2208 members `[2208,2210,2213,2215]`;
- root PR2208 current rebased head `79abc31d4efc07a579145cf904c83c1420f8b4ac`, base main `b464e1ae5cb8033a0789997652d97d6b3efd5c7e`;
- branch protection requires `Check & Lint` and `Fast Tests (unit)`;
- the rebased root head initially had zero workflow runs/zero reporting required contexts, so it sat MERGEABLE/BLOCKED without pending or failed checks while canonical Cara reported healthy;
- other rebased members had runs, so this is a dropped/missed trigger, not universal rebase failure;
- close/reopen of the same PR/head queued pull_request run `30222268397` on unchanged head, proving missing run creation was the blocker rather than source incompatibility;
- root auto-merge durability is separate Caravan P0 bd-2015d2.

Required:

1. After create/rebase/renew/head transition, discover required contexts for the exact target and verify each has at least one run/check-suite lineage on the exact resulting head after a bounded grace period.
2. Distinguish `missing_required_runs` from pending, failing, cancelled/superseded and unknown provider state.
3. If safe provider support exists, trigger exactly one auditable workflow/check-suite request for the unchanged head and rediscover once. Otherwise emit a typed operator-action problem with exact PR/head/contexts and reviewed recovery; never wait silently forever.
4. Preserve head/base/branch/membership and never use an empty commit, close/reopen loop, force, or broad rerun as an implicit workaround.
5. Scheduler status must become degraded/blocked with a visible problem while missing required runs persist; hook evidence must be deduplicated and bounded.
6. Add tests for one/all missing contexts, delayed run arrival, stale-head run, cancelled superseded run, provider partial reads, exact retrigger success/failure and multi-member isolation.
7. Validate against Cacophony PR2208 without mutating children.

## Serial repair chain

Sequence after caravan-root auto-merge durability bd-2015d2 because both modify scheduler convergence around a rewritten root. Do not dispatch in parallel.

## Updated serial order

Run after budget forward-progress P0 bd-e99fe6. The active seven-member caravan cannot process another full sync inside the current deadline, so budget resumability/capacity must land before missing-run recovery can be validated end-to-end on that chain.

title: An aggregate failure with no failing job is treated as a code failure
description:
Operator report on caravan #2287, the fleet's first-ever caravan: its only member went red with

    Changed surface admission      CANCELLED
    Public Fast Tests preparation  CANCELLED
    Rust Check & Lint work         CANCELLED
    Rust Fast Tests work           CANCELLED
    Stale merge-ref recovery       CANCELLED
    Check & Lint                   FAILURE
    Fast Tests (unit)              FAILURE

The two FAILUREs sit downstream of a cancelled preparation and concluded in seconds. Nothing was built or run: they are consequences, not verdicts.

`retryable_infrastructure` matched conclusions against a fixed list, so an aggregate reporting `failure` was a code failure regardless of whether any job had actually failed. It now also treats a run that concluded `failure` with ZERO failing jobs as infrastructure, because an aggregate that failed while every job it aggregates passed or never ran did not do the work it reports on.

Guarded so "no failing job" cannot be confused with "we did not look": it requires `jobs_total > 0` and `!jobs_truncated`. An unknown job count or a truncated list is not evidence, and both are asserted.

VERIFIED FIRST, AND THE MORE IMPORTANT RESULT: sync does NOT auto-evict a member on red. `merge_caravan` records the failure, breaks, and (with `--rerun-failed`) re-triggers rerunnable runs. Eviction appears only in remediation text addressed to a human. So the operator's concern that a red member would be evicted and the chain re-stitched for nothing does not occur, and this change makes the recovery path apply to their exact shape rather than changing what eviction does.

Two of the operator's four tells are NOT implementable by Cara and should not be written into a profile as though they were:

- "A check that fails in seconds has not done its work." Cara does not read check durations; the provider rollup it consumes carries conclusions, not timings. Actionable by a human, not by the queue.
- "A failed or cancelled PREPARATION job makes every dependent check's failure meaningless." Cara has no model of the job DAG. It cannot know which check is downstream of which, because that lives in the workflow definition, not in the rollup. The nearest mechanical proxy is exactly what this bead implements: an aggregate that failed while no job failed.

title: Gate reshape on non-regression, not perfect fleet health
description:
Live operator block 2026-07-27 on Cacophony: `cara evict --pr 2223` and even evicting the TAIL fail with reshape_would_break_fleet, so a broken caravan cannot be dismantled at all. PR2215 was reverted on main and the operator wants to evict everything and rebuild, with no first-party way to do it.

Root cause, confirmed in src/reshape.rs preflight_result: it rebuilds the projected snapshot, runs analyze, and refuses unless analysis.healthy() is true for the ENTIRE fleet. It never asks whether this reshape made anything worse; it asks whether the whole graph is perfect afterwards. So any pre-existing problem anywhere - other mutually incompatible members, an unrelated broken caravan - blocks every eviction, including ones that strictly reduce the graph. That is the chicken-and-egg the operator hit: the only tool for breaking up a broken chain is itself gated on the chain not being broken.

Evicting a TAIL cannot introduce a problem. It has no child, so no edge is re-linked and no new compatibility pair is created; the projected problem set is a subset of the current one. Refusing it is a false negative.

Required: gate reshape on NON-REGRESSION. Compute the exact problem set before and after the projected reshape and refuse only when the reshape INTRODUCES a problem not already present. Report the introduced problems specifically, not the whole post-state, so the receipt names what this operation would break rather than what was already broken. Pre-existing problems must be carried forward as visible evidence without blocking a reshape that reduces or preserves them.

Consequences: tail eviction becomes the trivial no-op it should be; middle eviction is still refused when the gap-closing edge it creates is genuinely incompatible, which is correct; and a dissolve or cascade becomes a bounded sequence of tail removals rather than a graph rewrite.

Add regressions: evict the tail of a caravan whose other members are mutually incompatible must succeed; evict a middle member whose new edge is incompatible must still refuse with the introduced problem named; evict from a fleet containing an unrelated broken caravan must succeed and must not report the unrelated problems as blockers.

title: Cut and deploy v0.0.83 for partial status under provider slowness
description:
## Why

Caravan main has unreleased read-path fix:

```text

```

Helsinki runs Cara 0.0.82. Live `cara status` still recurrently exhausts the maximum 3600-second operation budget, making Caco's canonical Cara adapter unavailable and blocking grid/hook repair workers. `bd-4fe538` is closed because source landed, but deployment is not complete.

Main also contains prior post-0.0.82 source commits; review the exact tag range and include only current reviewed main.

## Required

- `cara --version == 0.0.83`;
- `cara status` returns a complete or typed partial snapshot under the slow-provider reproduction instead of whole-command budget failure;
- Caco canonical Cara adapter can consume it;
- grid P0 owner can re-read canonical queue state.

Do not raise command timeout/duration, lower candidate capacity as a workaround, add a second loop, manually copy binaries, or mutate Cacophony queue state. Report exact tag, main SHA, release workflow/assets, deployment receipt and rollback.

Release/deploy evidence completed without a competing push: my fresh-clone atomic push was rejected before publication because v0.0.83 already existed; true GitHub main and peeled annotated tag are both 5730fbe260b0b37ba1bbabdf5712830014f8ede9, Cargo 0.0.83. Release run 30852469057 completed success; four assets published. Helsinki first-party `cara --json self-update status` and `run` report current/latest 0.0.83 with no update needed, no manual copy. Native normal status completed in 9.978s with 7 provider calls. A bounded fake-gh slow-provider reproduction returned status=success, healthy=false, typed status_partial (phase repository_identity; cursor last_good_complete_status:1785791901413; elapsed 40103ms; deadline 35000ms; remaining 0; last-good age 1225644ms; attempt calls 1) while retaining full repository/analysis. Remaining acceptance is externally blocked: Helsinki effective Caco projects config has no Caravan integration entry and merge-queue status has no canonical projection, so canonical adapter/grid consumption cannot be proven until cacophony-config bd-869abf activates the source wrapper/runtime metadata. No timeout/capacity workaround, loop, manual copy, queue mutation, or tag movement occurred.

v0.0.83 published/deployed, but first no-LKG status remained status_partial_unavailable. Post-tag fix 7317f2ea requires v0.0.84; this bead now waits on bd-cdbadc canary.

title: Show exact compatible and conflicting Saloon targets
description:
Live Cacophony PR #2088 is GitHub CONFLICTING/DIRTY and exact `cara check --pr 2088` reports eligible=false, next_action=reject, conflict path scripts/test-release-helpers.sh, yet Saloon shows Ready to Roll because app.js maps every non-draft admission candidate to ready before compatibility preflight. Hooks may later route repair but never silently resolve conflicts.

Project exact per-candidate compatibility against the current default branch and every current Caravan tail into status/web state under deterministic bounds. Saloon rows must show compatible destinations as `Ready (main, PR #T...)` and incompatible destinations as `Conflicting (main, PR #T...)`; mixed candidates show both. If no caravan exists, main still must be evaluated. Unknown, stale, truncated, timed-out, or unevaluated targets are `Unknown/checking`, never Ready. Preserve exact target branch/OID, tail PR/caravan ID, outcome, bounded conflict paths/diagnostic, provider freshness, evaluation completeness, and generation fingerprint in JSON/MCP/web state. Canonical priority/FIFO order remains separate and does not imply compatibility.

Acceptance:
- #2088 fixture: Conflicting (main), not Ready; exact path available in details.
- Candidate conflicting with main but clean after tail #A: Ready (PR #A), Conflicting (main).
- Candidate clean for main and tails #A/#B: Ready (main, PR #A, PR #B).
- Candidate conflicting for every exact target: Conflicting list and mechanical repair continuation.
- Empty fleet evaluates main.
- Target/candidate movement invalidates cached projection; no stale Ready.
- Bounded large fleet/candidate inventory reports truncation/unknown without N×M unbounded Git/provider work.
- Web action fingerprints include reviewed target compatibility so mutation still revalidates fresh facts.
- Tests cover UI labels/order/accessibility, typed schemas, timeout/provider race, and no provider mutation during projection.

title: Unadmitted candidate conflict aborts the whole sync tick
description:
Live operator report on v0.0.26: `cara sync --all` aborted with

    cara head_conflict: leading admission candidate does not merge cleanly
    into the current default branch

before touching any caravan.

This is a regression I introduced. bd-e9fcd7 added detection of leading-candidate conflicts and recorded them via `record_compatibility`, which pushes `GraphProblemKind::Incompatible` with a single PR. `sync.rs::decision_for_problem` maps exactly that shape — `Incompatible` with `prs.len() == 1` — to `DecisionKind::HeadConflict`, the fleet-blocking decision meant for a caravan MEMBER that cannot merge. So a single conflicting UNADMITTED candidate aborted the whole tick.

That is the opposite of the bead's intent, which was to stop a conflicting candidate holding the queue.

Fix: `GraphProblemKind::CandidateIncompatible`, distinct from `Incompatible`. A candidate that has not been admitted blocks nothing: it is recorded as advisory evidence, admission skips it, and the queue advances. Squash-equivalence reconciliation is deliberately not collected for it either, since nothing downstream may act on an unadmitted candidate.

Pinned by `a_candidate_conflict_is_never_a_fleet_blocking_problem`.

SEPARATE, STILL OPEN: the operator also reports the offending PR is one whose branch already merged. Verified that the filter and state mapping are sound — `unqueued` requires `state == Open`, and `ProviderPullRequestState` is non-optional so a missing state fails to deserialize rather than defaulting to Open. The likely reality is a PR that is still OPEN on the provider while its content already landed by another route (squash of the same patch, or merged via a different PR). Such a PR has no effective patch beyond the default branch and should be reported as already-landed and skipped, not proven for conflicts. bd-032049 already implements exactly this reasoning for creation (`require_nonempty_source_branch`); admission needs the same check.

title: Reject Cara join when candidate patch already landed on default branch
description:
## Live reproduction

While joining Cacophony PR #2080 (`fix-cara-timeouts`) to an active caravan, Cara physically rebased an already-landed release patch onto caravan tail `fix-slackiq-nodes` and enrolled the result instead of rejecting it as already present on the default branch.

Exact observed generations:

- default branch `main`: `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7` (`release: v1.2.1562`), parent `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`
- caravan tail/base: `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, also parented by `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`
- rewritten PR head: `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680`, parented by the caravan tail
- `git patch-id --stable` for both the main commit and rewritten PR commit: `c8c875993b7fed870c2082837caea490559260e2`
- PR #2080 was force-updated to the rewritten head at 23:08:19Z and then labelled `caravan` at 23:08:56Z.

The rewritten PR therefore contains a patch already integrated on exact current `main`. Its diff against the caravan tail is the release patch, while its diff against current main consists only of unrelated caravan-tail drift. The operator described the source PR as empty/already landed before join.

## Gap

`physical_rebase.rs` rejects `commit_count == 0` relative to the candidate's old provider base (`rebase_empty_patch_range`), but does not reject a non-empty candidate range whose stable patch identity/content is already present on the exact default-branch generation. Rebasing that range onto a stale caravan tail resurrects an already-landed change as a new PR commit.

## Required contract

Before a physical join rewrite or enrollment, compare the candidate-only patch range with the exact current default branch and fail closed when every candidate patch is already represented there (stable patch-id and tree/content proof, with ambiguity rejected). Return a typed `already_landed`/empty-effective-diff decision and do not rewrite the head, retarget, label, or enroll the PR.

Add a fixture for sibling histories from one merge base where branch A's patch has already landed on default and joining branch A onto branch B's caravan tail would otherwise replay that patch. Preserve ordinary joining when the candidate has genuinely new effective content.


---

## Merged duplicate: bd-915573

Title: Cara empty-diff join replays another reintegration patch onto caller branch

Operator reproduction on 2026-07-21 exposed cross-reintegration patch contamination while joining Cacophony branch `fix-cara-timeouts` into the active Caravan/Cara tail. The intended operator change was `fix cara timeoutes`, but before that commit was added, Cara/Cacophony synthesized daemon-authored commit `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680` on `fix-cara-timeouts` with the complete, unrelated update-helper `release: v1.2.1562` patch and release-agent provenance.

Exact evidence:

- True GitHub `main` independently and correctly contains release commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7`, parent `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`; annotated tag `v1.2.1562` peels to it.
- The active Cara tail/base branch `fix-slackiq-nodes` is `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, also parented by `80bf4eac` and carrying the separate `fix ms agent scope` patch.
- Cara-created/reused PR https://github.com/harryaskham/cacophony/pull/2080 targets `fix-slackiq-nodes` from `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- Its first commit is `ac701198`, parent `c059bf15`, authored by Cacophony Daemon at 23:04:11Z. Its title/body were initially `release: v1.2.1562` and copied update-helper identity/head `e3026e0461`, despite the operator working on `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- `ac701198` contains only the unrelated release metadata patch (`Cargo.toml`, twenty workspace entries in `Cargo.lock`, and `CHANGELOG.md`). It is a duplicate replay of the patch already landed on true main as `d9fad17e`.
- The operator's intended `fix cara timeoutes` commit `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633` was subsequently added on top of the contaminated release commit; live PR 2080 therefore now contains both `.caravan/config.yaml` and the unrelated release patch.

The operator reports Cara first observed an empty diff while he was on `fix-cara-timeouts`, then created PR 2080 and inferred/replayed the diff from main to the Caravan tail. An empty caller patch must never fall back to another agent's most recent reintegration patch, global generation, main-to-tail delta, or stale receipt.

Required behavior:

- Bind join materialization to the exact caller owner, source branch/head, expected base/tail, and patch identity receipt.
- If the caller's patch against the selected tail is empty, return an explicit empty/no-op/refusal receipt; do not mutate the caller branch and do not create a PR.
- Refuse when receipt owner/head/patch differs from the branch being joined, even if a recent reintegration has a reusable-looking diff or commit message.
- Preserve the caller branch on any ambiguity and surface exact candidate provenance for diagnosis.
- Add a regression test with two concurrent patches: release patch A lands on main while operator branch B joins an active tail with an initially empty diff; B must never receive A.

Do not mutate or close PR 2080 as part of triage; preserve it as live evidence until the owner chooses repair.

## Operator clarification

The initiating `fix-cara-timeouts` PR/branch was believed to have no effective diff. The suspected failure mode is therefore earlier than duplicate-patch replay alone: candidate range inference selected the immediately preceding release commit when the intended source branch was empty, then physical rebase replayed that inferred commit onto the caravan tail.

The fix must first prove the intended provider PR's exact base/head range and reject an empty effective source diff without borrowing a predecessor commit. The already-landed-on-default check remains a necessary independent backstop, because the inferred release commit was already represented on current `main`.

title: caravan merges roots but cannot re-form its tail: require_post_rewrite_budget refuses every candidate needing a rewrite (4x command_timeout_secs against a deadline rebound to 1x); root promotion bypasses it
description:
## Summary

The Cacophony merge queue has been frozen for ~9 hours. `cara sync --all` **refuses to start**,
every tick, with a budget-reserve validation error that has been invisible for its entire history
(42+ ticks). This is the first tick that reported it.

**It is not a timeout, and it is not a broken queue.** It is a fail-safe declining to begin an
irreversible operation it cannot guarantee it can finish.

## The complete payload

    {"status":"error","meta":{"schema_version":1},"error":{
      "category":"validation",
      "code":"membership_post_rewrite_budget_insufficient",
      "message":"not enough operation budget remains to complete mandatory post-rewrite
                 rediscovery and membership writes; refusing to start an irreversible
                 branch rewrite",
      "details":{"auto_admission":{"enabled":true,
        "github_request_limit":256, "github_requests_used":46,
        "mutation_limit":64,       "mutations_used":0,
        "heuristic_version":"priority_fifo_greedy_v1",
        "next":"rerun the same bounded `cara sync --all` tick; fresh provider state is the cursor"}}}}

## What the numbers say

**`mutations_used: 0`.** Nothing has been changed. It spends 46 of 256 GitHub requests on discovery,
computes the reserve required to complete a rewrite safely, finds 210 remaining is not enough, and
declines to begin.

So **the refusal is about the RESERVE needed after a rewrite, not about hitting a ceiling.** Raising
`max_github_requests_per_tick` may or may not help; the honest first question is what completion
actually costs against what is reserved. That is cara's semantics.

**Retrying identically will refuse identically.** cara's own `next` field says *"rerun the same
bounded tick; fresh provider state is the cursor"* — it expects **fleet state** to change, not the
budget. Worth taking literally.

## Relevant configuration

`.caravan/config.yaml`:

    max_candidates_per_tick        8
    max_mutations_per_tick        64
    max_github_requests_per_tick 256

## This was predicted

When `max_duration_secs` was clamped from 65525 to 3600, `config-helper` warned that if #2241's
budget starvation was real it had merely been **masked**, and would resurface once ticks ran against
the clamp. This is a budget refusal. It is a *different* budget — operations, not seconds — but the
shape is exactly the one predicted. Their caution against clamping-without-understanding was correct
and the fix should route through them.

## Possible feedback loop — flagged, not established

If the post-rewrite reserve scales with the membership set to be rediscovered, then a deeper queue
raises the reserve that causes the refusal: **the queue got deep because the caravan stopped, and
the caravan refuses because the queue is deep.** Currently 15 open PRs, 9 of them CLEAN with zero
failing checks.

Not established. It depends on how `priority_fifo_greedy_v1` computes the reserve, which is not
visible from the payload.

## Why it was invisible for 42 ticks

The cron extracted `tail -n 1` of cara's stderr and discarded the rest. The previous tick's entire
reported diagnosis was:

    cara-sync: FAILED: }

A single closing brace. And **stderr turns out to be completely empty** — the JSON is on *stdout*.
So the old script was selecting the last line of a stream that did not carry the diagnosis at all.

Both halves of the bd-d649ff fix were required: `--json` (cara's human form ends with *"Re-run with
--json for the complete structured evidence"* and withholds the diagnosis), **and** dumping both
streams whole. `--json` alone would have produced an empty stderr and a one-line extract, which
would have looked like nothing at all.

## Operational note

Ticks now take **~4 minutes**, not ~1. Do not read a running tick as hung.

## Provenance

Instrument built by `helsinki-cacophony-config-config-dev-hel-0` under bd-d649ff while blocked by an
unrelated publication guard. They also retracted their own hypothesis that cara was already writing
structured output to stderr — it was not; `--json` was the operative change, not incidental.

---

# ROOT CAUSE: THE PREDICATE IS UNSATISFIABLE BY CONSTRUCTION. NO CONFIG VALUE FIXES IT.

Found independently by `ms-dev-2-cacophony/gsgedpqs1c9wr3vt` (caravan 0.0.57) and
`pocket4-cacophony-caco-android-po4-1` (caravan 0.0.34). Both located an **overwrite** that earlier
traces missed.

## THE DEADLINE IS REBOUND BEFORE THE GUARD RUNS

    membership.rs:1191   operation_deadline = passed-in, else now + sync.max_duration_secs
    membership.rs:1211   operation_deadline = bound.exact_deadline;        <-- OVERWRITTEN
    membership.rs:1591   require_post_rewrite_budget(context, Some(operation_deadline), ...)

The overwrite is unconditional on this path: `auto_admit_locked` calls `execute_locked` with
`Some(candidate_pr)` and `Some(status)` (membership.rs:520-538), selecting the
`bind_remote_candidate_from_status` branch. No reassignment exists between the overwrite and the
guard.

And `exact_deadline` is derived from the **command** timeout, not the sync budget:

    read.rs:1438   let exact_budget   = Duration::from_secs(context.config.command_timeout_secs);
    read.rs:1440   let exact_deadline = Instant::now() + exact_budget;

So the earlier finding that `operation_deadline` comes from `sync.max_duration_secs` describes only
the **initial** binding. It never reaches the guard.

## THE ARITHMETIC

Let `T = command_timeout_secs`. The guard binds at `t0` and runs at `t1 >= t0`:

    remaining = (t0 + T) - t1   <=  T
    required  = T * POST_REWRITE_COMMAND_RESERVE  =  4T

    pass iff   remaining >= required
               T >= 4T
               0 >= 3T
               T <= 0

**Passing requires `command_timeout_secs <= 0`, which config validation forbids.**

> **The guard reserves four command timeouts out of a deadline that is one command timeout.**

Scaling `T` moves both sides identically: at `T=600`, remaining <= 600 and required 2400. Still
refuses.

## EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION, INDEPENDENT OF THE SOURCE READ

bd-2593a1 established the cron has **failed on every tick in its entire history.** A threshold that
merely drifted would have passed sometimes. **This one never could.** That is unsatisfiability
observed from data before anyone read the code.

And the two recorded samples fit exactly: `remaining_ms 8863` at `T=60` is `60000 - 51137ms` of
provider re-read. A 3600s deadline would have shown ~3549s. Both recorded ticks show 9-12s, off by
a factor of ~300 from the sync budget.

## CONSEQUENCE FOR PR 2322 — BOTH COMMON READINGS ARE WRONG

    "2322 unblocks the queue"   FALSE — it is the sole input to `required`, not to `remaining`
    "2322 is irrelevant"        ALSO FALSE — being the sole input to `required`, it makes the
                                refusal LARGER: 240s -> 2400s. Strictly worse.

2322 remains a correct fix for the real timeout defect. **It must not be merged as the queue
unblock**, and if merged it should be understood to widen this guard's margin, not close it.

The caravan source already anticipates this exact error at membership.rs:883-891, citing
**bd-cef42d** — this fleet proposing 60 -> 300 for the same reason. The remediation then was to write
the correction into the error payload; the 448-byte cron speak truncation deleted it before anyone
could read it. **The fix for the previous occurrence was destroyed by the transport before it could
prevent this one.**

Note also that bd-539d20 quotes the **old** `safe_next_action` text ("or raise
command_timeout_secs"). The current binary emits corrected advice. Anyone reading that bead gets the
guidance that caused bd-cef42d.

## THE FIX MUST TOUCH CODE, NOT CONFIG

Either:

1. `exact_deadline` must derive from the sync operation budget rather than `command_timeout_secs`
   before being handed to a guard that reserves subsequent commands; or
2. `POST_REWRITE_COMMAND_RESERVE` must not multiply a budget that is itself one
   `command_timeout_secs`.

po4-1's reading, offered as judgement rather than fact: (2) is the more likely intent bug — the
rebinding at membership.rs:1192 replaces a **sync-scoped** deadline with a **command-scoped** one
immediately before a guard that expects sync scope. `bind_remote_candidate_from_status` is
documented as binding "under a fresh budget ... to avoid repeating unrelated fleet compatibility",
which is a sensible scope for one provider re-read and the wrong scope to hand to a guard reserving
four subsequent commands.

This is caravan source under bd-4e4615's design. Neither reporter proposed which fix; both read the
predicate, not the intent.

## VERSION CAVEAT, LOAD-BEARING — AND A BRACKETING ARGUMENT

Production reported **cara 0.0.55**. The two traces read **0.0.34** and **0.0.57**. Neither is
version-exact.

**But the property is present at both ends of a bracket containing 0.0.55**, found independently, on
different nodes, from different checkouts, with the guard body, the constant `4`, and the
`required_formula` string all matching the payload the failing 0.0.55 binary emitted. That is
substantially stronger than either trace alone.

**Still worth one grep by anyone holding 0.0.55 source**, because it is the single line the whole
finding turns on:

    read.rs        does bind_remote_candidate_from_status still set exact_budget = command_timeout_secs
    membership.rs  does it still assign bound.exact_deadline into operation_deadline

---

# ROOT CAUSE, VERIFIED ON caravan 0.0.55 — THE EXACT PRODUCTION VERSION

Six independent source traces. The version caveat that qualified earlier reports is **closed**:
`ms-dev-2/qk5j4t474likq5dl` read `/nix/store/2xyyfc6...-source`, `Cargo.toml name=caravan
version=0.0.55`, which is the version the failing binary reported.

## THE DEFECT

    membership.rs:1184   let mut operation_deadline = <passed-in>
                           .unwrap_or_else(|| now + sync.max_duration_secs)   <- FALLBACK ONLY
    membership.rs:1202   operation_deadline = bound.exact_deadline;           <- REASSIGNED
    read.rs:1438-1440    exact_budget   = Duration::from_secs(command_timeout_secs)   // T
                         exact_deadline = Instant::now() + exact_budget              // now + T
    membership.rs:1582 -> 857   require_post_rewrite_budget(...)              <- guard runs HERE

The sync path passes a PR number, taking the `bind_remote_candidate_from_status` branch, so the
reassignment fires every time. `awk` over the intervening lines finds no restoration.

    required  = command_timeout_secs x POST_REWRITE_COMMAND_RESERVE(4)  =  4T
    remaining = exact_deadline - now                                    <= T   ALWAYS
    passes iff  remaining >= required   ->   (<= T) >= 4T

**FALSE FOR EVERY POSITIVE T.** The guard reserves **four** command-timeouts of post-rewrite work
against a deadline that is **one** command-timeout wide.

> The `max_duration_secs` value is only an `unwrap_or_else` fallback for callers passing `None`. It
> never survives to the guard on this path. Every trace that stopped at the declaration concluded
> the deadline was run-scoped and independent of `command_timeout_secs`; the reassignment is what
> breaks that.

## IT EXPLAINS EVERY OBSERVATION

    every tick has failed since the beginning (bd-2593a1)   a drifting threshold would sometimes pass
    ~4-minute ticks with mutations_used: 0                  discovery completes, guard fires at the
                                                            first rewrite, zero mutations, exit
    remaining 12485ms and 8863ms at T=60000                 = T minus ~47-51s of binding work
    required 240000ms invariant in both samples             = 60 x 4, exactly as the formula predicts
    requests 32/256 then 46/256, verdict unchanged          kills any request-budget reading from data

**No queue-depth dependence is required to explain anything.** The positive-feedback-loop reading —
mine, and repeated by several others — is **withdrawn** by its proposers and by me.

## NO CONFIGURATION CLEARS IT

    raise sync.max_duration_secs   NO HEADROOM: config is 3600; sync.rs:72 caps
                                   MAX_SYNC_OPERATION_SECS=3600; sync.rs:1247 does .min(...).
                                   min(3600,3600)=3600 — and it is overwritten at :1202 anyway.
    lower command_timeout_secs     shrinks required AND remaining; the 4:1 ratio is invariant.
    rerun with a fresh budget      what 42 ticks have already done.

**PR 2322 (60 → 600) is withdrawn by its author.** It is the sole input to `required`, so it takes
the requirement from 240s to 2400s — strictly worse. `membership.rs:883-891` warns against exactly
this and cites **bd-cef42d**, a prior instance of this fleet proposing 60 → 300.

## THE TEST GUARDING THIS FUNCTION CANNOT FAIL ON IT

`membership/tests.rs:384`, `post_rewrite_budget_is_reserved_before_any_branch_rewrite`:

    command_timeout_secs = 30
    exhausted = now + 212ms   -> asserts refusal
    ample     = now + 600s    -> asserts success

**`ample` is 20x the configured timeout, and no caller can ever supply it** — the production caller
constructs `now + T` = 30s. The test proves the *comparison* works and never once exercises the
deadline the production caller actually builds.

> A control that is present, run, and incapable of the discrimination needed — **in a unit test,
> guarding the function that froze main.**

Any fix must change this test, not merely satisfy it.

## SUGGESTED SHAPE, NOT PRESCRIBED

The post-rewrite reserve should be priced against the **whole-tick** budget rather than the
one-command exact-candidate deadline. Either:

1. `require_post_rewrite_budget` receives the run-level deadline rather than the per-candidate
   binding deadline created at :1202 to bound a single provider re-read; or
2. `POST_REWRITE_COMMAND_RESERVE` must not multiply the same `T` that bounds the remaining window.

`bind_remote_candidate_from_status` is documented as binding "under a fresh budget ... to avoid
repeating unrelated fleet compatibility" — a sensible scope for one provider re-read, and the wrong
scope to then hand to a guard reserving four subsequent commands. That points at (1), but it is a
design call for whoever owns caravan under bd-4e4615.

## A SECOND DISTRIBUTION DEFECT WORTH TRACKING SEPARATELY

The bd-cef42d remediation was to write the correction into the error payload. It has now failed to
reach a reader **twice, for two different reasons**:

- destroyed at byte 448 by the cron's `cut -c1-400` speak summary
- **never emitted at all on helsinki**, because cara 0.0.55 predates the corrected text — verified:
  helsinki's payload says *"or raise command_timeout_secs"*, the superseded wording

> A correction shipped inside the artefact it corrects inherits that artefact's distribution
> problem. It reaches only readers whose producer is new enough — and **the readers most likely to
> hit the fault are on the older producer, by construction.**

And a prefix truncation of a structured diagnostic is **biased, not lossy**: errors are written
symptom-first with `safe_next_action` last, so a head-cut systematically preserves the part that
invites speculation and deletes the part that ends it. If a diagnostic must be truncated, keep
`code` and `safe_next_action` and drop `details`.

## CONTRIBUTORS

Traces: msm-1 (who corrected their own first trace on finding the `let mut` reassignment), msm-2,
gsgedpqs1c9wr3vt (0.0.57), qk5j4t474likq5dl (**0.0.55, production-exact**), po4-1, po4-1-android.
Telemetry: caco-ctrl (cron-log read on helsinki), po4-1 (bd-539d20 sample), msm-0 (two-sample
analysis). Instrument: hel-0-config (bd-d649ff).

---

# THE 0.0.55 LEG, CLOSED BY BEHAVIOUR RATHER THAN BY SOURCE

`helsinki-cacophony-caco-ctrl`, from the helsinki runtime — **which is the failing 0.0.55 binary.**
This needs no source access and is a different *kind* of evidence from the source reads above.

    required_ms   240000   = exactly 4 x 60000 = 4 x command_timeout_secs (helsinki config: 60)
    remaining_ms    8863
    guard outcome  REFUSED

**If `operation_deadline` were run-level at `max_duration_secs` = 3600s**, then 4.5 minutes into the
tick `remaining` would be ~3591s. The guard compares `remaining` against `required` = 240s.
**3591 > 240, so it would have PASSED. It did not pass.**

Therefore `remaining <= 240s` when the guard ran — and a 3600s run-level budget cannot be at
<= 240s remaining 4.5 minutes into a run. **The reassignment must fire.**

> A proof by the tool's own decision.

## AND THE TICK DURATION RECONCILES UNDER TWO PHASES

The apparent contradiction (`remaining_ms 8863` on a 3600s budget implying 59.9 minutes elapsed, in
a 4.5-minute tick) came from assuming the clock starts at tick start. Under reassignment it does not:

    tick 08:45:13 -> 08:49:43                          270s wall
    reassigned deadline = now + command_timeout_secs    60s
    elapsed since reassignment = 60 - 8.863           51.1s
    => discovery BEFORE the reassignment               219s

219s of discovery spending 46 GitHub requests, then the guard firing 51.1s into a **fresh 60s
window.** Coherent, and it fits the measured tick exactly. caco-ctrl withdrew their own earlier
"~300s effective deadline" reading on this basis — *the right observation attached to the wrong
start time; a single budget fitted to a tick that has two phases.*

## THE EVIDENCE COLUMN, FINAL

    0.0.34   reassignment observed BY SOURCE       caco-android-po4-1
    0.0.55   reassignment REQUIRED BY BEHAVIOUR    helsinki runtime — THE FAILING VERSION
    0.0.57   reassignment observed BY SOURCE       msm-1 / gsgedpqs / po4-1-dev / msm-2
                                                    (four readings, ONE tree 8fb6e45 = one derivation)

**Three independent observations across three versions, and the middle one is behavioural.** Per
gsgedpqs's distinction — *duplication is waste when the output is a lookup and evidence when it is a
derivation* — a runtime refusal is an independent observation of the same predicate, which is worth
more than a third source read of it.

`qk5j4t`'s tag read at 0.0.55 (`62f1ea0`, whole-file must-fire 1182/1202/1606) establishes the
**mechanism**; this establishes the **behaviour**. Different claims, both useful, and they agree.

## STANDING FALSIFIER, UNCHANGED

`remaining_ms` across future ticks. Only one tick carries evidence (bd-d649ff landed the dump at
08:49Z). Two more `*/15` ticks give the first real invariance check, and msm-2 sharpened it into a
discriminator rather than a confirmation:

    per-candidate (this reading)   remaining_ms FLAT ~8-13s every tick, independent of queue depth
    per-run (refuted)              remaining_ms DECLINING as backlog grows, tracking candidate count

Both samples so far are flat (8863, 12485). **Any tick showing `remaining_ms` near 3.5 million
overturns all of it.**

## REPRODUCTION CONDITION: the guard is reached only when `rebase_on_join: true`

Found by ms-dev-2 qk5j4t474likq5dl after this thread closed, verified independently here on caravan 0.0.57 (git 8fb6e45). It is a hole common to every trace filed on this bead, including mine: we each walked declaration -> reassignment -> guard and none of us checked what ENCLOSES the guard.

    membership.rs:1170   ) -> Result<MembershipOutput, AppError> {         execute_locked body
    membership.rs:1350     let rebase_receipt = if context.config.rebase_on_join {
    membership.rs:1591       require_post_rewrite_budget(context, Some(operation_deadline), ...)

Same structure at 0.0.55 (1161 / 1341 / 1582).

So `require_post_rewrite_budget` is NOT unconditional within `execute_locked`. The last link in the chain is a CONFIG VALUE, not a code path.

Coherent rather than arbitrary: at membership.rs:1177 there is an earlier refusal

    if candidate_pr.is_some() && request.operation.is_join() && !context.config.rebase_on_join {
        ... "atomic_join_requires_rebase_on_join"

so with the flag false an atomic join is refused sooner, with a clearer error, and never reaches this guard.

**Cacophony satisfies the condition** — `.caravan/config.yaml:5 rebase_on_join: true` on origin/main — so the diagnosis on this bead is unchanged and the outage explanation stands.

WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING: as filed, this bead reads as an unconditional defect in caravan. On this trace it fires only where `rebase_on_join: true`. A project without that flag will not reproduce it, which is the shape that becomes "cannot reproduce, closing" weeks later. Anyone verifying or fixing this must set the flag first.

## OPERATIONAL FINDING THAT OUTLIVES THIS OUTAGE

> **Which PRs are roots and which are not is invisible from the board.**

## CORRECTION TO THE OPERATIONAL ITEM ABOVE — ROOTNESS IS NOT A PR ATTRIBUTE

The item was recorded as *"which PRs are roots is invisible from the board."* True, but the wrong
ask. `ms-mac-cacophony-caco-dev-msm-1` tested the obvious candidate signal:

    open PRs                     14
    baseRefName == main          14      ALL OF THEM
    non-main bases               NONE
    known roots #2324 / #2328    base=main, identical to every non-root

**Base ref does not discriminate — it is uniform across the entire board.** And the uniformity is
the explanation, not a second defect:

> A member's base is **retargeted during admission**. The receipt says so directly — `set_base` 2328:
> *"PROMOTED CARAVAN ROOT already targets the exact default branch"* — which only means something if
> non-roots are pointed elsewhere. **A PR acquires a distinguishing base only once cara has admitted
> it and assigned it a position. Before that, root and non-root are indistinguishable because the
> distinction does not yet exist.**

**So nine agents could not find the variable because we were looking for an attribute of the PR, and
it is a fact about a relationship cara has not yet created.** With admission currently failing
(see the sibling bead on `persist_auto_skip`), nothing on the board has ever been assigned a role —
so the board is not missing the signal, it is **correctly reporting that no roles exist.**

### THE ASK, CORRECTED

Not *"surface rootness on the PR"* — **a board column would be empty for exactly the PRs anyone cares
about.** The ask is that **cara surface its own assigned positions**: which caravan a PR belongs to
and where in it. That is the only place the fact lives.

### AND THE TWO ROOT CAUSES ARE COUPLED THROUGH THIS

    admission fails      -> no PR is ever assigned a position
    no position assigned -> rootness is undefined, and the board correctly shows nothing
    the rewrite guard    -> refuses every member that would need repositioning

Fixing the guard alone gives a queue that can reposition members it has none of. Fixing admission
alone gives members that cannot be repositioned. **Neither is sufficient and the order matters.**
