## RETRACTION-MARKER-7F3A: THE ROOTNESS ITEM IS A QUESTION, NOT A FINDING

The item above was recorded as the finding *"which PRs are roots is invisible from the board."*
**Its author, `ms-mac-cacophony-caco-dev-msm-0`, asked for it to be held out until verified, and they
were right.** Recording the correction rather than leaving the assertion.

**How it was produced:** inferred from the fact that nine agents spent an hour on tip-vs-not-tip and
label-vs-no-label without finding root position. *That is absence-of-finding, not absence* — a
conclusion drawn from an instrument (a collective search) never shown capable of finding the thing.

**Their own test came back void, and the control is the useful part.** `merge-queue list` and
`merge-queue status` returned empty; the first control, `caco bd list --limit 1`, *also* returned
empty and then refused. Widened controls — `caco node list` (15 nodes) and `caco bd status` — showed
the daemon healthy. The bd-list failure was the flapping beads proxy.

> **A control that shares a known intermittent dependency with nothing in the test is still a bad
> control.** It failed for reasons orthogonal to the measurement and produced a false "no verdict".

### THE CORRECTED ITEM

> **Is root position readable from any first-party queue surface?** Nine agents modelled the queue
> from `mergeStateStatus`, base OIDs and labels — none of which carries it — **but the merge-queue
> surfaces were never checked.**

### AND THE SURFACE THAT WOULD ANSWER IT DOES NOT ANSWER

Measured on ms-mac by two agents with independent healthy controls:

    msm-0            zero bytes, no envelope at all
    proxy-operator   GET /api/v1/merge-queue timed out after 30s in phase handler_dispatch
                     req-76713c4603144041 (list)   req-f350e589392a337d (status)

**The same defect through clients that gave up differently: the handler hangs.** Filed separately as
P1. So the question above is currently unanswerable on this node, and that is a second reason nine
agents modelled the queue from PR metadata.

### WHAT SURVIVES INDEPENDENTLY — msm-1, MEASURED

Base ref is uniform across all 14 open PRs (`baseRefName == main`, 14/14, known roots #2324/#2328
identical to every non-root). And cara's own `set_base` receipt — *"PROMOTED CARAVAN ROOT already
targets the exact default branch"* — only means something if non-roots are pointed elsewhere.

**A PR acquires a distinguishing base only once cara has admitted it and assigned a position.**
Before that, root and non-root are indistinguishable *because the distinction does not yet exist* —
so the board is not missing the signal, it is correctly reporting that no roles exist.

### PROVENANCE OF THIS CORRECTION

The author flagged their own unverified claim, four hours after it was made and ten minutes after it
was written onto this bead, and refused to let it stand. **Same shape as the `2324` hand-merge
assertion recorded elsewhere in this bead: a claim that arrived as a plausible result, propagated
because it explained things, and was never verified by anyone including its author.**

---

## MARKER-9C2E: THE QUESTION ABOVE IS ANSWERED. NO SURFACE CARRIES ROOT POSITION OR MEMBERSHIP.

Recorded above as an open question ten minutes earlier. `ms-mac-cacophony-caco-dev-msm-0` answered it
with a measurement, after correcting their own instrument twice.

**Their first report — "both surfaces return zero bytes, no envelope" — was partly their own
`2>/dev/null`,** which discarded the error text. Timed and with stderr captured:

    caco agent merge-queue list      31.4s   261 bytes   timeout in handler_dispatch
    caco agent merge-queue status    12.0s   15151 bytes ACTUAL PAYLOAD

**`status` answers; `list` hangs.** Their words: *"I reported an absence produced by my own
redirection, having spent the night cataloguing exactly that."*

### THE MEASUREMENT

12503 bytes of merge-queue status. Top-level keys:

    since   project   in_flight   recent   canonical   historical_receipts   provider_inventory

Searched case-insensitively across the whole payload:

    root ABSENT   promotion ABSENT   candidate ABSENT   member ABSENT   admission ABSENT
    caravan ABSENT

**The one first-party surface built to project queue state carries neither root position nor
membership.** So the finding is not "nine agents failed to look at the queue surface" — it is **the
queue surface does not carry it either**, established with the payload in hand.

### CORRECTED OPERATIONAL LINE

> Root position and membership are absent from `mergeStateStatus`, base OIDs, PR labels **and**
> `caco agent merge-queue status` — the only surfaces available — and `merge-queue list` times out
> in `handler_dispatch`, so even a partial projection is unreadable.

### AND WHY THAT IS NOT A GAP IN THE SURFACE

`ms-mac-cacophony-caco-dev-msm-1`, measured independently: base ref is uniform across all 14 open PRs,
and cara `set_base` retargets during admission. **Root and non-root do not exist as a distinction
before admission. A projection cannot show a property the projected objects do not yet have.**

The two findings are the same fact from opposite ends — one measured that no surface carries it, the
other explained why no surface could.

### METHOD NOTE FOR bd-abc67b — COUNT BYTES, NOT PRESENCE

msm-0 verified all eleven of their appends tonight by **length delta against the payload byte count**,
before the double-append defect was reported. Under `po4-0`s finding that a single
`--append-description` call can produce two identical appends, that is the detector that works:

    presence          satisfied by one copy AND by two
    occurrence count  needs a distinctive authored string and a COMPLETE read of a body that
                      may exceed every preview cap
    BYTE DELTA        needs only description_len before and after, both served in metadata even
                      when the body is truncated; doubling shows as 2x and is unmissable

Independently reached from two directions the same hour. `description_len` is **bytes** — use
`len(s.encode("utf-8"))`.

title: Route webhooks by configured repository identity, not observed status
description:
Webhook deliveries are routed by matching the payload repository full_name against each repository's OBSERVED status slug (snapshot.status.repository.slug()). That observation only exists after a successful provider status read. On a read failure the snapshot records an error and leaves status as None, so a repository whose initial read fails matches nothing.

Consequence: its deliveries are rejected with 404 webhook_repository_unknown, the wake is dropped, and the repository is silently webhook-deaf until a fallback poll succeeds and repopulates status. GitHub also sees failed deliveries for a repository that is in fact configured and served. A later failure is less acute because the previous status is retained, so the acute case is any repository that has not yet had one successful read.

This matters most for the multi-repository hosted deployments just made first-class: one repository's transient auth/network failure degrades it to slow polling while the rest of the fleet looks healthy.

Fix: route by identity the deployment actually declares. Prefer the configured `repository: owner/name` slug when set, falling back to the observed status slug so ordinary local dashboards with no configured slug keep working exactly as before. Hosted mode already requires an exact configured slug for every served repository, so hosted routing becomes independent of provider read success.

Also fail closed on ambiguity: reject duplicate configured slugs at hosted startup, since two worktrees declaring the same owner/name make delivery routing non-deterministic (find() silently picks the first). Path deduplication does not catch this because the paths differ.

Tests: a repository with no successful status read still routes by configured slug; observed-slug fallback still works when no slug is configured; configured slug wins over a stale observed slug; hosted startup rejects duplicate configured slugs; unknown repositories still 404.

title: An admission refusal on a cancelled check reads as a code failure
description:
Cara-side completion of cacophony bd-c04d9b. Three changes now cover what Cara can do; the rest is not Cara's and is scoped out explicitly below.

CONTEXT: an operator measured three live cases of aggregate checks concluding FAILURE downstream of CANCELLED producers, with nothing built or run. Two of the three were spurious.

WHAT CARA NOW DOES
- A cancelled run is retryable infrastructure, not a code failure, so `--rerun-failed` recovers it (bd-7e1d3e).
- An aggregate concluding `failure` with ZERO failing jobs is infrastructure, which is the mechanical signature of a gate short-circuiting on a missing prerequisite (bd-09bf73).
- An admission refusal on a pull request carrying a cancelled check now SAYS SO, and points at a rerun instead of a repair. Previously it read "fix it before admission rather than stacking work behind it", which invites exactly the wrong action when the failure is a consequence.

WHY THE THIRD ONE MATTERS EVEN THOUGH BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED: Cara cannot distinguish an aggregate-consequence failure from a real one, because the rollup reports only the aggregate's own conclusion. The skip itself is correct either way, since an absent result is not a passing result. What was wrong was the STATED REASON, which told a reader to repair code that was never built. A skip is generation-bound and self-clears on a green rerun, so a spurious skip costs one rerun; acting on a wrong reason costs an eviction and a re-stitch.

CORRECTING THE BEAD'S PREMISE, verified in source rather than argued: THE QUEUE DOES NOT EVICT ON RED. `grep` for eviction calls in sync.rs and loop_runner.rs returns nothing; eviction is operator-invoked only, and appears in sync solely as remediation text addressed to a human. So "a queue that evicts on red would have evicted three PRs and been wrong about two" describes a hypothetical queue, not this one. The correctness risk is real but it lands on a HUMAN acting on a misleading reason, which is precisely what the third change addresses.

STILL NOT CARA'S, and deliberately not taken: requirements 1, 3 and 4 of bd-c04d9b. Once cacophony's aggregate converts cancelled producers into a red code-like required status, the information Cara would need is destroyed before it arrives. Distinguishing producer outcomes has to happen where the aggregate is computed. Two of the operator's four mechanical tells are also outside Cara's reach for the same kind of reason: it reads neither check DURATIONS nor the job DAG, so "failed in seconds" and "downstream of a cancelled preparation" remain human judgements.

description:

Caco-merger verified and used the superseding Caravan build at canonical `aa8934e`, then resumed PR #1962 repair session `pr-1962-05fe82fe80c6`.

- Exact PR head remained `05fe82fe80c692613463a888bd4df5bc34d4ddee`; target main remained `90bebd5c`.
- Session/workspace materialized successfully from the canonical object cache and reached `state/phase=resolving`.
- Cara reported `already_exists=true`, `conflicting_paths=[]`, and no provider mutation.
- Read-only staged-tree proof against target showed the expected 15 PR files but excluded `README.md` and `SPEC.md`.
- The required bd-b85ed6 shell-safe message-body contracts remain absent from those net files; only unrelated `caco pr push --body-file` text exists in SPEC.

- Cara correctly permits edits only to reported `conflicting_paths`; because the set is empty, caco-merger did not edit/stage README/SPEC and did not invoke `repair continue`.

The mechanical merge is conflict-free but semantically incomplete. The first-party repair flow has no exact audited way to authorize restoration of known same-PR contract paths outside `conflicting_paths`.

## Required outcome

- Add an explicit repair semantic-path grant surface (CLI/JSON/MCP) that amends one existing session with a bounded allowlist of repo-relative paths plus rationale/source evidence.
- Bind each grant receipt to repository, PR number, exact expected remote head, target/base OID, session ID/manifest fingerprint, caller/authority, timestamp/expiry, exact path list, and reason. Re-read all identity before accepting or using it.
- Permit edits/staging only within `conflicting_paths ∪ granted_semantic_paths`; continue must reject any changed/staged/untracked path outside that union.
- Distinguish a semantic grant from declaring a conflict. Preserve mechanical conflict evidence and make the grant visible in status/continue/publication receipts.
- Support content provenance for restoration, such as a reviewed source commit/blob/patch digest. For this live case, bind README.md and SPEC.md to the previously routed c915e231/bd-b85ed6 contract rather than allowing arbitrary prose.
- Fail closed on head/target/session drift, symlinks/path traversal, generated/forbidden paths, expired grants, authority mismatch, or content/diff scope beyond the reviewed receipt.
- Keep non-force publication, exact provider remote verification, operation-lock bounds, object-cache isolation, and no raw Git fallback.
- Add fixtures for empty-conflict semantic omission with two granted paths, unauthorized third-path edit, changed source blob, head/target drift, grant expiry/revocation, and successful fresh-CI publication receipt.
- Prove the canonical packaged-binary grant/status/continue flow and publish a landed SHA/version before live PR #1962 restoration. Preserve the current resolving session until then.

title: Make caravan-force bypass pending required checks through an explicit force path
description:

title: DO NOT RESTART sync loop unaudited - force_merge true means a tick MAY MERGE under the explicit-actor hold - loop was never running - joining is automatic - choice-019fa6d6
description:
Short by design. bd-3f99dc is truncated at 8000 of 11004 bytes, so this content is unreadable there; filed separately per the split-before-the-boundary rule.

## Two findings that collapse the queue stall

### 1. JOINING WAS NEVER AN AGENT ACTION

From `.caravan/config.yaml` at main 923c05cf, established by helsinki-cacophony-caco-ctrl against their own earlier position:

    line  5   rebase_on_join: true
    line 14   sync.actions.join_unlabelled_prs: TRUE
    line 30   join_failed hook -> ./scripts/cara-hook

Cara joins unlabelled PRs BY ITSELF during sync. No `cara new`, no `cara join`, no membership verb, no hold to lift.

Hours of fleet reasoning about admission verbs and membership holds addressed a lane that does not gate joining. The canary never needed `caco agent complete` either.

### 2. THE OPERATOR SYNC LOOP WAS NEVER RUNNING

`pgrep -f "cara sync"` and `ps aux` checked at 00:41, 02:00 and 04:46 — three times across four hours, NEVER PRESENT.

The `while true; do cara sync --all; sleep 600; done` announced at 00:51 produced ZERO ticks, not twenty. A bare shell loop dies with its terminal.

## Version hypothesis tested and REFUTED

caco-ctrl hypothesised the loop resolved a cara below the 0.0.12 config floor, dying at 0s per tick like the three dark Linux nodes. Tested from the agent shell AND a stripped login shell approximating the operator PATH:

    command -v cara -> /Users/harryaskham/.cargo/bin/cara
    cara --version  -> cara 0.0.13   (parses this config)

PATH puts /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin, /bin first, none containing cara; `~/.cargo/bin` precedes `~/.nix-profile/bin`.

ms-mac is NOT a fourth dark node. The binary was always correct. The join_failed hook has nothing recorded because no tick ever attempted a join.

## THE ENTIRE REMEDY

Restart the sync loop under something that survives terminal close — launchd, tmux, nohup. Joins begin on the first tick.

No membership decision. No hold lifted. No admission verb. No queue defect.

## DURABLE REQUIREMENT for the cron design

A bare `while` loop is not a supervision strategy.

The cron needs PROCESS SUPERVISION and PER-PASS RECEIPTS, because four agents spent hours unable to distinguish "loop running and refusing to join" from "loop absent" — and the answer was the second. Every hypothesis tested (head-of-line, DIRTY head, max_candidates_per_tick, head_merge_actor, binary version, membership holds) was investigating a process that did not exist.

A single receipt line per tick naming the verb, the caravan count, and the unqueued count would have ended it immediately.

## CRITICAL AMENDMENT: restarting the loop is a MERGE-AUTHORIZATION decision, not process management

The remedy above — "restart the loop under supervision, joins begin, nothing else required" — is TRUE AND INCOMPLETE. Do not act on it as written.

`.caravan/config.yaml` line 4, verified directly on main 923c05cf:

    force_merge: true

So `cara sync --all` does not merely JOIN. **A tick may MERGE.**

Merging sits inside the explicit-actor hold active at revision 7, renewed seven times on unmet conditions. Restarting the loop would therefore start a process that can merge fleet-wide under a hold specifically forbidding unaudited merge actors — an accidental bypass rather than a deliberate authorization.

Found by helsinki-cacophony-caco-ctrl on a config re-read, after both they and the router had published the incomplete remedy.

### Raised as choice-019fa6d6, safe option first

1. LEAVE STOPPED until the operator wakes and restarts it themselves, having seen the force_merge implication
2. authorize ONE bounded tick by a named owner on a verified-0.0.13 node, accepting it may merge
3. authorize a tick AND narrow the explicit-actor hold so cara-driven merges are legitimate rather than accidental

caco-ctrl recommends 1; the router concurs. Nothing degrades overnight — all 15 candidates are CLEAN or repairable and lose nothing by waiting. Merging fleet-wide with PR2245's cancelled-producer fix still unlanded, after a night in which several confident instructions proved wrong, is precisely when not to widen a lane.

## METHOD LESSON, volunteered by caco-ctrl against themselves

They narrowed the membership lane, then observed `cara check` begin reporting eligible/canonical, and read that as the hold releasing.

**It was not.** Joining was never gated by the hold — `join_unlabelled_prs: true` means Cara joins unlabelled PRs by itself. The eligibility observed had nothing to do with their change.

A CHANGE FOLLOWED BY A CORRELATED OBSERVATION IS NOT A DEMONSTRATED MECHANISM. They did not test the alternative because the result matched what they expected.

That is the same failure named hours earlier — test the case in front of you, skip the complement — committed after naming it. The defence requires asking "what else would produce this observation?" even when, especially when, the change appears to have worked.

title: sync --all exceeds bounded client window and strands a dead operation lock
description:
## Helsinki Cacophony canary

Installed `cara 0.0.1` SHA-256 `2c4b26031301d6730c54029eb24abc2765550ebeb406e1794a13ee4fb7b3ee99` successfully created Caravan #2008 and enrolled its configured maximum eight members. A subsequent root-checkout command:


```json
{"pid":3406790,"operation":"sync_decision_checkout","token":"3406790-1784334101494090487-1","owner_alive":false,"age_secs":198,"stale_after_secs":1800,"stale":false}
```

- Bound `sync --all` provider inventory/decision work below documented command/client ceilings for a 30-PR repository and an eight-member caravan, or stream/return an accepted operation receipt before the ceiling.
- Release the operation lock through cancellation/termination-safe ownership cleanup when the owning process exits; a dead owner must not strand a fresh non-stale lock solely because the client timed out.
- Preserve fail-closed exact-token recovery for genuinely ambiguous/live ownership.
- Add canaries for SIGTERM/client disconnect during `sync_decision_checkout`, dead owner below the default stale age, live owner, PID reuse/token mismatch, and provider mutation indeterminacy.
- On cancellation after possible provider writes, persist enough operation phase/provider receipts that the next `status`/`sync` can prove replay/no-op safely.
- Keep bounded status JSON and stdout/stderr contracts from bd-f7c3bc.

Implementation/live canary checkpoint on rebased e98eff main: sync now owns one absolute budget `min(5*command_timeout,150s)`, shares it across initial/final status and provider runners (normal child cap remains 30s), and avoids a third full discovery by checking out the exact PR snapshot already embedded in a decision. A later acquisition automatically removes only a twice-read exact-token owner whose PID is affirmatively dead, at any age; live/PID-reused/changed-token cases remain fail-closed. Unit canary sends real SIGTERM to a child holding `sync_decision_checkout`, verifies fresh dead checkpoint survives, then exact recovery succeeds below 30m. title: Honor configured sync deadline; remove binary 285-second cap
description:
## Problem

Landed `bd-738a89` added binary constant `MAX_SYNC_EXECUTION_SECS=285` and computes:

```rust
sync_operation_budget(context).min(Duration::from_secs(MAX_SYNC_EXECUTION_SECS))
```

The justification is Helsinki's current five-minute Caco automation timeout. That is deployment policy embedded in every Caravan binary, and it silently overrides repository `.caravan/config.yaml` (`sync.max_duration_secs: 3600`). Status/capacity projections use the configured budget while the live process uses another hidden budget, so planning and execution disagree.

## Required

- Remove `MAX_SYNC_EXECUTION_SECS` and the deployment-specific `sync_execution_budget` clamp.
- One complete sync tick must use the typed, validated `sync.max_duration_secs` from repository config as its wall-clock deadline.
- Include discovery, root-first evaluation, parking, planning, mutation, reconciliation, event serialization, and hook delivery inside that same deadline.
- Hook child processes must inherit the remaining operation deadline; a configured hook timeout may lower but never extend the parent sync deadline.
- Status, plan, capacity, refusal and runtime receipts must report the same configured/effective deadline—no hidden binary ceiling.
- Keep the schema's documented global safety maximum if it has an architecture-level reason, but repository values below that maximum must be honored exactly.
- Deterministic tests: values 10/480/3600 are exact; hooks near deadline cannot overrun; root-first returns typed continuation; deployment wrapper fixture proves configured 480 finishes inside outer 540 and schedule 600.
- Remove/repair SPEC and README language claiming a universal 285-second live-process cap.

## Release fence

No `v0.0.88` tag/run exists. Release bead `bd-65efdb` must remain held until this fix lands on Caravan main and Cacophony's repository config sets `sync.max_duration_secs: 480`. Reuse v0.0.88 only after exact-head CI is green; do not publish the current provisional metadata commit first.

title: Cancellation must not auto-evict: make cancellation-to-eviction opt-in config, and let the ci_failure hook agent decide by default
description:
A cancelled CI job should never, by itself, evict a caravan member. Eviction on cancellation should be opt-in config; by default the `ci_failure` hook should fire and an agent should decide.

WHY

Cancellation is not a verdict. It means the job did not finish, most often because runner capacity was contended, a newer push superseded the run, or a producer job upstream was killed. The change under test was never evaluated.

Measured on cacophony, 2026-07-30, three cases hit while hand-landing PRs:

    PR #2292   preparation CANCELLED  ->  2 aggregate checks FAILURE in 4-7s   re-ran: CLEAN
    PR #2287   5 jobs CANCELLED       ->  Check & Lint + Fast Tests FAILURE    advised re-run, not evict
    PR #2284   gh pr checks: FAILURE  ->  API conclusion: CANCELLED, ZERO failing steps   re-ran: PASSED

TWO OF THREE WERE SPURIOUS. A queue evicting on red would have evicted three PRs and been wrong about two of them - including #2287, which was the only member of the first caravan ever formed on this repository. It would have dissolved that caravan and re-stitched a chain for nothing.

This is not rare. It is the common case whenever the runner pool is contended, which on this fleet is most of the time.

Related and important: cacophony's aggregate required checks CONVERT cancelled prerequisite jobs into terminal failures (bd-c04d9b, P0, labelled queue-wedge). So from the forge's own summary view, a cancellation is indistinguishable from a real failure. Any eviction policy reading "red" is therefore reading a value that conflates the two.

PROPOSED

1. DEFAULT: a cancelled required check does not evict. Fire the `ci_failure` hook with the classification available to the agent, and let it decide: re-run, fix in place, split, or evict.

2. OPT-IN CONFIG: a repository-level setting to treat cancellation as evictable, for cases where that is genuinely correct - for example a repo whose cancellations only ever mean superseded-by-newer-push, where eviction is cheap and correct.

3. The hook payload should carry enough to classify without another round-trip:
   - per-check `conclusion` from the provider, not a summarised view
   - whether any prerequisite/producer job was cancelled
   - job duration (a required check failing in seconds has not done its work)
   - whether the job recorded zero failing steps despite `conclusion: failure`

Those four are mechanical and need no judgement. An agent should only be spending judgement on the residue: a genuine failure that may or may not be related to the change.

4. Distinguish MEMBER from CANDIDATE in the policy. Refusing a candidate is cheap and changes no chain. Evicting a member re-links the chain around it. The bar for the second should be higher, and cancellation should never clear it.

CONTEXT: the operator's position is that cancellation-to-evict should be opt-in and otherwise the hook agent uses judgement. This bead records that decision and the evidence behind it. Triage guidance for the hook agent is in `.cacophony/profiles/caravan.md` in the cacophony repo.

title: Fail closed when a merged Caravan branch name is reused under a child
description:
Current PR identity and provider mutations are bound to PR number plus exact head/base OIDs, but graph edges are derived by matching an active child baseRefName to active PR headRefName. Race: Caravan parent A on branch B merges; child C still targets B; before sync retargets C, an unrelated new PR D reuses branch name B. GitHub moves B, C now resolves against D, and derive() can silently treat D as C parent because active heads_by_branch takes precedence over merged_by_head. Clean compatibility may not reveal the provenance change.

Fail closed on this historical/active branch-name collision rather than silently reparenting. At minimum, when a child base name is exposed by both a retained merged Caravan PR and a different active PR, report a typed branch-reuse/ambiguous-predecessor graph problem with old/new PR numbers and exact OIDs; do not arm/merge/retarget until operator resolves or the old child is safely advanced. Prefer a durable edge identity bound by join receipt/audit (predecessor PR + generation) if needed beyond conservative detection.

Acceptance:
- Parent merged + child still targeting old branch + new active PR reuses name: invalid graph, zero provider mutation.
- Reuse after every old child has been retargeted: allowed as independent PR.
- Multiple historical uses, active duplicate heads, deleted/fork heads, and provider head/base movement remain fail closed.

title: A discovery timeout blames the running phase for the whole budget
description:
`cara status` failed twice against cacophony with:

    github_discovery_timeout
    phase: repository_label_inventory
    command: gh label list --repo harryaskham/cacophony --limit 1000
    elapsed_ms: 68644 / 71244, deadline_ms: 59999

Read plainly, that says the label inventory took 68 seconds. It does not. Measured directly against the same repository: 20 labels, 819ms.

THE DEFECT: both call sites pass `started.elapsed()`, the total time since discovery began, while the error labels it with whichever phase happened to be RUNNING when the operation deadline expired. The phase that is running when a budget expires is not necessarily the phase that consumed it. A phase costing under a second is reported as having taken sixty-eight.

THE HARM IS MISDIRECTION, and it is measured rather than hypothetical. On the strength of that reading I told the operator the label call exceeded the whole per-command budget and advised raising `command_timeout_secs` in cacophony's config. That advice was aimed at the wrong command. The budget is being spent by earlier phases, PR discovery and compatibility analysis across roughly thirty open pull requests. An operator and two agents were sent after `gh label list`.

THE FIX: report `phase_elapsed_ms` and `elapsed_ms` as separate fields, and state both in the human message, so the cheap phase can never read as the expensive one. The discovery call site legitimately passes the same value twice, because discovery is the first phase and nothing ran before it to spend any budget; that is now stated at the call site rather than left implicit.

WHY THE EXISTING TEST DID NOT CATCH IT: it was named `status_deadline_error_reports_total_elapsed_and_phase` and asserted exactly the conflation, that `elapsed_ms` equals the number passed alongside a phase name. It encoded the bug as the specification. Renamed and replaced with one asserting the two numbers are distinct and both surfaced.

This is the same class as the `caravans` field misreading from earlier today: a surface that is internally consistent, never contradicts itself, and answers a different question from the one the reader is asking. It differs in one respect that makes it worse. The `caravans` field is CORRECT and merely invites a wrong question, whereas this attributes a real number to the wrong cause, so it does not merely permit a wrong conclusion, it supplies one.

title: Make dashboard workspace and docked evidence rails independently scrollable
description:
Operator reports Caravan web dashboard becomes unusable with four active caravans: the middle pane does not provide one coherent scroll area, caravan cards shrink below useful detail height, Saloon competes for its own constrained scroll, and Evidence opens as an obscuring overlay. Decisions & Blockers also accumulates historical dissolved-member notices with no clear dismissal affordance.

Implement one coherent desktop layout contract:

1. Repository overview/configured-repository row stays fixed at the top of the center column.
2. Everything below it (Active Topology, concat control, Saloon and all Saloon subrows) lives inside one nested vertically scrollable center workspace.
3. Caravan cards/rows keep a minimum natural height sufficient for their complete member trail; adding caravans must extend the outer workspace rather than shrink rows. Horizontal member trails may retain horizontal scrolling.
4. Remove competing internal vertical scrolling from caravan-list and Saloon groups; the center workspace owns vertical scrolling.
5. Evidence becomes a docked right rail, never a popover/overlay. The desktop grid supports independently open Evidence and Attention rails:
   - both closed: repositories | center
   - Evidence only: repositories | center | evidence
   - Attention only: repositories | center | attention
   - both: repositories | center | evidence | attention
   Evidence is immediately left of Attention.
6. Evidence and Attention each have independent vertical scrolling, close buttons, toolbar toggles and persisted local open/closed state. Center content reflows at every 0/1/2-rail state.
7. Responsive/mobile layout remains single-column and rails become ordinary stacked panels, not fixed overlays.
8. Decisions may be locally dismissed only when the problem is historical/non-blocking (`dissolved_member`). Live fleet blockers, candidate problems and repository errors cannot be dismissed. Dismissal is scoped by repository plus stable problem fingerprint and survives refresh via localStorage. A visible `Restore dismissed (N)` affordance re-enables historical entries.
9. Attention counts/overview metrics use visible decisions, not locally dismissed history; dismissal never alters provider labels, graph health, CLI status or engine policy.
10. Add source-contract tests for the new DOM/CSS/JS structure and dismissal safety.

This is UI-only. Do not add speculative merge/landing behavior. Existing opt-in auto-admission already grows caravans while CI is pending; parking already frees active capacity.

## Validation and browser acceptance

Implemented on current v0.0.82-based main and validated without provider or queue mutation.

Source/runtime validation:
- `node --check src/web_assets/app.js` — green
- embedded source-contract test — green
- `cargo test --lib web::tests` — 25 passed
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — green
- `just validate` on the rebased publishable tree — 841 library tests + 22 binary tests + integration/contract/doc checks all green

Real Chromium layout evidence from local read-only `cara web`:
- desktop viewport: 1440x900
- both rails open grid: repositories 220px | center 625px | Evidence 310px | Attention 285px
- Evidence is immediately left of Attention; both are visible, docked, independently scrollable, and non-overlapping
- configured repository overview remains fixed while `.dashboard-scroll` owns center `overflow-y: auto`
- synthetic four-caravan DOM render: center `clientHeight=705`, `scrollHeight=955`
- all four caravan rows measured exactly 220px high
- caravan-list and Saloon inner containers both measured `overflow-y: visible`
- mobile CSS stacks repository, Evidence, Attention, and content in one normal-flow column

Dismissal safety is pinned by the embedded source contract: only literal `dissolved_member` is allowlisted, repository-scoped stable fingerprints persist in localStorage, visible metrics use the filtered set, restore is explicit, and live repository errors/other problems have no dismissal control.

title: Joining behind a single-member caravan is untested
description:
Joining a second member is the property a merge queue exists for, and it has never once happened in cacophony. Forming the first caravan proves ADMISSION; stacking proves the harder half.

The existing coverage (`greedy_planner_forms_empty_fleet_then_uses_first_compatible_tail`) joins behind a TWO-member caravan. Cacophony's live fleet is a caravan with EXACTLY ONE member, #2287, where head and tail are the same pull request. That shape was untested, and it is precisely the next step production will take.

Adds `a_clean_candidate_joins_behind_a_single_member_caravan`, modelling the live shape directly: one labelled member, one clean unqueued candidate, asserting `evaluate_auto_candidate` returns `Join(2287)` rather than `New` (a rival caravan) or `Skip`.

It passes, which is the useful result: the stacking path is sound for the shape cacophony is actually in, so when a tick runs, 2292 should stack behind 2287 rather than forming a second caravan. That is a de-risking of the next production step rather than a bug fix.

Written because the same reasoning that caught every defect tonight applies here: the existing test proved stacking in a shape the operator does not have. Verifying the shape they DO have, before the tick runs, is cheaper than diagnosing it afterwards — and this one can be verified without merge authority, which the tick cannot.

title: Add just stress to shake out timing-dependent tests before release
description:
Add a `just stress` recipe that repeatedly runs the test suite in the pinned development shell, so timing-dependent failures surface before an immutable version number is burned.

Incident: v0.0.71 was tagged at 0f95799 after a green `just validate`, then its release workflow failed on remote_lease::tests::two_concurrent_hosts_never_both_acquire. The tag is immutable and had to be superseded by v0.0.72. `just validate` runs `cargo test --all` exactly once, so any race that fails intermittently can pass locally by luck and fail in CI.

This is the same shape as the v0.0.59 incident already recorded in the justfile: a gate that runs the wrong thing once looks green and publishes a broken release.

Add `stress rounds filter`, running `cargo test --lib` for the given filter repeatedly inside `nix develop`, printing the round number and failing fast on the first red round. Default to the whole lib suite so it catches order- and timing-dependent failures generally rather than only tests whose names happen to contain a keyword.

Be explicit in the recipe comment that this is a probabilistic shake-out, not a proof of absence: the racy lease fake that burned v0.0.71 failed roughly 6 of 12 runs, so a handful of rounds would have caught it, but a rarer race can still slip through. Record the incident so the reason the recipe exists is not lost.

title: Cara force heads are rejected by auto-merge invariant before force handling
description:
## Live failure

Cacophony PRs #2053 and #2056 were exact one-member caravans with `caravan-force`, clean compatibility to current main, source/Android checks green, and required checks blocked only by runner Public Fast Tests preparation. Both had native auto-merge disabled.

`cara sync` returned `invalid_graph` before any mutation:

`caravan head #2053 must have squash auto-merge enabled`

The call stack validates the complete fleet graph before CI observation and `force_merge_head`, so an externally force-labelled head cannot reach Cara's audited force branch unless auto-merge is already armed. #2053 also blocked a current-branch sync for #2056 because global graph validation failed on the first unrelated invalid caravan.

Attempting to satisfy the invariant externally with `gh pr merge --auto --squash` merged #2053 immediately because branch protection did not hold it, bypassing Cara's audit/permission/compatibility receipt. The operator then authorized an out-of-Cara admin path for exact green/runner-blocked PRs; #2056/#2057 landed only through that fallback.

## Required behavior

- A current exact `caravan-force` head with `force_merge: true` must reach force validation without requiring pre-existing native auto-merge.
- Cara must validate exact head/default compatibility, external force intent, ADMIN permission, CI evidence, competing landers, and one-shot audit comment before mutation.
- It must atomically force-squash or safely arm-and-force without exposing a window in which native auto-merge can land outside Cara.
- Syncing one selected caravan must not be blocked by an unrelated force-labelled caravan's repairable auto-merge invariant; either repair the selected graph deterministically or return a scoped decision.
- Preserve zero-write behavior on head/default/label/permission drift and at most one force attempt per tick.

## Acceptance

Fixtures cover force head with auto-merge off, unrelated invalid caravan plus selected valid force head, branch protection that would merge immediately on auto-arm, stale force labels, and idempotent post-merge replay. Live Cacophony force no longer requires raw `gh --admin` fallback.

title: Persist caravan-root squash auto-merge across scheduler rebase and head transitions
description:
Live Cacophony caravan2208 repeatedly loses required root squash auto-merge after scheduler/head transitions and becomes degraded until an operator re-arms it.

Evidence:

- caravan2208 members remain `[2208,2210,2213,2215]`, compatibility clean;
- root auto-merge was armed, then mistakenly disarmed; canonical Cara emitted `auto_merge_invariant: caravan head #2208 must have squash auto-merge enabled`;
- re-arming at 2026-07-26T21:21:45Z immediately restored healthy/problems=[];
- after subsequent scheduler rebase/head transition, root head moved to `79abc31d4efc07a579145cf904c83c1420f8b4ac`, base main at `b464e1ae5cb8033a0789997652d97d6b3efd5c7e`, `autoMergeRequest` became null again, and canonical state returned DEGRADED with the same invariant at ~22:03Z;
- caravan label/membership remained intact; no owner mutation explains away the required scheduler durability.

Required:

1. Treat root squash auto-merge as scheduler-owned convergent state. Every sync that creates, rebases, renews or advances a caravan root must idempotently ensure the exact current root head has SQUASH auto-merge armed.
2. Re-read provider state after head/base mutation and persist a provider receipt proving auto-merge on the resulting head, not the pre-rebase generation.
3. If arming fails or is externally disabled, report typed cause/provenance and retry only through bounded sync policy; never require operator babysitting as normal convergence.
4. Preserve distinction: native auto-merge on an unadmitted candidate makes it structurally ineligible, while native SQUASH auto-merge on the admitted caravan root is required.
5. Add tests for create, root rebase/head rewrite, CI transition, external disarm, idempotent replay, stale provider response, and no mutation of child members.
6. Validate against Cacophony caravan2208 without manually mutating its children.

No Cacophony provider action is authorized by this bead; source fix/release belongs in Caravan.

## Second re-arm receipt

Authenticated Cacophony choice `choice-019fa07d-03ef-7180-b0ee-98556a35f2d7` selected one exact re-arm. Pre-mutation reconciliation found the desired state already satisfied: PR2208 current head `79abc31d4efc07a579145cf904c83c1420f8b4ac` had SQUASH auto-merge enabled at 2026-07-26T22:13:58Z, caravan label/membership intact, and canonical Cara healthy/problems=[]. Therefore controller performed no duplicate provider mutation. Durability defect remains: root arming disappeared at least twice across transitions and required subsequent convergence.

## Provenance correction and duplicate consolidation

The re-arm observed at 2026-07-26T22:13:58Z was performed by `helsinki-cacophony-cluster-ctrl` under the `caco-ctrl` lease, not by Cara or the operator. Provider state did not expose who/why clearly enough for controllers to distinguish engine convergence from human repair. This strengthens the acceptance requirement for auditable engine arming provenance.

Cacophony bead bd-8db3a1 captured the same defect and is consolidated here because the source fix belongs in Caravan. Its useful additional framing is incorporated: distinguish required root arming from unrelated-candidate exclusion, and never normalize periodic operator re-arm as the solution.

## Third root arming loss

PR2208 lost required squash auto-merge a third time on the same caravan. Cluster control re-armed it under lease and canonical state immediately returned healthy. Two of the three observed losses occurred without agent/controller disarm action, confirming a real scheduler/provider durability defect rather than only the original mistaken manual disarm. Preserve exact arming provenance and transition receipts in the fix.

## Live caravan2208 validation (read-only; zero provider mutations)

Observed on ms-dev-5 between 2026-07-26T22:5xZ and 23:1xZ with the fix build. No Cacophony provider action was taken and no child was mutated.

**1. The defect recurred again and needed a further out-of-band re-arm.**
A direct GraphQL read showed PR2208 head `79abc31d4efc07a579145cf904c83c1420f8b4ac`, base `main`, `autoMergeRequest: null`, caravan label/membership intact -- the same DEGRADED shape as originally reported. By 23:11Z the same PR read back armed with `enabledAt: 2026-07-26T23:06:11Z`, `enabledBy: harryaskham`, `mergeMethod: SQUASH`. That is another out-of-band re-arm, not engine convergence: exactly the operator-babysitting loop this bead removes.

**2. Root cause proven from live no-write planning output.**
`cara plan sync --all` (no-write path; `provider_mutations: 0`, `branch_mutations: 0`) returned every physical plan for the caravan2208 chain as `already_satisfied: true` with `old_head_oid == new_head_oid`:

    #2208 already_satisfied=True  79abc31d4efc -> 79abc31d4efc
    #2210 already_satisfied=True  2e02a53116fc -> 2e02a53116fc
    #2213 already_satisfied=True  c9fe0b2baf3a -> c9fe0b2baf3a
    #2215 already_satisfied=True  90ce3e98bef2 -> 90ce3e98bef2
    #2223 already_satisfied=True  c17fd2b9e1d9 -> c17fd2b9e1d9
    #2225 already_satisfied=True  9f2586b04d54 -> 9f2586b04d54
    #2227 already_satisfied=True  94373464efe6 -> 94373464efe6

No branch is being rewritten at all, yet pre-fix `apply_physical_chains` disarmed native auto-merge on *every* selected member including root #2208 on *every* tick before applying nothing. Any later failure in that same tick (CI stop, budget error, provider error) then left the root disarmed with nothing to re-arm it. That is the durability window behind the repeated DEGRADED `auto_merge_invariant` and the repeated manual re-arms.

Two contributing defects were found alongside it:
- `reconcile_caravan` returned the CI decision *before* re-arming, so any failing member generation guaranteed the root stayed disarmed;
- required root arming was decided from the discovery list projection, which can still expose a pre-rewrite `autoMergeRequest`.

**3. The live generation is pinned as a hermetic regression fixture.**
`live_caravan2208_root_converges_without_touching_its_children` reproduces members `[2208,2210,2213,2215]`, root head `79abc31d...` on `main@b464e1ae...`, `autoMergeRequest` null; asserts the reported `auto_merge_invariant` problem appears; then proves the engine converges it with a sealed receipt on the exact resulting head, `root_head_rewritten` provenance, exactly one provider mutation, and byte-identical child snapshots. `live_caravan2208_replay_is_a_proven_no_op` proves the following tick writes nothing.

Out of scope, not actioned: the live plan stopped on the pre-existing `physical_sync_budget_insufficient` guard (`minimum_additional_ms: 1105823`), a Cacophony `sync.max_duration_secs` budget matter unrelated to this fix.

## Fix summary (Caravan)

- New `src/root_auto_merge.rs`: sealed `RootAutoMergeReceipt`, auditable `RootAutoMergeProvenance` (owner `caravan-scheduler`, component, operation id, derived trigger, observed-before state and provider actor, `engine_armed`), derived `RootAutoMergeTrigger` (`idempotent_replay`, `root_admitted`, `root_head_rewritten`, `root_base_advanced`, `externally_disarmed`, `non_squash_method`) and typed `RootAutoMergeFailureCause`.
- `SyncProgress::ensure_root_squash_auto_merge` re-reads the exact current root from a fresh single-PR provider read, refuses to prove anything against a generation the tick did not verify, arms and re-reads until squash auto-merge is proven on the *resulting* head, and seals a receipt. Bounded arming attempts and confirmation reads; on exhaustion it emits retryable `root_auto_merge_not_durable` with `operator_action_required=false`.
- Root arming now converges *before* a failing-CI stop.
- Physical rebase only disarms members whose branch generation is actually rewritten.
- Receipts surface in `SyncOutput.root_auto_merge`, in decision error details, in human output, and as a new `root_auto_merge_armed` event.
- Raced state/draft/base/`caravan`/`caravan-evicted` transitions still stop with an exact-field `stale_precondition`; unrelated label churn does not.
- Preserved distinction: native auto-merge on an unadmitted candidate remains structural ineligibility; only the admitted root requires SQUASH auto-merge.

- the branch was adopted through first-party `caco pr adopt`, merged current main, resolved one SPEC conflict, committed, and pushed non-force to the same PR;
- git status is clean.

This blocks `cara check/new/join/sync` formation from the actual PR checkout. Caco-merger must not attempt `cara sync` after a crashing status and remains on its existing audited native path for this PR.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce with a current PR branch whose local/published head contains a merge commit and whose branch name is a Cacophony immutable generation ref.
- Eliminate all panic/abort/unsafe crash paths: every current-PR resolution failure must return a structured JSON error/decision envelope and nonzero normal exit, never SIGSEGV.
- Add deterministic tests for: root checkout with no current PR; ordinary current PR branch; Cacophony generation branch; adopted PR worktree; merge-commit head; stale metadata source head versus newer published head.
- Preserve stdout/stderr separation and large JSON handling from bd-f7c3bc.
- Prove `cara --json status`, `cara --json check`, and the preflight for `cara new/join/sync` are safe from the adopted PR #2008 worktree shape.
- Return an installed-path Helsinki canary request with exact fixed Caravan SHA/version/receipt.

## Regression after operator updater — root status and sync also crash

The operator updater replaced the previously passing installed binary with another `cara 0.0.1` binary:

- current installed SHA-256: `0e88ba61fcb6df4aaf95b609d714d8caae9942be4a0cfcccabb4912e4e59f813`;
- daemon Caravan checkout still reports `e451ed9c02860f9dea408cd68890fdde56c8846a`;
- all three required GitHub labels are present with correct metadata.

From the managed **Cacophony root checkout** (not the adopted worktree), both operator-requested commands now deterministically SIGSEGV:

```text
~/.cargo/bin/cara --json status
exit=139 stdout_bytes=0 stderr_bytes=0

~/.cargo/bin/cara --json sync --all
exit=139 stdout_bytes=0 stderr_bytes=0
```

This broadens the blocker: the crash is no longer limited to current-PR/adopted-worktree resolution. `sync --all` can crash before producing any receipt or decision envelope even with repository labels initialized. No PR mutation was observed; caco-merger stopped immediately.

Acceptance must now include root-checkout installed-binary status and sync-all canaries in addition to adopted-PR coverage, and identify why the operator-installed build hash regressed while the earlier exact-e451 build (`57674e...`) passed root status.

Diagnosis complete; no Caravan status/domain patch. Canonical Helsinki job tj-cc939cc0 proves installed SHA 2c4b2603 (fresh ambient cargo build, glibc 2.42 coherent) returns healthy 30-PR status when `NIX_LD` and `NIX_LD_LIBRARY_PATH` are unset, and SIGSEGVs with inherited managed runtime variables. Preserved core PID 3112435 NT_FILE proves loader/libc mismatch: glibc 2.40 loader plus glibc 2.42 libc; crash is dlsym inside std::Thread::new before a structured status result is possible. Independent matrix: installed/fresh ambient SHA 2c4b passes root and adopted PR #2008; devshell SHA 57daaa and Nix package SHA be2931 use glibc 2.40 and pass clean but deterministically exit139 on both shapes under foreign 2.42 library injection. Cacophony P1 bd-d7d543 owns invocation sanitization and deployment bd-0b9bec depends on it. Accidental duplicate bd-b93947 was marked duplicate. This bead should close redirected; the acceptance demand for a Caravan panic fix is inapplicable because failure occurs in the dynamic loader/runtime environment.

## Current-checkout fallback also SIGSEGVs

Direct operator recovery instructed caco-merger to use `nix run ~/.cacophony/daemon/checkouts/caravan -- <args>` while the installed binary is stale. On Caravan source checkout exact clean head `10db52bcc3415d480a42a7729ecb29691f8fa01b` (`cara 0.0.1`), from the clean first-party PR2012 worktree:

```text
nix run /home/harry/.cacophony/daemon/checkouts/caravan -- check --json
exit=139
stdout_bytes=0
stderr_bytes=0
```

The same current checkout returns `cara 0.0.1` for `--version`, so Nix evaluation/build succeeds and the crash occurs in Cara's PR/current-worktree check path. A prior global-form invocation (`-- --json check`) also produced no usable output. No provider mutation followed: caco-merger failed closed and used its audited exact-head manual path only for the independent green P0 PR2012, outside the active PR2008 hold.

Acceptance should canary both argument orders through installed and `nix run <checkout>` paths and require a structured success/error envelope rather than zero-output exit or SIGSEGV.

### Root-cause clarification

This fallback observation does **not** overturn the closed loader-environment diagnosis above. The managed merger runtime inherited the same foreign `NIX_LD` / `NIX_LD_LIBRARY_PATH` class; wrapping Cara in `nix run` does not sanitize those variables before the produced binary starts. Treat the zero-output SIGSEGV as additional invocation-sanitization evidence for Cacophony `bd-d7d543`, not as a new Caravan domain/status defect. A valid fallback canary must explicitly unset the foreign loader variables before invocation.

That leaves the specification stale against shipped, security-relevant behavior: an operator reading SPEC would not learn that hosted mode exists, that it refuses interactive mutations, or what read_only and remote_fenced mean. title: The dry-run reports its no-writes guarantee as a literal, not a measurement
description:
`cara sync --dry-run` and `cara plan sync` print `NO PROVIDER WRITES` and report `mutated: false`, `provider_writes: 0`. Those two fields are the entire safety claim of a dry-run: an operator authorising a real tick reads them and acts.

Both were HARDCODED LITERALS in the constructed `SyncPlanOutput`, not measurements.

WHY THAT IS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A STYLE POINT. `plan_sync` does not run against a stub. It builds a real `GitHubMutationAdapter` and calls `prepare_physical_chains`, which is THE SAME code path the mutating tick uses. The plan is safe today because that path performs only reads and a `--dry-run` lease preflight. If any shared helper on that path ever performs a write, the plan would perform it AND CONTINUE REPORTING ZERO, because the number was never derived from anything.

That is the exact shape of several defects fixed here today: a field that is correct, never contradicts itself, and is constructed rather than observed. It cannot fail a test, it cannot look wrong in the output, and it silently stops being true the moment someone changes code elsewhere.

THE FIX: derive both from `completed_mutation_count(&progress)`, the same counter the mutating path uses to enforce its own per-tick mutation budget. `provider_writes` is now the measured count and `mutated` is `provider_writes > 0`.

Verified against the live fleet: the measured value agrees with the previous literal, `provider_writes: 0`, so the guarantee held. The point is that it is now CHECKED rather than promised, and a future violation becomes visible in the output and in tests rather than invisible everywhere.

FOUND BY REVIEWING ANOTHER AGENT'S CHANGE. `--dry-run` landed on sync while I was writing a worse fix for the same discoverability problem, and I dropped mine. Reading their implementation to satisfy myself it was safe is what surfaced this: the routing is genuinely correct, exactly one planner and an early return before any mutation path, and the weakness is in what the planner REPORTS rather than what it does.

title: A historical problem aborts every tick while status reports healthy
description:
bd-61024a classified `DissolvedMember` as historical so it reports without gating: `healthy()` stopped counting it and `cara status` correctly returned `healthy: true` with three dissolutions listed.

Sync did not get the message. `cara plan sync --all` aborted:

    cara invalid_graph: caravan member #2200 was closed without merging, so its caravan no longer exists

So `status` reported a healthy fleet while EVERY TICK FAILED. That is worse than either consistent outcome: an operator reads healthy, authorises a tick, and the tick aborts on a pull request closed days ago that nothing can now change. I introduced this myself, in the change that was supposed to prevent a wedge, and it wedges the mutating path instead of the reporting one.

THE MECHANISM. Both sync gates skipped problems using `is_candidate_scoped()`. That predicate names ONE non-blocking category. When bd-61024a added a SECOND non-blocking category, historical, the gates kept asking the old question, so a historical problem fell through into `decision_for_problem` and became `InvalidGraph`.

Fixed by asking the question the gates actually mean: `!problem.kind.blocks_fleet()`. A tick must stop for exactly the problems that gate the fleet and no others, which stays correct if a third non-blocking category is ever added.

WHY THE COMPILER DID NOT CATCH IT, which is the part worth keeping. bd-604e38 made `blocks_fleet()` an exhaustive match precisely so a new variant cannot be added without deciding what it means, and that worked: adding `DissolvedMember` forced a decision there. It did nothing here, because these call sites call a PREDICATE rather than matching. An exhaustive match protects the classification, not its consumers. I had already written that lesson down after bd-604e38 failed to close the class, and this is the same failure with the same shape: a rule applied at one site and not its siblings, ninth instance, mine.

Verified in situ rather than by test alone: `cara plan sync --all` against the live fleet now returns a plan with NO PROVIDER WRITES instead of aborting, and `cara status` still reports the three dissolutions with `healthy: true`.

title: Detect required contexts with zero reporting runs on a rebased head
description:
Live evidence on caravan root 2208: Cara rebase head 79abc31d had ZERO workflow runs while the branch requires Check and Lint plus Fast Tests (unit), so the PR sat MERGEABLE/BLOCKED indefinitely with 0 failed and 0 pending while canonical status reported healthy with problems=0. The other three rebased members each got a run, so the missed trigger is intermittent and provider-side.

Confirmed source cause: sync::classify_checks treats an empty check set as pending. `let pending = checks.is_empty() || ...` returns CiDisposition::Waiting, so "no run was ever created for a required context" is indistinguishable from "runs are queued". Sync then waits forever and status shows no problem.

Required behaviour: after a bounded grace period measured from the exact rebased head publication, verify that every REQUIRED status context has a reporting run bound to that exact head OID. If a required context has zero reporting runs, emit typed caravan_member_missing_required_runs carrying PR number, exact head OID, and the precise missing contexts, and keep it clearly distinct from pending and from failing. Optionally retrigger the same-head workflow through a reviewed first-party path; never fabricate a check result. The empty-checks-equals-waiting shortcut must no longer silently mask a never-triggered required context.

Constraint learned from the live workaround: closing and reopening the PR did retrigger CI on the same head and proved recovery, but it also disarmed root auto-merge. Root auto-merge is REQUIRED by Cara, so any recovery path must preserve or re-arm it. Arming provenance and disarm reporting are tracked separately in bd-93e366; keep these deduped.

title: Sync strips a human-applied join-skip label because it has no receipt
description:
`caravan-join-skipped` is Cara's own generation-bound automatic admission skip, backed by an `AutoJoinSkipReceipt` comment. Auto-admission validates the receipt against the current generation and, when it no longer matches, posts an invalidation comment and REMOVES the label so the candidate can retry.

The stale branch is entered when the receipt does not match OR WHEN THERE IS NO RECEIPT AT ALL:

    if retained.as_ref().is_some_and(|receipt| skip_receipt_matches(..)) { continue; }
    // ... otherwise: post invalidation, remove_label(AUTO_ADMISSION_SKIP_LABEL)

`retained` is `None` when nobody has posted a receipt, which is exactly the state of a label applied BY A HUMAN. So an operator applying `caravan-join-skipped` to hold a pull request has it stripped by the next sync tick. Not on the next push, not when the generation changes: on the next tick, because there is no receipt to validate and "no receipt" takes the same branch as "stale receipt".

HOW THIS SURFACED, and it is the reason it is filed as a defect rather than a curiosity. An operator is holding cacophony PR2276 for review because it is +2606/-16 and touches SPEC.md. It is not draft and carries no labels, so nothing mechanically holds it while `force_merge: true` is set. I advised applying `caravan-join-skipped`. That advice was WRONG and would have produced a hold that silently evaporated, which is worse than no hold at all, because the operator would believe the pull request was protected.

THE FIX: only remove a label Cara itself applied. A stale receipt authorises removal; an ABSENT receipt does not, because it means the label came from somewhere else. Cara should leave a foreign hold alone and say so, rather than stripping a marker it never wrote.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE: the existing behaviour is correct for the case it was designed for, and the receipt is exactly the evidence that distinguishes the two cases. It is already fetched. Nothing new needs to be measured; the code simply has to stop treating "no evidence I did this" as "evidence I may undo it".

This is the same class as the rest of today's findings: two different things sharing one representation, where the code silently picks the wrong one because nothing forces it to distinguish them.

title: Cara owns squash-merge and base retargeting so auto-merge is not needed
description:
Operator directive 2026-07-27: an accidental merge into the next caravan member instead of main was observed. Auto-merge will be disabled on the cacophony repo, and Cara must own the full landing lifecycle so behaviour is not a mix of Cara and provider auto-merge.

## Problem

Today landing is split between two actors. Cara selects and validates admission, while GitHub auto-merge performs the actual merge. Because each chain member is based on its predecessor rather than main, provider auto-merge can fire against a stale base and land a member into the next caravan member instead of into main. That is the accidental merge the operator saw. Two actors mutating the same refs also makes ordering and blame hard to reason about.

## Required behaviour

1. Cara performs the squash-merge itself, on each tick, for the valid and compatible HEAD, rather than delegating to provider auto-merge.
2. Cara retargets the base of the next chain member to `main` once its predecessor lands, so no member is ever merged into a sibling.
3. Compatibility is revalidated against current `main` immediately before mutation; abort on drift rather than merging a stale evaluation.
4. Exactly one merge actor. With auto-merge disabled, Cara must not re-arm it, and must fail closed rather than falling back to a provider merge path.
5. Preserve existing FIFO admission ordering, priority labels, and the rule that rejection never causes automatic leapfrogging.
6. Preserve pause and suspension semantics: an active pause record must still stop landing.
7. Emit exact receipts per landing: PR number, head SHA, base SHA, resulting main SHA, and the retarget applied to the successor.

## Explicitly accepted trade-off

The operator accepts that one-merge-per-tick is slower than parallel auto-merge. Safety and reasoning clarity are the priority.

## Acceptance

- With repository auto-merge disabled, a multi-member chain drains fully through Cara alone.
- No member ever lands into another member; every landing target is `main`.
- A stale-base member is retargeted and revalidated before landing, or refused.
- Suspension and pause records still block landing.
- Receipts are sufficient to reconstruct the exact landing order after the fact.

## Context

Current canonical Cacophony queue state is degraded with auto-merge suspended under pause record actor `ms-mac-cacophony-caco-dev-msm-0`, caravan_head 2053, reason "External runner pin failures bd-536622/bd-617fb3". Related recent evidence includes the Caravan root #2210 arming decision and the physical-sync budget refusals tracked under bd-bbc981. This bead is the architectural fix that removes the dual-actor hazard rather than re-arming auto-merge.

---

## Merged duplicate: bd-e1c6ce

Title: [P0] Make Caravan the sole squash-merge actor with retarget-before-merge ordering

Direct operator architecture decision: disable native GitHub auto-merge for Cacophony. Caravan becomes the sole leased merge actor. On each tick it must retarget the current caravan head to main when its predecessor merged, revalidate against the new base, squash-merge exact head into main, then promote the next member. Remove the existing `auto_merge_invariant` in the same release; otherwise repo-level auto-merge disable makes every caravan permanently degraded.

Strict operation order:
1. If caravan head base != main and predecessor is merged, retarget head base to main.
2. Wait for/recompute exact merge-base, compatibility, required contexts and zero-run diagnostics against the NEW base/head.
3. Only when exact head is valid/compatible/green, squash-merge it to main under Caravan lease.
4. Emit provider receipt and verify main contains the resulting tree before promoting next member.
5. Promote next member and repeat on a later tick; no native auto-merge actor.

Never merge before retarget/revalidation. Live failure receipt: PR2213 was CLEAN but still based on predecessor generation branch. Native auto-merge landed commit `3da6addbf0b1` into `agent/ms-dev-3/cacophony/8x5t4zp7luvs0a4q-pr-gf9e8151b76a9dae6b883c59a249700a7ca933540`, not main; compare against main is DIVERGED, behind_by=3, so content never reached main. Caravan then re-rooted to2215 with the same dangling-base condition. Fix must safely handle the whole remaining chain, not one head.

Safety/acceptance:
- single leased mutation actor; exact repository/head/base/required-check re-read and abort-on-drift;
- idempotent squash receipt, provider request IDs, main tree containment postflight;
- retry/indeterminate classification with no duplicate merge;
- atomic promotion plan integrated with bd-9ead1b realistic sync budgeting;
- tests for stale predecessor branch, wrong-target refusal, required checks becoming stale after retarget, concurrent main movement, provider timeout after merge, and multi-member drain;
- migration of existing caravans with no native auto-merge and no content loss;
- SPEC/config/status update: no `auto_merge_invariant`; report Caravan merge authority and next exact action.

Coordinate Cacophony removal of native arming/rearming and runner provisioning. Do not mutate Cacophony PRs in tests.

## Operator refinement 2026-07-27 08:39 BST — exact mechanism and interim policy

The operator specified the concrete design rather than leaving it open:

### New typed option: `auto_merge_head`

Caravan gains an explicit `auto_merge_head` option controlling whether Cara itself merges the caravan head. It will be **disabled in cacophony**, so Cara performs the sync on head rather than delegating to provider auto-merge. This makes the behaviour a typed configuration decision per project rather than an implicit split between two actors.

### Required sequencing

1. Cara syncs/merges the caravan **head** when it is valid and compatible.
2. When PR2 subsequently reaches head, its target is retargeted to `main`.
3. Provided nobody else has pushed to `main` in the interim, that retarget is a **content-identical rebase** — no semantic change, no re-review needed.
4. The no-other-push condition must be checked, not assumed. If `main` moved, the member is revalidated (or refused) rather than silently rebased onto different content.

### Interim operator policy, until this lands

The operator will **manually merge** items that reach caravan head, to work around auto-merge being disabled. Agents must therefore expect operator-performed merges at head during this window and must not:

- interpret an operator merge at head as a queue fault, race, or drift to repair;
- re-arm provider auto-merge to "unblock" the chain;
- open replacement PRs or re-land already-merged content because a landing was performed manually.

Verify against real `main` before concluding anything is unlanded; a stale local mirror has already produced one false not-landed report this cycle.

### Operator intent

Stated explicitly: "Lets get this right once and for all." This is a durable architectural fix, not a workaround, and the interim manual merges are scaffolding to be removed once `auto_merge_head` exists and Cara owns head sync.

## Field refinement: prefer tree equality over "main did not move" (from ms-dev-3 ex9vj4iedmpf8g3y, 2026-07-27)

The retarget safety check should compare **trees**, not merely assert that `main` has not moved.

Rationale, with live evidence from that agent: Cara `rebase_on_join` already produces content-identical rebases whose old and new commits share a tree — observed going `20b4a8d887` -> `ccc3af5c2d` with tree `3efd0de751` on both. A tree-equality check therefore:

- **accepts** the common safe case where `main` moved but touched disjoint paths, which a naive "main did not move" check would reject;
- **still refuses** a genuinely different rebase where content actually changed.

This widens the safe path without weakening the guard, and reduces spurious refusals during normal concurrent activity on main. Recommend implementing the no-other-push condition as: retarget is permitted when the resulting tree is identical to the validated tree; otherwise revalidate or refuse.

Corroborating context from the same report: PR #2239 was verified against the real GitHub API rather than the local mirror — real main `12eee6c279` does not contain the change, PR is OPEN/CLEAN with all six required contexts green on head `616dcfcbf9`. That agent is holding it untouched and unarmed per the interim policy.

## Postcondition requirement: assert REACHABILITY, not merge-state (from ms-dev-3 33t2dm7w5ou3zetd, 2026-07-27)

This is the check that would have caught the incident at the moment it happened rather than hours later.

`#2213` reported `MERGED` while its merge commit was **unreachable from `main`**, and nothing surfaced that. Provider merge-state is therefore insufficient as a landing postcondition.

Required after any head merge:

```
git merge-base --is-ancestor <merge_commit_oid> origin/main
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/<merge_commit_oid>...main --jq .status   # expect "ahead" or "identical"
```

Cacophony already holds itself to this pattern in the `bd-98b2fc` merged-generation preflight, so this is consistency with an existing product contract rather than a new invention.

Live evidence from the provider API, independently reproduced against `ssh://git@github.com/harryaskham/cacophony.git` with local `origin/main` = `12eee6c279` byte-identical to `gh api .../commits/main`:

```
#2213 merge 3da6addbf0 ...main -> diverged  ahead_by=4  behind_by=3
#2213 head  c9fe0b2baf ...main -> diverged  ahead_by=4  behind_by=3
#2210 merge 176fd149d3 ...main -> ahead     ahead_by=1  behind_by=0   (control)
```

A true ancestor of `main` compares as `ahead, behind_by=0`, as the `#2210` control shows. `#2213` returns `diverged`, so its work is genuinely not on `main` by the providers own reckoning. Note this is explicitly **not** a claim of lost work: `#2213` head is an ancestor of `#2215` head, so the chain still carries the content and the ordinary drain lands it. No hand-recovery, cherry-pick, or re-land should be attempted.

## Sizing correction: revalidate-or-refuse is the HOT path, not an edge case

Measured on `origin/main` by the same agent: **30 commits in 24h, 10 in 12h, 4 in 6h** — roughly one push every 45 minutes, during a period when the queue was largely stalled. 4 of the 30 were releases independent of the caravan.

So "main moved in between" will be the common branch, not the exception. The revalidate-or-refuse path must be engineered as the hot path: efficient, well-tested, and not a rarely-exercised fallback. This also strengthens the case for the tree-equality check above, since strict "main did not move" would refuse constantly at this commit rate.

## Canonical tracking correction

This bead is CLOSED as duplicate. Canonical live implementation is `caravan:bd-f8cf99`, owner `caravan:oqzipq640ex5hh6t` on ms-dev-6. All unique operator acceptance and `auto_merge_head` refinement were copied there. Do not claim, reopen, implement, or route work against this record.

## Implementation aid: Cara already emits the tree oid needed for the check (from ms-dev-5 r0clfm7p8z1dgv50, 2026-07-27)

Caras existing check output already carries the material required to implement the no-other-push condition — no new computation is needed.

For that agents candidate, the check returned a synthetic **merge tree oid** `883fa5bd8e9518ec610c9d7c06c4d114859ceec3`, identical to the compatibility rows `merge-tree result`. Comparing that tree oid before and after a retarget is:

- a **deterministic content-identity test**, and
- an **automatic detector of an intervening push to main**, because a moved `main` simply produces a different merge tree.

This converges with the tree-equality proposal already recorded above, and means the implementation can reuse existing compatibility-analysis output rather than adding a separate main-movement probe. One comparison satisfies both requirements.

Independent provider-truth verification from the same agent, using `gh pr view` / `gh api` against `harryaskham/cacophony` directly rather than any local mirror: main tip `12eee6c279974d2695a9273d77beefd7e1d2fc44`; PR #2223 OPEN at head `c17fd2b9e1d97790a2827721d7c2490d0df23745`; compare main -> that head reports `diverged`, so main genuinely does not contain #2223. This independently corroborates the same main sha reported by ms-dev-3, from a different agent and node.

Also recorded for chain state: PR #2224 head `1b81d50f9607e34a3c221ff35f92bd5e45f1e578` is based directly on main, never auto-merge armed, join-skipped label and dead letter intact, local tree clean, parked under the caco-ctrl hold.

## CORRECTION to the reachability postcondition: content-existence is the sound test under squash merge (from ms-dev-5 ln8ys7uvrmriol3i, 2026-07-27)

This partially corrects the reachability postcondition recorded above, and the correction is right.

**In a squash-merge repository, testing whether a PRs merge commit is an ancestor of `main` is an unreliable landed-test.** Squash merging never places the PRs own merge commit on `main`, so a `diverged` result can be a false negative. The `compare/main...<merge_commit_oid>` probe must not be trusted on its own by anyone.

**The sound test is content existence at the ref:**

```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/<path-the-PR-adds>?ref=main
```

A 404 means the content is genuinely absent from `main`. This cannot be fooled by squash, rebase, retarget, or mirror staleness, and it is a content-level fact independent of commit topology.

**Router independently verified this**, directly against github.com rather than accepting the report:

```
gh api repos/harryaskham/cacophony/contents/docs/design/pr-cara-join-live-canary-generation4.md?ref=main
  -> HTTP 404 Not Found
gh api repos/harryaskham/cacophony/commits/main --jq .sha
  -> 12eee6c279974d2695a9273d77beefd7e1d2fc44
```

So PR2213s sole added file is confirmed absent from `main` at that exact sha. Three agents on two nodes independently report the same main sha.

### Reconciling the two postconditions

They are complementary, not contradictory, once the subject of the check is stated precisely:

1. **Landed test (strongest, use this to conclude landed/unlanded):** does the PRs content exist at `?ref=main`. Immune to squash/rebase/retarget/mirror.
2. **Merge-target postcondition (use this immediately after a merge operation):** assert that the commit the merge operation actually produced is reachable from the branch it was supposed to land on. This is what catches the original incident, where the merge landed onto the predecessor branch instead of `main` while reporting `MERGED`.

Check 2 must be applied to the resulting `main` sha returned by the merge, not to a PR merge-commit oid interpreted as an ancestor of `main`. Implement both; do not implement only the ancestry form.

Disposition note: PR2213s owner is `h8e3rwcgdxmggus0` on ms-dev-3. No re-land, replacement, or claim is proposed by any reporting agent; the point is only that a verified content-level absence must not be written off as mirror staleness, since that owners bead may read done while the file is absent from main.

## CORRECTION to the reachability postcondition: content-existence is the sound landed-test under squash merge (from ms-dev-5 ln8ys7uvrmriol3i, 2026-07-27)

This partially corrects the reachability postcondition recorded above, and the correction is right.

**In a squash-merge repository, testing whether a PR merge commit is an ancestor of `main` is an unreliable landed-test.** Squash merging never places the PR own merge commit on `main`, so a `diverged` result can be a false negative. The `compare/main...<merge_commit_oid>` probe must not be trusted on its own.

**The sound test is content existence at the ref:**

```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/<path-the-PR-adds>?ref=main
```

A 404 means the content is genuinely absent from `main`. This cannot be fooled by squash, rebase, retarget, or mirror staleness, and it is a content-level fact independent of commit topology.

**Router independently verified this directly against github.com** rather than accepting the report:

```
gh api repos/harryaskham/cacophony/contents/docs/design/pr-cara-join-live-canary-generation4.md?ref=main
  -> HTTP 404 Not Found
gh api repos/harryaskham/cacophony/commits/main --jq .sha
  -> 12eee6c279974d2695a9273d77beefd7e1d2fc44
```

PR2213 sole added file is confirmed absent from `main` at that exact sha. Three agents across two nodes independently report the same main sha, each using provider-truth methods.

### Reconciling the two postconditions

They are complementary once the subject of each check is stated precisely:

1. **Landed test (use to conclude landed/unlanded):** does the PR content exist at `?ref=main`. Immune to squash, rebase, retarget, and mirror staleness.
2. **Merge-target postcondition (use immediately after a merge operation):** assert that the commit the merge operation actually produced is reachable from the branch it was supposed to land on. This is what catches the original incident, where the merge reported `MERGED` while landing onto the predecessor branch instead of `main`.

Check 2 must be applied to the resulting `main` sha returned by the merge, not to a PR merge-commit oid interpreted as an ancestor of `main`. Implement both; the ancestry form alone is insufficient.
