## Two combined corrections from field agents (2026-07-27)

Recorded together because neither is complete without the other. Router previously attempted to append the first of these; the write returned ok=true twice without persisting, so this is a single consolidated append.

### A. Landed-test correction: content existence, not merge-commit ancestry (ms-dev-5 ln8ys7uvrmriol3i)

In a SQUASH-merge repository, testing whether a PR merge commit is an ancestor of main is an unreliable landed-test. Squash never places that commit on main, so `diverged` can be a false negative. Do not trust `compare/main...<merge_commit_oid>` alone.

Sound test is content existence at the ref:

```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/<path-the-PR-adds>?ref=main
```

404 means genuinely absent from main. Immune to squash, rebase, retarget, and mirror staleness.

Router verified independently against github.com: `docs/design/pr-cara-join-live-canary-generation4.md?ref=main` returned HTTP 404 while `commits/main` returned `12eee6c279974d2695a9273d77beefd7e1d2fc44`. Three agents on two nodes independently reported that same main sha using provider-truth methods.

Reconciliation with the reachability postcondition recorded earlier: they are complementary once the subject is precise.
1. Landed test: does PR content exist at `?ref=main`. Use this to conclude landed/unlanded.
2. Merge-target postcondition: assert the commit the merge OPERATION produced is reachable from the branch it was meant to land on. Apply to the resulting main sha, not to a PR merge-commit oid treated as an ancestor of main. This is what catches the original incident where a merge reported MERGED while landing onto the predecessor branch.

Implement both. The ancestry form alone is insufficient.

### B. Carry-forward must be ASYMMETRIC: carry PASSES only, never FAILURES

This completes the tree-oid proposal recorded above. Tree-oid identity proves content identity, so prior validation genuinely applies — but only for passes.

Rule: on merge-tree-oid match across a retarget, carry forward SUCCESSFUL required checks; DROP failures and re-run them.

Rationale, and it is logical rather than a special case: a PASS asserts a property of the CONTENT, so it transfers with identical content. A FAILURE may assert a property of the ENVIRONMENT — a closed sibling generation, a provider metadata timeout, a cancelled run — none of which are properties of the tree.

Worked example from PR2227, whose three red checks are all bogus and none examined source:

```
Changed surface admission  fail 24s  <- verdict belongs to CLOSED PR2229 sharing the head SHA (bd-b47dec)
Check & Lint               fail  6s  <- downstream of admission, compiled nothing
Fast Tests (unit)          fail  5s  <- downstream of admission, ran zero tests
```

That content genuinely has not changed, so the tree oid would match perfectly. A SYMMETRIC carry-forward rule would therefore treat a tree-identical rebase as licence to reuse those verdicts and make the false red PERMANENT. Today the only escape is that a rebase mints a new SHA and yields fresh check runs; symmetric carry-forward would remove that escape and strand correct candidates forever.

A second observed failure mode was `provider_metadata_unavailable`, a transient GitHub API failure that died in materialization before any validation ran (bd-51c6cf) — again a property of the environment, not the tree.

Cost asymmetry favours this: worst case is re-running a genuinely failing check, which is cheap relative to permanently stranding a correct candidate.

### Optional defence in depth: duration sanity check

A required check that failed in under about 10 seconds validated nothing. Observed calibration: genuine lint failure on 2210 took 3m37s; a real admission pass takes about 50s; the bogus failures above took 24s, 6s, and 5s. A sub-threshold failure is a strong signal of an environment/admission artefact rather than a content verdict.

## LIVELOCK NOW OBSERVED, NOT PREDICTED — carry-forward is load-bearing (ms-dev-5 ln8ys7uvrmriol3i, 2026-07-27, router-verified)

Router independently verified both findings against github.com.

### 1. Main advances faster than a pipeline can complete

Actual commit timestamps on main:

```
09:05:42 39998c2396
09:11:13 e473cb91ba
09:11:34 13077396ab
09:11:45 4a0da91bd0
09:12:01 8abaf9221a
09:12:20 7524b3b9e9
09:21:45 bebbac7322
```

Six advances inside about sixteen minutes, five of them within sixty-seven seconds. (Not asserted to be six discrete pushes rather than batched commits; the CI effect is identical either way.)

Measured requirement for a full pipeline is thirty-five to forty minutes of stable head. At this cadence the head member can NEVER finish validating: each advance mints a new SHA, starts a new run, abandons the previous one. The queue therefore cannot drain, so main only moves by manual merges, which advance main and re-trigger the rebase. That is a closed livelock loop and it is now observable rather than theoretical.

PR2215 confirms it: head moved 90ce3e98bef2 -> 255db7da1c95 via retarget-rebase, invalidating everything previously reported about its runs. Current state head 255db7da1c95, mergeable MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED.

### 2. The duplicate-run pattern is systematic, not an occasional race

On the brand-new head 255db7da1c95, verified via the actions API:

```
2026-07-27T09:52:19Z run 30255739415 completed CANCELLED
2026-07-27T09:53:19Z run 30255809635 pending
```

Sixty seconds apart, same SHA, first cancelled by the second. Same shape as the previous head (07:26 cancelled, 07:33 live, seven minutes apart), reproduced IMMEDIATELY on a fresh SHA. So bd-6b6bb8 is not an occasional race: a single dispatch appears to reliably produce a doomed run plus a real one. Cost: one wasted runner slot per attempt, plus cancelled-job rows left in the rollup, which is the origin of the sub-ten-second false reds recorded earlier.

### Design consequence

This is the strongest argument yet that carry-forward on merge-tree-oid match is LOAD-BEARING rather than an optimisation. Without it, at the current main cadence the head cannot validate at all. With it, a content-identical rebase inherits its passing checks and the cycle breaks.

The asymmetry rule still governs: carry the PASSES, drop and re-run the FAILURES. That also prevents the cancelled twin runs 5s/6s/0s rows from being inherited.

Independent cheap win: if one dispatch reliably produces a cancelled twin, fixing that halves runner load and removes the main source of false red rows, independently of the carry-forward work.

## Landed-test provenance: two questions, not one (ms-dev-3 ex9vj4iedmpf8g3y, router-verified, 2026-07-27)

The `?ref=main` content-existence test recorded earlier is necessary but NOT sufficient on its own, and the failure is instructive: the same test produced two different WRONG answers about the same PR within fifteen minutes.

`?ref=main` answers "is this content on main NOW". It does not answer "did this PR land". Those diverge in two distinct situations:

1. **Closed-looking window before a sweep completes.** PR2215 sampled at 17:43:36Z appeared closed with its added files 404 on main; conclusion drawn was work loss. Wrong — it merged nine minutes later at 17:52:45Z as `cbb5de5cfb5f5015967332eafc73a289d4f56c2d`.
2. **Revert after merge.** At 17:56:57Z commit `ca0ac5362047` by Harry Askham reverted that merge, so the files were 404 again. Concluding "never landed" would also be wrong.

Correct discriminator, verified by two agents independently:

```
gh pr view N --json mergedAt,mergeCommit
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/<mergeCommit>...main --jq .status   # expect ahead/identical
```

For PR2215 this returns `ahead, ahead_by: 2, behind_by: 0`, proving the merge commit IS an ancestor of main and the PR genuinely landed before being reverted.

**Rule:** deciding whether a PR LANDED requires mergedAt + mergeCommit + ancestry of that commit against main. Content-existence at `?ref=main` then separately answers whether it is STILL there. Report both; do not collapse them into one verdict.

The reporting agent characterised this well: it is the same failure mode as stating which tree a measurement came from, in a different costume — provenance on the measurement rather than care in taking it. Both wrong answers came from a correctly-executed test answering a different question than the one asked.

This sits alongside the Cara-owns-squash-merge and base-retargeting work already specified here rather than as a separate lane, because they solve the same problem from two directions: this bead makes landing deterministic and single-actor, and the cron+hooks make breakage self-healing instead of requiring operator intervention.

## OPERATOR SCOPE ADDITION 2026-07-27 20:26 BST — clean unwind on eviction, plus cron/hooks confirmed here

Operator: "for now cara sync should be run only by caco-ctrl to advance the queue and highlight any failures. we want eventually cara sync to be run in a cron which has hooks that trigger agents to spin up cheaply and fix the queue. For the dirty PRs that conflict with the main due to the cara stack that unwound, drop those commits. in future we need cara to cleanly unwind these on eviction"

### NEW REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR: clean unwind on eviction

When a caravan member is evicted or the stack otherwise unwinds, Cara must cleanly unwind the affected members rather than leaving them carrying inherited commits from a stack that no longer exists.

This is the ROOT FIX for a conflict class that has cost real operator time today. Concrete evidence: after the stack unwound, six of thirteen open PRs went DIRTY/CONFLICTING against main purely because they still carried inherited commits from removed predecessors. The operator had to authorize owners to manually drop those commits — a per-PR manual remedy for what should be an automatic consequence of eviction.

Requirements:
- eviction of a member must leave remaining members in a state that merges cleanly against the current default branch, or explicitly report why it cannot;
- a member must never silently retain commits belonging to an evicted or landed predecessor;
- the unwind must be observable, with receipts naming the evicted member, the affected successors, and the commits dropped from each;
- it must be idempotent and safe to re-run, and must fail closed rather than partially unwinding.

Interim manual remedy, now operator-authorized: owners of PRs conflicting due to stack inheritance may drop the inherited commits and keep only their own work. Scoped strictly to that case — not general rebasing, replacement PRs, re-landing, or re-arming auto-merge. Note `ahead_by` includes inherited commits, so it cannot be used to size a PR own contribution; PR2227 is nine commits of which six are inherited.

Cara sync is run ONLY by helsinki-cacophony-caco-ctrl for now, to advance the queue and surface failures. This supersedes the earlier operator-drives-it-manually posture. The cron target recorded above remains the destination: cara sync on a caco cron whose hooks spin up cheap agents to fix the queue as it breaks.

### Related direction

Ephemeral agents are being wound down now that most PRs have landed. Longer term the operator wants pi-daemon matured in caco until it is the main agent type, which is relevant to how the cron hooks should spawn their repair agents — cheap logical agents rather than full tmux workers.

title: cara sync leaves its worktree parked on the last PR branch it evaluated, so every later read silently uses that branch's config
description:
`cara sync` leaves its worktree checked out on the last PR branch it evaluated. Every subsequent read of that worktree - by a human, an agent, or `cara status` itself - silently uses that branch's config and source instead of the project's. This has now produced one wrong three-hour diagnosis and one prematurely-closed bead.

SUPERSEDES the closed bd-6f234e, which recorded the symptom (worktree 95 commits behind main on a dead agent's branch) and was closed once a cron reset was added. The reset fixed the scheduled path only. The underlying behaviour is unchanged and the trap is still live.

MECHANISM, from the reflog:

    97e2023ff HEAD@{20:01}: checkout: moving from caravan-main to agent/ms-dev-3/...ex9vj4ie
    bfa8a3991 HEAD@{20:00}: reset: moving to origin/main
    bfa8a3991 HEAD@{20:00}: checkout: moving from caravan-main to caravan-main

The cron resets to origin/main and runs. `cara sync` then checks out a PR branch to evaluate it, and leaves it there. Between runs, the worktree is on an arbitrary agent branch.

WHAT IT COST, concretely, tonight:

Running `cara status` manually on helsinki returned:

    cara: sync.max_duration_secs must be between 1 and 3600

I diagnosed an off-by-one in cara's validator - the tool refusing the exact upper bound its own message declares valid - filed it as a P1, escalated it to SIX named agents as a one-character fix gating the entire merge queue and PR #2308, and reported it to the operator repeatedly for three hours as the highest-leverage change available.

All of it was wrong. cara's check is inclusive and correct:

    if !(1..=MAX_SYNC_DURATION_SECS).contains(&self.sync.max_duration_secs)

The value being validated was not 3600:

    value on origin/main:  max_duration_secs: 3600   # max permitted
    value on HEAD:         max_duration_secs: 65525  # Intentionally high to get around
                                                     # sync budget errors

Commit e473cb91b on a dead agent's branch. The worktree was parked there, so every manual read got that config.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN JUST BEING CAREFUL:

  1. THE WORKTREE LOOKS AUTHORITATIVE. It is at a well-known path, it is the tree cara
     itself uses, and nothing about reading it suggests you are looking at a random PR
     rather than the project. An operator or agent investigating a cara problem will
     naturally read it.
  2. THE SCHEDULED PATH AND THE MANUAL PATH DISAGREE. The cron resets first, so `cara sync`
     via cron sees origin/main and works. A human running `cara status` seconds later sees
     something else entirely and concludes the tool is broken. Two observers, same machine,
     same minute, opposite conclusions.
  3. IT DEFEATS THE REPAIR THAT WAS ALREADY MADE. The operator created a `caravan-main`
     branch and added fetch-and-reset to the cron specifically to fix this. Both were
     correct. The tree still ends up parked, because nothing restores it afterwards.

THE FIX: restore the base branch when a sync completes. The worktree then means something
between runs, and a missing or delayed reset stops being silently destructive.

WORTH CONSIDERING ALONGSIDE: cara could refuse, or loudly warn, when the tree it is about
to reason from is materially behind its base. A sync worktree 95 commits behind produced
wrong compatibility answers for days and no surface reported it.

SEPARATE ISSUE SURFACED BY THIS, worth its own bead if someone agrees: the 65525 was written
deliberately - "Intentionally high to get around sync budget errors". Someone hit real
budget errors and escaped them by writing an invalid value. If 3600 is genuinely too low for
real syncs, the ceiling should be raised in cara rather than exceeded in config.

Filed by operator-proxy, who caused the wrong diagnosis and would like the next person not
to repeat it.

title: Investigate second root caravan forming while a live tail exists
description:
Observation requiring evidence, not a confirmed defect. Two single-member caravans formed in Cacophony where the auto-admission path appears to permit only join-or-skip.

Observed (read-only `cara --json status` from ~/cacophony, cara 0.0.74):
- 08:43:38Z PR #2338 created (agent ms-mac-cacophony-caco-dev-msm-2, bd-08564f), later admitted, caravan 2338 with member [2338], base main, head 0fad9f54.
- 09:21:21Z PR #2339 created (agent ms-mac-cacophony-caco-dev-msm-1, bd-0fbc94).
- A watch after 09:21 showed caravan 2338 live AND #2339 as the selected admission candidate, with pauses [] so no hold applied.
- By 10:01Z status showed TWO caravans, 2338 [2338] and 2339 [2339], each single-member, both based on main. #2339 did not stack: a joined member would carry the tail head branch as its base, not main.

Why this looks anomalous. In sync.rs, evaluate_auto_candidate computes current_tail_generations, which includes every caravan with a resolvable tail with no eligibility filter beyond that. When that list is non-empty the function iterates tails, returns Join on the first eligible tail, and after the loop returns Skip. The New branch is reachable only when tails.is_empty(). Cacophony drives admission through scripts/cara-ci-sync.sh, which runs `cara --json sync --all` and never calls `cara new`, and its config enables rebase_on_join, sync.actions.join_unlabelled_prs, and auto_admission. So a second root caravan forming while tail #2338 was live does not match the modelled path.

Candidate explanations, undetermined from status plus code alone:
1. #2339 was admitted by explicit owner intent (an agent or operator naming it), which legitimately forms a new caravan regardless of live tails.
2. Another surface created the caravan, for example a caco reintegration mode rather than Cara auto-admission.
3. A genuine gap in auto-admission where a new caravan can form despite a live tail, which would explain why multi-member stacking has never been observed in this fleet.

Decisive evidence not yet gathered because the observer is authorized to run only `cara --json status`: Caravan's journal (`cara log` in ~/cacophony) records CaravanCreated versus PrJoined with the admission selector and reasons, and `cara plan sync` would predict whether the next candidate (#2340) joins an existing tail or forms a third caravan. `cara plan sync` performs no marked provider or Git writes and counts real completed mutations rather than asserting zero (bd-216da5), but it does consume provider reads.

Next step is operator authorization to run one of those two read-only surfaces, then either close this as expected explicit-intent behavior or convert it into a defect with exact journal evidence.

RESOLVED — root cause found, and it is not a Caravan defect.

Cacophony's Cara auto-admission has not run for five days, so the join-versus-new evaluation that produces stacking never executed.

Evidence:
- .github/workflows/cara-sync.yml is the deterministic Cacophony Cara scheduler and is `workflow_dispatch: {}` only. It carries no schedule trigger, so it never fires automatically.
- Its most recent runs are all from 2026-07-27 and every one of the last eight concluded failure. The last run is 30292712770 at 2026-07-27T18:12:17Z.
- Those runs failed in the bootstrap phase, not in Cara: "Cara bootstrap source unresolved: the event payload carried no default branch, so the trusted current-main bootstrap ref cannot be resolved", then "bounded trusted default-branch checkout failed or exceeded its five-minute ceiling". The workflow pins its trusted source to the CURRENT default branch (bd-3e6836); on workflow_dispatch the event payload did not carry the default branch it expects.
- Meanwhile caravans 2336, 2337, 2338 and 2339 formed and merged across 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-01, so admission is being driven by some surface other than `cara --json sync --all`.

This explains every observation that prompted this bead. #2339 forming its own caravan while tail #2338 was live is not evaluate_auto_candidate returning New: that function was never invoked. current_tail_generations, the join-first loop, and the Skip fall-through are all correct as written and remain unrefuted. It also explains why no multi-member caravan has ever been observed in this fleet: the only surface that evaluates joining a candidate onto a live tail is auto-admission inside sync, and that has not run since 2026-07-27.

Consequence for the operator's stacking question: stacking cannot be observed while the scheduler is dead, regardless of how many PRs queue up. Whatever currently creates these single-member caravans is not the join-evaluating path.

Operator actions, both outside this observer's authority and in Cacophony rather than Caravan:
1. Repair the cara-sync.yml bootstrap failure so the trusted default-branch ref resolves on workflow_dispatch.
2. Dispatch the workflow, or add a schedule if continuous admission is intended, since workflow_dispatch alone means admission only ever runs when a human triggers it.

No Caravan code change is indicated. Close this bead once the operator has seen the finding; reopen only if a sync tick actually runs and still forms a second root caravan while a live unheld tail exists.

CORRECTION (2026-08-01, operator supplied canonical scheduler source): the prior resolution claiming Cacophony auto-admission had not run for five days was WRONG.

I inspected the wrong scheduler surface. `.github/workflows/cara-sync.yml` is intentionally workflow_dispatch-only/off; it is not the live scheduler. The canonical live scheduler is `~/.cacophony/daemon/checkouts/cacophony-config/automation.yaml`, which defines enabled cron `cara-sync` on Helsinki every five minutes (`*/5 * * * *`). That cron updates Cara, resets the dedicated Cacophony worktree to current main, then runs `cara sync --all --json`, capturing stdout/stderr separately and failing the tick on error. `caco cron list --name cara --verbose` confirms the same effective entry.

Therefore all conclusions derived from stale GitHub workflow history are invalid: auto-admission was not proven dead; the parallel one-member caravans are not explained by a five-day scheduler outage; and cacophony bd-68fda0 was misfiled and must be retracted/closed by an actor with Cacophony scope.

Correct live explanation supplied by the operator: bd-10303b intentionally prevents rewrite-requiring automatic tail formation. The two-root state is expected under that current P0 work, and recovery is tracked in bd-b6d25b as an atomic caravan-to-caravan concat operation plus UI control. Keep concat behind the automatic tail-reformation fix; do not interrupt bd-10303b or current P0 work.

Reasoning failure to preserve: I treated one repository workflow as the sole scheduler without checking first-party `caco cron list` or the canonical automation.yaml. The correct first step for scheduler claims is inspect the effective first-party scheduler catalog and canonical config, then inspect implementation-specific hosted workflows only as secondary surfaces.

title: Membership mutation receipts drop recorded GitHub App Git transport telemetry
description:
Live acceptance blocker found while executing bd-71e444 against disposable Caravan PR #15 with released `cara 0.0.78`.

## Measured result

The physical `cara --json new --create-pr` operation succeeded in App mode and produced one exact force-with-lease rewrite:

- App: `caravan-agentic-merge-queue`, installation `150598516`
- old head `529dab29f4bf7859b267d886867c961f4253de14`
- new head `b2e8cacf4b3efe30aa1f0e3228e40915b4637910`
- exact lease `refs/heads/canary/bd-71e444-app-actor-20260801:529dab29...`
- provider timeline force-push actor: `caravan-agentic-merge-queue[bot]`
- API PR/comment/label actors: the same bot

So the transport works and provider identity parity is proven from GitHub facts.

But the successful `new` JSON envelope has no `provider_api` field at all. `evict` is the same. The operation therefore omits the secret-free fields the model and deployment contract already define:

- `auth_source: github_app_installation`
- `github_app_slug`
- `github_app_installation_id`
- `github_app_token_expires_unix_secs`
- `github_app_git_transport: https_credential_helper`
- `github_app_git_repository: harryaskham/caravan`

A separate read-only `status`/`check` exposes API identity (`auth_source`, slug, installation), but naturally performs no physical Git push and does not expose Git transport. There is therefore no Cara receipt that binds API and Git transport identity for the mutating operation, even though `ProcessRunner::record_github_app_git_transport` records it internally.

This contradicts `README.md` / `docs/github-app.md`, which say status, check, sync, loop, JSON, and MCP receipts expose App identity plus exact Git transport/repository. It prevents bd-71e444 from satisfying its telemetry acceptance without substituting source inspection for runtime evidence.

Sanitized live evidence is attached as project file `file-f49c5884ce1f-1785615826481` (`bd-71e444-evidence.json`, sha256 `f49c5884ce1f71104d8a35b6d7932f61418f22bbb6f7f8597f5695687e102d7a`). PR #15 was evicted, closed, de-labelled, branch-deleted, and never merged; main remained exact.

## Required fix

Attach the final operation runner's `GitHubApiTelemetry` to every membership/mutation output that can issue provider API or remote Git operations (`new`, `join`, `renew`, `rejoin`, `evict`, reshape/split as applicable), using the same stable field/schema already exposed by read outputs. Merge telemetry from discovery/provider and physical Git runners so the final envelope names the one selected App principal and Git transport/repository.

No token/key/broker stdout may enter the envelope, error, journal, or test artifact.

## Tests

- App-mode physical `new` receipt contains exact slug/installation, `https_credential_helper`, and exact repository after a push.
- API and Git selections cannot disagree; mismatch still fails before mutation.
- Ambient mode remains behavior-compatible and never invents App fields.
- JSON/MCP/CLI typed outputs remain parity-compatible.
- Token sentinel absent from receipt, error, journal and snapshots.
- No provider mutation behavior changes; this is projection of already-recorded secret-free telemetry.

title: One conflicting unqueued PR prevents any caravan from ever forming
description:
Cacophony has never once formed a caravan. Three defects in the same code path caused it, and each hid the others. Found by writing a test for the operator's ACTUAL shape (empty fleet, several unqueued PRs, FIFO-leading one conflicting) rather than the shape the existing test used (empty fleet, one clean candidate).

1. THE HEAD-OF-LINE FIX HAS BEEN DEAD SINCE v0.0.27, AND I KILLED IT.
   bd-fd9b11 made admission skip a mechanically conflicting candidate by matching `GraphProblemKind::Incompatible`. bd-0efaf2 then changed the PRODUCER in graph.rs to emit `CandidateIncompatible`, but the consumer guard in read.rs still named `Incompatible`. Since graph no longer emits that kind for candidates, the guard never fires: a conflicting leading candidate holds the front again, exactly the bug the operator reported. Every test stayed green because the read.rs unit test injected a problem with the OLD kind by hand, so it exercised a path production could no longer reach.

2. AN UNADMITTED CANDIDATE'S CONFLICT MARKED THE WHOLE FLEET UNHEALTHY.
   `GraphAnalysis::healthy()` was `problems.is_empty()`. A candidate that is in no caravan and blocks nothing therefore made the fleet unhealthy, which cascades into check eligibility.

3. `check` INHERITED OTHER CANDIDATES' CONFLICTS.
   `check_analysis` seeded its problem list from the entire fleet, so PR A's incompatibility made unrelated PR B ineligible. With an empty fleet and any one conflicting unqueued PR, no clean candidate could ever be admitted, so bootstrap was impossible.

Together: one conflicting PR anywhere in the unqueued set prevented the first caravan from ever forming. Cacophony had 11-15 unqueued PRs with 2234 conflicting.

Fix: consumer guard matches the kind actually emitted; `healthy()` ignores CandidateIncompatible; `check` inherits fleet problems except other candidates' incompatibilities. Pinned by sync/tests.rs::a_conflicting_leading_candidate_still_lets_a_clean_one_form_the_first_caravan, which asserts all three properties at once: no fleet-blocking problem, the queue elects the clean follower, and the empty fleet evaluates to AutoCandidateTarget::New.

LESSON: the pre-existing empty-fleet test proved bootstrap worked in a shape the operator never had. A test whose fixture is simpler than production can certify a broken path indefinitely.

title: Publish a reusable CI-admission gate action
description:
Counterpart to cacophony/bd-5d71e6 (consumer) and cacophony/bd-52b4d2 (interim workflow fix). Caravan should own the question "is existing CI evidence still exactly valid for this PR generation" so adopting repositories do not re-derive Caravan semantics from fragile GitHub event heuristics.

Ship a reusable GitHub action plus the underlying typed command. It reads the repository-owned .caravan/config.yaml and exact provider facts (PR number, head OID, base ref/OID, merge tree, membership, labels, generation) and returns a decision other jobs can be conditional on:
- ci_valid: content-identical promotion retarget; prior head-SHA checks still apply; no re-run needed.
- ci_required: physical rebase produced a new head, or base retarget changed the merge tree; run CI, scoped to changed surface.
- ci_force_accepted: caravan-force head where the operator explicitly accepted CI state; no blocking re-run, audit preserved.
- ci_not_applicable: unenrolled or ordinary PR; Caravan has no opinion.
- ci_unknown: anything unproven; fail open to RUNNING CI, never to skipping it.

Evidence requirements: every decision names the exact facts it rests on, so a human can audit why CI was skipped. The promotion path must record tree equality between the pre- and post-retarget merge trees in its receipt, since Caravan already computes the would-be-rebase tree to choose retarget versus rebase. That receipt is the authoritative source for ci_valid.

Safety boundary, explicit: the gate is advisory about COST, never about SAFETY. It may only assert that exact existing evidence still applies; it may never assert that a head can merge without evidence. It must never report success for a head with no prior successful run, and consumers must keep required contexts reporting.

Rejected alternative, recorded: making repository CI workflow_dispatch-only and having Caravan drive which refs run when. That inverts ownership, makes the queue engine a single point of failure for all testing, and breaks CI for ordinary contributors on unenrolled PRs.

Sequence after caravan/bd-f8cf99 lands, since the promotion receipt and retarget-versus-rebase decision are its outputs.

title: Foreground loop must survive retryable ticks and provider read-after-write lag
description:
Live Cacophony dogfood: `cara loop` exited on a `rebase_stale_lease` retry_tick error after the default branch advanced mid-tick (expected 94d6ebb, actual d65aba6), and a separate `cara sync --all` aborted with `rebase_midpoint_head_stale` right after a successful force-with-lease push, leaving the caravan head with auto-merge disabled until an operator reran it. Human evidence for both was dumped as "structured evidence is too large" instead of the exact OIDs.

## Required behavior

- The unbounded foreground loop must never exit on a domain failure. Each failed tick dispatches its canonical event to configured hooks, records bounded evidence (code, disposition, wake class, retryable, next action), streams a compact operator line, and ticks again. Only an explicit stop signal ends the loop, and the summary reports total, failed, and consecutive-failure counts. `loop --once` keeps returning one typed error for schedulers, and manual mode keeps its TTY decision shell while surviving ordinary failures.
- Provider read-after-write lag must not be reported as a stale generation. After an exact proven push, verification retries the exact expected OID under a bounded attempt/delay budget, and midpoint discovery gets one bounded re-read. Any other observed generation still fails closed.
- Compact human rendering for `rebase_stale_lease`, `rebase_midpoint_head_stale`, and `rebase_midpoint_pr_missing` shows branch, expected/observed OIDs, auto-merge state, and the safe next action instead of a size-truncated JSON blob.

## Acceptance

Hermetic driver fixtures prove retryable and external-decision failures keep ticking with hook dispatch and bounded retained evidence, that retained failures stay bounded, and that a signal still stops cleanly. Live Cacophony ticks converge across default-branch movement without operator restarts.

title: cara sync has no dry-run, so authorising a tick means approving an unbounded action described only by a prediction
description:
`cara sync` has no dry-run, so the only way to find out what a tick will do is to let it do it.

OBSERVED 2026-07-30. A caravan maintainer agent needed to predict the outcome of a tick before running it, because its standing watch instruction forbids `sync` and the operator needed to authorise the action. With no dry-run available, it had to:

  1. read the admission rules in source
  2. reason about which rule applies at which stage
  3. state a prediction
  4. and explicitly caveat that the prediction was derived from reading code, not from a simulation

It also got the prediction WRONG on the first attempt, and caught itself twenty minutes later. It had told the operator that a BLOCKED candidate would make the queue wait. On re-reading it found that admission and merge apply DIFFERENT rules:

    AT ADMISSION   pending bars nothing; has_failing_check refuses only
                   Failure, Cancelled, TimedOut, ActionRequired
    AT MERGE       pending means wait; a member with in-flight CI is not merged

It had run the merge-time rule against an admission-time question. That is an easy and entirely reasonable mistake, and it is exactly the class of mistake a dry-run exists to make impossible.

WHY THIS MATTERS

1. It makes authorisation expensive. An operator asked to approve a tick has no way to see what the tick would do. The approval is therefore for an unbounded action described by a prediction, which is a much larger thing to grant than "apply these specific changes".

2. It makes the cautious answer "no". Every mutating queue operation becomes a judgement call under uncertainty, so a careful agent under a restrictive watch instruction will decline, and the queue stops moving. That is precisely what happened here - the queue sat correctly positioned to produce its first two-member chain while everyone waited for a decision nobody could inform.

3. It costs the same predictive work every time. The agent's careful source reading is not reusable and not verifiable by anyone else without repeating it.

WHAT WOULD HELP

`cara sync --dry-run` reporting, without mutating anything:

  - which candidates would be SKIPPED and the exact reason for each
  - which would be ADMITTED, and into which caravan
  - the resulting membership
  - whether any member would become eligible for MERGE in this tick, which is the
    part with real consequences under force_merge: true

The analysis half already exists - `cara status` and `cara check` run it read-only every time. What is missing is the projection of the admission and merge decisions that would follow from that analysis.

RELATED: `caco agent reintegrate --dry-run`, `caco bd update --dry-run`, and `caco release trigger --dry-run` all exist for exactly this reason. The queue is arguably the surface where it matters most, because its actions are the least reversible.

title: Publish a first-party Caravan CI-admission gate over promotion/merge receipts
description:
Counterpart to cacophony/bd-5d71e6. That bead needs a reusable gate that answers exactly one question -- 'is this existing CI evidence still exactly valid for this exact head/base?' -- without re-deriving Caravan semantics from GitHub event shape in workflow YAML.

bd-f8cf99 already lands the evidence this needs:
- sealed root_promotion receipts (exact head, base before/after, default branch, predecessor and its merged state, derived trigger);
- sealed root_merge receipts with the authorizing CumulativeTreeProof (candidate_tree, merge_result_tree, identical, and the exact target default-branch OID);
- physical rebase receipts for the 'new head, must re-run' case.

What is missing is the publication surface. Recommended shape: one first-party 'cara gate --pr N --json' subcommand emitting the typed decision from the same code path sync uses, with the composite action as a thin wrapper. No decision logic in YAML or JS, one implementation, one set of receipts.

Design points to settle while implementing:
- distinguish head-SHA-attached check runs (survive a retarget, because promotion never rewrites the head) from merge-ref-computed jobs (refs/pull/N/merge is recomputed on base change). The cumulative-tree proof is exactly what makes a merge-ref job provably content-identical; without it the gate must fail open to running CI.
- a proof is only valid against the exact default-branch OID it was constructed against; a moved default branch is 'unproven', never 'valid'.
- decide whether the gate should compute member-level tree proofs (currently proofs are collected for caravan roots) and price the extra merge-tree per member.
- caravan-force needs an explicit tie-break: cacophony/bd-5d71e6 asks the gate both to report success for required contexts and never to report success for a head with no prior successful run. A forced head must surface a visibly distinct forced conclusion, never a plain green indistinguishable from a real pass.

Do not implement inside bd-f8cf99: that bead is complete as the landing contract, and this is an additive publication surface.

title: Move environment-dependent Caravan hook acceptances out of blocking Nix install builds
description:
## Failure

A second operator-supplied emulated-aarch64 ordinary Nix install failed while building Cacophony's Caravan dependency because environmental/load/process acceptance tests run in the blocking install build.

Exact failing tests in `tests/hook_example.rs`:

- `operator_action_notifies_a_human_instead_of_spawning_an_agent`
- `an_unresolvable_caravan_files_one_bead_and_dispatches_one_agent`

Both panic at line 107 on the invariant `a hook must never fail the tick that observed the problem`.

This blocks the dependency chain `caravan -> caco -> Home Manager / Nix-on-Droid` even though the failure is an integration/environment acceptance signal rather than a deterministic compile, unit, build, or version-contract failure.

## Required change

Do not weaken either behavior assertion.

Move load/process/environment-dependent hook and integration acceptances out of the ordinary blocking Nix install derivation into a scheduled/manual non-blocking CI lane.

That lane must retain the exact assertions and run them in an environment that can exercise their process, notification, bead, dispatch, and webhook dependencies.

On failure, route the exact bounded evidence through the configured feedback webhook so one canonical bead is filed or refreshed; repeated identical failures must dedupe instead of creating a bead storm.

Deterministic unit, build, schema, and version checks remain blocking for ordinary Nix builds and installs.

## Acceptance

1. An emulated-aarch64 ordinary Nix install of Caravan as Cacophony's dependency does not execute the environmental hook acceptances and can complete when deterministic checks pass.
2. Scheduled/manual CI still executes both named tests without weakening their assertions.
3. A forced environmental failure produces one bounded feedback-webhook receipt and one canonical bead/link; an identical rerun refreshes or dedupes that record rather than filing another bead.
4. A passing scheduled/manual run files no failure bead.
5. The CI result names the exact test, architecture, environment, source revision, and failure phase without leaking credentials.
6. Documentation states which tests are install-blocking and which are non-blocking environmental acceptance.

## Related

Pi Daemon tracks the analogous Attic+aarch64/non-blocking acceptance work as `bd-184815`. This bead owns only Caravan's hook/load/process integration lane.

Implementation completed on agent commit a8a76ff: the hook_example integration target now requires the environmental-hook-acceptance feature; ordinary Cargo/Nix/PR/release checks exclude it; schedule/manual workflow hook-acceptance.yml runs every assertion unchanged and reports one bounded redacted failure with a stable architecture/environment-class/phase fingerprint. Passing runs file nothing; forced-failure drills exercise the same path. Receiver-side fingerprint-to-bead idempotency is intentionally owned by Cacophony bd-52cf42, with no Caravan-local workaround. Focused validation: workflow lint and shellcheck, deterministic lane contract, feedback fingerprint unit test, all four explicit hook assertions, default-vs-feature target discovery, rustfmt, diff check, and targeted clippy all pass.

title: cara sync leaves its worktree parked on the last PR branch it evaluated, so every later read silently uses that branch config
description:
`cara sync` leaves its worktree checked out on the last PR branch it evaluated. Every subsequent read of that worktree - by a human, an agent, or `cara status` itself - silently uses that branch's config and source instead of the project's. This has now produced one wrong three-hour diagnosis and one prematurely-closed bead.

SUPERSEDES the closed bd-6f234e, which recorded the symptom (worktree 95 commits behind main on a dead agent's branch) and was closed once a cron reset was added. The reset fixed the scheduled path only. The underlying behaviour is unchanged and the trap is still live.

MECHANISM, from the reflog:

    97e2023ff HEAD@{20:01}: checkout: moving from caravan-main to agent/ms-dev-3/...ex9vj4ie
    bfa8a3991 HEAD@{20:00}: reset: moving to origin/main
    bfa8a3991 HEAD@{20:00}: checkout: moving from caravan-main to caravan-main

The cron resets to origin/main and runs. `cara sync` then checks out a PR branch to evaluate it, and leaves it there. Between runs, the worktree is on an arbitrary agent branch.

WHAT IT COST, concretely, tonight:

Running `cara status` manually on helsinki returned:

    cara: sync.max_duration_secs must be between 1 and 3600

I diagnosed an off-by-one in cara's validator - the tool refusing the exact upper bound its own message declares valid - filed it as a P1, escalated it to SIX named agents as a one-character fix gating the entire merge queue and PR #2308, and reported it to the operator repeatedly for three hours as the highest-leverage change available.

All of it was wrong. cara's check is inclusive and correct:

    if !(1..=MAX_SYNC_DURATION_SECS).contains(&self.sync.max_duration_secs)

The value being validated was not 3600:

    value on origin/main:  max_duration_secs: 3600   # max permitted
    value on HEAD:         max_duration_secs: 65525  # Intentionally high to get around
                                                     # sync budget errors

Commit e473cb91b on a dead agent's branch. The worktree was parked there, so every manual read got that config.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN JUST BEING CAREFUL:

  1. THE WORKTREE LOOKS AUTHORITATIVE. It is at a well-known path, it is the tree cara
     itself uses, and nothing about reading it suggests you are looking at a random PR
     rather than the project. An operator or agent investigating a cara problem will
     naturally read it.
  2. THE SCHEDULED PATH AND THE MANUAL PATH DISAGREE. The cron resets first, so `cara sync`
     via cron sees origin/main and works. A human running `cara status` seconds later sees
     something else entirely and concludes the tool is broken. Two observers, same machine,
     same minute, opposite conclusions.
  3. IT DEFEATS THE REPAIR THAT WAS ALREADY MADE. The operator created a `caravan-main`
     branch and added fetch-and-reset to the cron specifically to fix this. Both were
     correct. The tree still ends up parked, because nothing restores it afterwards.

THE FIX: restore the base branch when a sync completes. The worktree then means something
between runs, and a missing or delayed reset stops being silently destructive.

WORTH CONSIDERING ALONGSIDE: cara could refuse, or loudly warn, when the tree it is about
to reason from is materially behind its base. A sync worktree 95 commits behind produced
wrong compatibility answers for days and no surface reported it.

SEPARATE ISSUE SURFACED BY THIS, worth its own bead if someone agrees: the 65525 was written
deliberately - "Intentionally high to get around sync budget errors". Someone hit real
budget errors and escaped them by writing an invalid value. If 3600 is genuinely too low for
real syncs, the ceiling should be raised in cara rather than exceeded in config.

Filed by operator-proxy, who caused the wrong diagnosis and would like the next person not
to repeat it.

title: helsinki cron runs cara 0.0.22 from the nix store while 0.0.51 writes the journal: unknown-variant failure reads like corruption but is version skew
description:
The scheduled caravan sync on helsinki runs cara 0.0.22 from the nix profile while everything else uses 0.0.51 from ~/.local/bin. The newer binary writes journal record types the older one cannot parse, so every scheduled sync now dies on a file that is not corrupt.

THE OBSERVED FAILURE, reported by the operator:

    Caravan sync failed for Cacophony: cara journal_record_invalid: invalid complete
    journal record in /home/harry/.cacophony/daemon/checkouts/cacophony/.git/caravan/events-v1.jsonl:
    unknown variant `candidate_incompatible`, expected one of `missing_head`,
    `multiple_heads`, `branching`, `cycle`, ...

THE JOURNAL IS NOT CORRUPT. Running cara 0.0.51 against that exact file reads it cleanly and renders the records in full:

    ! CandidateIncompatible [#2245]: leading admission candidate does not merge cleanly into t...
    ! CandidateIncompatible [#2259]: leading admission candidate does not merge cleanly into t...

Those are correct and useful - GitHub independently reports both PRs as DIRTY. The records are exactly right; the reader is too old to know the word.

THE VERSION SKEW, measured on helsinki:

    cron-resolved PATH:  $HOME/.nix-profile/bin:/run/current-system/sw/bin:/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin
    -> resolves          /home/harry/.nix-profile/bin/cara    cara 0.0.22

    also present:        /home/harry/.local/bin/cara          cara 0.0.51

    journal:             68 records, first `candidate_incompatible` at line 43,
                         13 occurrences, file last written 2026-07-29 21:09

The nix-profile entry is a SYMLINK INTO THE NIX STORE. It is pinned by the flake, so `cara self-update` cannot modify it - which is why the operator's self-update appeared not to take. His update went to ~/.local/bin, which the cron's PATH does not include.

THE FIX, one directory, and the ORDER MATTERS:

    export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.nix-profile/bin:/run/current-system/sw/bin:/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin:$PATH"

`.local/bin` MUST precede `.nix-profile/bin` or the store-pinned 0.0.22 keeps winning.
`.cargo/bin` is needed for `caco`, which the cron calls on its first working line.

Verified on helsinki in a clean `env -i` shell reproducing exactly what cron gets:

    cara -> /home/harry/.local/bin/cara    cara 0.0.51
    caco -> /home/harry/.cargo/bin/caco

The operator is nix-switching helsinki so both paths carry the current version, which is the
better long-term answer. Until that lands, the PATH order is the interim.

THE DESIGN QUESTION WORTH SEPARATING OUT: should an unknown journal variant be FATAL?

A reader encountering a record type it does not recognise currently refuses the entire sync. An alternative is to skip unknown variants with a warning naming the variant and the minimum version that understands it - which turns a hard stop into a legible degradation and makes mixed-version fleets survivable. cara already does version-compatibility checking elsewhere (`min_cara_version`, `check_reader_compatibility`), so the concept exists; it is simply not applied at the journal-record level.

That matters beyond this incident: any fleet where one node self-updates and another is
pinned by a package manager will hit this, and the failure gives no hint that VERSION is the
issue. "unknown variant `candidate_incompatible`" reads like data corruption. It is not.
It is a reader from before that word was invented.

True main already contains the release as distinct commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7`, parented on main `80bf4eac`, with tree `b54319dc`. Cara replayed that already-main release delta into the child because the selected tail was stale. Consequently PR #2080 includes unrelated `CHANGELOG.md`, `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock` release changes alongside the intended `.caravan/config.yaml` change. Initial PR title/body also came from the replayed release/update-helper commit rather than the unique source commit; the operator subsequently corrected the metadata manually.

Provider events show force-pushes as the branch was materialized. Preserve PR #2080 and branch/event evidence until diagnosis is complete.

## Expected behavior

Before any rewrite, push, PR creation/update, or enrollment, Cara join must prove the selected caravan root/tail is current with the configured base or otherwise has a safe, explicit sync plan. Joining a branch based on newer main to a stale tail must never silently absorb missing-main commits into the child.

Cara must either:

- transactionally sync/rebase the caravan root/tail to current main and then replay only the source branch's unique commits/patch; or
- fail closed with an exact stale-root decision before provider mutation.

Join planning/apply must receipt-bind source repo/branch/head/parent/tree/patch identity, selected caravan/root/tail heads, configured base head, and expected resulting tree. Apply must revalidate all identities and verify the published child contains exactly the unique source patch. PR title/body provenance must come from the intended source commit/operator metadata, never an absorbed main/release commit.

## Regression fixtures

- A source branch based on newer main joining a stale one-PR caravan tail: assert no missing-main commit is replayed into the child.
- Root-current-main invariant drift between preview/apply: fail before push/PR/label mutation.
- Unique source commit plus unrelated release commit already on main: resulting child contains only the unique source patch and uses its title/body provenance.
- Empty unique source patch after subtracting current-main ancestry: return an explicit no-op and perform zero provider mutations.

## Safety

Do not merge PR #2080 in its current form: it duplicates main's release delta and is based on stale non-main ancestry. Do not close, retarget, join again, or otherwise mutate it while preserving the reproduction evidence.

## Canonical Cara 0.0.6 graph and audit evidence

Read-only `cara status --json` with released 0.0.6 confirms:

- active caravan id/root `2079`, members `[2079, 2080]`;
- configured default branch observation `main@d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7`;
- PR2079 root `main@80bf4eac -> fix-slackiq-nodes@c059bf15`, auto-merge armed;
- PR2080 child `fix-slackiq-nodes@c059bf15 -> fix-cara-timeouts@21097975`, auto-merge disabled;
- PR2080 synthetic merge/tree `0bd617a166018d3f2c9b949fa67e9cbd746ecc01` / `4413f2fa0dc545e8df41671b8cad6a72a2d7a0ac`;
- compatibility reports both stale-root-to-current-main and child-to-tail as mechanically clean, demonstrating that clean mergeability alone failed to enforce root-current-main ancestry/provenance.

The same released binary's `cara log --pr 2080 --limit 100 --json` returns zero matching records even though provider history records the branch force-push and caravan label. Therefore no durable operation receipt is discoverable from the canonical journal for this mutation. The fix must also guarantee a durable preview/apply operation receipt for join attempts, including no-op/refusal outcomes and every provider mutation identity, so this class of provenance failure is auditable without reconstructing it from GitHub events.

## Merged duplicate: bd-0fe6ad

Title: Reject Cara join when candidate patch already landed on default branch

## Live reproduction

While joining Cacophony PR #2080 (`fix-cara-timeouts`) to an active caravan, Cara physically rebased an already-landed release patch onto caravan tail `fix-slackiq-nodes` and enrolled the result instead of rejecting it as already present on the default branch.

Exact observed generations:

- default branch `main`: `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7` (`release: v1.2.1562`), parent `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`
- caravan tail/base: `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, also parented by `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`
- rewritten PR head: `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680`, parented by the caravan tail
- `git patch-id --stable` for both the main commit and rewritten PR commit: `c8c875993b7fed870c2082837caea490559260e2`
- PR #2080 was force-updated to the rewritten head at 23:08:19Z and then labelled `caravan` at 23:08:56Z.

The rewritten PR therefore contains a patch already integrated on exact current `main`. Its diff against the caravan tail is the release patch, while its diff against current main consists only of unrelated caravan-tail drift. The operator described the source PR as empty/already landed before join.

## Gap

`physical_rebase.rs` rejects `commit_count == 0` relative to the candidate's old provider base (`rebase_empty_patch_range`), but does not reject a non-empty candidate range whose stable patch identity/content is already present on the exact default-branch generation. Rebasing that range onto a stale caravan tail resurrects an already-landed change as a new PR commit.

## Required contract

Before a physical join rewrite or enrollment, compare the candidate-only patch range with the exact current default branch and fail closed when every candidate patch is already represented there (stable patch-id and tree/content proof, with ambiguity rejected). Return a typed `already_landed`/empty-effective-diff decision and do not rewrite the head, retarget, label, or enroll the PR.

Add a fixture for sibling histories from one merge base where branch A's patch has already landed on default and joining branch A onto branch B's caravan tail would otherwise replay that patch. Preserve ordinary joining when the candidate has genuinely new effective content.

## Merged duplicate: bd-915573

Title: Cara empty-diff join replays another reintegration patch onto caller branch

Operator reproduction on 2026-07-21 exposed cross-reintegration patch contamination while joining Cacophony branch `fix-cara-timeouts` into the active Caravan/Cara tail. The intended operator change was `fix cara timeoutes`, but before that commit was added, Cara/Cacophony synthesized daemon-authored commit `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680` on `fix-cara-timeouts` with the complete, unrelated update-helper `release: v1.2.1562` patch and release-agent provenance.

Exact evidence:

- True GitHub `main` independently and correctly contains release commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7`, parent `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`; annotated tag `v1.2.1562` peels to it.
- The active Cara tail/base branch `fix-slackiq-nodes` is `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, also parented by `80bf4eac` and carrying the separate `fix ms agent scope` patch.
- Cara-created/reused PR https://github.com/harryaskham/cacophony/pull/2080 targets `fix-slackiq-nodes` from `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- Its first commit is `ac701198`, parent `c059bf15`, authored by Cacophony Daemon at 23:04:11Z. Its title/body were initially `release: v1.2.1562` and copied update-helper identity/head `e3026e0461`, despite the operator working on `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- `ac701198` contains only the unrelated release metadata patch (`Cargo.toml`, twenty workspace entries in `Cargo.lock`, and `CHANGELOG.md`). It is a duplicate replay of the patch already landed on true main as `d9fad17e`.
- The operator's intended `fix cara timeoutes` commit `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633` was subsequently added on top of the contaminated release commit; live PR 2080 therefore now contains both `.caravan/config.yaml` and the unrelated release patch.

The operator reports Cara first observed an empty diff while he was on `fix-cara-timeouts`, then created PR 2080 and inferred/replayed the diff from main to the Caravan tail. An empty caller patch must never fall back to another agent's most recent reintegration patch, global generation, main-to-tail delta, or stale receipt.

Required behavior:

- Bind join materialization to the exact caller owner, source branch/head, expected base/tail, and patch identity receipt.
- If the caller's patch against the selected tail is empty, return an explicit empty/no-op/refusal receipt; do not mutate the caller branch and do not create a PR.
- Refuse when receipt owner/head/patch differs from the branch being joined, even if a recent reintegration has a reusable-looking diff or commit message.
- Preserve the caller branch on any ambiguity and surface exact candidate provenance for diagnosis.
- Add a regression test with two concurrent patches: release patch A lands on main while operator branch B joins an active tail with an initially empty diff; B must never receive A.

Do not mutate or close PR 2080 as part of triage; preserve it as live evidence until the owner chooses repair.

## Operator clarification

The initiating `fix-cara-timeouts` PR/branch was believed to have no effective diff. The suspected failure mode is therefore earlier than duplicate-patch replay alone: candidate range inference selected the immediately preceding release commit when the intended source branch was empty, then physical rebase replayed that inferred commit onto the caravan tail.

The fix must first prove the intended provider PR's exact base/head range and reject an empty effective source diff without borrowing a predecessor commit. The already-landed-on-default check remains a necessary independent backstop, because the inferred release commit was already represented on current `main`.

Duplicate investigation signal merged from bd-6f3cc3: live canary independently identified the same stale-root physical-rebase shape and adds explicit empty/no-unique-change PR refusal plus already-main patch-equivalence/drop acceptance. Canonical bd-35e822 remains the sole P0 under MSM0; do not implement separately.

## Post-reproduction provider repair

Later provider topology was manually repaired without closing the bug:

- PR2079/root was force-updated to `570e26ea`, parented on release main `d9fad17e`; root squash auto-merge is armed.
- PR2080/child was updated to `829e768b`, parent `570e26ea`, containing only the intended timeout commit/diff.
- The absorbed `ac701198` release delta is no longer present in the live child diff.

This repairs the live unsafe topology but does not erase the reproduced Cara defect. Preserve the original force-push/label event history, exact old heads/trees, zero-record `cara log` result, and regression requirements above. The fix must prevent the initial stale-tail absorption and provide durable operation receipts; a later manual topology correction is not proof of correct join behavior.

## Subsequent root movement clarification

A later read after the initial repair observed PR2079 head advanced again from `570e26ea` to `889dfe2779c72f39306ce5e43a364d17c424bb4a`, a merge commit `Merge branch 'main' into fix-slackiq-nodes` with parents `570e26ea` and `6764c4c2`. PR2080 remains at intended-only commit `829e768b`, parent `570e26ea`, while its provider base branch now resolves to PR2079 head `889dfe27`. This later movement does not change the original defect or evidence; it further demonstrates why join/apply receipts must bind exact root/tail/base heads and fail or explicitly resync on drift rather than relying on branch names.

## Descendant invalidation gap after root movement

Canonical `caco agent merge-queue list` / Cara projection later reported `healthy=true` with both candidates fresh after the root branch moved:

- PR2079/root head `889dfe27` is a merge of prior repaired root `570e26ea` plus current main `6764c4c2`.
- PR2080/child remains head `829e768b`, parent/provider-base OID `570e26ea`; its synthetic merge still records parents `[570e26ea, 829e768b]`.
- `compare 889dfe27...829e768b` is diverged; the child is behind the live root by two commits and their merge base is historical root `570e26ea`.
- Despite that branch-name/base-OID mismatch, projection marks PR2080 `stale_base=false`, `stale_head=false`, and a merge candidate.

Acceptance must enforce descendant invalidation/cascade: whenever a caravan root or intermediate member advances, Cara must transactionally cascade/rebase every descendant to the new exact parent, or mark the caravan invalid/paused before any merge candidate can proceed. Status and merge-queue projection must compare each child's recorded provider base OID with the live parent branch head and must never report healthy/fresh/mergeable from a historical base OID after that branch moved. Add fixtures for root force-update and root merge-update with an unchanged child, including drift between discovery and apply.

## Root-advance false-healthy evidence (2026-07-22)

After the repaired root PR #2079 advanced again to `889dfe27`, child PR #2080 remained based on prior root `570e26ea` with head `829e768b`. Read-only ancestry comparison reports diverged and child two commits behind root, while released Cara's canonical projection still reports `healthy=true`.

Acceptance must therefore cover root advancement after enrollment: descendants must be transactionally rebased/cascaded with durable receipts, or canonical status must fail closed with exact root/child ancestry evidence. A diverged descendant must never remain false-healthy. PRs were left untouched and PR #2078 remains held.

## Eventual descendant-cascade recovery receipt

Provider topology was subsequently corrected again:

- PR2080 head `77199f2597` now targets live root/base OID `889dfe2779`.
- `compare 889dfe2779...77199f2597` reports ahead 1, behind 0.
- The child contains only the intended `fix cara timeoutes` commit, parented directly on `889dfe2779`.

This is the desired eventual descendant-cascade topology and repairs the later false-healthy historical-base state. Preserve it as a recovery receipt, not evidence that the original join was safe: the initial stale-tail release absorption, provider mutations without a journal record, and intermediate projection that reported a historical-base child fresh/healthy all remain the reproduced defects. Regression acceptance must prove this exact cascade occurs transactionally or the caravan is marked invalid before status/merge eligibility.

Additional live topology failure 2026-07-21: root PR2079 merged as fe68beb5 at 23:41:52Z. Descendant PR2080 remains OPEN, base branch fix-slackiq-nodes at merged root head889dfe27, label caravan, auto-merge absent. It was not retargeted/promoted to main as new root and now blocks new normal joins. Ordinary PR2082 published_unjoined immediately afterward with provider_mutated_by_cara=false. Acceptance addition: root merge must transactionally promote/retarget the first child to current main, preserve ancestry, enable head auto-merge, update membership/journal/status, and leave later joins unblocked; crash/reconcile must repair this exact partial state.

## Root-merge promotion receipt and missing head intent

After PR2079 merged as `fe68beb5` at 2026-07-21T23:41:52Z, Cara eventually promoted/retargeted PR2080 correctly:

- base is `main` at exact OID `fe68beb5`;
- head is `2fbe7597`, one intended commit directly parented on `fe68beb5`;
- the prior stale root-branch base is gone;
- PR2080 still carries the `caravan` label, but `autoMergeRequest=null` and provider merge state is `BLOCKED`.

Thus root-merge descendant promotion eventually cascaded ancestry correctly, but failed to establish the promoted member's new head intent. Acceptance: promotion/reconcile/sync must atomically retarget/rebase the descendant, verify its exact intended patch/tree, promote it to caravan head, and arm configured squash auto-merge in the same receipt-bound operation. A promoted head with caravan membership but no auto-merge must be classified invalid/actionable, never healthy or complete. Add idempotent recovery fixtures for provider success after partial retarget, partial rebase, label-only state, and missing auto-merge, with drift refusal and rollback/audit receipts.

## Immediate terminal-state clarification

An independent provider read immediately after the promotion snapshot observed PR2080 already `MERGED`, not still open/blocked: head `2fbe7597`, base `main`, intended-only commit/diff, with post-merge `autoMergeRequest=null` and merge-state `UNKNOWN`. Therefore the earlier open `BLOCKED`/null-auto-merge observation was a real intermediate partial state that subsequently converged to merge. Preserve its timestamped receipt as a transient atomicity/reconciliation gap; do not describe it as the current terminal state. Acceptance remains: Cara must either arm head intent atomically during promotion or explicitly classify and reconcile the partial state with durable receipts, so an observer never treats the intermediate caravan-label/null-auto-merge state as healthy or terminal.

Post-land duplicate audit correction: initial 36a491b covers stale-root and source-range provenance but not the merged duplicate requirement where an equivalent patch already exists on current main under a different commit OID. Reopened canonically to add stable patch/content subtraction before final closure.

Live follow-up regression: plain/new root admission without an explicit --pr can enter source-provenance preflight with status.current_pr=None and current_branch=main, producing misleading join_empty_source_noop against main. title: Accept a backtick-quoted Beads declaration and name the exact PRs in fleet problem rows
description:
`parse_beads` rejects a backtick-quoted `Beads:` declaration that `metadata_value` would accept, so one quoted body invalidates its whole generation. Because the resulting problem is repository-wide and the human-readable renderer drops `problem.prs`, that single body prints an identical `InvalidGenerationMetadata` row on every unrelated candidate's `cara check`, which reads as fleet-wide breakage.

## Exact mechanism

`parse_generation_fact` resolves the five `Cacophony-*` trailers through `metadata_value`, which unquotes a backtick-wrapped value. `parse_beads` does not unquote its tokens, so it filters on a raw `` `bd-74b155` `` that cannot `strip_prefix("bd-")`. The bead set comes back empty, `missing.push("Beads")` fires, and the generation is invalid even though every other field parsed exactly.

Cacophony PR #2215 is a hand-authored recovery body that quotes its bead list to match the surrounding `Agent:`/`Branch:` prose:

    Beads: `bd-74b155`

Every other open generation body publishes the plain form and parses correctly.

## Why it read as fleet-wide

`read.rs` pushes generation findings onto `fleet.problems`, which is repository-scoped. `cara check --pr <any>` therefore prints #2215's row regardless of which candidate was asked about. The three human-readable renderers in `main.rs` formatted only `{kind}: {message}` and dropped `problem.prs`, so nothing on screen attributed the row to #2215. The JSON envelope was always correct (`.data.problems[].prs == [2215]`).

Three independent Cacophony agents concluded from that output that every generation PR was failing metadata parsing, and a P1 blocker was filed against the wrong side of the contract. Verified by reproduction: `cara check --pr 2233 --json` returns `prs: [2215]` while the text row names no PR at all.

## Fix

1. `parse_beads` unquotes each token before validating it, so plain, per-token-quoted, and whole-list-quoted declarations all resolve to the same ids. Already-open plain bodies are unaffected; a declaration naming no well-formed bead is still incomplete.
2. All three `main.rs` problem renderers share one helper that names the exact PRs, so a repository-wide row can no longer read as a defect in the candidate the operator asked about.

Filed from Cacophony bd-e4dbcb, where the symptom was first reported. No PR body was mutated, and no generation was retargeted, merged, or replaced.

title: Resolve Git repository root before config discovery and init
description:
Operator reproduction: invoking Cara from a nested directory inside a Git repository reports the repository as uninitialized and then attempts to create `.caravan/` in that nested working directory. Cara currently binds `AppContext.repository_path` and the default `.caravan/config.yaml` to ambient cwd instead of the canonical worktree root.

Resolve the exact repository/worktree root before default config discovery and every Git/GitHub/domain operation (for example, a bounded `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` contract). Default `.caravan/config.yaml`, common Git metadata, operation locks, repairs, status cache identity, dashboard repository IDs, and init writes must consistently use that root. Explicit `--config PATH` remains explicit: define whether relative overrides resolve from invocation cwd or canonical root, preserve the documented contract, and reject symlink/path escape where existing safety requires it.

Acceptance:
- From root and multiple nested subdirectories, `cara status`, `init`, `sync`, navigation, lock, log, web/action context, and JSON/MCP resolve one identical repository/config identity.
- Nested `cara init` creates only `<root>/.caravan/config.yaml`, never `<cwd>/.caravan`.
- Outside Git returns a typed repository-not-found/config continuation and writes nothing.
- Linked worktrees resolve their own worktree root while shared common-Git state remains common where intended.
- Bare repository, symlinked cwd/config, relative and absolute explicit config overrides, `-C`/environment edge cases, and paths containing spaces are covered.
- Root discovery is bounded, noninteractive, secret-free, and occurs before mutation.
- Focused fixtures, CLI/JSON/MCP parity, strict Clippy/fmt, full configured tests, docs/help.

title: Only web can target a repository the caller is not standing in
description:
Every command except `web` resolved its repository from the invocation directory, so answering a question about a repository required standing in it.

That is a working constraint rather than a preference. An operator or agent watching one checkout could not read another without changing directory, and it directly limited useful work: a read-only watch was pinned to a single path even when the interesting state lived in a different worktree. The operator hit this while comparing `~/cacophony` against `~/.cacophony/caravan-worktrees/cacophony`, which are the same repository seen through different working trees with different HEADs.

THE CAPABILITY ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS REACHABLE FROM ONE SUBCOMMAND. `cara web` takes `--repo`. `AppContext::load_from_directory(directory, config)` was already implemented and already used; it was simply private, and `load()` wrapped it with `std::env::current_dir()`. So the general form was written, tested by every existing caller, and exposed nowhere.

Adds `--repo <PATH>` as a global argument alongside `--json` and `--config`, and routes `load_context` through `load_from_directory` when it is present. Absent, behaviour is exactly as before: infer from the working directory.

Verified from an unrelated working directory:

    cd /tmp
    cara --repo ~/cacophony status
      CARAVAN  harryaskham/cacophony @ main  healthy
      auto-admission=true heuristic=priority_fifo_greedy_v1 candidates=8 duration=3600s

WHY GLOBAL RATHER THAN PER-COMMAND: the repository is context for the whole invocation, not a parameter of one verb, which is the same reason `--config` is global. Adding it per-subcommand would have needed it on roughly twenty commands and would have made the omission on any one of them a silent inconsistency.

SCOPE NOTE: this changes where policy is READ from, so `--repo` also determines which `.caravan/config.yaml` applies unless `--config` overrides it. That is the intended behaviour and matches `load_from_directory`'s existing contract, but it is worth stating because a stale worktree's config has already caused a multi-hour misdiagnosis on this fleet.

title: Fix racy lease test fake that unsoundly proved mutual exclusion
description:
The local test fake proving cross-host mutual exclusion is itself racy, so the exclusion proof is unsound and CI is flaky. This blocked the v0.0.71 release: `remote_lease::tests::two_concurrent_hosts_never_both_acquire` failed in the pinned CI shell with 2 successful acquisitions instead of 1, while passing locally.

Root cause: `FakeCas::acquire` performs check-then-act across two separate critical sections. It locks state to read any existing live grant, drops the guard, and then calls `replacement()`, which re-locks to insert the new grant. Two threads can both observe no live holder in the gap and both succeed.

This is a defect in test infrastructure, not in production behavior: real exclusion is delegated to the external broker's atomic compare-and-swap, and `CommandRemoteWriterLease` never implements CAS locally. But the fake is the primary local evidence for the core safety property of remote fencing, so an unsound fake means the property was never actually proven by that test, and releases can fail at random.

Fix: make `FakeCas` acquisition atomic by performing the liveness check and the grant replacement in one critical section, matching the atomicity a real CAS backend guarantees. Keep fencing tokens monotonic per key and preserve existing typed contention and takeover semantics.

Strengthen the test so a regression is caught reliably rather than by timing luck: run many repeated rounds with several concurrent hosts against a fresh backend each round, and assert exactly one winner every round plus strictly monotonic fencing tokens across rounds.

Default path must remain zero-probe/zero-write.

## Landed at 2c4e5c6, released as v0.0.78

The reviewed native Stack path is executable behind explicit per-repository opt-in:

- Native virtual mode now permits checkout-free and automatic joins with `rebase_on_join: false`; ordinary membership converges singleton/create/add representation, and evict/split run durable native rebuild.
- Help, README, SPEC, design, App setup, and provider validation evidence now describe explicit opt-in execution rather than preview.

Focused integration coverage includes: no-ready-prefix sync waits before lock and writes no checkpoint; pre-submit crash becomes indeterminate without provider access; durable checkpoint survives process boundaries/removes idempotently; all 826 library tests and full just validate green. Default-path parity remains enforced.
