title: cara sync --all NO-OPS on empty caravan - cron must call ADMISSION verb new/join then sync - checkout-free via --pr - admission ONLY when caravans=0
description:
Continuation of bd-f8cf99, which is at the ~8000-char description cap (cacophony/bd-48d9c1) and can no longer accept appends. This analysis was lost FOUR times to that cap before being filed here.

## First live evidence from the operator 10-minute ticker (ms-mac, 2026-07-28)

Operator ran: while true; do cara sync --all; sleep 600; done

Observed candidate order and states:

    pos 1  #2216  DIRTY     <- the actual head
    pos 2  #2223  BLOCKED
    pos 3  #2227  BLOCKED
    pos 4  #2234  DIRTY
    pos 5  #2245  DIRTY
    pos 6  #2254  CLEAN
    pos 7  #2255  CLEAN

Cara processes IN ORDER, so the only two MERGEABLE candidates sat sixth and seventh behind five unmergeable members. The ticker faithfully re-confirmed every ten minutes that the head could not move, and landed NOTHING.

Confirmation: last merge PR2251 at 19:20:56Z, main head unchanged at 923c05cfb7 from 21:26:41Z, board byte-identical before and after the loop started.

## Design consequence: more frequent sync CANNOT fix this

DIRTY is a merge conflict and no amount of syncing resolves a conflict. The queue was never starved of sync passes; it was starved of REPAIR.

That makes the repair-agent HOOKS the load-bearing half of the cron target, not the timer. The correct trigger is not "time has passed" but "the head of the queue is unmergeable", and the correct hook action is to repair or evict THAT SPECIFIC MEMBER.

Requirements this adds:

- detect HEAD-OF-LINE STALL specifically, distinguishing "nothing to do" from "cannot proceed past member N"
- report WHICH member blocks and WHY; DIRTY and BLOCKED need different remedies (conflict repair vs check failure)
- escalate after N identical no-progress passes rather than re-confirming forever
- offer EVICTION as a remedy, not only repair, which ties directly to the clean-unwind-on-eviction scope on bd-f8cf99

## Second-order lesson: QUEUE ORDER, not notice order

The tempting first move was PR2245: the only member with a repair already built and unpushed, and itself the bd-c04d9b fix that removes the cancelled-producer stall mechanism. But repairing position 5 changes nothing while position 1 is DIRTY.

Any repair-hook implementation must select work by QUEUE POSITION, not by which member is cheapest or most attractive to fix. A hook that greedily fixes the easiest DIRTY member would burn effort without ever moving the head.

## No receipts makes failure indistinguishable from success

Router could see the queue was not moving but could not tell whether the loop had died, was failing every pass, or was succeeding-but-blocked. Process inspection found no cara sync process at all and still could not discriminate. The correct diagnosis came from reasoning about ORDERING, not from any signal the loop emitted.

Concrete argument for per-pass receipts: a bare loop makes total failure and quiet success look identical from outside.

## Head disposition note

PR2216 (bd-b5d189) measured ahead 2, behind 43-44 against main 923c05cfb7, carrying only two own commits across SPEC.md and three hot caco crate files. That is neither a stale base nor a one-file collision; rebase, RECREATE or evict are all plausible and it is a bigger decision than the others. Escalated to the operator as the sole critical path.

## SUPERSEDING FINDING: the head-of-line analysis above was WRONG. The real cause was the VERB.

Recorded here rather than replacing the text above, because the earlier analysis is honest evidence of how the failure looked from outside and is worth preserving as such. But do not design from it.

### What actually happened

The operator loop ran `cara sync --all` every ten minutes for three and a half hours and moved nothing, while reporting healthy.

Cara reported: `caravans: []`, `unqueued: [2216, 2223, 2227, 2234, 2245, 2254, 2255, 2257, 2258, 2259]`, `merge_candidates: []`, `problems: 0`, `healthy: true`.

From cara 0.0.13 help, verbatim:

    sync   "Idempotently synchronize one or all caravans until a decision point"
    --all  "Synchronize every caravan rather than only the current branch's caravan"

With zero caravans there is nothing to iterate. `sync --all` synchronized an EMPTY SET and correctly reported success.

### Membership verbs are separate and were never invoked

    new      "Create a one-PR caravan from the current branch"
    join     "Append the current PR after a caravan tail"
    renew    "Reevaluate an evicted PR as a new caravan"
    rejoin   "Reevaluate and append an evicted PR after a caravan tail"

`sync` ADVANCES. It cannot CREATE. A timer calling only `sync` can never start a queue.

### THE REQUIREMENT THIS ADDS TO THE CRON DESIGN

**The cron must invoke an ADMISSION verb, not bare `sync`.** Otherwise it reproduces exactly this failure: a loop that runs forever, reports healthy, emits no problems, and accomplishes nothing.

Specifically the cron must:

- detect `caravans == 0` with `unqueued > 0` as a distinct state requiring ADMISSION, not synchronization
- invoke the admission verb (`new` for the FIFO head, then `join` for successors) under whatever authority the design grants it
- treat "synchronized successfully, zero caravans, N unqueued" as an ALERT condition, not a healthy tick

### Why no receipts made this cost hours

Four agents watched the stall. None could tell whether the loop had died, was failing, or was succeeding-but-empty, because every observable signal said healthy. The correct diagnosis came from reading the binary HELP TEXT, not from any signal the system emitted.

A per-pass receipt naming the verb invoked, the caravan count before and after, and the unqueued count would have made this obvious on the first tick.

### Admission itself was never broken

`cara next-candidate --json` returned status=success with generation_integrity confirmed for 2216, 2223, 2227, 2234 and 2245, FIFO-ordered by immutable provider `created_at`, 2216 first at 2026-07-26T18:41:20Z. Cara knew exactly who to admit and refused nobody.

Full detail on cacophony/bd-1764a1.

## THE DURABLE CRON SHAPE IS AVAILABLE TODAY - no Cara change required

Found by helsinki:unknown:harry, verified independently by the router against cara 0.0.13 `--help` on ms-mac.

### The obvious objection, and why it is unfounded

Admission LOOKS checkout-bound: `new` says "from the current branch", `join` says "the current PR". A central cron has neither.

But both verbs support CHECKOUT-FREE admission by exact PR number. Verbatim from the binary:

    cara new  --pr <PR>        "Exact remote candidate PR for checkout-free root admission"
    cara join --pr <PR>        "Exact remote candidate PR. Required for checkout-free atomic integration"
    cara join --tail-pr <PR>   "Exact tail PR to use as the proposed merge target"
    cara join --head-pr <PR>   "Caravan head PR; resolve its current tail immediately before mutation"
    both:     --reason <TEXT>  "Human/agent admission rationale; otherwise a deterministic mechanical reason is used"
    new:      --priority-label "Exact configured agent-priority label. Without it, admission is FIFO"

### The three-step shape a cron can perform with no checkout

1. read `cara next-candidate --json` for the canonical FIFO head
2. if `caravans == 0`: `cara new --pr <head> --reason <automated admission receipt>`
   else: `cara join --pr <candidate> --head-pr <current head> --reason ...`
3. `cara sync --all` to advance

No working tree, no current branch, no PATH guessing once `runtime_bin` is pinned. Each step returns a structured envelope, which is exactly the hook surface needed to trigger a repair agent at a decision point.

### REQUIREMENT for whoever implements

`--reason` MUST carry the automated actor identity and the tick number, so an admission receipt is distinguishable from a human one after the fact. Membership is currently reserved by the Cara holds; if the cron and an operator both admit, the audit trail must be able to tell them apart. Without that, receipts cannot answer "who admitted this".

Note `--head-pr` explicitly "resolve its current tail immediately before mutation", which is the re-derive-at-moment-of-action discipline already built into the verb. Use it rather than caching a tail.

### Also confirmed

`--priority-label` exists if ordering ever needs to be explicit rather than FIFO. Not needed today; `next-candidate` already returns a correct FIFO order by immutable provider `created_at` with PR-number tie-break.

## RESOLVED: the loop was never running. Joining is AUTOMATIC and needs no admission verb.

Two findings that together collapse this bead. Both established 2026-07-28 ~03:47Z.

### 1. JOINING WAS NEVER AN AGENT ACTION

caco-ctrl established this against their own earlier position, from `.caravan/config.yaml` at main 923c05cf:

    line  5   rebase_on_join: true
    line 14   sync.actions.join_unlabelled_prs: TRUE
    line 30   join_failed hook -> ./scripts/cara-hook

**Cara joins unlabelled PRs BY ITSELF during sync.** No `cara new`, no `cara join`, no membership verb, no hold to lift.

So the extensive reasoning on this bead and elsewhere about admission verbs, membership holds, and who is authorized to admit was reasoning about a lane THAT DOES NOT GATE JOINING. The canary never needed `caco agent complete` either.

### 2. THE OPERATOR SYNC LOOP WAS NOT RUNNING AT ALL

Router checked `pgrep -f "cara sync"` and `ps aux` at 00:41, 02:00 and 04:46 — three times across four hours. NEVER PRESENT.

The `while true; do cara sync --all; sleep 600; done` announced at 00:51 produced ZERO ticks, not twenty. A bare shell loop dies with its terminal.

### The version hypothesis was tested and REFUTED

caco-ctrl hypothesised the loop might resolve a cara below the 0.0.12 config floor and die at 0s per tick, matching the three dark Linux nodes. Router tested from BOTH the agent shell and a stripped login shell approximating the operator PATH:

    command -v cara  -> /Users/harryaskham/.cargo/bin/cara
    cara --version   -> cara 0.0.13        (parses this config)

PATH order puts /usr/local/bin, /System/Cryptexes/App/usr/bin, /usr/bin, /bin first — none contain cara — and `~/.cargo/bin` precedes `~/.nix-profile/bin`.

**ms-mac is NOT a fourth dark node.** The binary was always correct.

### The join_failed hook avenue is empty

No ticks ran, so no join was ever attempted, so the hook never fired and has nothing recorded.

## THE ENTIRE REMEDY

Restart the sync loop under something that survives terminal close — launchd, tmux, nohup. Joins should begin on the first tick with no further action.

No membership decision. No hold lifted. No admission verb. No queue defect.

## What this bead should now carry forward

The DURABLE requirement is unchanged and is now better evidenced: a bare `while` loop is not a supervision strategy. The cron design needs process supervision AND per-pass receipts, because four agents spent hours unable to distinguish "loop running and refusing" from "loop absent" — and the answer was the second.

title: A skip label with no receipt reports as recoverable when it is permanent
description:
`cara status` reports a `caravan-join-skipped` label as:

    generation-bound automatic admission skip; sync revalidates exact evidence before retrying

That promise holds only when Cara wrote the label AND a matching receipt exists. When the label is present with NO receipt, `bd-239640` correctly refuses to remove it, because an absent receipt cannot be distinguished from a deliberate operator hold. The candidate is then excluded PERMANENTLY and nothing revalidates anything.

Both states render identically, and the rendered text asserts the recoverable one.

MEASURED COST, on this fleet, by me. I reported #2245, #2259 and #2314 as correctly skipped in roughly thirty consecutive watch cycles across twelve hours. All three carried the label with zero receipts. I read "sync revalidates exact evidence before retrying" and concluded they would self-release. They could not. #2245 was later recovered by a manual label removal and immediately re-evaluated as genuinely incompatible, which confirms the mechanism. #2259 and #2314 are still stuck as of this filing.

The anomaly was STABLE, and stability read as correctness: a skip that never releases across thirty cycles looks exactly like a permanently incompatible pull request being correctly held.

`bd-8b1160` fixed the CAUSE by writing the receipt before the label, so no new orphans form. It does nothing for orphans that already exist, and nothing about the reporting.

TWO FIXES, DIFFERENT COSTS.

Cheap and unconditional: stop asserting the recoverable outcome. State what this read actually knows, which is that a skip label is present, and that Cara removes it only when it can prove it wrote it. Zero additional provider calls.

Expensive and exact: detect the orphan directly. The receipt lives in PR comments, which the status snapshot does NOT carry; `sync` fetches them per-PR via `pull_request_comment_bodies`. Detecting orphans in `status` therefore costs one REST call per skipped candidate. That is bounded and small in practice, typically zero to three, but `status` already exceeded its 60s deadline twice tonight, so it is not free and should be a deliberate decision rather than a drive-by.

This bead does the cheap half. The exact half is worth doing where the comments are already in hand, which is `sync`, and that path can name an orphan precisely rather than hedging.

description:

title: The stale-policy guard is a single-variant check on a growing enum
description:
`is_stale_policy` is the guard that refuses a tick whose policy came from a stale checkout. It landed today against a P0 where a sync worktree sat 95 commits behind main and every config value, including the queue's own duration budget, came from a three-day-old commit.

It was written as a single-variant comparison:

    self.relation == ConfigRelation::DiffersFromDefaultBranch
        && self.behind_default_branch.is_some_and(|behind| behind > 0)

`ConfigRelation` has five variants. A `==` answers only for the variant it names and silently answers false for every variant added later. The variant someone is most likely to add is one describing a NEW parked shape, a detached head or a checkout on an unrelated PR branch, which is precisely the condition this guard exists to catch. It would compile, pass every existing test, and not fire.

`is_branch_local_proposal` on the same struct has the identical shape.

WHY THIS IS WORTH CHANGING RATHER THAN LEAVING: I made this exact mistake earlier today. `is_historical` was written as `matches!(self, Self::DissolvedMember)` on a seventeen-variant enum, one change after citing the lesson that an exhaustive match is what forces a decision. The distinguishing question is not whether the author was careful; it is whether the compiler asks when someone adds a variant. Here it does not.

Both are now exhaustive matches, so a new `ConfigRelation` cannot be added without deciding whether it is stale policy and whether it is a branch-local proposal.

AUDIT SCOPE, so this is not mistaken for a sweep: I checked every `matches!(self` in the non-test sources and applied one test, does the same impl block contain an exhaustive match that would force an author to visit this code. `AdmissionSelection`, `CiGateDecision` and `HeadMergeActor` all do, so their `matches!` are adequately guarded and are deliberately left alone. `OrderedRowDisposition` and `AdmissionOrderOutcome` do not, and are noted below rather than changed, because neither currently gates a decision the way this one does.

NOT CHANGED, AND FLAGGED AS A QUESTION FOR THE OWNER: `ConfigRelation::Unknown` is documented as "never treated as agreement", but `is_stale_policy` returns false for it, so a tick PROCEEDS when provenance could not be determined. That may well be deliberate, since refusing would wedge any environment where the default branch is not resolvable locally, such as a shallow clone. I have not touched it because fail-open here is a policy choice rather than an oversight, and the person who wrote the guard should decide.

title: Bind caravan-force intent to the exact head generation
description:
Architecture review found one important force-generation gap for deterministic join/sync.

Existing protections are good: membership join removes caravan-force rather than adding/carrying it as a control label; force executes only for a non-successful explicitly labelled head; graph/compatibility and physical-rebase preflight happen first; force re-verifies exact default OID, open/non-draft state, label presence, ADMIN, durable audit comment, non-head auto-merge disable, and exact provider precondition. Routine pr_cara_join must expose no force input and its receipt should prove force absent/removed.

Gap: with rebase_on_join=true, sync physically rewrites a head, rediscovers it, and then evaluates CI in the same tick. An old caravan-force label survives the head-SHA rewrite. Checks on the new generation are initially empty, so the old label can immediately force-merge the newly rewritten generation even if operator intent was attached to the prior SHA. The existing passing-with-stale-force test does not cover this rewrite transition. This weakens stale-head/operator-only semantics.

Required contract: bind force intent to an exact observed head generation (durable comment/marker or equivalent). Any Cara-owned head rewrite must consume/remove or invalidate pre-rewrite force intent; force after rewrite requires a fresh operator action on the new SHA. Add tests for forced-old-generation + physical rebuild + empty checks, stale force label during pr_cara_join, and explicit re-application on the new generation. Keep force absent from healthy sync/join receipts except an explicit invalidation/removal step.

Implementation landed true main at 35c08e6 (reintegration attempt r3jo86y5v9h80nf2-20260719T101948.863Z-26c489eb). Sync removes/audits old-generation caravan-force only after the complete global physical write barrier; membership now prepare_candidate first, then invalidates/audits stale force, then apply_prepared, so planning conflicts consume no intent. Already-satisfied exact generations preserve intent; rewritten generations require a fresh label. Composed with atomic join 780ac5d JoinReceipt. Focused atomic join/force/reapplication tests and strict all-target Clippy passed; prior full suite passed before the one-commit atomic-join rebase. Lifecycle finalization is blocked only by Caco invoking a nonexistent claude-plugin before_complete hook for this Pi worker despite refresh/reload; controller repair requested. Do not manually close; retry caco agent complete after hook resolution.

title: A caravan whose sole member is closed dissolves silently
description:
Cacophony CARAVAN #2287 ceased to exist and NOTHING reported it. Its sole member was closed at 11:13 after being republished as a new generation under a new branch. The operator found it by noticing that no open pull request in the repository carried the `caravan` label any more.

WHY IT WAS SILENT: `graph.rs` derives membership from pull requests that are OPEN + `caravan`, or MERGED + `caravan`. `PullRequestState::Closed` is not handled anywhere in that file, so a closed member is not reported as anything; it is simply absent.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. I built a three-member caravan and closed the MIDDLE member against the real analyzer:

    caravans: 2       #1 members=[1]   #3 members=[3]
    problems:         DanglingBase prs=[3]   AutoMergeInvariant prs=[3]
    healthy:          false

So the multi-member case was ALREADY safe: the chain splits, the orphaned tail dangles, the fleet stops, and no queued work is lost or silently merged. The operator expected this case to be the worse one. It is the better one, and the difference is structural rather than a matter of degree: a sole member leaves NOTHING BEHIND to dangle, so there is no orphan to notice the absence.

THE FIX, and it is small because the evidence survives the close: PR2287 is CLOSED and STILL CARRIES the `caravan` label. Cara had everything it needed and never looked. A closed-unmerged pull request carrying the label is now a `DissolvedMember` problem naming the pull request, classified fleet-blocking, and mapped to `InvalidGraph` so a tick stops rather than proceeding as though the caravan had never existed.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: making membership FOLLOW a generation. The successor's patch may no longer be chain-compatible, and admitting it on the strength of a name match would put unproven work into a chain. bd-523dbf already built the owner-declared supersession marker binding a canonical PR to an exact head; what is missing is a CONSUMER in membership, which is a larger design question than this defect.

The regression test asserts BOTH shapes and was verified load-bearing: with detection disabled it fails with `left: []  right: [2287]`, reproducing the exact silence. Testing only the multi-member shape would have passed throughout, because that shape was never broken.

title: fleet.history reports zero merged caravans because labels were stripped
description:
`fleet.history` reports `merged_members_observed: 0` on a repository where 24 caravans merged between 18 and 30 July.

Measured, with the mechanism verified rather than inferred:

    cara status  history: merged=0  latest=(empty)     was 24, earliest 2026-07-18, latest 2026-07-30
                 dissolved: []                          was [2200] [2228] [2287]

    gh pr list --state merged --label caravan   returns 24 rows from a STALE label index
    each returned row's labels array            NONE
    rows actually carrying the label            0

Cara is not wrong here. It counts members with `has_label("caravan")` against fresh per-record data and answers honestly. What changed is the underlying evidence: an operator removed `caravan` labels from closed and merged pull requests as an urgent workaround for the null-rollup discovery crash (bd-54222d / bd-4e0430), and GitHub's label-filtered query still lists the pull requests while each record now reports no labels.

WHY THIS MATTERS. `fleet.history` exists BECAUSE of a specific failure: `caravans: []` was read as "no caravan has ever formed on this repository", by several agents across several days, and by me for roughly twenty consecutive watch reports. History was added so the fleet could prove it had worked before. That proof lives entirely in labels on merged pull requests, so an unrelated operational decision erases it, and the field silently returns to reporting zero — which is exactly the reading that caused the original confusion.

The same dependency applies to dissolution detection. bd-461c8b works precisely because a CLOSED pull request retains the label. Strip it and a caravan does not merely dissolve, it leaves no trace it ever existed; #2287, #2228 and #2200 were reported all evening and are now invisible.

THE WORKAROUND WAS NOT WRONG. The queue was down, the crash was live, and stripping labels was a reasonable fast mitigation. The real fix is on main and supersedes it.

THE DECISION SOMEBODY MUST MAKE, and it is an operator call rather than a code change:

  1. Once the pin advances past 90d3080 and discovery survives a null rollup, labels no longer
     need removing. Restoring them on MERGED pull requests restores the historical evidence.
     Closed ones are a judgement, since the label is what makes a dissolution visible.
  2. If labels are going to stay stripped, then `fleet.history` measures something erasable by
     an unrelated operational action and nothing says so. That belongs in the profile, so the
     next reader does not conclude from `merged=0` that the queue has never worked.

Filed as a bead rather than a message because `caco msg send` has been backpressured through four retries over roughly fifteen minutes.

title: Add optional cumulative rebase mode for physically chained caravans
description:
Operator-directed design/implementation lane. Add strict repository config `rebase_on_join: false` (safe default). When true, Caravan represents a chain both in GitHub PR bases and in Git ancestry so head A is based on exact default, joining B contains only B's patch rebased onto exact A, joining C is rebased onto exact B, and CI on each member validates cumulative A, A+B, A+B+C content.

This mode is explicit history rewriting, not the current virtual compatibility-only contract. Implement with isolated temporary worktrees, exact remote OID fetches, no caller-worktree mutation, full conflict simulation before the first provider write, same-repository/owned-branch and push-permission preflight, and exact `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<old-oid>`. Rediscover after every push/base mutation and return old/new head OIDs plus provider receipts. Never force a branch that moved or whose patch range is ambiguous/nonlinear unless a documented safe merge-preserving strategy exists.

Membership: `new` rebases the candidate-only series onto the exact current default; `join`/`rejoin` rebase candidate-only commits from its exact old base/merge-base onto the selected parent before setting the GitHub base. Sync must detect parent OID movement and cascade child-only rebases head→tail under exact leases. Eviction of B from A→B→C must preflight and perform `C --onto A B` (and cascade later descendants) so B content is actually dropped; falling back to the old base while retaining B's patch is not a successful eviction. Split at B must transplant B-only commits onto main and cascade descendants. Any conflict or ambiguous range is a typed resumable decision with zero speculative push.

Preserve current `rebase_on_join=false` behavior and SPEC compatibility. Add interruption/replay, stale lease, merge commit, signed commit, parent update, cascading descendants, evict middle/head/tail, split, conflict, and partial provider failure tests. Live-prove using clearly named disposable PRs on harryaskham/caravan only; do not use Cacophony fixtures. Verify CI trees are cumulative and attach exact tree/OID receipts.

Important limitation to document/test: because current heads squash-merge, retargeting B after A lands can still change GitHub merge-ref/check identity and trigger provider CI even when cumulative tree content is already proven. This mode improves semantic cumulative testing but must not claim instant no-rerun landing until an ancestry-preserving merge mode or audited exact-tree/check receipt policy is implemented.

CI trigger requirement discovered on live Cacophony chain: PR #1991 targets main and has CI; rebased child #1972 targets #1991's `agent/...` branch and has no checks because `.github/workflows/ci.yml` filters `pull_request.branches: [main]`. Rebase mode must preflight/report a compatible workflow trigger contract: CI pull_request must include all possible caravan parent base branches (e.g. remove the main-only filter or include `agent/**`/configured head patterns), and include the `edited` action because changing a PR base emits an edited event; current explicit types omit it. Ensure the post-rebase/base-update event runs on the correct cumulative merge ref. Add fixtures proving A(main), B(agent/A), C(agent/B) each receive the required check. For cumulative semantic proof, use an unfiltered dedicated Caravan stack check/full suite rather than path-skipping required checks. Fail closed with actionable config evidence when required CI cannot trigger on a non-main parent.

CI integration requirement discovered from live Cacophony chain #1991→#1972: GitHub Actions `pull_request.branches` filters the PR base. Repositories whose validation workflows trigger only for `main` will not run CI on downstream members based on another PR branch, so rebase_on_join cannot deliver cumulative validation by itself. Preflight/status must detect absent downstream expected checks and return a typed repository-policy decision with guidance. Documentation/acceptance must require validation workflows to trigger all Caravan base branches (or configured branch patterns) while deployment/release remains main-only. Live Caravan proof must confirm each downstream PR receives its required CI. Checks from a non-main merge ref still do not transfer after retarget/squash; retain the existing limitation.

CI trigger requirement discovered on live Cacophony chain: PR #1991 targets main and has CI; rebased child #1972 targets #1991's `agent/...` branch and has no checks because `.github/workflows/ci.yml` filters `pull_request.branches: [main]`. Rebase mode must preflight/report a compatible workflow trigger contract: CI pull_request must include all possible caravan parent base branches (e.g. remove the main-only filter or include `agent/**`/configured head patterns), and include the `edited` action because changing a PR base emits an edited event; current explicit types omit it. Ensure the post-rebase/base-update event runs on the correct cumulative merge ref. Add fixtures proving A(main), B(agent/A), C(agent/B) each receive the required check. For cumulative semantic proof, use an unfiltered dedicated Caravan stack check/full suite rather than path-skipping required checks. Fail closed with actionable config evidence when required CI cannot trigger on a non-main parent.

Operator-selected CI setup: GitHub Actions cannot filter `on.pull_request.branches` by PR label; that field matches the base branch. Recommended label-gated contract is an unfiltered `pull_request` trigger with types including opened/synchronize/reopened/edited/labeled/unlabeled, then job-level `if` running the stack/full check when base is main OR the PR has the `caravan` label. Thus ordinary main PRs and labelled non-main caravan children run, while unrelated non-main PR jobs skip. Rebase mode must inspect workflow/config and emit a clear project-configuration warning/error (`rebase_ci_trigger_missing`) with remediation when non-main parent bases cannot produce the configured stack check. `cara init/status/check` should surface readiness; sync must not treat an empty child check set as evidence CI passed.

Operator CI contract clarification: GitHub cannot event-filter by PR label and branches have no Caravan tag. Supported pattern is pull_request with no branches filter and types including opened,synchronize,reopened,ready_for_review,edited,labeled,unlabeled; job-level heavy-suite condition checks pull_request label caravan. Labeled covers enrollment and edited covers base retarget. Prefer an always-reported lightweight check plus conditional full suite so missing/skipped evidence is deterministic. Add strict config for expected Caravan check names and a bounded grace period; status/sync must warn/fail closed with code/evidence when an active downstream member has no expected exact-head check/workflow run, without constraining branch names.

title: Make the App git child fixture independent of parallel auth environment
description:
Regression in v0.0.67 validation reported while bd-67b62b ran the full suite: command::tests::app_git_transport_uses_broker_without_argv_secret fails intermittently only in parallel all-test execution, while direct and nix-develop exact runs pass. Preserve only unrelated platform runtime environment needed to launch the test binary; do not use a broad env_clear that breaks Nix/macOS dynamic library discovery.

Add assertions or a second poisoned-parent regression proving conflicting ambient auth/Git values cannot affect the child and never appear in output. Run the exact test repeatedly and `just validate` before publication.

ROOT CAUSE CORRECTION

Sanitized failure evidence showed the recursive child fixture's nested fake git/broker subprocesses timing out at the production five-second auth probe under a saturated parallel suite. This was not a demonstrated credential-selection race. The fix therefore removes nested auth/Git execution from the recursive child: the child now proves only deterministic environment scrubbing, while the existing non-recursive real `git credential fill` test continues to prove helper/token transport. title: Refresh physical-rebase lease after external default advance
description:
Live Cacophony v0.0.5 drain blocker from caco-dev-msm-2. In a clean isolated clone after merged PR2040/PR2042 and successful cara init, sole member #1958 has provider base e1f87cd while true main is 172de05. `cara status --json` records previous_default_oid=172de05 and compatibility clean, but consecutive `cara sync --all --json` attempts both fail `rebase_stale_lease` expected=e1f87cd actual=172de05. The typed continuation says rediscover/rerun, but rediscovery reconstructs the same stale lease, making recovery impossible.

Fix sync/physical-rebase planning so an external default-branch advance is incorporated into the fresh plan/lease after provider rediscovery. The first call may return a retry-tick stale precondition if the default moved during planning; the next exact tick must use current main, rebuild the head and descendants under exact force-with-lease, and then require fresh CI. Never weaken apply-time lease checks or force overwrite a concurrently moved PR branch.

Add a fixture matching status default advance followed by two sync ticks: old candidate/base evidence on tick one, fresh default on tick two, successful exact plan/apply, no repeated stale lease. Cover default moving again between plan/apply, completed-prefix recovery, and scheduler wake_class=retry_tick without LLM wake. Live acceptance is wrapper-sanitized status/sync on Cacophony #1958 after PR2040/2042.

This blocks Cacophony queue drain and corrected v0.0.5 publication. Also route the companion wrapper's stale v0.0.4 pin separately; do not use temporary unreviewed pins as release authority.

title: Head creation requires native auto-merge even when cara owns the merge
description:
Live operator report on cacophony, running the correctly nested `sync.head_merge_actor: caravan`:

    cara auto_merge_not_enabled: repository settings must allow squash
    auto-merge before creating a caravan head

    "next": "enable GitHub repository auto-merge and keep squash merge
             enabled, then rerun the same command"

The config was right; the gate was wrong. `src/sync.rs` already conditions its `auto_merge_not_enabled` precondition on the merge actor — the check sits in the `else` branch and only runs when the provider merges. `src/membership/policy.rs::preflight_repository` did not: it required `repository_allows_auto_merge` for every non-join operation regardless of actor.

So a repository that deliberately disabled provider-native auto-merge because cara owns the merge could still sync, but could never create a caravan head. The remediation text made it worse by naming only the repository setting, steering the operator toward re-enabling a native auto-merge that the single-merge-actor work exists to remove — and re-arming it is exactly what the standing directive forbids while that work is open.

Fix: gate the precondition on the actor and say so in the error. `preflight_repository` now takes `head_merge_caravan` from `status.head_merge.actor.caravan()` at all three call sites, and the `next` offers both routes, matching the sync path.

Native auto-merge is a precondition only when the provider performs the merge. When cara merges the green head itself, requiring a repository setting it will never use blocks the caravan for no reason.

title: One statusCheckRollup null from a closed PR aborts cara discovery entirely and stops the queue; removing the label does not help because the filtered query is stale
description:
A single `statusCheckRollup: null` in a provider response aborts cara's entire discovery phase, so one closed PR stops the whole merge queue. It is reproducible, it is happening right now, and the obvious workaround does not work.

THE FAILURE, reproduced repeatedly on helsinki with cara 0.0.51:

    cara github_discovery_failed: `gh pr list --repo harryaskham/cacophony --state closed
      --label caravan --limit 100 --json number,title,body,state,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,
      headRefName,headRefOid,headRepository,...`
      detail  invalid type: null, expected a sequence at line 1 column 1293
      next    inspect the separate stdout/stderr excerpts, repair malformed provider
              stdout, and retry

THE CAUSE, isolated by querying the same endpoint directly:

    closed caravan PRs: 28
    with NULL statusCheckRollup: [2308]

`#2308` is CLOSED. GitHub returns `statusCheckRollup: null` for it rather than `[]`. cara deserializes that field as a sequence, hits null, and fails the ENTIRE discovery - not just that record.

WHAT THIS COSTS: discovery is the first phase of `cara sync --all`. When it fails, nothing downstream runs. No admission, no chain planning, no merges. One closed PR in a 28-record response stops the queue completely.

Before the failure moved to discovery, a run got as far as:

    .. initial_discovery: discovered 4 caravan(s), 11 unqueued PR(s) in 49546ms
    .. physical_rebase_planning: planned 4 chain(s);
       admitted prefix [PrNumber(2300), PrNumber(2308), PrNumber(2311), ...]

So the queue is otherwise working - it forms caravans, plans chains and admits a prefix. It is being stopped by one null field.

THE OBVIOUS WORKAROUND DOES NOT WORK. An agent removed the `caravan` label from #2308 at 22:31:58, correctly reasoning that an unlabelled PR would drop out of the query. Verified state now:

    #2308 state=CLOSED labels=(none)
    events: 15:54:11 labeled caravan / 22:31:58 unlabeled caravan

And yet `gh pr list --state closed --label caravan` STILL RETURNS #2308, an hour and a half later, still with a null rollup. The label filter is serving stale results. So the fix was right and ineffective, and cara keeps choking on a PR that no longer qualifies.

That matters for the fix design: cara cannot rely on callers curating labels to keep its
queries clean, because label changes are not immediately reflected in the filtered query.

WHAT SHOULD CHANGE:

  1. TREAT A NULL SEQUENCE AS EMPTY. `#[serde(default)]` on the field, or deserialize as
     `Option<Vec<_>>` and map None to empty. A closed PR having no check rollup is a normal
     provider response, not malformed data.
  2. DO NOT FAIL THE WHOLE PHASE FOR ONE BAD RECORD. Skip the record, name it, and continue.
     A 28-record response should not be all-or-nothing. The current error even says "repair
     malformed provider stdout", which frames GitHub's normal output as corruption and
     sends the reader to fix the wrong thing - I spent twenty minutes on that.
  3. NAME THE OFFENDING RECORD. The error gives a byte column. It could give the PR number.
     I had to fetch the same query myself and diff it to find #2308.

RELATED: this is the same shape as caravan:bd-35a9fd, where a journal record type the
reader did not recognise also aborted the whole sync rather than being skipped with a
warning. Two instances of the same design choice - a single unparseable element failing an
entire batch - both currently stopping the queue.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:harryaskham

title: Reserve post-rebase provider budget before membership branch mutation
description:
Live Cacophony cara new on branch fix-slackiq-nodes created PR #2079 and successfully force-with-lease rewrote exact head 98b89de→c059bf1 onto main 80bf4ea, then attempted mandatory `gh pr view 2079` with only 212ms left in the shared operation deadline. It returned github_mutation_timeout after remote branch mutation. Receipts were correct/resumable (rebase receipt present, membership provider receipts empty), and rerun can continue, but Cara should not begin an irreversible branch rewrite without enough bounded budget for mandatory post-rewrite rediscovery and membership writes.

Before apply_prepared/provider mutation, reserve/prove a minimum remaining phase budget for post-rewrite status/candidate refetch, exact head/base verification, labels/base/auto-merge/comment operations, and final receipt. If insufficient, fail before branch mutation with typed membership_operation_budget_insufficient, required/remaining ms, zero-write evidence, and config guidance. Preserve one absolute operation deadline; do not silently extend it. Interrupted/indeterminate provider phases remain resumable from GitHub state.

Acceptance:
- Fixture consumes budget during discovery/preflight until below reserve: no branch/provider write and exact next action.
- Successful rewrite leaves enough budget and completes membership.
- Crash/timeout after an externally completed rewrite still resumes idempotently on the same PR/head without duplicate PR/rewrite.
- Already-satisfied rebase path uses a smaller accurate reserve and can resume the live #2079 generation.
- Cover New/Renew and Join/Rejoin, slow provider refetch, command_timeout > operation duration, and exact completed-prefix receipts.
- Human/JSON/MCP docs explain rerun safety and budget tuning.

title: cara status exhausts max operation budget and makes canonical queue adapter unavailable
description:
## Live regression

On Helsinki with Cara 0.0.82, the canonical read-only status path recurrently fails:

```text
operation deadline exhausted before this phase: 0ms remained, below the 750ms minimum any command can use;
raise sync.max_duration_secs or lower sync.max_candidates_per_tick so a tick completes within its budget
```

A previous observation failed with 558ms remaining. The repository config already pins:

```yaml
command_timeout_secs: 60
sync:
  max_candidates_per_tick: 8
  max_mutations_per_tick: 64
  max_github_requests_per_tick: 256
  max_duration_secs: 3600  # max permitted
```

Raising max duration is impossible/clamped. This is distinct from closed `bd-10303b` (`membership_post_rewrite_budget_insufficient` before an irreversible rewrite): the failing command is `cara status`, a read-only analysis surface. It should never need a mutation/post-rewrite reserve, and it currently causes Caco's canonical Cara adapter to report unavailable while direct invocations intermittently succeed.

## Impact

- Grid/PTTY P0 `cacophony:bd-0f8d3d` remains blocked because canonical queue status is unavailable.
- Hook repair workers and controllers cannot prove queue health/ownership even though provider/Cara operations may be healthy.
- The five-minute sync cron may emit only a generic budget error instead of hook decisions.
- Operators are tempted to lower candidate count or add a second loop, neither of which fixes a read-only status contract.

## Required

1. Trace the budget owner/phase for `cara status`; distinguish provider-discovery budget, command timeout and sync mutation deadline.
2. `status` must use a read-appropriate bounded budget and return a complete or explicitly partial typed snapshot; it must not reserve mutation/post-rewrite time.
3. If provider enumeration cannot finish, preserve last-good/partial sections with a typed `status_partial` receipt naming exhausted phase and cursor, rather than making the entire canonical adapter unavailable.
4. Bound per-provider calls and expose elapsed/remaining budget plus provider request counts.
5. Add deterministic fixtures with >8 candidates, slow provider responses and near-deadline phases. Prove status remains useful and never suggests raising an already-maxed duration.
6. Preserve `sync --all` mutation fail-safes; do not weaken post-rewrite reserve semantics.
7. Validate Caco's canonical Cara adapter and the blocked grid worker can consume the corrected status.

P0 because queue automation, hook response and operator recovery all depend on this read surface; repeated status unavailability is currently freezing otherwise mechanical work.

Implemented on f9c61df. CLI `cara status` now owns a dedicated 35s read budget with a 2s completion reserve; child calls remain bounded by command_timeout_secs and the path never reads sync.max_duration_secs, mutation capacity, or post-rewrite reserves. Complete statuses atomically persist an 8MiB/24h/config-fenced secret-free snapshot under Git common metadata. A later timeout returns status=success with the flattened last-good status marked healthy=false plus typed status_partial evidence: exhausted phase, last-good cursor/age, elapsed/deadline/remaining ms, and current attempt GitHub request telemetry. This shape preserves repository/data fields consumed by Caco canonical_queue and therefore projects degraded rather than unavailable. With no valid last-good, status_partial_unavailable has read-only guidance and never suggests raising maxed sync duration/lowering candidate count. Human CLI prints partial evidence while exiting success. Mutating status_with_deadline/sync paths are unchanged and cannot consume partial status. Fixtures cover independent read-vs-3600s sync budget, >8 candidate last-good under slow provider timeout, Caco-adapter JSON fields, request counts, config fencing, size/age bounds, and no mutation-bound guidance. Focused tests, cargo fmt, git diff check, and clippy --lib --bin cara -D warnings passed.

Commit amended to cb2e39d to pin the exact outer Caco canonical adapter envelope (`status=success`, `data.repository`, `data.healthy=false`, `data.status_partial`, attempt request counts) in the >8-candidate slow-provider fixture. All prior validation remains green.

title: cara init creates an untracked config that makes sync refuse its own worktree
description:
## Cacophony canary

Sanitized packaged Cara (`cltv-run caravan#cara`, version 0.0.1, store binary `/nix/store/04rswfnfk55a8rpcims63c82zay8v2aq-caravan-0.0.1/bin/cara`) ran from the clean managed Cacophony checkout.

Read-only status correctly reported `repository_not_initialized` for mutations despite all three labels matching. `cara init` then succeeded and returned:

```json
{"ready":true,"config":{"path":".caravan/config.yaml","state":"created"},"labels":[{"name":"caravan","state":"already_present"},{"name":"caravan-evicted","state":"already_present"},{"name":"caravan-force","state":"already_present"}]}
```

The immediately following `cara sync --all` failed before any provider mutation:

```json
{"code":"head_conflict","details":{"checkout":{"error":{"code":"dirty_worktree","details":{"status":"?? .caravan/\n"},"message":"refusing to switch branches because the worktree has tracked or untracked changes"}}}}
```

Cara's own init-created config therefore makes the same repository ineligible for sync's required decision checkout. This deadlocks the documented init→sync recovery path unless the operator manually relocates/ignores the file.

Acceptance:
- `cara init` must place local operational config where its own dirty-worktree guard ignores it safely, or create/verify a reviewed repository-local ignore contract without hiding unrelated files.
- A successful init followed immediately by status/check/sync in an otherwise clean worktree must not fail `dirty_worktree` because of the exact init-owned file.
- Never weaken the dirty-worktree guard for arbitrary `.caravan/` content; recognize only the exact validated config path/inode or use an external state path.
- Add fixtures for newly created config, pre-existing correct config, tracked config, unrelated untracked file beside config, symlink/path escape, alternate `--config` outside the worktree, and branch checkout cleanup.
- Preserve idempotent repository-label/resource receipts and ensure no provider mutation occurs before checkout safety passes.

title: A null check rollup on a closed PR takes down every read
description:
`cara status` against cacophony failed outright, twice in a row:

    github_discovery_failed
    `gh pr list --repo harryaskham/cacophony --state closed --label caravan --limit 100 ...`
    invalid type: null, expected a sequence at line 1 column 1293

GitHub returns an explicit `"statusCheckRollup": null` for a pull request that never ran checks. `PullRequestJson::status_check_rollup` is a `Vec<CheckJson>` with `#[serde(default)]`, which supplies a default for a MISSING field and does nothing for an explicit null, so deserialization fails and the WHOLE discovery fails with it.

THIS IS A DEFECT I INTRODUCED. Before bd-61024a wired dissolution detection to real discovery, closed pull requests were never fetched, so a null rollup could not appear. The first closed caravan member with no checks broke every read of the fleet. Measured on the live data: of 28 closed labelled pull requests, exactly one had a null rollup, PR2308 — closed, unmerged, and therefore precisely the dissolved member the feature exists to report. The feature was disabled by the first instance of the thing it detects.

SEVERITY IS THE PART WORTH NOTING. It does not degrade the new capability, it takes down `cara status` entirely: no caravans, no candidates, no admission state, no problems. It is intermittent in the worst way, appearing only once such a pull request enters the window, which is exactly when someone is most likely to be looking.

The fix deserializes an absent-or-null list as an empty list. A provider that distinguishes "no checks" as `null` rather than `[]` is not malformed, and refusing it should not cost every read-only surface at once.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, because I nearly dismissed it: the first failure looked like the transient provider errors seen all evening. I ran the exact command by hand three times, got clean 174KB responses each time, and could easily have concluded "transient, moves on". What distinguished it was a SECOND consecutive failure from cara while the manual command kept succeeding — the same command working outside the tool and failing inside it is not a network problem. The error detail carried the answer verbatim, `invalid type: null, expected a sequence`, and reading it rather than the error CODE is what located the field.

RELATED, AND NOT FIXED HERE: `labels` is the same `#[serde(default)] Vec<..>` shape and would fail identically on a null. It is not changed because no observed payload has a null there, and I would rather fix what is evidenced than sweep speculatively; the helper is in place if it is ever seen.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: Stop a conflicting unqueued candidate from wedging every sync tick
description:
Live P0 observed on Cacophony 2026-07-29: `cara sync --all` aborted every tick with

    cara invalid_graph: leading admission candidate does not merge cleanly into the current default branch

against a fleet with ZERO caravans and four unqueued PRs (#2227, #2245, #2259, #2275), with `CandidateIncompatible` recorded for #2245 and #2259. Nothing could ever be admitted: the queue was wedged by pull requests that were never in it.

Root cause: bd-fd9b11 correctly introduced the candidate-scoped `GraphProblemKind::CandidateIncompatible` in `graph.rs`, but every downstream gate still treated ANY graph problem as fleet-blocking:

- `sync::validate_rebase_preflight_graph`
- `sync::validate_graph`
- `force::validate` (`force_graph_invalid`)
- `force_intent` unrelated-problem gate
- `GraphAnalysis::healthy()`

None of them excused the new kind, so it fell through `decision_for_problem` to `_ => DecisionKind::InvalidGraph` and aborted the whole tick.

Fix: `GraphProblemKind::candidate_scoped()` and `GraphProblem::blocks_fleet_operations()` make the invariant explicit and apply it at every member-scoped gate. A conflicting unadmitted candidate stays fully reported (admission still names it, and head-of-line receipts still explain it) but can never block a member operation or a tick.

This is the same invariant as bd-be8b44 (ineligible is not blocking), extended to the problem kind added afterwards.

title: Reserve a realistic proportional physical sync budget
description: Live P0 on caravan 2210 with six members: cara sync refuses BEFORE any mutation with physical_sync_budget_insufficient, required 3840000ms, remaining 3455426ms, 32 command slots. Config is max_duration_secs 3600 and command_timeout_secs 120, so the reservation is the fixed worst case 32 * 120s = 3840000ms, which exceeds the entire run budget and scales worse with每 additional member. The consequence is that even a planned cheap base-retarget plus auto-merge arm cannot execute at all. Required: reserve a realistic proportional budget from the actual planned command set rather than a fixed worst-case slot count, or allow already-planned bounded provider repairs to proceed under the remaining budget. A shortfall must degrade to a per-caravan diagnostic that still lets independent caravans converge, never a whole-run refusal. Add regression coverage for a six-plus member caravan under a constrained duration budget, and assert that planned cheap operations still execute. Note: canonical is currently healthy only because the PR2210 owner manually applied base main and armed squash; that is NOT scheduler proof.

title: A tail stranded by a dissolved member is fleet-fatal with no route back
description:
bd-461c8b now reports a caravan member closed without merging, which covers the single-member case: the caravan is gone and the queue says so. Its own comment names what it does not cover — *"where a tail survived it dangles and the fleet stops"*. This bead is that remainder, and it is the expensive half.

## What happens today when a MIDDLE member is superseded

Two cases, both fleet-fatal rather than chain-local.

**Successor opens while the old member is still OPEN.** `generation.rs:459` emits `SupersededGeneration`, `read.rs:1009` maps it to `GraphProblemKind::SupersededGeneration`, and `model.rs` classifies that `blocks_fleet() == true`. `validate_graph` returns `decision_error`, so *every* caravan and all admission stop — not just the affected chain.

**Old member CLOSED (what PR #2287 did).** A closed PR is not a member (`is_active_caravan_member` requires `Open`) and is not in `merged_by_head` (requires `Merged`). Its children resolve their base to nothing and get `DanglingBase`. That is fleet-blocking, and the only escape hatch, `recoverable_dangling_problem` (`sync.rs`), requires `predecessor.state == Merged`:

    predecessor.state == PullRequestState::Merged
        && predecessor.has_label("caravan")
        && child.base.name == predecessor.head.name
        && matching_predecessors == 1

A closed-not-merged predecessor can never satisfy that. So the tail is stranded on a branch belonging to nothing, the tick aborts, and **there is no route back in code** — no `--cascade` equivalent, no rejoin path, nothing.

The single-member case that dissolved the first Cacophony caravan was the mild one: no children to strand.

## Done in this bead

Naming. A child stranded by a departed member now says which member it lost and why, instead of reporting an anonymous `targets non-member branch`, which is indistinguishable from a PR pointed at a branch that was never in a caravan. Regression test asserts the departed member appears in `problem.prs` and the message; a second test pins that an unrelated base stays anonymous. Verified the test fails with the production lookup reverted and the test kept.

## Decision still required, and it is not mechanical

A stranded tail needs a route back. `recoverable_dangling_problem` cannot simply be widened to accept a closed predecessor, because the two cases differ in meaning:

- **merged predecessor** — its commits are on the default branch, so advancing the child's base to the default branch is a no-op on content.
- **closed, superseded predecessor** — its commits are *not* landed, but they are still in the child's branch history because the child was stacked on it. Advancing the child's base to the default branch silently enlarges the child's diff to include the superseded work.

So the choice is one of:

1. Advance the tail to the default branch and accept that it absorbs the superseded commits, refusing unless the successor is merged or the diff is unchanged.
2. Offer the tail as a rejoin candidate against the successor named by `GenerationFinding.canonical_pr`, requiring a rebase the owner performs.
3. Evict the tail with the existing tail-first `--cascade` ordering and report it, treating a dissolved predecessor as equivalent to an evicted one.

Whichever is chosen, the refusal must name the dissolved predecessor specifically rather than surfacing a generic dangling base — the naming above is the prerequisite for that, not the fix.

title: Release Cara 0.0.83 with read-only status-budget fix
creator: helsinki:caravan:helsinki-cacophony-caco-ctrl

title: Add repository-wide max_caravans capacity with default one
description:
## Operator direction

Caravan currently has a derived/per-chain member capacity, but no repository-wide cap on how many independent active caravans may exist. This allowed multiple one-root caravans to occupy queue/CI/merge attention concurrently. The operator is temporarily force-merging heads to drain the fleet and requires a durable typed cap.

## Required config

Add:

```yaml
sync:
  max_caravans: 1
```

- Typed integer, minimum 1.
- Default is 1 when omitted, including old config fixtures and generated defaults.
- This is independent from `max_candidates_per_tick`, mutation/request budgets and derived per-caravan member capacity.

## Counting semantics

- Count active, non-parked caravans only.
- `terminal_red.action: park` chains do not consume the cap.
- Invalid fragments, closed/merged history and candidates not yet admitted do not consume it.
- A paused but still active caravan should report explicitly whether it consumes capacity; prefer yes unless the pause contract already makes it outside active scheduling.

## Behavior

1. When active count is below cap, normal deterministic priority/FIFO admission may create at most enough new roots to reach the cap.
2. When at cap, automatic sync must not create another independent caravan. It may still append compatible work to the one active caravan, converge/rebase/advance/merge existing chains, park terminal-red chains and perform non-root repair.
3. Existing repositories with active count above a newly lowered cap are preserved. Do not evict, merge, pause, relabel, rewrite or select a winner merely to enforce the cap. Stop new root creation and let existing chains drain naturally.
4. Explicit `cara new` must honor repository policy and return a typed `max_caravans_reached` refusal with current/cap/active IDs. It must not bypass the cap merely because a human named a PR. Join/rejoin to an existing caravan remains governed by compatibility and per-chain capacity.
5. A parked caravan becoming active again must revalidate capacity. If reactivation would exceed the cap, preserve it parked/paused with a typed decision instead of displacing another chain.
6. `status`, `plan sync`, web/MCP/text output and hook evidence expose cap, active count, capacity-consuming caravan IDs and first blocked root candidate.
7. Config parser/schema/docs/init examples include the field and default. Unknown/zero/negative/overflow values fail validation.

## Determinism and tests

- With no caravans and several eligible PRs, default config creates exactly one root using current priority/FIFO ordering.
- Once that root exists, later unrelated candidates cannot create another root; compatible candidates may join it.
- A terminal-red parked root frees capacity; next eligible candidate may create one new active caravan.
- Three pre-existing active caravans under cap=1 remain intact and converge, while no fourth root is admitted.
- Repeated ticks are idempotent and do not oscillate labels or capacity ownership.
- Explicit new/refusal, parked reactivation, status partial snapshots and mixed-version omitted-field behavior have deterministic fixtures.

## Rollout

No live config edit in this source bead. Land source, release Cara, then set the Cacophony repository explicitly to `max_caravans: 1` (matching the new default) and prove one active non-parked caravan while preserving parked chains.

P0 by operator direction: queue capacity must be repository-wide, not only per-chain, so mechanically independent PRs do not create an unbounded number of simultaneous caravans.
creator: helsinki:caravan:harry

title: cara new does not mention that a joinable caravan already exists
description:
Every caravan on the cacophony fleet is single-member, and the reason is invisible at the moment it is decided.

Measured from the control-label audit markers, which record the intent behind each transition:

    PR2300 new    PR2308 new    PR2295 new    PR2287 new
    PR2215 JOIN   (merged 2026-07-27, appended to an existing caravan by an automatic actor)

So `join` works and has run end to end here. What is happening now is that every caravan is created with `new`, which by definition makes a ONE-PR caravan, while five clean candidates sit in the queue behind an existing caravan nobody joins.

`cara new` says nothing about this. It creates a separate caravan and reports success, which is correct: sometimes a separate caravan is exactly what the caller wants. But the caller is not told that an alternative existed, so an automation hardcoded to `new` produces single-member caravans forever and the cost is invisible to whoever reads the output.

An operator spent a day trying to establish whether stacking worked. The answer was one query away in the audit markers, and would have been in front of them at creation time if `new` had mentioned it.

ADVISORY ONLY, DELIBERATELY. `new` continues to do exactly what it is asked. It now also reports the caravans that already exist, so a reader sees the choice that was made on their behalf. It does NOT refuse, warn, or recommend, because a separate caravan is legitimate and Cara cannot know the caller's intent. It also does NOT claim the candidate would join cleanly, since proving that needs a compatibility check this path has no reason to pay for; `cara check --pr X --head-pr Y` answers that question and is read-only.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: The classification totality guard omits the variant it exists to catch
description:
`every_kind_is_classified_exactly_once` exists to keep the problem classification total. It is the guard against the failure that has now recurred nine times here: a rule applied at one site and not its siblings. It was blind to the variant that caused today's P0.

TWO FAULTS, BOTH MINE, BOTH INTRODUCED WHILE FIXING THAT P0:

1. The variant list is HAND-MAINTAINED and `DissolvedMember` was never added. A totality guard that enumerates by hand is only total for what somebody remembered to type.

2. The assertion was `assert_ne!(blocks_fleet(), is_candidate_scoped())`, which partitions correctly ONLY while those are the only two categories. bd-61024a added a third, historical. `DissolvedMember` is false for both, so had it been in the list the old assertion would have FAILED, correctly, and forced the question. That is exactly what a guard is for, and it was silenced by omission rather than by argument.

Both together mean the guard could not have caught bd-226a07, where a historical problem gated no fleet but aborted every tick.

ALSO FIXED: `is_historical` was written as `matches!(self, Self::DissolvedMember)`. A `matches!` answers for the variants it names and silently answers false for every variant added later, which is the precise shape `blocks_fleet` is an exhaustive `match` to prevent. I wrote the anti-pattern into the classification whose whole purpose is to prevent it, one change after citing that lesson.

Now: `is_historical` is exhaustive, so a new variant cannot compile without a decision; the list includes `DissolvedMember`; and the assertion counts categories, requiring each kind to be in exactly one of fleet-blocking, candidate-scoped, or historical.

Verified load-bearing by mutation: reverting `is_historical` to a `matches!` naming the wrong variant fails with "Unknown must be exactly one of fleet-blocking, candidate-scoped, or historical".

The list remains hand-maintained, which I am recording rather than hiding. Rust offers no stable way to enumerate a variant set without a derive or macro, so the residual risk is that a future variant is added to the enum and not to this list. The exhaustive matches in `blocks_fleet` and `is_historical` do force a decision at the point of definition, so the list controls only whether the PARTITION is checked, not whether the classification is made.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: Create-PR membership rereads the pre-rewrite head and refuses its own exact push
description:
Live released `cara 0.0.79 new --create-pr` on the disposable bd-71e444 App canary returned `stale_remote_revision` AFTER its own exact physical branch push succeeded.

## Exact live sequence

Repository `harryaskham/caravan`, disposable branch `canary/bd-71e444-app-telemetry-v079-20260801`, PR #16.

- pre-operation provider head: `004616d5fe0ecabff510d60a11e1fc1b066312dd`
- current default: `1d2194abdd6bedbcf36350cb1c7ecb5a2fcd98f2`
- Cara App force-pushed rebuilt head: `f494a810fac2dc44f21f7160cd8341c1a530e768`
- rebuilt head's parent is exact default `1d2194a`; tree is expected
- GitHub timeline event at 2026-08-01T21:14:30Z attributes the force-push to `caravan-agentic-merge-queue[bot]`

The same command then exited 1:

```json
{
  "code": "stale_remote_revision",
  "message": "remote ref `refs/heads/canary/bd-71e444-app-telemetry-v079-20260801` moved since discovery",
  "details": {
    "expected_oid": "004616d5fe0ecabff510d60a11e1fc1b066312dd",
    "advertised_oid": "f494a810fac2dc44f21f7160cd8341c1a530e768",
    "resumable": true
  }
}
```

No membership label/comment had been written, so the failure was fail-closed, but an irreversible provider branch write had completed and the operation falsely classified its own exact result as an external/stale movement.

After fetching/resetting the disposable local branch to the advertised exact head and retrying `new --pr 16`, the same operation succeeded idempotently with `rebase_receipt.already_satisfied=true`, then completed membership. This proves the first refusal was not a foreign branch race.

## Likely boundary

The physical apply correctly performs the old-head lease push. Mandatory post-push rediscovery or a later compatibility/branch resolution appears to retain or reuse the pre-push candidate snapshot (possibly the warmed full-status/cache path used for `--create-pr`) and compares remote new head against expected old head. The path is sensitive: the earlier v0.0.78 PR #15 canary succeeded in one pass, while the v0.0.79 canary had recent status/check reads and reproduced the stale comparison.

## Required fix

After a successful exact physical push, every create-pr/new continuation must bypass/invalidate pre-push cached candidate facts and bind the candidate to `rebase_receipt.new_head_oid` before compatibility and membership writes. A real external move after the push must still refuse against the NEW expected head.

## Tests

- warm the relevant status/candidate cache on old head;
- run `new --create-pr` with `rebase_on_join=true` and an exact successful force-with-lease push;
- post-push rediscovery sees the new provider head and the operation returns success, not `stale_remote_revision`;
- external movement from the new head still refuses;
- branch write receipt/error remains resumable if any later provider mutation genuinely fails;
- no duplicate branch push or PR creation on exact retry.

The disposable PR was subsequently completed, evicted, closed, de-labelled and branch-deleted; default branch stayed exact.

Implementation completed on agent commit 7a98ffe. After every exact physical membership push, Cara now invalidates the polling status cache and uses a dedicated post-rewrite discovery path for all continuations, including new --create-pr whose original candidate selector is None. That path verifies the provider branch against rebase_receipt.new_head_oid, replaces only the lagging candidate head plus matching generation fact before compatibility analysis, and then leaves compatibility advertisement and membership mutation preconditions to verify the same new generation again. External movement from the new head still fails closed with the rebase receipt. Added a stale-provider-head binding fixture covering the created-PR shape and retained the existing external-head/default/membership race fixture. Focused validation passed: new binding test, operation-budget continuation test, external race test, cargo fmt, git diff check, and cargo clippy --lib -D warnings.
