title: Make graph problem classification compiler-enforced
description:
Follow-up to bd-299d3e, which closes the CLASS rather than the instance.

That bug was a consumer guard written as `problem.kind == GraphProblemKind::Incompatible` while the producer had moved to `CandidateIncompatible`. Nothing failed: the comparison simply never matched, the head-of-line skip silently stopped working, and every test stayed green. An equality comparison against an enum variant is invisible to the compiler when the enum grows or a producer changes which variant it emits.

Audited the whole enum for other dead guards by extracting produced vs consumed variants: none remaining. So this is prevention, not another live bug.

Fix: classify on `GraphProblemKind` with an EXHAUSTIVE match instead of comparing variants at each call site.

    GraphProblemKind::blocks_fleet()        - describes the fleet
    GraphProblemKind::is_candidate_scoped() - describes one unadmitted candidate

`healthy()`, the admission skip, and the `check` problem seeding all call these now.

VERIFIED THE GUARD ACTUALLY GUARDS: adding a hypothetical variant to the enum fails the build with

    error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: `GraphProblemKind::HypotheticalNewVariant` not covered

so a future variant cannot be introduced without somebody deciding whether it blocks the fleet. Also pinned by model.rs::every_kind_is_classified_exactly_once, which proves the two halves partition the enum, and an_unadmitted_candidate_conflict_never_blocks_the_fleet for the specific variant whose misclassification stopped every caravan from forming.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: DissolvedMember cannot fire: discovery never fetches closed PRs
description:
bd-461c8b added `GraphProblemKind::DissolvedMember` so that a caravan member closed without merging is reported instead of silently vanishing. It cannot fire. It is dead code on real data, and it is my own defect from earlier today.

MEASURED against the live fleet:

    PRs reaching `analyze`: 32     by state: {merged: 24, open: 8}
    closed PRs present: NONE       #2287 present: false
    reported problems: candidate_incompatible x2, no DissolvedMember

Discovery fetches exactly three sets: all open PRs, open labelled PRs, and recently MERGED labelled PRs. Closed-unmerged pull requests are never requested, so the detection's input never arrives.

THE FORGE HAS THE DATA. `gh pr list --state closed --label caravan` returns 20 rows, of which THREE are genuinely closed-unmerged: #2287, #2228, #2200. Three real dissolutions, none of them reported by Cara, and #2287 is the one an operator found by hand this morning by noticing no open pull request carried the label any more.

WHY I MISSED IT, because the mechanism matters more than the bug. I verified that "the evidence survives the close" by checking the FORGE: PR2287 is closed and still carries the `caravan` label. That was true, and it was the wrong thing to check. What needed verifying was whether Cara's DISCOVERY fetches it, which it does not. I checked the data source and not the pipeline, then wrote a test that constructed a closed pull request by hand, which passed precisely because the fixture supplied what the producer never does.

That is the eighth instance of this exact failure mode in this repository, and the first one I have introduced myself while actively cataloguing it: a consumer tested against inputs it constructs, where the producer supplies something else. My own note on it says the thing that catches it is verifying the mechanism IN SITU rather than in isolation. A single `cara status` against the live fleet, checking whether the new problem actually appeared for #2287, would have caught it in seconds. I never ran it, because the unit test passed.

THE FIX: fetch closed labelled pull requests alongside the existing merged-labelled query, bounded by the same limit, and keep only those that are genuinely unmerged so a merged PR is never double-counted as a dissolution.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: No test asserts that a tick never evicts a red member
description:
No test asserted that a sync tick never evicts a caravan member. The guarantee held, but only as an unrepeatable observation: I verified it by grepping `sync.rs` and `loop_runner.rs` for eviction calls and finding none.

WHY THAT WAS NOT GOOD ENOUGH. The claim is load-bearing OUTSIDE this repository. An operator set cancellation policy partly on the strength of my telling them, twice, that the queue does not evict on red. A grep is a point-in-time observation about the code as it was that afternoon; it does not survive somebody adding an eviction call tomorrow, and the person who adds it will have no reason to know a policy decision elsewhere depended on its absence.

Measured context: five pull requests went red and returned green untouched in a single session, none needing any change (#2292, #2284, #2285, #2295, #2287). Evict-on-red would have been wrong five times out of five. The single-member case is where it costs most, because eviction re-links the chain around the member and there is no chain left to re-link.

WHAT IS ASSERTED: a red member, a CANCELLED member, and a cancelled member under `--rerun-failed` each complete a tick with no eviction mutation, no `caravan-evicted` label, and the `caravan` label intact. The three are covered together because eviction could be introduced on any one of those paths independently, and a test covering only the red path would pass while the rerun path evicted.

VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING by mutation rather than by assertion: injecting an `add_label("caravan-evicted")` into the CI-failure path makes it fail with "red: the member must not be labelled evicted". The mutant was then removed and the full suite re-run.

This closes the gap between what I told an operator and what the code guarantees, which matters more than usual because they acted on it. It deliberately does NOT add an eviction-on-cancellation config knob, which was the other proposal: there is no auto-eviction path to switch off, so adding one to default it off would create the hazard rather than guard against it.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: A null sequence in provider JSON makes the whole repository undiscoverable
description:
A closed pull request carrying an explicit null in a sequence field makes the entire repository undiscoverable.

OBSERVED LIVE on cacophony, 2026-07-30:

    cara status
    -> github_discovery_failed
       gh pr list --repo harryaskham/cacophony --state closed --label caravan ...
       returned invalid JSON: invalid type: null, expected a sequence at line 1 column 1293

MEASURED CAUSE. Querying the same command directly shows GitHub emitting an explicit null rather than an empty array:

    #2308 null fields: mergedAt, statusCheckRollup
    #2287 null fields: mergedAt
    #2228 null fields: mergedAt
    #2200 null fields: mergedAt

PullRequestJson declared both labels and status_check_rollup with serde(default). That attribute covers an ABSENT field; it does not cover a field that is present and null. One closed pull request with no checks therefore took out every read of the repository.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE FIELD. The failing surface is the diagnostic surface. cara status is what an operator or agent runs to find out why the queue is unhappy, and it returned nothing at all. This is the same shape as bd-a4a7e9, where a mutating-path bound silenced every read.

FIX: a null_as_empty deserializer on both sequence fields. Empty is the faithful reading of a null rollup, and it stays fail-closed downstream because Cara never treats absent checks as success.

VERIFIED: with the fix, the same live repository reads cleanly again — three caravans, 24 merged members, six ordered candidates — where a moment earlier every read failed.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-1

title: Candidate snapshot reports a superseded base as fresh (stale_base=false on an outdated base.oid)
description:
Cara's merge-candidate snapshot records a base OID that has been superseded on the provider for over an hour, while simultaneously asserting the candidate is fresh and its base is not stale. The two fields contradict each other inside a single snapshot entry.

Observed on live Cacophony, captured in one pass with sources labelled:

- `cara status --json`, `data.merge_candidates` entry for PR `#2210`: `base.name=main`, `base.oid=1a09ceecefa7...`, and in the same entry `freshness=fresh`, `stale_base=false`, `stale_head=false`, `stale_reasons=[]`.
- True `main` at that moment was `9d6278a10f08a9ac1e4c3669aca2dceee572ed12`. `1a09ceecefa7` was superseded by the `release: v1.2.1575` commit at 03:30 UTC; the snapshot `observed_at` was `unix:1785128898`, roughly 05:08 UTC, so the base had been superseded for about 1h38m.
- PR `#2232` shows the same shape, `base.oid 1a09ceec` with `stale_base=false`. PR `#2233` was the only candidate recorded on current `main`.

Why this matters:

- `stale_base` is the field a planner or an operator would trust to decide whether a rebase is required. If it can report `false` against a demonstrably superseded base, then any decision keyed on it is unsound, including forward-progress and rebase-cost work.
- It is a self-inconsistency rather than mere staleness. A snapshot that is simply old would show an old base AND old freshness metadata. Here the base is old while the freshness assertion is affirmatively negative, so a consumer cannot detect the problem by comparing timestamps.
- It plausibly bears on `bd-e99fe6` (physical-sync budget deadlock), because projected rebase work and base drift are exactly what a planner would derive from these fields. Plausibly only: this is NOT asserted as the cause, and the budget formula `required_ms = command_slots x command_timeout_secs` is independently established.

Suggested acceptance:

1. `stale_base` must be true whenever the recorded `base.oid` is not the current provider tip of `base.name`, or the field must be renamed to describe what it actually measures.
2. Snapshot entries should carry the provider tip they were compared against, so a consumer can verify the freshness claim rather than trust it.
3. Add a regression test where the base advances between snapshot capture and read, asserting the freshness fields flip.

Related but distinct, and NOT a defect: the same capture showed `auto_merge.enabled=false` for `#2210` while live GitHub showed it armed. That one is ordinary snapshot staleness, since the arm was restored at 05:12:47Z and the snapshot predates it. Recorded here only so a future reader does not conflate the two.

Environment: Cara `0.0.10` as resolved on the helsinki runtime; `ad14f74` not deployed. Observed by the helsinki profile worker under a read-only watch, which explicitly declined to propose a mechanism; base and provider state verified independently by cluster control.
creator: helsinki:cacophony:helsinki-cacophony-cluster-ctrl

title: Consult the forge mergeability verdict before merging
description:
The forge's own mergeability verdict was never fetched or consulted anywhere in the source; the only occurrences of `mergeStateStatus` were in comments.

The operator's instruction was "BLOCKED alone should disqualify a row". Measured against live cacophony first, that turns out to be unsafe as stated:

    PR 2259  mergeable=CONFLICTING  mergeStateStatus=DIRTY
    PR 2276  mergeable=MERGEABLE    mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED   <- red
    PR 2279  mergeable=MERGEABLE    mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED   <- CLEAN, correctly elected
    PR 2245  mergeable=UNKNOWN      mergeStateStatus=UNKNOWN

2279 is BLOCKED too. GitHub returns BLOCKED whenever branch protection is not yet satisfied, which includes required checks that are merely still RUNNING. Gating admission on it would refuse every candidate whose CI has not finished and stall the queue completely — reinstating the exact wedge that was just fixed.

So the field is fetched and consulted at MERGE time only, which is where it is both safe and genuinely useful: by then required checks are already proven green, so a forge that still declines knows something Cara does not (an unsatisfied protection rule, a required review, a rule added since discovery). Attempting the merge anyway only burns an API call and produces a confusing provider error.

- New `RootMergeFailureCause::ForgeRefusesMerge`, refusing on BLOCKED, DIRTY or DRAFT immediately before the merge call.
- `merge_state_status` is `Option<String>`: absent means not fetched or the forge had not computed it (UNKNOWN), which is neither permission nor refusal, exactly like an absent CI conclusion.
- Pinned by a_blocked_forge_verdict_does_not_bar_admission, which asserts the placement rather than the mechanism, because the placement is the part that was nearly got wrong.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: Successful force merge leaves caravan-force on the merged PR
description:
v0.0.64 documents `caravan-force` as one-shot durable PR intent and explicitly says a successful merge consumes it. The first live force merge disproves that postcondition:

    PR #2331 state=MERGED merged_at=2026-07-31T19:19:11Z
    labels=[caravan, caravan-force]

Source confirms the cause. `force_merge_head` records the administrator squash receipt, emits ForceMergeCompleted, and promotes the child, but never performs a provider `remove_label`. Its local `before_labels.remove("caravan-force")` only constructs audit evidence; it does not mutate GitHub.

Required behavior:

- Reserve capacity for both administrator squash merge and force-label consumption before entering the irreversible merge.
- Do NOT remove force before the merge: a failed merge must retain durable intent.
- After successful merge, use the fresh merged PR snapshot from the merge receipt as the exact precondition and remove `caravan-force` from GitHub.
- Record the label-removal receipt before child promotion and completion events, so successful completion means intent is actually consumed.
- If label removal fails after merge, return a typed partial-mutation error proving the merge completed and naming only the residual label cleanup; never retry or duplicate the merge.
- Exact retry against an already merged PR must not attempt another merge. A repair/cleanup path may remove a residual historical force label idempotently.

Tests:

- Successful forced merge removes the label and records merge then remove-label order.
- Merge failure preserves the label.
- Label-removal failure reports merged=true/provider evidence and does not promote/merge again.
- Ordinary non-forced merges are unchanged.
- The live #2331 shape is represented as the regression.

title: Example hook aborts on SIGPIPE when a payload has many matching lines
description:
CORRECTED AFTER VERIFICATION. Not a live bug. Keeping this as a small hardening of a worked example, and as a record of the investigation.

The SIGPIPE mechanism is real in general. Reproduced standalone:

    set -euo pipefail
    v="$(sed -n 's/^\(x[0-9]*\)$/\1/p' "$1" | head -n 1)"

    two-line input    -> rc=0
    200k-line input   -> rc=141, value empty

But it is NOT reachable in this hook. Line 41 reads `PAYLOAD="$(head -c 65536)"`, so the input is bounded to 64KiB, and the substitution only shrinks each line to a short captured value. sed's total output therefore stays under the pipe buffer, so sed always finishes writing before head exits and is never signalled. Confirmed empirically: a 360,011-line payload through the UNPATCHED hook still exits 0.

So my earlier claim on this bead was overstated. I verified the mechanism in isolation and then asserted it applied here without testing the hook itself end to end. Testing it end to end is what disproved it.

Remaining justification for still changing it, which is weaker and should be judged on its own merits: this file is an EXAMPLE that operators copy into their own schedulers. `sed | head -n 1` under `set -euo pipefail` is only safe here because of the 64KiB bound several lines earlier. Anyone lifting the extraction into a hook without that bound inherits a latent abort. Replacing it with a pipeline-free `first_line` helper removes the footgun from the thing people copy.

Also recorded so it is not rediscovered: do NOT "fix" this with sed `T;q`. `T` is a GNU extension; BSD sed on macOS rejects it with "invalid command code T" and silently yields an empty field, which would disable wake-class routing on operator machines. Verified on macOS.

title: Sync leaves the worktree parked on a decision's PR with no record
description:
Operator observation 2026-07-30, confirmed from the helsinki reflog: the caravan sync worktree keeps ending up parked on a pull request branch and staying there.

    97e2023ff HEAD@{20:01}: checkout: moving from caravan-main to agent/ms-dev-3/...ex9vj4ie
    bfa8a3991 HEAD@{20:00}: reset: moving to origin/main

Read upward: the cron resets to origin/main, and then within a minute cara checks out a pull request branch to evaluate a decision and leaves the worktree there. Nothing was actively reverting the worktree; cara simply never returns it to its base.

CONFIRMED IN SOURCE: navigation::checkout_decision_snapshot performs checkout_exact on the decision's pull request and returns. There is no restore step anywhere on that path.

WHY THIS WAS DESTRUCTIVE BEFORE THE CRON RESET EXISTED: the worktree sat on whatever pull request cara last inspected, in one case 95 commits behind main for days, and every policy value was read from that old commit. That is bd-6f234e, now fixed by refusing a tick under provably stale policy.

WHAT LANDED FOR THIS BEAD: sync.checkout_on_decision, default true, which preserves the historical interactive behaviour of leaving the operator on the pull request that needs repairing. An unattended sync worktree sets it false, and the decision then carries an explicit skipped checkout receipt naming the pull request, so the between-runs state of the worktree is always explained rather than implied.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, and this is the decision worth recording: cara does not automatically restore the base branch after a decision checkout. Restoring unconditionally would silently remove the repair affordance that interactive users rely on, and would do so at exactly the moment a human is being handed a broken pull request. An explicit policy toggle keeps both behaviours available and makes the choice visible in configuration rather than hidden in a code path.

title: Caravan sync worktree parked on a dead agent's branch 95 commits behind main: stale config and compatibility computed against the wrong base
description:
The caravan sync worktree on helsinki was parked on a dead agent's abandoned PR branch, 95 commits behind main. Every compatibility decision the queue made was computed against a three-day-stale base, and every config value it read came from that old commit.

FOUND 2026-07-30 while investigating two symptoms the operator reported:

  1. "max_duration_secs IS 3600 in our caravan config" - but something was using a
     different value.
  2. "we have 2 caravans of 1 PR and yet our unjoined errors are about other PRs
     conflicting with MAIN, not with the TAILS of each."

THE STATE, measured on helsinki:

    cd ~/.cacophony/caravan-worktrees/cacophony
    branch:              agent/ms-dev-3/cacophony/ex9vj4iedmpf8g3y-pr-g97e2023ff1c7279f8590aa4a2118c97a45b7cfac
    head:                97e2023ff
    behind origin/main:  95 commits
    dirty:               0
    unpushed:            0
    stashes:             5

Note the branch owner: `ex9vj4iedmpf8g3y`. That is a DEAD AGENT - the same one that held bd-c04d9b (a P0 describing the CI cancellation defect) in_progress for three days until it was released during a stranded-claim audit earlier the same day. The caravan has been syncing from an abandoned checkout belonging to an agent that no longer exists.

THIS EXPLAINS BOTH SYMPTOMS AT ONCE:

  - STALE CONFIG. Any value read from the worktree - including max_duration_secs - comes
    from a commit 95 behind main. The operator's current config was never being read.
  - CONFLICTS AGAINST A STALE MAIN. Compatibility was being computed against a base three
    days old. PRs that are perfectly compatible with real main would read as conflicting.
    The operator's observation that errors referenced main rather than the caravan tails
    is the visible symptom of comparing against the wrong tree entirely.

The five stashes suggest prior manual intervention in this worktree that nobody recorded.

THE OPERATOR'S FIX: create a dedicated `caravan-sync-branch`, because `git checkout main` in that worktree fails with "fatal: 'main' is already used by worktree at /home/harry/.cacophony/daemon/checkouts/cacophony" - the daemon checkout holds main.

WHAT I WOULD ADD, and this is the part that prevents recurrence:

  A named branch fixes today. It does NOT stop the same drift happening again, because
  the drift happened precisely because nothing kept the worktree fresh. The sync should
  FETCH AND HARD-RESET to origin/main at the start of every run rather than assuming
  currency:

      git -C "$CARAVAN_SYNC_WORKTREE" fetch origin main
      git -C "$CARAVAN_SYNC_WORKTREE" reset --hard origin/main

  Since the worktree has no unpushed commits and exists only to compute compatibility,
  there is nothing to preserve. Detaching at origin/main would work equally well and has
  the advantage that it cannot silently become "a branch someone committed to".

  ALSO: something should notice. A sync worktree 95 commits behind is a condition the
  queue could detect and refuse, or at minimum report, rather than silently producing
  wrong compatibility answers for days. That is the same class as bd-9051fc - the
  information was locally available and nothing consulted it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR PAST DECISIONS: any caravan admission or rejection computed while this
worktree was stale is suspect. In particular, PRs rejected as "mechanically incompatible
with the exact current default branch" may have been compatible all along.

title: Joining a child onto a stale root absorbs already-main deltas into the child generation
description:
## Live reproduction

During the `pr_cara_join` canary, operator-created root PR #2079 (`fix-slackiq-nodes`, head `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`) remained based on stale main `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`. Live main later contained release v1.2.1562 as squash commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7` with parent `80bf4eac`.

The local branch used for child PR #2080 (`fix-cara-timeouts`) inherited the release source commit `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680`, whose parent is stale-root head `c059bf15`, then added intended timeout commit `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633`. Cara admitted #2080 after stale root #2079 without first converging the root onto current main. Provider state became:

- caravan: `2079 -> 2080`
- #2079 base: `main@80bf4eac` (stale)
- #2080 base: `fix-slackiq-nodes@c059bf15`
- #2080 displayed files include Cargo/CHANGELOG v1.2.1562 even though equivalent release patch is already on live main as `d9fad17e`.

The operator began from what appeared to be an empty `fix-cara-timeouts` branch and expected only the timeout edit. Cara's stale-root admission made the child look as though it invented/absorbed the release delta. This is unsafe/misleading canary topology; PR #2078 is being held until #2079/#2080 are resolved.

## Required behavior

Before appending a child, Cara must converge or refuse a caravan whose root base OID is not live default-branch OID. It must not construct a child generation on a stale root where an already-main patch is represented by a parallel squash/source commit.

## Acceptance

1. Reproduce with stale root `R` from main `M0`, live main `M1` containing squash-equivalent patch `S`, and child source ancestry `R -> S-source -> C`.
2. `join` either atomically advances/rebuilds the root to `M1` before calculating the child, or returns a typed stale-root decision with zero child/provider mutation.
3. After successful convergence, the child provider diff contains only `C`; the duplicate `S-source` patch is dropped as already satisfied.
4. Receipt records old/live main OIDs, root rewrite, duplicate/empty patch disposition, final child base/head/tree, and exact provider mutations.
5. Empty/no-unique-change branches are refused before PR creation/admission instead of allowing inherited predecessor commits to masquerade as the requested change.
6. Add a live/hermetic regression and ensure status/dashboard never describes the absorbed main delta as child-authored work.

title: Add best-effort queue optimisation and auto-admission to sync
description:
## Operator direction — 2026-07-20

Make repeated `cara sync --all` ticks reconcile the fleet and continuously adopt eligible unlabelled PRs, so one Cara loop/controller can eventually drain a long queue without external orchestration scripts.

## Configuration

Add a strict opt-in config surface such as:

```yaml
sync:
  actions:
    join_unlabelled_prs: true
```

Default remains false. Cacophony will opt in.

## Required algorithm

1. Reconcile and validate existing caravans first using normal idempotent sync. A real invalid graph, provider invariant, mechanical/semantic decision, or operator action stops the tick; do not hide it by admitting around it. Waiting CI, held, and healthy states remain structurally valid.
2. If no caravan exists, use the canonical priority/FIFO candidate to form one. Otherwise inspect candidates in configured-priority then immutable-FIFO order and caravans in existing deterministic caravan order.
3. For each candidate, try current tails deterministically. Join to the first exact tail for which candidate/tail and whole-fleet compatibility preflight succeeds. Use the landed atomic remote join receipt, rebase-on-join, and exact-lease contracts; rediscover after every mutation.
4. If no tail works, mark the exact candidate generation with `caravan-join-skipped` plus a durable reason/comment receipt, then consider later candidates in the same tick. This opt-in behavior is an explicit exception to current no-leapfrog automatic admission.
5. A skip must not block manual `new`/`join`/`rejoin`. Bind it to repository, candidate PR/head/base, tested tail generations, default generation, config fingerprint, heuristic version, compatibility reasons, actor, and time. Candidate head/base/config/tail/default/heuristic changes make evidence stale and eligible for automatic retry/removal; unchanged generations are not retried every tick.
6. Bound one tick by wall clock, GitHub API budget, and maximum mutations/candidates. Return exact joins/skips, remaining candidates, and continuation. Retry is idempotent.
7. Expose the heuristic version in status/sync receipts. It is deliberately evolvable; deterministic behavior is required for one version, not permanent optimisation semantics. `priority_fifo_greedy_v1` is sufficient and need not claim a global maximum.
8. `cara loop` and `cara loop --once` consume the same sync behavior. GitHub Actions normally run bounded `--once` ticks from PR/check/workflow/default-branch events plus a schedule, rather than one unbounded hosted job.

Cover empty fleet, one/many caravans, compatible/incompatible candidates, generation-bound skip invalidation, manual override, concurrent tail movement, candidate push, partial crash, API/mutation budget exhaustion, repeated drain, and no admission before existing-fleet convergence. Preserve exact provider rereads, operation lock, and complete audit receipts.

This is the sync-owned best-effort fleet optimiser. Do not add a separate top-level reconcile command unless needed for read-only planning.

title: Separate explicit membership authority from automatic FIFO admission

title: Cara sync outer timeout starves green caravan root merge
description:
## Live recurrence: green root never merged

Cacophony PR #2425 was admitted by Cara at 2026-08-04T09:58:24Z, labelled `caravan`, and emitted `caravan_created`. Its exact current CI generation became fully green at 10:42:35Z (`Check & Lint` and `Fast Tests (unit)` success). It remained open until the operator manually squash-merged it at 12:01:56Z.

Cacophony config deliberately uses:

```yaml
sync:
  head_merge_actor: caravan
  max_duration_secs: 3600
```

Therefore GitHub `autoMergeRequest=null` and repository `allow_auto_merge=false` are expected; Cara itself must perform the squash through `root_merge`. The admission audit text incorrectly said “squash auto-merge is enabled,” which describes the historical GitHub actor, not current Caravan-owned mode.

Fresh process/daemon evidence proves why the merge actor never ran:

```text
cara sync --all --json              running >300s
wchan                               hrtimer_nanosleep
daemon automation 'cara-sync': command timed out after 300s
```

The Caco automation wrapper kills the command at 300 seconds while Cara permits a 3600-second tick. The shell is terminated before its error branch can dump `SYNC_OUT`/`SYNC_ERR` or emit `sync_failed`, explaining the missing failure notification. Repeated ticks can therefore spend their full outer budget on analysis/provider convergence and die before root-merge evaluation. #2426 only joined at 11:24Z, 42 minutes after #2425 was green, so it was not the original blocker.

## Required

1. Bound/reorder `sync --all` so already-admitted exact-green caravan roots receive merge evaluation within the outer scheduler budget; repository-wide analysis cannot starve root landing indefinitely.
2. Align Cara `max_duration_secs` and Caco automation timeout, or add a shorter internal deadline that returns a typed partial/progress receipt before the parent kills it. Never configure inner max > outer without a termination margin.
3. On outer timeout, preserve stdout/stderr/current phase/caravan cursor and emit `sync_failed`; do not lose temp files with the killed shell.
4. Under `head_merge_actor: caravan`, audit copy and receipts must say Cara owns direct squash; never claim GitHub auto-merge was armed.

title: Queue conflict selection is untested against real producer output
description:
Follow-up to bd-857b84, closing the reason it was invisible rather than the instance.

`cara queue --status conflict` returned zero matches on a fleet carrying two conflicting candidates, and every unit test in `src/next.rs` passed throughout. They asserted the status codes and the fail-open behaviour, and never asked graph analysis what kind it actually emits, so they certified the consumer's assumption instead of the contract between producer and consumer.

That is how all seven instances of this drift hid. A test that constructs its own inputs cannot detect a producer changing what it emits.

Adds `next::tests::conflict_matches_what_graph_analysis_actually_emits`, which drives the selection from real `analyze` output rather than a hand-built `GraphProblem`.

VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, in both directions, because a green test never seen failing is exactly what produced this situation:

    producer changed to emit `Incompatible`   -> test result: FAILED
    producer restored                          -> test result: ok

So if the emitted kind drifts again, this fails at the surface that consumes it, not merely at the producer.

Note what this does NOT claim: it does not close the class. `==` against an enum variant stays invisible to the compiler, and an eighth instance remains possible wherever a fresh comparison is written instead of using the classifier. What it does is make one specific high-traffic surface fail loudly instead of reporting an empty queue to a scheduler as if it were healthy.

title: A tick discards its compatibility cache between rediscoveries
description:
Compatibility analysis is 78% of a read on the cacophony fleet, and a tick pays it from cold at least three times.

Measured, three consecutive `cara status` runs, 40 pull requests in the graph:

    total 40159 ms | compatibility_analysis 31488 (78%) | github_discovery 8033
    total 39045 ms | compatibility_analysis 30722 (79%) | github_discovery 7581
    total 40433 ms | compatibility_analysis 32109 (79%) | github_discovery 7589

Two runs immediately before those exceeded the 60s deadline outright with `github_discovery_timeout`, so this fleet reads close enough to the ceiling to fail intermittently.

`GitCompatibilityChecker` DOES cache prepared branches, keyed by `(branch_name, exact_oid)`, so repeated checks within one read do not re-fetch. But `GitCompatibilityChecker::new` is called inside the status read itself (read.rs:704), so every read starts cold. A sync performs at least three reads — initial discovery, midpoint rediscovery, final rediscovery — and throws the cache away between them, paying the full fetch and merge-tree cost each time.

WHY REUSE IS SAFE, which is the part that makes this worth doing rather than a tempting shortcut: the cache key includes the EXACT OID. A branch that moved between rediscoveries has a different key and misses the cache, so reuse cannot serve a stale tree. That is the same property the rest of the pipeline relies on: `prepare_branch_snapshots_with_runner` verifies advertisement before AND after fetching, and a moved ref already surfaces as `stale_remote_revision`. Rediscovery exists to re-read authoritative state, and it still would; what is discarded is only the local preparation of revisions that provably did not change.

SCOPE, HONESTLY. This accounts for roughly 60 to 90 seconds of a tick, not for the 3587 seconds observed in cacophony:bd-539d20. I measured it while looking for that hour and did NOT find it here. Filing this on its own evidence rather than as an explanation of that P0, because I have twice today built a theory on a partial trace and been wrong in ways that cost an operator time.

NOT CLAIMED. It is a cross-cutting change to how the checker is constructed and threaded through sync, and it wants a fresh pass rather than the tail of a very long session.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN DEFERRAL REASON, recorded because it was wrong and would mislead whoever picks this up.

I wrote that this is "a cross-cutting change to how the checker is constructed and threaded through sync". It is not. `GitCompatibilityChecker.prepared` is a per-instance
`RefCell<BTreeMap<(String, String), CommitOid>>`. Making it process-global requires NO signature changes anywhere: it is a change inside the checker. `read.rs` already contains two precedents for exactly this shape, `STATUS_CACHE` and `LABEL_CACHE`, the latter with a `LABEL_CACHE_MAX_AGE` of 600s.

I asserted the shape without checking it and then used that assertion as grounds to defer. That is the same failure this session kept producing elsewhere: a property claimed rather than verified.

TWO REAL CONSTRAINTS the implementation must respect, which the current per-instance cache gets for free:

  1. THE KEY MUST INCLUDE THE REPOSITORY AND REMOTE. Today the key is (branch_name, oid) and
     the checker instance supplies repository + remote implicitly. A process-global map keyed
     the same way would collide across repositories, and `cara web` serves several at once.
     The key must become (repository, remote, branch_name, oid).

  2. IT NEEDS A BOUNDED TTL, not unbounded lifetime. The cached fact is "this exact revision
     is already prepared LOCALLY". That stops being true if the object is pruned or the repo
     is garbage collected, which is not hypothetical: an agent had a nix runtime collected
     mid-run tonight. A short TTL in the style of LABEL_CACHE bounds the exposure while still
     covering the several reads inside one tick, which is where the benefit is.

WHERE THE BENEFIT IS, stated precisely so nobody measures the wrong thing: within a single
`cara status` the checker is already created once and the cache already works, so a global
cache changes nothing for a single read. The gain is across the THREE-PLUS reads inside one
`cara sync` (initial discovery, midpoint rediscovery, final rediscovery). Measuring repeated
`cara status` invocations will show no improvement and is not evidence against the change.

title: Classify unreachable compare refs instead of failing candidate selection
description: Cara-owned A/B handoff from Cacophony P0 bd-220916 (Harry, 2026-07-26). title: Fence local and hosted writers with a remote CAS lease
description:
Child of bd-b15483. Add the remote compare-and-swap writer lease required before local and hosted Caravan processes may both be capable of writing one repository. The existing operation.lock remains the inner same-machine lock; it cannot fence separate hosts.

FIRST SLICE / BACKEND CONTRACT

Introduce a backend-neutral RemoteWriterLease trait/protocol and strict non-secret config selecting `writer_mode: local_only` (default), `read_only`, or `remote_fenced`. Do not ship a pretend in-memory/file remote backend. `remote_fenced` requires one explicit external lease-broker executable or reviewed service adapter supplied by deployment, never repository-controlled secret material.

Lease identity: exact provider host/owner/repository, App installation where configured, writer owner ID, operation ID, expiry, heartbeat deadline, and opaque monotonically increasing fencing token. Acquire is atomic create-or-CAS against prior version; renew/release require exact owner+operation+fence; stale takeover returns a strictly greater token. Broker JSON is strict, bounded, secret-free, and independently deadline-bounded.

MUTATION FENCE

Every mutating CLI/MCP/webhook path must acquire remote lease BEFORE local operation.lock when mode is remote_fenced. Thread an immutable lease guard/fencing receipt through GitHubMutationAdapter, native Stack adapter, direct merge/labels/comments/base updates, force intent, physical git push, repair, priority, pause/resume, reshape/eviction, and webhook sync. Immediately before every provider or branch write, revalidate/renew the exact fencing token; losing/expiring/indeterminate lease fails before the write. A local-only writer refuses startup if deployment also advertises hosted writer ownership; read/plan remains available.

No automatic failover in this slice unless broker CAS semantics are proven. Service outage, malformed response, timeout, token regression, owner mismatch, and release ambiguity fail closed with typed bounded receipts. Break-glass takeover is explicit, audited, and cannot reuse a token. Never infer success from time alone.

TESTS

- Deterministic fake CAS backend proves exclusion, monotonic takeover tokens, exact renew/release, stale owner refusal, heartbeat expiry, and ambiguity recovery.
- Two concurrent simulated hosts can never both pass a mutation fence.
- Every mutation adapter has a source/contract guard requiring a live fence in remote_fenced mode.
- Lost lease between provider pre-read and write yields zero write calls.
- Lost lease between rewrite and force-with-lease push preserves remote head and reports resumable evidence.
- local_only default is behavior-compatible and performs zero remote lease calls.
- read_only permits status/check/plan and rejects all mutations.
- Broker secrets never enter config, argv, errors, receipts, journal, or process display.

HOSTED WORKERS REMAIN OUT OF SCOPE until this contract lands. Document one-writer deployment as the only safe production topology meanwhile.

PROTOCOL CHILD LANDED

bd-53d3a2 landed at 6874222 with strict broker/CAS/guard types, deterministic exclusion/ambiguity tests, and reserved startup-closed writer config. This does not enable hosted writes. Remaining work on this bead is the mutation-fence integration across every provider/Git write seam and read_only enforcement.

MUTATION SEAM CHILD LANDED

bd-ab5dca landed at 7c25479. Every current provider and remote Git write is explicitly marked, conservative inference rejects omitted markers, FencedCommandRunner revalidates before marked writes and preserves inner budgets/auth/telemetry, and RemoteLeaseGuard implements the seam. Production operations still do not construct the wrapper; read_only/remote_fenced remain startup-closed. Remaining work is operation-scoped acquisition before operation.lock and propagation of the fenced runner through all mutation paths.

title: Return typed output-limit evidence when command stdout exceeds its capture bound
description:
Reflect-session follow-up from bd-f7c3bc: the immediate blocker raises bounded provider stdout capture to 32 MiB and fixes real 181 KiB GitHub JSON. If a future command exceeds that bound, ProcessRunner still appends a truncation marker and the provider layer reports invalid JSON rather than a first-class output-limit error. This is not a v1 blocker at current query bounds.

Implemented at exact rebased generation bca93894 over updater main e4309b2. Any stdout or stderr overflow returns `CommandRunError::OutputLimit` with child exit status before UTF-8/JSON decoding; timeout remains primary with bounded diagnostic text. Read/provider, compatibility, init, membership and sync surfaces return typed `command_output_limit`, separate stream evidence, mutation/receipt context and safe retry guidance—never malformed JSON. title: The plan describes a tick that would refuse before starting
description:
`cara plan sync --all` renders a complete, confident plan for a tick that would refuse before doing anything.

Verified against the live fleet with a config whose only fault is an out-of-range tick budget:

    $ cara plan sync --all --config <max_duration_secs: 65525>
    PLAN SYNC  NO PROVIDER WRITES  repository harryaskham/cacophony
      1. PhysicalPreflight/WouldMutate PR #2300 rebase_branch
      ... 17 steps, no warning, no mention of the budget ...

    a real tick with the same config is refused at sync_with_lock with `invalid_tick_bounds`

`validate_tick_bounds` is called in `sync_with_lock` and nowhere else. `plan_sync` does not call it, so the preview describes seventeen operations that cannot happen.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC: `plan sync` exists so somebody can decide whether to authorise a real tick without running one. A plan that says WouldMutate for a tick that will refuse at step zero is worse than no plan, because it converts "I checked" into false confidence. This is the same argument that motivated bd-070cdf, where a no-write plan reported `github_mutation_failed` for a read failure: the dry-run is the one surface that must not mislead, because it is consulted precisely by people who do not yet trust the tick.

It is also a direct consequence of the fix that landed for bd-a4a7e9, correctly: tick bounds moved OUT of config load so a bad budget could no longer silence read-only surfaces. That was right. What it did not do is give the read-only preview a way to say the tick would still refuse. The check moved and the preview was not taught about it.

THE FIX SHOULD NOT BE TO REFUSE. Making `plan sync` reject an invalid budget would re-break exactly what bd-a4a7e9 repaired: the read-only surface an operator needs in order to diagnose the bad budget. The plan should still render, and should additionally report that a real tick would refuse, naming the violated bound. Diagnostic, not gated.

title: Classify failed CI decisions with exact failed-step lineage evidence
description:
Operator-requested Cara information gap. `cara sync --all` correctly returned `ci_failure` for Cacophony PR #1991 and listed failed check names plus rerunnable run ID `29646903145`, but it did not expose why the run failed. The merger had to inspect the GitHub Actions job log directly to discover that the selected ref was stale: expected head `affacaba74132a4642c6aa06021bb8fa5e381097`, selected merge ref `ff68423484b0be2ffe0a2dd70999c8d518c0887b`, parents `[251d04e9be9742cbf9a9d2cfa0a194601e5a2561, 329c42e2a22db8146dada382811927e38ee80e50]`. A blind `cara sync --rerun-failed` would have rerun the same stale event rather than validate the current candidate.

Live PR #1991 run 29646903145 REST evidence confirms run association head 97d698c differs current expected affacaba despite run head_sha affacaba; failed job 88086568032 step `Verify exact CI ref lineage`. Thus stale generation must recommend fresh candidate, never rerun. Coordinating with bd-021727 shared MergeCandidateIdentity/SyntheticMergeCandidate/Freshness commit faa55fe; that slice must land first, then this lane will reference it in sync decisions/suggested actions. Current coherent tip de820c4 on main@397d1a5 includes: bounded raw Actions facts; shared MergeCandidateIdentity with independent stale_base/stale_head; sync-owned deterministic stale/current/infra/source/cancelled/unknown classification; exact fresh-trigger/rerun/repair/wait actions; stale runs excluded from rerunnable_run_ids; current infrastructure only rerunnable; CI decision/event JSON carries bounded job/failed-step receipts. Added stale-run vs current-source tests, including --rerun-failed fail-closed behavior. Also corrected default movement attribution: a caravan label alone is Unknown, never unproven CaraOwned. Only strict safe-character `ci-selected-ref-receipt` fields escape; raw text and unrelated lines are discarded, parser requires exact commit/base/head and two parents, and test proves a nearby TOKEN value is absent from serialized evidence. Missing/non-206/malformed/truncated receipts are typed and sync fails closed to fresh-trigger. Live endpoint verified 206 and receipt exact selected ff684... parents [251d04e...,329c42e...]. title: cara log reports records: 0 for a repository whose journal is in another checkout
description:
`cara log` reads the bounded event journal from the git-common-dir of the checkout it is invoked in:

    let common = PathBuf::from(output.stdout.trim());   // git rev-parse --git-common-dir
    let directory = common.join(JOURNAL_DIR);           // journal.rs

So the journal is per-checkout. A tick run from checkout A is invisible to `cara log` in checkout B of the same repository, and B reports `records: 0`.

`records: 0` is indistinguishable from "no tick has ever run". That is not a hypothetical: it produced a wrong answer to the operator today.

## How it misled, concretely

Asked whether a clean unadmitted PR had been *declined* or merely *not looked at*, I ran `cara log` from `/Users/harryaskham/.cacophony/daemon/checkouts/cacophony`, got `records: 0`, and reported that there was no evidence any sync tick had ever executed on Cacophony.

The real journal was in a different checkout's common dir, `/Users/harryaskham/cosmos/.git/modules/projects/cacophony/caravan/events-v1.jsonl`, with **248 records**:

    ready_pr_unqueued   182
    sync_failed          32
    join_failed          16
    caravan_created       6
    pr_joined             6
    eviction_failed       5
    evicted               1

Ticks had run many times, and `ready_pr_unqueued` is precisely the "I looked at this PR and did not queue it" evidence that was being asked for. The artefact existed and had been accumulating; it was simply not visible from where the question was asked.

## Why this is the same class as the surfaces being catalogued today

The recurring defect this week is two different states rendering identically. This is that, one level up: the *evidence* distinguishing the states is real and correct, but scoped to a directory nobody else reads. A repository-wide question cannot be answered from a repository-wide place, and the failure mode is silent — an empty list, not an error.

## Change required, either is defensible

1. **Journal per repository rather than per checkout.** Key the journal by repository identity so `cara log` is answerable from any checkout of the same repo. Correct, and larger: needs a location that multiple checkouts and nodes can agree on.
2. **Minimum: make the scope explicit.** Have `cara log` report which checkout/common-dir it read, and state that this journal is local to it. `records: 0` must stop being able to mean "never happened" when it only means "never happened *here*".

(2) is worth doing regardless of whether (1) is taken. An empty result whose scope is invisible is a trap, and it caught an agent that was specifically hunting for this class of defect.

title: Initialize required Caravan labels safely on first repository use
description:
Operator asked whether Cara initializes a repository by creating its operational labels. Current `cara` v0.0.1 does not.

Source contract in `membership.rs` defines required labels `caravan`, `caravan-evicted`, and `caravan-force`, calls `require_labels`, and fails before provider mutation with `required_labels_missing`: “Caravan's operational labels must exist before the first mutation”, next “create caravan, caravan-evicted, and caravan-force labels, then rerun the same command”. No `gh label create`/repository-label creation implementation exists.

Acceptance:
- Add an explicit idempotent repository initialization surface (`cara init`) or a clearly documented safe first-mutating-use initialization phase.
- Create exactly the required labels with stable names, colors, and descriptions: active member, evicted member, and operator force exception.
- Read-only `status`/`check` must never mutate; they should report initialized/missing/mismatched label state and the exact next command.
- Before first `new`/`join`/`renew`/`rejoin`/`sync` mutation, require initialization or perform it only through an explicit opt-in flag; never silently broaden permissions.
- Use optimistic repository-label preconditions and idempotent create-if-absent behavior. Existing correct labels no-op; concurrent creation converges.
- If an existing label has unexpected metadata, fail with a bounded decision point rather than overwriting operator-owned configuration.
- Report missing GitHub label-write permission distinctly and make no PR/base/auto-merge mutation when initialization fails.
- Add fixtures for empty repo, partially initialized labels, existing correct labels, metadata mismatch, concurrent init, permission denial, status read-only, and retry after indeterminate create.
- Update `cara help`, SPEC, and first-use docs with repository initialization workflow.

Related live cutover blocker: `caravan/bd-f7c3bc` (Cara status JSON parsing failure). caco-merger must stay on its audited manual provider path until inventory and initialization are safe.

## Helsinki first-use/label acceptance finding

Independent live inspection confirms the current implementation does **not** initialize repository labels:

- daemon Caravan checkout: `e451ed9c02860f9dea408cd68890fdde56c8846a`;
- installed binary: `cara 0.0.1`, SHA-256 `0e88ba61fcb6df4aaf95b609d714d8caae9942be4a0cfcccabb4912e4e59f813` (operator updater refreshed the binary after the earlier installed-path proof);
- `cara --help` has no `init` command;
- `membership.rs` defines `REQUIRED_LABELS = ["caravan", "caravan-evicted", "caravan-force"]` and `require_labels` returns `required_labels_missing` before mutation with manual-create guidance;
- no create/ensure repository-label implementation exists in the inspected source.

Cacophony's live repository is now externally/manual-initialized with all three correct labels, so the requested idempotent create is a no-op rather than a write:

- `caravan`: color `5319E7`, description `Active member of a Caravan PR chain`;
- `caravan-evicted`: color `B60205`, description `Removed from a Caravan chain pending renew or rejoin`;
- `caravan-force`: color `D93F0B`, description `Allow configured force handling for known CI failures`.

Root-checkout `cara --json status` is healthy after bd-f7c3bc, but that healthy inventory must not be interpreted as proof that Cara created the labels; they already exist from external setup. The first-use init acceptance remains unmet and this bead is the canonical tracker.

## Merged duplicate: bd-046d79

Title: Add idempotent Cara repository initialization for required labels

## Operator expectation

While integrating Cara into Cacophony, Harry asked whether first use correctly initializes a repository by creating the `caravan`, `caravan-evicted`, and `caravan-force` labels.

Current behavior does not initialize them. `cara status` can inventory an unlabelled repository, but mutation paths call `require_labels` and fail before provider mutation with `required_labels_missing`, instructing the operator to create all three labels manually and rerun. There is no `cara init` command.

The Cacophony repository currently has all three labels, verified through GitHub, but they were provisioned externally rather than by Cara first-use initialization.

## Acceptance

- Add an explicit, idempotent first-party initialization surface such as `cara init` (CLI/MCP), or an equally clear reviewed first-use path.
- Create exactly the required labels with documented names, descriptions, and colors:
  - `caravan`
  - `caravan-evicted`
  - `caravan-force`
- Preserve compatible existing labels without mutation; fail closed on incompatible definitions unless an explicit repair option is chosen.
- Return stable receipts distinguishing created, already-present, incompatible, and provider-failed labels.
- `cara status` should report repository initialization readiness and the exact next command when labels are missing.
- `new`, `join`, `renew`, and `rejoin` continue to fail before graph mutation if initialization has not completed.
- Add provider fixtures for empty repo, partial labels, compatible existing labels, incompatible metadata, retry after partial provider failure, and idempotent replay.
- Document whether automatic initialization is ever allowed; avoid hidden label mutation from a read-only `status` call.

Filed from the first Cacophony Cara cutover. This belongs in the Caravan project, not Cacophony.

Operator expansion (2026-07-18): `cara init` is the reviewed first-use surface and must cover both local config and GitHub repository readiness. title: sync gives no route to its own read-only preview
description:
`cara sync` performs admission and merge. Asked "what will a tick do before I authorise it", the natural place to look is `cara sync --help`, which lists `--all`, `--json`, `--config` and `--rerun-failed`. There is no `--dry-run`, so the honest conclusion from that surface is that no preview exists.

That conclusion is WRONG, and the cost was real: over three messages I told an operator that a tick's outcome could not be previewed, asked them to authorise it on a prediction I had derived by reading admission rules in the source, and explicitly warned that the prediction might be wrong. The operator was being asked to accept merge risk on my reasoning.

`cara check --pr <candidate> --head-pr <caravan>` answers exactly that question, read-only. Against the live fleet it reported, without mutating anything:

    CHECK  #2296  eligible  JoinTail
      next: Join after #2300
      admission selection=explicit intent=join target_caravan=#2300 blocked_by=[] provider_mutated=false
      Clean: cara-web-justfile@0fb897ce -> ...pr-g440a5914@f19e7b1c conflicts=[]
      problems: []

Everything the authorisation actually needed: eligible, clean, unblocked, and the exact target caravan.

THE DEFECT IS DISCOVERABILITY, not capability. `cara sync --help` says "Idempotently synchronize one or all caravans until a decision point" and offers no route to the preview. A reader who wants to know what a tick will do has no reason to look at a different subcommand, and `check`'s own summary, "Validate current or proposed caravan state without mutation", does not obviously mean "preview what sync would do".

Adds a line to `sync --help` pointing at `cara check --pr <pr> --head-pr <caravan>` as the read-only preview. Small, but it closes a gap that cost an operator three rounds of unnecessary risk assessment and nearly cost an unverified merge authorisation.

THE GENERAL FAILURE, which is mine and recurring: I treated a boundary as terminal after checking ONE surface. This is the fourth instance today of the same shape, and I had already written the counter-rule down: check whether a read-only path answers the same question before treating a limit as real. Knowing the rule did not help, because the surface I consulted answered my literal question correctly. `sync` really has no `--dry-run`. It was the question that was too narrow, not the answer that was wrong.

title: Require a complete-group GitHub Stack merge lease
description:
Track the external prerequisite for executable GitHub native Stack merging. The 2026-07-31 disposable sandbox proved `PUT .../merge-async` leases only the selected top SHA: after 202, a lower PR was rewound to an ancestor while preserving the upper chain, and GitHub merged every selected PR at the changed lower generation. Cara can detect the changed head afterward but cannot prevent the merge.

Acceptance requires a documented provider field or equivalent preventive mechanism that atomically binds every selected PR head (or one immutable complete Stack generation), plus a repeated disposable-repository race proof. An allowlist, branch-policy assumption, post-merge receipt, or narrowed timing window is insufficient. Until then `github_stack_backend_read_only` remains closed and native batch rollout is blocked. Evidence: `docs/validation/github-native-stack-sandbox-2026-07-31.md` at Caravan main `7b85524`.

## Operator-directed client-side preventive path

GitHub's `gh stack` v0.0.8 has no merge command; source contains no `merge-async` client. It manages local branch/PR topology and sync/rebase, while GitHub's web merge uses the same top-SHA-only provider endpoint already sandboxed.

Operator requested implementing an equivalent preventive mechanism. Evaluate an ephemeral exact-ref repository ruleset that atomically prohibits update/deletion of every selected source branch before the final full-generation read and remains active through async terminal proof. Submit only after exact ruleset readback and exact Stack reread; persist ruleset identity with UUID; delete by exact identity after terminal/abort, with ambiguous deletion rediscovery. Prove in a disposable repository that ordinary and administrator pushes are blocked, direct Stack merge still succeeds, partial-prefix rewriting of unselected refs still succeeds, crash residue is safely recoverable, and no default/Caravan path gains Administration calls.

This path is acceptable only as explicit GitHub-mode policy because ruleset mutation requires Administration(write), which the baseline least-privilege App intentionally forbids. If no-bypass exact-ref rules cannot prevent owner/admin movement or cannot be restored safely, retain the external blocker.

## Provider proof (2026-08-01)

The same private disposable repository proved the exact-ref ruleset approach end-to-end. Ruleset 20181221 targeted the first two source refs with no bypass actors and exact update+deletion restrictions; readback reported `current_user_can_bypass: never`. Repository-owner SSH push returned GH013, and owner-authenticated REST force-update and delete both returned HTTP 422 while the lower head remained unchanged. Direct partial Stack merge still succeeded under UUID `282bd37c-e4e1-435f-b6ec-5109ca9eaf14` at `07005d1f...`; the unselected third PR was rebased/retargeted by GitHub. Exact ruleset deletion plus absence proof restored pushes. The repository was re-archived and remains tracked for deletion by bd-7aa0aa.

Implementation in progress adds a REST-only ruleset lock adapter with deterministic operation identity, exact no-bypass policy verification, zero-write retries, ambiguous create/delete rediscovery, exact-generation release, provider-write fencing, and a locked wrapper around async submit/poll. Unlocked async submit/poll are no longer public provider APIs. README, SPEC, `cara help`, App permission docs, design, and sandbox evidence explicitly distinguish `gh stack` topology management from web/API merge and explain the Administration(write) lock requirement.

## Implementation complete on agent branch (`f370be2`, Cara 0.0.75)

- Added `src/github/stack_lock.rs`: deterministic operation-scoped exact-ref ruleset lock, active/no-bypass/current-user-never-bypass proof, update+deletion rule validation, bounded inventory, same-operation changed-generation collision, exact zero-write retry, ambiguous create/delete rediscovery, exact-generation verification/release, capability-confirmed absence, sealed receipts, and provider-write classification.
- The only public async merge APIs are now `native_stack_merge_submit_locked` and `native_stack_merge_poll_locked`. They verify the exact lock immediately before the final full Stack reread/PUT and before every UUID poll. The persisted outer checkpoint seals both UUID intent and ruleset generation; lock loss forces `indeterminate`. Unlocked transport methods are private.
- `GitHubStackAsyncMergePlan::branch_lock_plan` binds lock identity to the same operation, Stack number, selected PRs, refs, and exact heads.
- Added 14 focused lock/locked-merge tests within 39 total Stack tests.
- `cara help` now has a tested `GITHUB NATIVE STACKS (EXPLICIT PREVIEW)` section explaining that `gh stack` has no merge command, web/API merge is top-SHA-only, the exact ruleset lock contract, indeterminate recovery, and explicit Administration(write) requirement.
- README, SPEC, App permissions, native Stack design, and live sandbox report carry the same contract.

Validation: `just validate` green on the pinned CI block; 784 library tests plus all binary/integration suites passed; formatting, warning-denied all-target Clippy, CLI help, and MCP manifest passed.

Correction: focused coverage is 7 direct ruleset-lock tests plus 2 public locked submit/poll tests, within 39 total Stack tests.

Rebased over v0.0.75 and advanced the reviewed release candidate to Cara 0.0.76; final agent head is a0d9b01. Focused Stack tests and warning-denied all-target Clippy remain green after rebase.

title: A cancelled CI run is treated as a code failure, not infrastructure
description:
`retryable_infrastructure` classified `timed_out`, `startup_failure`, `stale` and `action_required` as infrastructure, but NOT `cancelled`. So a cancellation was treated as a genuine code failure and was ineligible for the bounded rerun recovery path.

Live shape from cacophony bd-c04d9b (PR2208, run 30222268397): every producer job was CANCELLED under runner-capacity pressure, the aggregate required checks went FAILURE in six seconds, and not one test or lint step had failed. A five-member caravan could not advance, and clearing it needed a human.

A cancellation is a capacity or supersession event, not a verdict on the code: the producer simply never produced a result. It now joins the infrastructure set, so `cara sync --rerun-failed` can re-trigger it.

WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: it does not make a cancelled run count as success anywhere. Absent validation still fails closed for admission and for merge, because an absent result is not a passing result. Cancellation only becomes eligible for recovery, and that path is already opt-in via `--rerun-failed` and already bound to the exact current head, so a stale superseded generation is never resurrected. A genuine `failure` stays out of the set and is asserted so, because sweeping it in would loop forever on work that cannot go green by itself.

Covers requirement 2 of cacophony bd-c04d9b from the Cara side. Requirements 1, 3 and 4 are cacophony's own CI: the aggregate check converting cancelled producers into a red code-like required status is a workflow design issue in that repository, and Cara cannot distinguish it from a real failure once the aggregate reports FAILURE. That distinction has to be made where the aggregate is computed.

description:

Before disabling auto-merge, invalidating control labels, or any branch write, prove/reserve enough absolute-deadline budget for per-member final remote/PR revalidation, exact lease pushes, midpoint provider rediscovery, base/CI reconciliation, and final receipt. A provider race remains retryable, but unchanged provider lag/deadline exhaustion must not hot-loop or consume control intent.

title: Give each Cara candidate an independent bounded discovery budget
description:
## Live Cacophony blocker

An operator-authorized Cara enrollment pass reached deterministic provider time-budget exhaustion without mutation:

- Cara v0.0.5 sync preserved PR #2053 enrolled/paused at exact head `53d8ed4e` and recorded skips for PRs #1952, #1955, #1978, #1980, and #1989.
- The retry tick then returned `github_discovery_timeout` at PR #1994 with only 339 ms of Git-fetch budget available.
- A direct, operator-allowlisted attempt to enroll clean PR #2059 exact head `27a06a55` refused `git_compatibility_timeout` with 1 ms remaining after full-fleet preflight.
- Provider state was not mutated.

## Required behavior

- Separate full-fleet discovery/preflight budget from exact candidate compatibility/admission budget.
- Allocate each explicitly selected candidate a fresh bounded budget that prior candidate scans cannot consume.
- Reuse safely cached provider/topology data where exact head/base/freshness permits, with drift refusal.
- Persist a deterministic continuation cursor/receipt so retry ticks resume rather than restart the full fleet scan.
- Exact allowlisted admission must not traverse every unrelated PR before checking its target.
- Return typed timing breakdowns for provider listing, Git fetch, compatibility, and mutation phases.
- Preserve fail-closed no-mutation semantics on every timeout.
- Add regressions for a large candidate fleet followed by exact candidate enrollment with near-exhausted global budget.

## Acceptance

PR #2059 or an equivalent exact candidate can receive a full independent compatibility budget and either enroll successfully or return a semantic refusal; it must not fail merely because previous full-fleet discovery consumed the shared deadline.

Cacophony has 30+ open PRs. - Exact priority/new admission must not spend the entire operation deadline before `ls-remote`.
- Continue bounded automatic admission after generation-bound skips without starving the first safe root.
- Preserve exact head/base/provider receipts and fail closed on actual drift.
- Add 40-PR delayed-provider fixtures proving sync and direct high-priority new complete or return a meaningful bounded decision with nonzero execution budget.

- PR 2059 remained completely unmodified by the failed v0.0.5 attempt.

title: Bound native GitHub caravans to eight-entry merge batches
description:
GitHub native Stack mode needs a finite admission batch so continuous arrivals cannot grow one provider Stack without bound and serial post-merge generation invalidation cannot consume the entire queue. Add an explicit `max_caravan_length` contract whose absent/default `stack_type: caravan` path remains behavior-identical, while `stack_type: github` defaults to 8 and validates within GitHub's 2..=100 Stack limit.

At capacity, deterministic admission opens or grows another Caravan rather than extending the full Stack. Sync never waits merely for occupancy: it submits the maximal contiguous green prefix from the bottom, and when all <=8 entries are ready it lands the whole batch through one native atomic merge. Bind admission/sealing to the exact Stack generation and operation lock so arrivals cannot alter an in-flight selected prefix. Expose exact capacity/full-batch evidence in status and receipts. This is the Aviator-style bounded-batch behavior requested during the live #2331 -> #2330 squash/promotion CI rerun observation.

Acceptance: default/explicit Caravan mode has no changed capacity or Stack API calls; GitHub mode defaults to 8, explicit values are strictly validated, the ninth candidate forms/joins another eligible Caravan, and a fully green eight-entry Stack is selected as one atomic merge group.

## Safety prerequisite

The 2026-07-31 bd-67b62b sandbox resolved the lower-head lease question negatively: after a 202 response, a lower rewind preserving upper ancestry merged the group at a changed lower generation. Keep this batching slice draft/preview-only until GitHub exposes a preventive complete-group generation lease. The capacity/read-model design remains valid, but an eight-entry executable merge cannot be acceptance criteria under the current API.

## Landed on main at 64fb5f7

- `max_caravan_length: Option<u32>` in `.caravan/config.yaml`, validated strictly to GitHub's 2..=100 Stack range. Absent configuration keeps `stack_type: caravan` behavior-identical (no new admission limit on upgrade); `effective_max_caravan_length()` applies the default of 8 only after explicit `stack_type: github`.
- `configured_batch_bound` gates admission independently of the physical apply reserve, so it also applies in GitHub mode where `rebase_on_join` is required to be false and the dynamic capacity gate never runs. Reaching the bound is ordinary fullness, never a capacity defect: `caravan_batch_capacity_exhausted` carries exact caravan/bound/member evidence and suggests another caravan rather than a drain-only remedy.
- A full batch is never extended and never stalls the queue: tails at the bound are marked `batch_full`, skipped with a reason naming `max_caravan_length`, and when every visible caravan is full the candidate deterministically opens a new caravan. Skip-receipt fingerprints now include the effective bound so changing it invalidates stale receipts.
- Status projects the effective bound (`min(batch, dynamic)` when both apply), per-caravan `at_capacity`, and a full-batch-specific next action; the dynamic capacity defect is reported only when physical rebuilding is on.
- Merge selection is unchanged and still lands the maximal contiguous ready prefix, so sync never waits for occupancy while a fully ready batch lands as one atomic native merge.

Five focused tests cover default-path preservation, in-range/out-of-range validation, refusal evidence, GitHub-mode defaulting without rebasing, and full-batch redirection to a new caravan. `cara help`, README, and SPEC state the contract. Complete `just validate` was green before landing.

title: Post-rewrite budget guard deterministically refuses every Cara candidate that needs rewriting
description:
Canonical Caravan-source work item for the defect evidenced in Cacophony bead `bd-10303b`.

Observed contract failure: `require_post_rewrite_budget` prices the post-rewrite reserve as `POST_REWRITE_COMMAND_RESERVE` (four commands) multiplied by `command_timeout_secs`, but evaluates it against a deadline rebound to approximately one `command_timeout_secs`. Once a candidate reaches the rewrite path, the guard therefore cannot pass. Root promotion still drains through a different path, producing partial liveness: roots merge while a caravan tail that needs rebasing/rewriting cannot re-form.

The Cacophony configuration workaround merged in PR #2322 raises the command timeout so ticks can proceed, but does not repair the Caravan-source invariant. The source fix belongs here.

Acceptance criteria:

- A candidate requiring the configured rewrite/rebase path can complete within a bounded tick without requiring four full command-timeout windows inside a one-window deadline.
- Budget accounting uses actual remaining tick budget and the commands that will run, or otherwise reserves a coherent bounded budget before entering the rewrite.
- A no-op/already-satisfied candidate does not pay the physical rewrite reserve.
- Root promotion and tail rewrite both retain bounded forward progress; one candidate cannot consume the whole tick indefinitely.
- Refusal receipts report required budget, remaining budget, command count, phase, and whether any provider mutation occurred.
- Tests reproduce the 4x-versus-1x invariant, then cover root-only, one rewritten child, multiple candidates, near-deadline refusal before mutation, and resumed next-tick progress.

Related Caravan work includes closed `bd-4e4615` and the existing budget/reservation beads. Treat this as a measured recurrence/new invariant rather than reopening an unrelated historical fix without comparison.

title: cara queue --status conflict silently matches nothing
description:
`cara queue --status conflict` silently returned zero matches on a fleet that demonstrably carried two conflicting candidates. Found by running the command against live cacophony, not by a test.

    cara --json queue --status conflict   ->  selected=None, matches=0
    cara --json status                    ->  problems: candidate_incompatible [2245],
                                                         candidate_incompatible [2259]

`src/next.rs` filtered on `GraphProblemKind::Incompatible`. Graph analysis stopped emitting that variant for unadmitted candidates when `CandidateIncompatible` was introduced, so the filter matched nothing and the surface reported an empty queue position as if it were a healthy one.

This is the SAME producer/consumer drift as bd-299d3e, in code I wrote AFTER that fix, and the compiler could not help because `==` against an enum variant is not a classification. The unit tests passed because they asserted the status codes and the fail-open behaviour, never asking the real analysis what kind it actually produces.

Two changes:

- `next.rs` filters on `problem.kind.is_candidate_scoped()`, the classifier, rather than naming a variant.
- New `graph.rs::an_unadmitted_candidate_conflict_is_emitted_as_candidate_scoped` asserts the PRODUCER'S actual output. The emitted kind is a wire contract between analysis and every consumer, so it is now pinned as a fact consumers can be checked against, instead of each consumer assuming.

Verified live before and after: `--status conflict` now returns 2245 and 2259 with their exact reasons. Also verified the other positions in situ, which is how this was caught at all: `ready` selects 2276, `skipped` returns three, `evicted` correctly empty, and a combined `--status conflict,skipped,ready` returns matches in the requested order.

Kept msm2's explicit `CandidateIncompatible` arm in `decision_for_problem` and allowed `clippy::match_same_arms` with a reason, rather than collapsing it. That arm exists to be visible, not to compute a different value, and collapsing it would restore the silent default that caused the original outage.

title: Skip merge-preserving replay for a squash-merged root
description:
Live block on Cacophony PR2215 under cara 0.0.13 with head_merge_actor caravan. Cara refused with rebase_merge_replay_conflict: the independently clean final merge tree cannot be reproduced by the audited merge-preserving sequencer without an intermediate conflict. Evidence: expected_merge_tree 1a13539e7485e3219dc7e16334ffd5b9d8f8aff1 is independently CLEAN, conflicting_paths crates/caco-cli/src/lib.rs and crates/caco-daemon/src/canonical_queue.rs, merge_commits 255db7da1c95b82a03f7a9cdcfa65bb73882c2c7 and 25876d4f856f7b22079c156671c7ad928eb42cc2, stderr shows Rebasing 7/9 then Could not apply the "merge: resolve main into cumulative root PR2215" commit. No remote or provider mutation was attempted, which is correct.

Root cause: the PR merged main into itself, so its history contains merge commits. Replaying that history commit-by-commit re-hits conflicts the author already resolved by hand in the merge commit, with no stored rerere resolution to replay them. The destination tree is fine; only the reproduction path fails.

Product gap: under head_merge_actor caravan the ROOT is squash-merged, so its history is discarded at landing. Insisting on a merge-preserving replay of a root whose squash merge tree is already proven clean is work that can only fail and buys nothing. History replay genuinely matters for CHILDREN, whose ancestry must physically follow the chain, and it matters when rebase output is published as the new head; it does not matter for a root about to be collapsed into a single commit.

Required behaviour: when the actor is caravan and the candidate is the root that will be squash-merged, and the squash merge tree against the exact current default branch is independently proven clean, land it directly without requiring a merge-preserving replay of its history. Keep every existing guard: exact head and base re-read immediately before mutation, proven clean merge tree, required checks satisfied or explicit force, merged-main reachability postflight before the landing counts, and zero-write abort on any drift. Do not extend this to children, and do not use it to bypass a genuinely conflicting tree.

Also note the sync_failed hook for this event exited 124, a timeout, so the refusal was not reported to any external actor.

Operator confirmed the intent: we squash merge it in the end anyway.
