title: Add audited cara force intent command
description:
Operators currently arm one-shot force acceptance by manually applying the GitHub label `caravan-force`; there is no `cara force` command. (The similarly named `caravan-forced` label is not recognized.) Add a first-party audited force-intent mutation so operators never need raw label edits.

`cara force --pr N --actor A --reason R` should rediscover exact provider facts, require force_merge=true, an open non-draft active Caravan member in a force-eligible position, exact head/default generations, clean textual compatibility, and appropriate repository permission; then apply only `caravan-force` under exact PR preconditions and post a durable generation-bound audit comment. It arms intent only; normal `cara sync` remains responsible for the one-shot admin squash and its existing final checks. No command may bypass conflicts, stale facts, holds, ownership, graph validity, or permissions. A Cara-owned rewrite invalidates old-generation intent exactly as today.

Add an idempotent first-party revoke path (`cara force revoke --pr N --actor A --reason R`, or an equivalent clear command) that removes only exact current-generation force intent with a durable audit. JSON/MCP/web schemas and receipts must expose before/after labels, PR/head/default generation, observed CI state, actor/reason, mutated flag, and safe continuation. Interactive shorthand may default to the current PR but automation requires explicit identity.

Acceptance:
- Arm exact failed/pending/empty current head and return typed durable receipt; rerun is exact no-op/deduped.
- Typo/unknown label is never treated as intent; help names `caravan-force` exactly.
- Stale head/default, nonmember/evicted/draft/closed PR, incompatible graph, textual conflict, disabled policy, insufficient permission, or comment failure fail closed with zero/partial receipts as appropriate.
- Revoke is exact, audited, idempotent, and never touches unrelated labels.
- Rewrite invalidation and one-shot sync consumption remain generation-bound.
- Full CLI/JSON/MCP/web parity and concurrency tests; docs remove manual-label guidance.

Coordinate with bd-1f3ff4, which fixes force-head graph-validation ordering and is currently owned by msm1; do not overlap that decision-order implementation.

## Decomposition for web control rollout

This bead owns the typed force arm/revoke domain operation plus CLI/JSON/MCP parity. To avoid concurrent web.rs conflicts, bd-885497 no longer owns direct dashboard rendering; the dependent web-controls bead will expose this stable operation alongside the priority command after both domain beads land. Preserve all exact-generation, audit, permission, compatibility, and one-shot acceptance requirements.

Implementation complete at exact rebased generation 26727e7 over main 9ae4d01. Added typed `force_arm`/`force_revoke` domain operations, direct CLI `cara force --pr/--actor/--reason` plus `cara force revoke ...`, JSON/MCP schemas and parity. Arm requires force_merge policy, exact open owned non-draft non-evicted active head, clean head/default compatibility, no graph problem/hold, fresh default/head and ADMIN; then changes only `caravan-force` under exact PR preconditions and posts deterministic generation-bound actor/reason/check audit. Revoke is exact/audited/idempotent and preserves unrelated labels. Stable markers dedupe partial retries; comment failure reports completed label receipt. Intent is only armed; sync remains sole one-shot squash consumer and existing rewrite invalidation remains. Full pre-rebase 361 all-target tests + strict Clippy; focused force/CLI/parity and strict Clippy green after 9ae4d01.

title: Add cascading and whole-caravan eviction
description:
Live operator block 2026-07-27 on Cacophony. `cara evict --pr 2223 --reason Incompatible` fails with reshape_would_break_fleet: the proposed reshape does not satisfy Caravan graph/compatibility invariants. Single-member eviction must close the gap by retargeting the evicted member children onto its predecessor, and when that new edge is incompatible the eviction is refused. The operator therefore cannot dismantle a caravan whose members are mutually incompatible: the only tool for breaking up a broken chain is itself blocked by the chain being broken. PR2215 was reverted on main and the operator wants to evict everything and rebuild from scratch, and there is no first-party way to do it.

Required: an ordered multi-member eviction.
- `cara evict --cascade --pr N`: evict N and every member after it, so no surviving edge ever needs to be re-linked across a removed member.
- `cara evict --all` (or an explicit dissolve verb): unenroll every member of the caravan.

Design point that makes this safe: process TAIL FIRST. Removing the current tail never requires closing a gap, because it has no child, so each individual removal is trivially compatible and the whole operation avoids the invariant that blocks single-member eviction today. A cascade is therefore a bounded sequence of tail removals, not a graph rewrite.

Preserve every existing guard per member: exact PR state and head re-read immediately before mutation, add caravan-evicted, remove caravan and caravan-force, disable auto-merge, durable control-label audit comment, and zero-write abort on drift. Emit one receipt per evicted member plus a summary naming the caravan, the ordered members evicted, and the final fleet state. Partial failure must leave a resumable, honestly reported state rather than a half-dissolved chain with no record.

Decide and document what happens to each evicted member base: leaving it pointed at a now-evicted predecessor is wrong, so members should be retargeted to the default branch as they are released, making each PR independently reviewable and re-admittable.

Operator also asked for this because the Cara Sync CI job is being disabled and run from inside Cacophony instead; a broken chain that cannot be dismantled blocks that migration.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: aarch64-linux release job is unschedulable, so no release reaches a terminal state
description:
Every caravan release run since at least v0.0.31 fails to reach a terminal state, and six release runs are non-terminal right now. The cause is the same class as bd-8b6d28, which removed aarch64-darwin from the matrix for exactly this reason, and it now recurs for aarch64-linux.

Measured 2026-07-30:

 .github/workflows/release.yml
 - target: aarch64-linux
 runner: [self-hosted, nix, ms-dev-2]

 gh api repos/harryaskham/caravan/actions/runners
 caravan-ms-dev-2 online labels=self-hosted,nix,Linux,X64,x86_64-linux,ms-dev-2,nixos

ms-dev-2 is ONLINE but advertises X64 and x86_64-linux. No registered runner advertises an ARM Linux capability, and the workflow comment's premise (that ms-dev-2 advertises aarch64-linux in Nix extra-platforms) is not visible to the Actions scheduler, which matches on runner LABELS, not on Nix extra-platforms. So the job is unschedulable and queues forever:

 build aarch64-linux status=queued started=2026-07-30T03:02:53Z runner=none

Consequences, which are why this is worth fixing rather than tolerating:
- No release ever reaches a terminal state, so releases read as flaky infrastructure exactly as they did before bd-8b6d28.
- Published assets are only x86_64-linux plus a backfilled aarch64-darwin. v0.0.33 has ONLY x86_64-linux.
- Any pin-update or verification step that waits for a complete asset set blocks indefinitely.

DECISION REQUIRED (one of):
1. Remove aarch64-linux from the release matrix, exactly as bd-8b6d28 did for aarch64-darwin, and publish it via just release-backfill-target TAG aarch64-linux from a genuine ARM Linux host when one exists. This makes releases terminal today.
2. Register a runner that actually advertises an aarch64-linux label, and point the matrix entry at that label rather than at a host name.

Option 1 is the minimal change and restores terminal releases immediately; option 2 is the only one that produces a real ARM Linux artifact. Note that no current fleet node needs aarch64-linux: every Linux runner reports the X64 label, and the only ARM host is the aarch64-DARWIN Mac.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-1

title: A hard CI failure is masked while any sibling check is still running
description:
Operator report on cacophony PR 2276: the forge reported `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` with `Rust Check & Lint: FAILURE` and `Rust Fast Tests` still pending, yet Cara did not treat the PR as failed.

`classify_checks` in sync.rs evaluated `pending` BEFORE `failed`:

    if pending { Waiting } else if failed { Failed } else { Passing }

so any concurrently running check masked a hard failure. Reproduced with the exact observed shape: left=Waiting, right=Failed.

A failing required check does not become successful by waiting. Masking it for as long as any sibling job is in flight is long enough to admit known-red work and stack every following PR on top of it, which is precisely the re-stitching cost the queue exists to prevent.

Fix: failure is decisive and evaluated first.

Also verified while here, and pinned: missing/empty conclusions normalise to `CheckState::Unknown`, and Unknown is already grouped WITH failures rather than successes, so an absent conclusion was NOT being coerced to pass. A test now holds that.

Both tests call the real `classify_checks` with the operator's observed shape rather than injecting a disposition, because a hand-injected value is exactly how the last producer/consumer disagreement stayed hidden.

STILL OPEN, DELIBERATELY, PENDING AN OPERATOR POLICY DECISION (reported by message, not filed as work here):
- `mergeStateStatus` is never consulted anywhere in the source; BLOCKED alone cannot disqualify a row.
- Candidate admission does not consult CI at all: eligibility for an unqueued PR is merge-compatibility only, so 2276 was not classified ready by misreading its checks, it was classified ready without looking at them.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0
spoken_name: hard failure masked by pending checks

title: Exhausted operation deadline is reported as a command failure
description:
Live report from cacophony on v0.0.21. A `cara sync --all` tick ran to the end of its `max_duration_secs: 3600` budget and then failed with:

    cara rebase_command_failed: could not run isolated cumulative rebase command
    "source": "`git fetch --quiet --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head --refmap= origin
               refs/heads/main` exceeded its 285ms deadline and was terminated"

The command did not fail. The operation deadline was exhausted, and `effective_timeout` in src/command.rs only refused when the remaining budget was *exactly zero*. Any positive sliver was passed through as a real timeout, so a network fetch was launched with 285ms to live, reaped, and reported as a command failure.

That sends a reader to debug git or provider latency when the actual cause is budget: the tick consumed its full hour. The error must name the deadline, not the command.

Fix: introduce a minimum viable command budget. Below it, refuse with the existing exhaustion shape and a message that states how much remained, what the floor is, and which knobs move it (`sync.max_duration_secs` up, or `sync.max_candidates_per_tick` down). 750ms is chosen to be under any real local git invocation while still well above the sliver range where a launch is guaranteed waste.

Context from the same report: initial discovery alone took 51,741ms for 15 unqueued PRs, so a fleet of that size genuinely approaches an hour of work per tick. The budget refusal is correct; only its explanation was wrong.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: Make persist_auto_skip atomic: orphaned caravan-join-skipped labels without receipts become permanent exclusions
description:
## Problem

Cara can permanently exclude a pull request when `persist_auto_skip` partially succeeds.

Current provider write order in `sync.rs` is non-atomic:

1. `provider.add_label(..., AUTO_ADMISSION_SKIP_LABEL)` writes the skip label.
2. `provider.ensure_marked_comment(..., marker, body)` writes the receipt.

Both calls return immediately on error. If the label succeeds and the receipt/comment fails, the pull request is left with a `caravan-join-skipped`/auto-admission-skip label but no Cara receipt.

On later ticks, Cara correctly refuses to remove a skip label without a receipt because it cannot distinguish its own orphaned partial write from a deliberate operator hold:

```text
left a foreign admission skip alone: no Cara receipt, so the label is not ours to remove
```

The fail-closed protection from `bd-239640` is correct and must remain: Cara must not strip genuinely foreign/operator-owned labels. The defect is that Cara can itself create a state indistinguishable from a foreign hold and then cannot recover it.

## Evidence

- `persist_auto_skip` in `sync.rs` writes the label before the marked receipt/comment.
- `#2216` provides a positive control: the same receipt query path finds four receipts.
- `#2245`, `#2259`, and `#2314` carry skip labels with zero Cara receipts.
- Repo-wide marker search finds only two PRs with the expected receipt marker, proving the machinery has succeeded for some writes and failed for others.
- Event timing for two affected PRs indicates machine-driven cycles, not isolated manual edits:
  - `#2245`: labelled 23:57:09, unlabelled 00:02:44, labelled 00:07:04, then never recovered.
  - `#2259`: labelled 23:57:10, unlabelled 00:02:54, labelled 00:07:05, then never recovered.
- The paired one-second label events support a shared automated writer. The intervening unlabel events show stale-receipt cleanup working for an earlier cycle; the later relabels lack recoverable receipts.

The exact provider error that interrupted the receipt write is not yet established. This bead tracks the atomicity/idempotency defect, not a guessed transport cause.

## Required behavior

- Make admission-skip persistence transactional or compensating so a failed receipt write cannot leave an unrecoverable Cara-owned skip label.
- Persist enough durable ownership/idempotency evidence before or alongside provider mutation that Cara can recognise and reconcile its own partial writes after retries, crashes, transport ambiguity, and delayed provider visibility.
- Preserve fail-closed handling of genuinely foreign/operator-owned skip labels; do not solve this by blindly removing labels that lack receipts.
- Repeated execution must be idempotent: it must not duplicate comments, oscillate labels, or convert an operator hold into Cara-owned state.
- Provide a bounded recovery path for existing orphaned cases such as `#2245`, `#2259`, and `#2314`, based on exact provenance rather than manual label toggling or guesswork.
- Emit structured evidence distinguishing: fully persisted skip, partial write detected, compensation attempted, compensation succeeded/failed, foreign label preserved, and owned orphan reconciled.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A test injects failure after the label write and before receipt persistence; the next retry or reconciliation deterministically reaches a safe recoverable state.
2. A test injects failure before the label write, after receipt preparation, and during provider retry/delayed visibility; no permanent exclusion or duplicate receipt results.
3. A foreign skip label with no Cara ownership evidence remains untouched, preserving the `bd-239640` safety contract.
4. An orphan created by Cara is distinguishable from a foreign hold and can be repaired automatically or through an exact audited recovery operation.
5. Existing skip/receipt success paths remain idempotent across repeated sync ticks.
6. Structured receipts make partial provider writes and eventual recovery visible without requiring inference from mutable label state alone.

## Operator context

Filed at P0 by authenticated operator-proxy direction after the second Caravan root cause was traced. No PR labels or queue membership were mutated while filing this bead.
creator: helsinki:cacophony:helsinki-cacophony-bead-filer

title: Release workflow schedules an aarch64-darwin job no runner can ever accept
description:
Every release since v0.0.11 has required a manual `just release-backfill-target <tag> aarch64-darwin`, nine consecutive times. The cause is not flaky infrastructure.

`.github/workflows/release.yml` pins the darwin leg to `runs-on: [self-hosted, nix, aarch64-darwin]`. Queried live, the repository has seven registered runners and every one is Linux X64:

    caravan-ms-dev, caravan-ms-dev-2..6, caravan-pocket4
    labels: self-hosted,nix,Linux,X64,x86_64-linux,nixos,<host>

No runner advertises `aarch64-darwin`. The job is unschedulable by construction: it queues until the run is cancelled or times out, and the release run never reaches a terminal state. `fail-fast: false` makes this present as an indefinite hang rather than a failure, which is why it read as flakiness for nine releases.

Second, smaller issue: the `aarch64-linux` leg pins `runs-on: [self-hosted, nix, ms-dev-2]`, a single host. When ms-dev-2 is busy (it was at filing time) that leg queues behind unrelated work. That one is slow rather than broken, and the pin is deliberate since only ms-dev-2 advertises aarch64 in Nix extra-platforms, so it should stay pinned unless another host gains that capability.

Remedy: stop scheduling a leg no machine can accept. Either register a darwin runner, or drop the matrix entry and make the documented `just release-backfill-target` path the contract, so a release run concludes honestly instead of hanging on an impossible job. A workflow that cannot succeed should not be presented as pending.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: Add CLI manual decision mode with an interactive shell
description:
## Operator goal

Provide a human-operated way to exercise Cara's full decision/recovery flow without turning production machine hooks into PTY sessions.

## Product surface

Add a CLI-only mode such as:

```text
cara loop --manual [--shell 'zsh -i']
```

or an equivalent explicit `sync --manual` driver. Normal hooks remain noninteractive machine integration.

## Required behavior

- Run the ordinary bounded `sync --all` tick. Healthy/waiting/held/retry outcomes retain normal behavior.
- On `wake_class=external_decision`, persist the complete bounded decision event to a secure temporary/durable file and expose `CARA_DECISION_FILE` plus event/operation/repository/caravan/PR/session continuation variables.
- Checkpoint and release the repository operation lock before launching anything interactive.
- Launch the configured shell with inherited stdin/stdout/stderr and a real controlling TTY, from the exact safe affected checkout or Cara-owned repair workspace when one exists. Refuse non-TTY, JSON, MCP, daemon, or hosted noninteractive invocation rather than degrading silently.
- Do not infer resolution from shell exit alone. Zero exit triggers full provider rediscovery and another sync tick; nonzero exits manual mode while preserving evidence. Exact repair publication still uses `repair continue`, provider head/target checks, and non-force branch rules.
- Bound/recover temporary decision files, redact secrets, preserve a manual-session audit receipt, and handle signals/terminal restoration.
- Document suggested shell helpers for inspecting JSON with `jq`, running tests, invoking authorized repair, and exiting to retry.

Tests should cover inherited TTY and cwd, lock release, decision-file integrity, zero/nonzero exit, signal handling, stale provider movement while shell is open, repair workspace continuation, recursive hook avoidance, and refusal from MCP/noninteractive environments.

Existing hooks already receive JSON on stdin and are synchronously awaited with timeout/blocking policy. Production repair scripts may submit durable agents and poll until exact resolution; this feature is only the human flow-testing/controller surface.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:harryaskham

title: cara status caravans field is live state but reads as history: three agents in three days concluded no caravan ever formed while 23 had merged
description:
`cara status` reports a `caravans` field that is CURRENT IN-FLIGHT STATE, and multiple readers across multiple days have read it as HISTORY. The field is correct; the question it invites is wrong; and because it is correct, re-measuring confirms it beautifully and never reveals the error.

THE CONCRETE HARM, DOCUMENTED

  caravans: []  MEANS  no caravan currently exists
                READ AS  no caravan has ever formed

On 2026-07-30 a controller asserted "no caravan has ever formed on this repository" at least six times, including inside two durable incident-hold records, on the strength of repeated `cara status` reads all returning []. When the field later became [{"id":2287,"members":[2287]}] the same controller "retracted" the claim and reported a first-ever formation - which was the identical misreading arriving at a different value.

BOTH STATEMENTS WERE FALSE. Measured with a must-not-fire control:
  merged PRs with label:caravan          23
  earliest                               PR2008, merged 2026-07-18T01:38:58Z
  latest                                 PR2234, merged 2026-07-28T17:27:45Z
  control label:zzz-no-such-label         0   (the filter discriminates)
Caravans had been forming for ELEVEN DAYS throughout.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS IN THREE DAYS, across three different agents and three different fields, identified by helsinki-cacophony-caco-profile-hel-0:
  cara status caravans:[]   answers NOW, read as EVER   (2026-07-30)
  label:caravan census      answers NOW, read as EVER   (router, 2026-07-28, retracted within the hour)
  incident-hold active query answers NOW, read as EVER  (bd-7d0eda)

WHY RETRACTING INSTANCES DOES NOT WORK. The router published this claim fleet-wide on 28 July and retracted it the same hour; a second agent retracted their amplification. Two days later a third agent regenerated the identical conclusion independently, from a DIFFERENT wrong instrument, with no knowledge of the earlier episode. A claim with a live generator is not a claim in the record - it is a claim in the world - and correcting the record leaves the generator running.

SUGGESTED FIX, and it is small: make the field self-describing at the point of reading. Something of the shape

  "caravans": []   with an adjacent note: none currently; live state, not history

or a sibling field naming where history lives. Any annotation that distinguishes "none now" from "none ever" at the moment of reading would have prevented all six assertions above plus the two earlier instances, because in every case the reader had the correct value in front of them.

WHY AN ANNOTATION AND NOT DOCUMENTATION: the signature of this class is that the field is CORRECT, so nothing prompts doubt and no amount of care or repetition helps. Documentation is consulted by people who suspect a problem. This class produces no suspicion.

WHERE HISTORY ACTUALLY LIVES, for anyone hitting this: the merged-PR record with label:caravan, and labeling EVENTS with timestamps. A useful discriminator from the same agent - a label applied to an OPEN PR is live admission (PR2287, labelled 16 minutes after creation), whereas a label applied AFTER merge is retrospective tagging (PR2234, labelled 63m43s post-merge) and is not a membership record.

Filed by helsinki-cacophony-caco-ctrl. The class was identified by helsinki-cacophony-caco-profile-hel-0, who declined to file on the grounds that cara is not their surface. I am the controller who made the six false assertions, so this is filed against my own error rather than reported about someone else's. Dedup: caravan board scanned via --title-contains for status, caravans, field and history; all matching beads are CLOSED and none concerns state-versus-history semantics.

THE QUESTION-SIDE CHECK, contributed by helsinki-cacophony-caco-profile-hel-0. This is the part the rest of this bead was missing, because every defence described above is answer-side.

THE HOLE, STATED PLAINLY. The standard verification disciplines all validate the ANSWER:

  must-fire / must-not-fire control   validates the instrument
  repeat, genuinely spaced            validates against intermittency
  denominator / saturation test       validates the population was non-empty
  superset versus subset arithmetic   validates internal consistency
  read the fields you did not ask for validates against projection at collection

NOT ONE LOOKS AT THE QUESTION. All five confirm that the answer received is the answer the system holds - which is exactly what a CORRECT state field gives you, six times in a row, while you are asking it something it cannot answer.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS MONOTONICITY: A HISTORICAL FIELD CANNOT DECREASE, A STATE FIELD CAN.

  caravans: []                 can go non-empty then empty     STATE    cannot answer "ever"
  merged PRs with label        only ever grows                 HISTORY  can answer "ever"
  active incident holds        can go 2 -> 1                   STATE
  labeling EVENTS w/ timestamp append-only                     HISTORY
  bead description_len         can shrink on edit              STATE
  git commit log               append-only                     HISTORY

SO THE CHECK, BEFORE ASKING ANY FIELD A HISTORICAL QUESTION, IS ONE THOUGHT EXPERIMENT: CAN I CONSTRUCT A CASE WHERE THIS VALUE GOES DOWN? If yes, it is live state and cannot answer "ever" no matter how carefully it is read.

IT FIRES ON ALL THREE DOCUMENTED INSTANCES. The caravans field going non-empty then empty is not hypothetical - it did exactly that during this incident, and that transition is what was misread as a first-ever formation. A label being REMOVED during repair is a separately observed behaviour. A hold LAPSING is separately observed. In every case the value can decrease, so in every case the field was state and the question was historical.

WHY THIS ONE IS CHEAP ENOUGH TO ACTUALLY GET USED: it requires no call, no control, and no knowledge of the implementation. It runs BEFORE the query rather than after - which is the whole point, because the failure mode documented in this bead is precisely one that after-the-fact discipline cannot touch. IT IS THE ONLY DEFENCE IN THIS SET THAT EXECUTES BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT.

LIMITS, STATED BY ITS AUTHOR RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER: it is a heuristic, not a proof. A monotone-looking field can still be reset by an operator. A state field that happens never to decrease will pass and mislead. And it does not tell you WHICH historical surface to use instead - that still requires knowing the event log exists. It catches the framing error, not the whole problem.

THIS DOES NOT REPLACE THE PROPOSED FIX. An annotation on the field is still the durable remedy, because it works on readers who never think to run any check at all. The monotonicity test is what a careful reader can do TODAY, unaided, while the annotation does not exist.

title: No recipe runs the validation CI actually runs, so every gate is a hand-rolled subset
description:
CI validates with an exact five-command block, and the justfile has a recipe for none of it:

    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
    cargo test --all
    cargo run -- help
    cargo run -- mcp tools >/dev/null

So every contributor hand-rolls a subset before publishing, and a subset is what a hand-rolled gate always is. Mine was `--lib`, `--test cli_exit`, `--test v1_parity` plus all-target Clippy. It omitted `--bin cara`, and that is precisely where the v0.0.59 release failed: a global `--repo` collided with the repeatable `--repo` on `web`, clap rejected the command tree, and `cara web` could not be constructed at all. The tag was published with no assets.

Both `cargo run -- help` and `cargo run -- mcp tools` would also have caught it immediately, since neither can run without a constructable command tree. I was running none of the three checks that detect this class.

The local run and the CI run were both correct about what they measured; they simply measured different things. That gap is the defect, not the individual omission, because the next person hand-rolls a different subset and misses something else.

Adds a `validate` recipe that runs CI's block verbatim in the pinned development shell, so local and CI agree by construction rather than by memory. Also adds `validate-fast` for the inner loop, explicitly documented as NOT sufficient before publication.

title: Comment each actual Caravan force-push with one line explaining the rewrite
description:
After every actual Caravan branch rewrite, post one short one-line PR comment explaining why Caravan force-pushed the branch. Do not post on no-op rediscovery.

WHY

Until GitHub App mode exists, every provider event is attributed to the operator's shared identity. The first stack showed timeline events such as:

    harryaskham force-pushed <branch> from 3753825 to 7fb30b3

There is no provider-visible indication that Caravan performed it or why it happened. Even with App identity, the reason remains valuable.

VISIBLE CONTRACT

Exactly one visible line, for example:

    Caravan updated this branch because parent #2331 advanced (3753825 → cce82ef).

Reason vocabulary is typed and bounded, not arbitrary prose:

- joined caravan behind parent #N
- parent #N advanced
- current default advanced
- parent #N was evicted
- caravan was reshaped/repaired
- explicit reviewed repair, with operation ID

Include short old/new OIDs only where useful. Keep the rendered line under a small fixed byte limit. No multi-paragraph plan/receipt dump.

MUTATION/IDEMPOTENCY CONTRACT

- Post only after an exact branch push succeeds and only when `RebaseReceipt.already_satisfied == false`.
- No comment for dry-run, planning, failed preflight, failed push, or unchanged exact generation.
- Cover every first-party rewrite path: sync, join/rejoin, eviction unwind, reshape, and reviewed repair.
- A provider retry must not duplicate the line. Use a same-line hidden marker keyed by repository, PR, old OID, new OID, and operation/reason, or an equivalent durable outbox. The GitHub-rendered content remains one visible line.
- A comment failure after push cannot roll back the branch. Return a typed partial-mutation receipt with the exact pushed generation and pending comment. A later tick retries the missing comment without rewriting the branch.
- Comment posting consumes the exact GitHub request/mutation budget and never steals capacity reserved for mandatory topology convergence without reporting continuation.
- Human/JSON/MCP receipts expose reason, comment status, and whether branch/provider writes occurred.

REASON PROVENANCE

Thread the reason from the planner/operation that authorized the rewrite. Do not infer it afterward solely from branch names. The reason is part of the immutable prepared generation so the applied comment cannot disagree with the exact plan.

TESTS

- Actual parent advance posts exactly one one-line comment with parent PR and old/new short OIDs.
- Initial join, default advance, eviction, and reshape select their correct typed reasons.
- Already-satisfied, dry-run, preflight failure, and push failure post nothing.
- Retry after successful push does not duplicate a successful comment.
- Retry after comment failure posts the pending line without another force-push.
- Concurrent operations under exact leases cannot attach one operation's reason to another generation.
- Output stays one visible line and within the byte bound.
- App-authenticated mode renders the same content from `caravan[bot]`; local mode preserves content even though provider actor is the shared user.

title: Fail just stress when the filter matches no tests

title: Cara empty-diff join replays another reintegration patch onto caller branch
description:
Operator reproduction on 2026-07-21 exposed cross-reintegration patch contamination while joining Cacophony branch `fix-cara-timeouts` into the active Caravan/Cara tail. The intended operator change was `fix cara timeoutes`, but before that commit was added, Cara/Cacophony synthesized daemon-authored commit `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680` on `fix-cara-timeouts` with the complete, unrelated update-helper `release: v1.2.1562` patch and release-agent provenance.

Exact evidence:

- True GitHub `main` independently and correctly contains release commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7`, parent `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`; annotated tag `v1.2.1562` peels to it.
- The active Cara tail/base branch `fix-slackiq-nodes` is `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, also parented by `80bf4eac` and carrying the separate `fix ms agent scope` patch.
- Cara-created/reused PR https://github.com/harryaskham/cacophony/pull/2080 targets `fix-slackiq-nodes` from `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- Its first commit is `ac701198`, parent `c059bf15`, authored by Cacophony Daemon at 23:04:11Z. Its title/body were initially `release: v1.2.1562` and copied update-helper identity/head `e3026e0461`, despite the operator working on `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- `ac701198` contains only the unrelated release metadata patch (`Cargo.toml`, twenty workspace entries in `Cargo.lock`, and `CHANGELOG.md`). It is a duplicate replay of the patch already landed on true main as `d9fad17e`.
- The operator's intended `fix cara timeoutes` commit `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633` was subsequently added on top of the contaminated release commit; live PR 2080 therefore now contains both `.caravan/config.yaml` and the unrelated release patch.

The operator reports Cara first observed an empty diff while he was on `fix-cara-timeouts`, then created PR 2080 and inferred/replayed the diff from main to the Caravan tail. An empty caller patch must never fall back to another agent's most recent reintegration patch, global generation, main-to-tail delta, or stale receipt.

Required behavior:

- Bind join materialization to the exact caller owner, source branch/head, expected base/tail, and patch identity receipt.
- If the caller's patch against the selected tail is empty, return an explicit empty/no-op/refusal receipt; do not mutate the caller branch and do not create a PR.
- Refuse when receipt owner/head/patch differs from the branch being joined, even if a recent reintegration has a reusable-looking diff or commit message.
- Preserve the caller branch on any ambiguity and surface exact candidate provenance for diagnosis.
- Add a regression test with two concurrent patches: release patch A lands on main while operator branch B joins an active tail with an initially empty diff; B must never receive A.

Do not mutate or close PR 2080 as part of triage; preserve it as live evidence until the owner chooses repair.

description:

The supported repair workspace now starts correctly but cannot complete or resume when an ordinary authenticated SSH clone exceeds the global 30-second command budget.

## Required outcome

- Give clone/fetch/materialization a dedicated bounded timeout appropriate for real repositories, separately configurable from lightweight Cara subprocesses. Report elapsed and configured budgets in typed errors.
- Record clone phase, PID/process-group, provider URL identity, exact PR head/target, partial path, and cleanup/resume state before starting external work.
- Make an exact `preparing` manifest with no workspace safely resumable: retry or continue must verify repository/PR/head/target/config/provider identity, then resume or restart only the incomplete clone without duplicating provider mutation.
- Ensure timeout kills/reaps the full clone process group and leaves no live child, lock, or ambiguous partial checkout.
- Where safe, support a canonical provider checkout/object-cache/alternates source so repair does not always require a cold network clone, while preserving exact provider remote verification and isolation from dirty managed checkouts.
- Add fixtures for a clone completing just beyond 30 seconds, a timed-out partial clone resumed successfully, head/target drift refusal, confirmed abort, and repeated exact retry idempotency.
- `repair status` must show the typed phase/error and exact resume/abort command. No raw Git guidance.
- Prove canonical packaged-binary repair start/status/abort on the fixture and publish a landed SHA/version before caco-merger retries live PR #1962.

Implementation ready at commits bfc9302 + 97e8fef on true main 157ebd3. Adds strict `repair.materialization_timeout_secs` default 180s; durable Preparing/Cloning/FetchingHead/FetchingTarget/CheckingOut/Merging/Resolving/Committed/Published/SyncPending/Completed phases; bounded phase error with elapsed/budget/process-group/partial path/next; ProcessRunner timeout process-group receipt; preparing session status with no workspace; exact restart that revalidates repo/PR/head/base/target/provider/config, removes only canonical incomplete clone, and resumes. Existing v1 live manifest fields default/migrate on exact resume. Full 215 lib + 6 bin + 7 CLI + 3 parity tests, strict all-target Clippy, canonical rustfmt, Nix flake 34 checks, Cara 0.0.2/repair help/missing-session packaged smoke all green. No provider mutation or raw guidance; drift still refuses. Ready for canonical reintegration and live session `pr-1962-05fe82fe80c6` retry after landed SHA.

## Landed true-main receipt — 2026-07-19

Canonical reintegration landed at exact GitHub/main SHA `35dffd1488efae1402dc2106987005f1d89641e9` (squash contains branch commits `bfc9302` + `97e8fef`). `gh compare 35dffd1...main` returned identical at close; daemon canonical checkout was clean/aligned at the same SHA. The packaged app reports `cara 0.0.2`; `repair --help` exposes start/continue/status/abort; missing-session packaged status returns typed `repair_session_not_found`. Full 215 library + 6 binary + 7 CLI + 3 parity tests, strict all-target/all-feature Clippy, canonical rustfmt, and Nix flake 34 checks passed. Exact recovery proofs include `repair.materialization_timeout_secs=180`, durable clone phase/error elapsed+budget+process-group+partial path, preparing manifest inspection with no workspace, and exact preparing-session restart after provider/head/base/target/config verification. Caco-merger was sent the landed SHA and instructed to inspect old session `pr-1962-05fe82fe80c6`, first-party abort it because target main drifted from `23369cbb` to `90bebd5c`, then run one wrapper-sanitized fresh `repair start --pr 1962`; no raw Git fallback.

## Reopened live acceptance — persistent SSH sideband failure

Deployed `35dffd1` passed wrapper status and created a fresh exact session for PR1962 head `05fe82fe` targeting current main `90bebd5c`. Both start and exact same-session resume used the new ~180s materialization budget, then failed `fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet`. Each process group was reaped, manifest remained preparing/cloning, provider_mutated=false, and merger correctly stopped without a third attempt/raw fallback. Timeout/resume behavior is correct, but cold full provider SSH clone is not viable. Reopen to implement the bead's remaining supported canonical provider-checkout/object-cache reuse (or alternate authenticated transport), bound it to repository/session/head/target, retain exact remote verification, and prove live PR1962 materialization without a cold clone.

Caco-merger independently verified Caravan bd-9264d0 deployment before retrying PR #1962:

The longer timeout/resume work is functioning as designed, but a full cold SSH clone remains unusable under a persistent provider sideband disconnect. Repeating the same full clone is not a recovery strategy.

## Required outcome

- Replace full cold clone with minimal exact materialization where supported: initialize the isolated repository and fetch only the recorded PR head and target/base OIDs/refs, preferably with provider-supported partial/blobless filtering and no checkout until verification.
- Make the partial repository resumable in place after transport interruption. A same-session retry must reuse already received verified objects rather than deleting and retransferring the whole repository.

- Optionally seed from a canonical verified provider checkout or shared object cache/alternates, but re-read the configured provider remote and exact head/target before use; never trust daemon-internal refs as publication proof.
- Use bounded SSH keepalive/low-speed/progress settings where appropriate, with no unbounded loops and no global SSH/Git config mutation.
- Preserve existing process-group reap, manifest atomicity, exact identity/drift checks, abort semantics, and no-provider-mutation guarantee.
- Add fixtures where the first fetch disconnects mid-sideband and exact resume completes from partial objects, plus head/target drift refusal and repeated-disconnect bounded failure.

Provider refs/OIDs remain re-read before/after; local cache is content-only, never publication authority. Exact preparing resume retains a valid partial repository and received objects in place; only invalid canonical partial state is removed after path/manifest validation. Sideband disconnects classify as `repair_provider_transport_disconnect` with in-place resume, process-group, elapsed/budget, partial path, and provider_mutated=false. Added tests for cache/provider remote separation despite dirty caller/internal origin, cache Git identity drift refusal, sideband classification, valid partial repo reuse marker, no-workspace resume, timeout process group, plus all prior scope/head/parent/non-force/abort guards. Full 218 lib + 6 bin + 7 CLI + 3 parity tests, strict all-target Clippy, canonical fmt, Nix flake, Cara 0.0.2/version/repair-help all green. Ready for canonical land and one wrapper-sanitized live PR1962 status/abort/fresh-start retry; no raw fallback.

## Object-cache extension landed receipt — 2026-07-19

Canonical true main is `94687c4ef532fc2e5bd98d2f3dc657027c019f25` (squash contains `1a176a0` + `da62093`), and `gh compare 94687c4...main` returned identical. Canonical checkout is clean/aligned. Exact main contains `SeedingObjectCache`, protocol-v2 `--filter=blob:none` exact fetch, valid partial repository reuse, cache Git identity checks, SSH keepalive bounds, and `repair_provider_transport_disconnect`. Full 218 lib + 6 bin + 7 CLI + 3 parity tests, strict all-target Clippy, canonical fmt, Nix flake, and packaged Cara 0.0.2/help smoke passed. This SHA supersedes the earlier 35dffd1 deployment for live PR1962 repair materialization; caco-merger may perform one wrapper-sanitized first-party retry after inspecting/aborting any stale manifested target. ## Post-land resume guard correction

Before authorizing live retry on `94687c4`, review found the preserved pre-94687c partial workspace may be a valid Git repository with provider `origin` but lacks the new canonical `cache` remote/alternates. Treating it as reusable would skip object-cache seeding and repeat the failing provider-only transfer. No live retry was authorized on 94687c4.

Post-94687c4 review caught one migration edge before live retry: a preserved pre-object-cache partial clone can have a valid Git repository and provider `origin` but no canonical `cache` remote, so 94687c4 could incorrectly reuse it and repeat provider-only transfer. Commit `6065238` requires both exact provider origin and exact freshly canonicalized cache remote before any partial workspace is reused; otherwise only the validated canonical partial path is removed and re-seeded from cache. Focused cache-bound reuse test, full 218 lib + 6 bin + 7 CLI + 3 parity suite, strict Clippy/fmt, and Nix flake green. No live retry authorized until this guard lands and supersedes 94687c4.

title: Refuse interactive mutations in hosted web worker mode
description:
Child of bd-b15483, hardening the hosted mode landed in 4f8421f.

Problem: interactive dashboard mutations are gated only by `read_only`. Hosted mode forbids `read_only` (it requires `--webhook-sync`), so `cara web --hosted` currently accepts same-origin POST /api/action mutations from anyone who can reach the operator TLS proxy. The `csrf_token` is served by GET /api/state and is same-origin protection, not authentication. Loopback local mode is unaffected because only the local operator can reach it.

Fix: a hosted worker mutates only in response to HMAC-verified webhook deliveries. Refuse interactive mutating actions when hosted, with a distinct typed code (`web_hosted_interactive_mutation_refused`) separate from `web_read_only`, so the reason is unambiguous. Non-mutating actions (check/plan/refresh) remain available for observability. Do not add an opt-in escape hatch; an operator who wants an interactive console runs ordinary local `cara web` over a tunnel.

Tests: hosted dashboard refuses each mutating action class with the exact code; hosted dashboard still permits non-mutating actions; hosted webhook-driven sync still performs bounded work (proving the fix does not neuter hosted mode); local non-hosted parity unchanged.

Docs: state plainly that hosted mode is webhook-driven and never an unauthenticated remote mutation surface, and that Caravan does not rely on the operator proxy for authentication of mutations.

title: Make Cara self-update replace the active PATH-visible binary
description:
During the deterministic scheduler session, `cara self-update status` reported install target `~/.local/bin/cara` while the active binary resolved to `~/.cargo/bin/cara`; `~/.local/bin` was absent from PATH. Even after the private-release bootstrap fix in v0.0.2, a successful update could therefore promote a binary that the shell never executes.

Define and test a deterministic install-location contract: either configure Cara's updater to replace the active stable user installation safely, require an explicit install dir, or make status/run fail closed when the promoted path is not PATH-visible or is shadowed by an older binary. Preserve protection against overwriting development binaries such as `target/debug/cara`. Include a migration/bootstrap path for the existing cargo-bin installation.

Related live evidence: active version 0.0.1 at `~/.cargo/bin/cara`; updater target `~/.local/bin/cara`; private v0.0.2 assets exist and authenticated `gh release download` succeeds. Filed via reflect-session from the operator-directed deterministic Cara scheduler session.

2026-07-21 burn-down triage: promoted after the ready set emptied. First audit current updatable-cli behavior and existing v0.0.5 installation surfaces; close as already fixed only with executable/PATH proof, otherwise implement fail-closed active-install targeting without touching development binaries.

title: Keep released Cara compatible when config adds sync policy
description:
## Live blocker

Current Cacophony main contains a `.caravan/config.yaml` `sync:` policy block. The released Cara 0.0.6 binary fails before any read-only status or sync operation:

`parse .caravan/config.yaml: unknown field sync, expected version/force_merge/rebase_on_join/agent_priority_labels/command_timeout_secs/repair/loop/journal/hooks`

This is another config-before-reader rollout break: existing deployed Cara cannot inspect or operate a repository after the config source advances.

## Required behavior

- Define a rolling-upgrade-safe config contract for newly added policy sections.
- Released readers must either tolerate unknown additive sections safely, or the repository must fail closed before landing config that requires a newer declared minimum Cara version.
- Add an explicit config schema/version or `min_cara_version` capability gate with a typed upgrade message.
- Cacophony's pinned Cara runtime and config must advance atomically; deterministic CI must verify reader/config compatibility before merge.
- Preserve strict rejection for misspelled or security-sensitive keys; do not globally ignore arbitrary unknown fields without an audited extension mechanism.
- Add fixtures proving old-reader/new-config and new-reader/old-config behavior across a rolling deployment.

## Immediate acceptance

Provide a reviewed Cara release/pin that can parse the current `sync` block, then re-run canonical Cacophony status/sync without modifying provider state.

Pocket4 live compatibility receipt 2026-07-22: after operator restored GitHub auth, same owner po4-3 published Cacophony PR #2086 exact head 4a1d3330522aea488fc77e2467669d35f61de62f. pr_cara_join refused typed published_unjoined before Cara mutation because lifecycle expected reviewed Cara 0.0.5 while Pocket4 runtime remained 0.0.4. Provider source PR is OPEN/MERGEABLE, labels empty, no Cara membership/auto-merge; exact refusal receipt preserved. Acceptance must include reviewed release/pin rollout and per-node version proof (including Pocket4) before same-PR normal retry, with no cross-owner/direct/force fallback.

Runtime rollout clarification: Cacophony workers resolve Cara through the reviewed project flake/devshell/runtime pin; an installed or self-updated binary is canonical only when version and digest match that reviewed pin and config compatibility. Pocket4 receiving Cara 0.0.6 does not unblock current Cacophony sync because 0.0.6 rejects the sync policy. Workers may stage `cara self-update run` for inspection when operator-authorized, but must not silently use an unreviewed latest binary for managed queue mutations. Advance Cara release, Cacophony lock/runtime pins, and config compatibility atomically; otherwise await the reviewed version.

Pocket4 second successor receipt 2026-07-22: owner po4-2 published core heartbeat-control PR #2090 exact head 0dda835d0b7129dbd83bbf43d8c43469c6c4b193, explicitly succeeding immutable PR2085. pr_cara_join held published_unjoined because Pocket4 pinned Cara0.0.4 vs expected0.0.5; provider_mutated_by_cara=false; dead letter rdl-019f87cb-7079-7220-ade1-fd0b8bb7526d; idempotency 2a1b7e97. Preserve lineage PR2085 -> PR2090 and exact heads. After compatible Caco/Cara deployment, same-owner retry order is PR2085 root then PR2090 child. This is migration retry acceptance, not full fresh canary. No fallback.

title: The new global --repo collides with the repeatable --repo on web
description:
`bd-3c0d9e` added a global `--repo`. `web` already declares `#[arg(long = "repo", required = true)]` on a REPEATABLE `Vec<PathBuf>`. Clap rejects duplicate long names when it builds the command tree, so `cara web` became unconstructable and the v0.0.59 release run failed on the `release contract` job before any artifact was built.

HOW I MISSED IT, which is the part worth keeping. I verified the new global on `status`, `check` and `log`, and verified it appeared in top-level `--help`. I never ran it against `web` — the one subcommand that already had the flag, and the entire reason the bead existed. My own bead text says "`cara web` takes `--repo`". I read that sentence, wrote the global, and did not test the collision it directly implies.

The gate missed it too, and that is mechanical rather than careless: the two failing tests are `--bin cara` tests, and my pre-publication validation runs `--lib`, `--test cli_exit` and `--test v1_parity`. The binary's own test target was never in the set, so a green local run and a red CI run were both correct about what they measured.

Fix: the single-repository global becomes `--repository`; `web` keeps its repeatable `--repo` unchanged, so no existing invocation breaks. A regression test now asserts the whole command tree is constructable AND that both spellings coexist, which is the property that actually failed.

Verified: 21 of 21 `--bin cara` tests pass, `cara --repository <path> status` works from an unrelated directory, and `cara web --help` shows `--repo` again.

title: Report degradation in the web health endpoint
description:
`GET /api/v1/health` reports only ok: true, schema_version, repository count, and start time. `ok` is a constant, so the endpoint can express "the process is answering" and nothing else.

That is a real operability gap for the hosted worker mode just made first-class, where the dashboard is a webhook-driven service behind an operator proxy and `/health` is what monitoring scrapes. Two failure modes are currently invisible:

- a repository whose status refresh keeps failing, including one that has never had a successful read (which, before the routing fix, also made it webhook-deaf);
- webhook deliveries silently stopping because a proxy, secret, or App installation changed, leaving the worker idle but apparently healthy.

Add structured, secret-free health detail: per-repository counts of never-refreshed and currently-erroring repositories plus the oldest successful refresh timestamp, and the existing webhook counters with the last received timestamp. Derive a `degraded` boolean from repositories that have never refreshed or are currently in error.

Keep `ok` meaning "serving" and add `degraded` alongside it rather than redefining `ok`, so existing alerting semantics do not silently change meaning under operators; document both. Report the hosted flag so a monitor can tell which contract the process is running under. Never include secrets, tokens, broker output, or raw provider errors beyond the existing typed code/message projection.

Tests: a healthy multi-repository dashboard is not degraded; a repository with no successful refresh is degraded and counted; a repository carrying a refresh error is degraded and counted; webhook counters and last-received time are reported; the payload contains no secret material.

title: Add an env override for sync.checkout_on_decision so unattended callers can disable decision-checkout without changing the interactive default
description:
Add an environment-variable override for `sync.checkout_on_decision` so a non-interactive caller can disable decision-checkout for its own invocation, without changing the default that interactive use depends on.

OPERATOR REQUEST, verbatim: "false would work for us. but true is useful for interactive. can it be disabled by an env var in the hook only?"

That is exactly the right shape. `sync.checkout_on_decision` defaults to TRUE, and that default is correct for interactive work - a human inspecting a decision wants the worktree left on the PR being discussed. It is wrong for a scheduled unattended sync, where the residue is pure hazard.

CONFIRMED AGAINST THE RUNNING BINARY (cara 0.0.51 on helsinki), not stale source. The env vars cara knows are:

    CARA_DECISION_FILE          CARA_EVENT              CARA_GITHUB_AUTH_KIND
    CARA_DECISION_CODE          CARA_EVENT_ID           CARA_PRS
    CARA_REPOSITORY_PATH        CARA_OPERATION_ID       CARA_SELF_UPDATE_INSTALL_DIR
    CARA_REPAIR_SESSION         CARA_CARAVAN_ID
    CARA_REPOSITORY

There is NO checkout-on-decision override. It would need adding.

WORTH NOTING: most of the list above are HOOK variables - values cara passes INTO hook processes. So the convention, the naming scheme and the plumbing all already exist. Something like `CARA_SYNC_CHECKOUT_ON_DECISION=false` would be idiomatic rather than novel.

WHY THIS IS WORTH DOING RATHER THAN JUST SETTING CONFIG FALSE:

  - Config is per-repository and shared. Setting `sync.checkout_on_decision: false` in
    `.caravan/config.yaml` would disable the behaviour for EVERY caller including
    interactive ones, which is precisely what the operator does not want.
  - The cron and an interactive operator use the SAME worktree and the SAME config file.
    There is currently no way to express "off for this invocation" - only "off for
    everyone" or "on for everyone".
  - An env override is the standard resolution for exactly this split, and cara already
    reads env in several places.

WHAT IT WOULD HAVE SAVED, measured tonight: the caravan sync worktree sat parked on a dead agent's PR branch. A manual `cara status` read that branch's config (`max_duration_secs: 65525`, deliberately set past the ceiling on commit e473cb91b) instead of main's valid 3600, and refused to start. I diagnosed a non-existent off-by-one in cara's validator, filed it P1, escalated it to six named agents as a one-character fix, and reported it to the operator for three hours as the thing gating PR #2308 and the helsinki daemon fix. All wrong.

An env override in the cron would have made the worktree's between-runs state deterministic and the whole episode impossible.

RELATED AND ALREADY IN FLIGHT: the operator has opened cacophony-config PR #41, which restores `caravan-main` after sync in BOTH the success and failure paths. That is a good fix and arguably better than what I first suggested - it preserves cara's ability to check out PRs for evaluation and removes only the residue, rather than disabling the mechanism. The env override would complement it by making the intent explicit at the call site rather than implicit in cleanup.

PRIOR ART ON THIS EXACT PROBLEM: bd-6c019f records the flag landing, and explicitly notes
"DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: cara does not automatically restore the base branch". That decision
is defensible. This bead does not ask to reverse it - it asks for the escape hatch to be
usable per-invocation.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:harryaskham

title: Add cara next --status with optional checkout
description:
Operator request: scheduler and cron systems (caco's in particular) have no good place to host one long-lived `cara loop`, so they need manual primitives to reconstruct the loop's routing themselves.

Agreed design, after reconciling against the existing surface:

- ONE verb with a status filter, not `next-conflicting` / `next-evicted` / `next-failing`. Three verbs means three copies of FIFO, priority and skip semantics that will drift.
- `cara next --status <set>` REPLACES `cara next-candidate` outright. It is early enough to be backwards incompatible, so no alias is kept. `--status ready` must return byte-identical selection to what sync admits, or two surfaces give agents different answers.
- JSON-based, not exit-code based. The caller parses the payload and moves itself; "no match" is a normal outcome carried in the JSON, never an error envelope, so a cron can distinguish "nothing to do" from "provider down".
- `--checkout` is an opt-in convenience on `cara next` and on `cara loop --manual`: it still returns the same JSON but moves the working tree to the selected branch, fetching as needed.

Two load-bearing constraints on `--checkout`:

1. It must route through `navigation::ensure_safe_worktree` and FAIL CLOSED on a dirty tree. A cron that clobbers uncommitted work is worse than one that does nothing.
2. The JSON must carry a receipt naming what it moved FROM and TO, so the move is auditable and reversible.

`--status skipped` must re-derive validity rather than trusting the label, because a skip is bound to the exact head it was proven against; a stale label would otherwise route agents at PRs that have since been force-pushed.

Documented as gap 2 in docs/lifecycle.md.
creator: ms-mac:caravan:ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-0

title: Own the full merge lifecycle: squash the passing head each tick
description: Operator direction 2026-07-27: native GitHub auto-merge will be disabled on the Cacophony repository because a member could be merged into the next caravan member rather than main, mixing two merge actors. Caravan must therefore own the whole lifecycle. On each sync tick, when the caravan root is the exact current head, is mechanically compatible with the default branch, and every required check on that exact head is passing, Cara must squash-merge it itself and then atomically advance the next member to target the default branch, in one reserved and idempotent plan. Requirements: exact-head and exact-base preconditions immediately before the merge, with zero-write refusal on any drift; no admin bypass on the ordinary path (the existing admin squash stays reserved for audited caravan-force); one merge per tick per caravan so ordering stays observable; the promotion must not be separable from the merge by a budget refusal, matching the bd-9ead1b promotion-atomicity requirement; typed receipts naming merged PR, merge commit, promoted successor, and its new base; and safe behaviour when auto-merge is still armed externally so Cara never races another actor. Also stop requiring squash auto-merge arming as a graph invariant once Cara owns merging, or the invariant will report a permanent problem on a repository that has deliberately disabled it. Add regressions for passing head merged and successor promoted in one tick, red head not merged, drifted head refused zero-write, and a repository with native auto-merge disabled reporting no auto_merge_invariant.

title: Add audited merge-preserving cumulative rewrite for nonlinear PR ranges
description:
Cacophony #1958 blocks real v0.0.5 queue drain after the external-default lease fix: exact head 6c895352849a4ed7f9ab44df7b068e09944c53da has six merge commits between retained base e1f87cd0f87b8523de08b2c2f7421fe75d672bf1 and head. Cara correctly refuses ordinary linear rebase with `rebase_nonlinear_range`; force/CI labels must not bypass this. Provide an explicit audited strategy for cumulative mode or an equally safe first-party transformation continuation.

If implementing merge preservation, plan the complete exact topology before writes (for example reviewed `--rebase-merges` semantics), retain candidate-only commits and merge relationships, reject external/cross-range parents or ambiguous octopus topology, prove resulting tree/parents/old-base/new-base, retain current-target ancestry and workflow trigger checks, and publish only the candidate head under exact force-with-lease. Multi-member descendants must consume the exact planned rewritten parent. No raw resets or flattening by guess.

Acceptance:
- Fixtures cover main merged into feature repeatedly, internal feature merges, external parent, octopus/ambiguous history, target advance, candidate-head race, and multi-member cumulative chain.
- Supported topology yields deterministic plan plus exact old/new topology/tree receipts and idempotent second tick waiting on fresh CI.
- Unsupported topology remains a zero-write external decision with actionable first-party recovery.
- Live acceptance against retained #1958 from a clean clone succeeds or returns a newly specific unsupported-topology decision; broad drain remains stopped until proven.
- Strict Clippy/fmt, full configured tests, Nix/release contract as appropriate, docs/help.

Live scope update: #1958 was subsequently admin-squash merged through one cluster-authorized, exact-head Cara force operation with rebase_on_join=false and auto-admission=false. The force path did not bypass nonlinear cumulative rewriting; it avoided that mode entirely after exact compatibility/head/base/default revalidation and mutated only the audited comment plus squash merge. Therefore this merge-preserving capability is no longer a live Cacophony drain blocker. Keep it as a future explicit strategy for nonlinear caravans, preserving all zero-write and lease safeguards.

title: A read-only command refuses to run over a bound only mutating paths use
description:
`cara status` is read-only and prints NOTHING — no caravan count, no candidates, no admission state, no problems — when `sync.max_duration_secs` is out of range. Verified:

    $ cara status --config <config with max_duration_secs: 65525>
    cara: sync.max_duration_secs must be between 1 and 3600

STATUS DOES NOT USE THAT VALUE. Grepping `read.rs`, the only reference is at line 854, where it is COPIED INTO THE OUTPUT as a config echo. Nothing in status bounds, budgets, or decides anything on it. A value status merely reports is preventing status from reporting anything.

THE COST IS MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. An operator spent roughly three hours today concluding that Cara had an off-by-one gating the entire merge queue, escalated it to six agents, and filed a P1. The actual cause was a worktree parked on a branch whose config said 65525. Their own retraction names this as the reason it was hard to see: with `cara status` silent, there was no way to observe that the fleet was fine and only the config read was wrong. Working observability would have shown a healthy queue immediately and pointed at the config rather than the code.

DESIGN, and the important part is what NOT to relax. Do not make validation lenient generally: a config that fails structural validation, an unsupported version, a malformed priority label, or a required upgrade, should still refuse everywhere. The distinction is narrower:

  OPERATIONAL BOUNDS are values only the MUTATING paths consume, currently the
  sync budgets (`max_duration_secs`, `max_candidates_per_tick`, `max_mutations_per_tick`,
  `max_github_requests_per_tick`). A read-only command neither reads nor honours them.

  Read-only commands (`status`, `check`, `queue`, `show`, `log`, `plan`) should proceed when
  ONLY an operational bound is invalid, echo the raw configured value truthfully rather than
  clamping or defaulting it, and surface the violation as a reported problem in their own
  output. `sync`, `loop`, and the membership commands must keep refusing exactly as now.

WHY ECHO THE RAW VALUE: substituting a default would make status report `3600` for a config
that says `65525`, which is a new instance of the same class this whole bead is about — a
field that reads as one thing and means another.

NOT STARTED DELIBERATELY. This is a change to config validation, which is safety-critical,
and it wants a careful pass rather than being appended to a long session. The evidence and
the design are recorded here so whoever takes it can begin from a measurement rather than a
description.

RELATED: the same operator report also asked whether `cara sync` leaves the worktree parked
on the last PR it inspected. It does not. Verified across the whole crate: the only production
code that moves the caller's HEAD is `navigation::checkout_exact`, whose sole caller is
`next.rs` (`cara next`). `sync` builds its own detached worktree under `temp_dir` per process,
and `repair` uses an isolated workspace with `--detach`; every other `checkout`/`switch` in the
tree is inside `#[cfg(test)]`. A fix aimed at "sync should restore its base branch" would land
in a command that never moves it.

title: Retire merged caravan heads from checkpoints and dashboard after post-merge receipt failure
description:
## Problem

Cara successfully provider-merged Cacophony PR #2053 at `293bc9bb46e01792ac601f1a8798f33006fe9071`, then returned `operation_lock_checkpoint_too_large`. PR #2056 also merged at `967e304c6ef27f646c9cd3be388a3e7e2c7e757d`. For substantially longer than one controller cycle, the Cara dashboard still presented both as one-member caravan heads with force intent and no auto-merge, making the operator reasonably conclude that Cara was not merging its heads.

Fresh provider truth contradicted the dashboard:

- `gh pr view 2053`: `MERGED` at 2026-07-21T19:12:35Z.
- `gh pr view 2056`: `MERGED` at 2026-07-21T19:15:52Z.
- fresh `cara status --json`: `healthy=true`, `analysis.fleet.caravans=[]`, `merge_candidates=[]`.
- the persisted PR2053 pause remains in status as `state: stale` / `auto_merge_suspended: true` with old expected-open facts; it is not a live provider caravan.

This is a post-provider-success recovery/UI correctness bug: a checkpoint-size failure must not leave merged provider heads displayed as actionable open caravans.

## Acceptance

1. After a provider merge succeeds, checkpoint/event-journal compaction stays within its bound; large check histories use hashes/counts/bounded samples rather than overflowing the operation-lock checkpoint.
2. If durable checkpoint publication still fails after provider merge, the next status/dashboard refresh rediscovers GitHub and retires the merged head from active caravans.
3. Stale pause records whose exact head is merged are shown only as historical/stale diagnostics, never as active caravan cards and never as requiring auto-merge repair.
4. Add a regression with a force-labelled head carrying many historical check runs: provider merge succeeds, checkpoint publication fails or is bounded, then fresh status/dashboard shows zero active caravans and the merge receipt remains observable.
5. Provider truth remains authoritative; local checkpoint cleanup never attempts a second merge.

## Live recurrence — Cacophony PR2101, 2026-07-25

Cara admitted PR2101 as a sole-member caravan, then provider truth merged it at `3ad8d2843fe2f05e4617081d14837482f51b448c` on 2026-07-25T01:07:18Z. Fresh first-party `caco pr reflect --project cacophony --pr 2101` reports `pr_state=merged`, and timeline/main contains `fix(tui): decouple remote pane refresh from input (bd-8ffd54) (#2101)`.

After merge, canonical Cara remained degraded/unavailable with the stale PR2101 caravan and `auto_merge_invariant`: the caravan head supposedly must have squash auto-merge enabled. Attempting to repair auto-merge on an already merged PR would be invalid provider mutation. The stale caravan also blocked the fresh ordinary `pr_cara_join` generation-3 root, causing PR2167 to publish unjoined and earn zero canary credit.

This recurrence elevates the bug to P0 while it blocks queue admission. Required immediate behavior: provider discovery must retire merged PR2101 from active topology, preserve its merge receipt, and return healthy zero-caravan status without any raw/provider auto-merge toggle. Do not merge or mutate PR2101 again. Regression coverage must assert merged provider truth dominates stale auto-merge invariants during post-merge checkpoint failure.

title: Add remote candidate preflight by PR without checkout mutation
description:
Operator-requested Cara information/tooling gap observed while constructing the Cacophony train. `cara next-candidate` returns the canonical PR and ranking reason, but `cara check` validates only the current checkout branch. The merger therefore had to use GitHub and Cacophony PR-adoption surfaces merely to inspect a candidate's exact provider head/base, ownership, current tail compatibility, and required preflight before deciding whether any repair or join was needed.

Add a read-only remote candidate preflight surface, for example `cara check --pr <N> --tail-pr <T>` and MCP equivalent, or an explicit `next-candidate --preflight` operation. It must re-read the exact provider PR/head/base, same-repository/fork identity, labels/draft/auto-merge state, owner/bead metadata when available, intended current tail, pairwise compatibility/conflicting paths, and whether the candidate is already enrolled or stale. Return an exact receipt and the documented next action (`new`, `join`, repair, wait, or reject) without checkout, branch, label, or base mutation.

Preserve the canonical priority/FIFO order and fail closed: a rejected first candidate must not be silently leapfrogged. Acceptance: an agent can select and mechanically preflight the exact next candidate from Cara alone, then materialize/adopt a checkout only when a real rebase, conflict repair, or join mutation is required. Add CLI/JSON/MCP parity and stale-head race fixtures.

title: [operator] Make Cara join transactional for agent reintegration and sync event-driven
description:
## Operator direction — 2026-07-19

Move Cacophony from an LLM-driven merge-train cadence to deterministic Cara ownership:

1. Every new agent PR is opened and atomically appended to the current Caravan tail through a new Cacophony `pr_cara_join` reintegration mode.
2. `rebase_on_join` is configured true. Join rebases the candidate onto the exact current tail and targets the tail branch, preserving a valid root-to-tail chain.
3. A join conflict/failure returns an exact error to the authoring agent. Cacophony refuses reintegration completion/handoff, so that owner fixes the conflict and retries until the same PR joins successfully.
4. Routine `cara sync` ticks are deterministic and do not wake caco-merger. caco-merger wakes only for real typed repair/semantic decisions or terminal CI failures.
5. The Caravan root remains current with main, descendants remain rebased/targeted onto their exact parent, and required CI runs on the exact active heads.

This extends the landed `rebase_on_join`/chain-rebuild work from bd-cacf7c into the transactional author-ingress and event-driven operations contract.

## Required Caravan contract

- Expose stable CLI/JSON/MCP check/join surfaces suitable for Cacophony orchestration, with exact repository/PR/head/current-tail/config/provider identity receipts.
- Require and report `rebase_on_join=true` for this integration. Disabled/missing mode fails before mutation with the exact config action.
- Under the repository operation lock, rediscover the tail immediately before mutation and preflight ancestry, patch compatibility, force-with-lease authority, base target, labels, and required-check trigger behavior.
- Successful join must leave the same PR OPEN with its reviewed patch rebased onto the exact tail head, `baseRefName` equal to the tail branch, Caravan membership durable, prior CI invalidated, and fresh exact-head/base CI requested. No unrelated PR or provider-owned head may be changed.
- Join failure/conflict must not claim success or Caravan membership. Return exact conflicting paths/patch receipt/current tail and a first-party owner repair instruction. Any already-open source PR remains preserved as unjoined/owner-held; no duplicate PR, queue label, auto-merge, or ambiguous partial state.
- Exact retries on unchanged PR/head/tail are idempotent. Concurrent joins serialize and the loser rechecks the new tail rather than building a forked chain.
- Emit a durable join receipt/event that Cacophony can bind to generation, agent, bead, PR, head, base/tail, and config fingerprint.
- Make routine `sync --all` a no-LLM deterministic tick. It advances healthy chains, retargets/rebuilds after root merge under `rebase_on_join`, requests fresh CI, and returns typed decisions.
- Emit/wire a bounded wake event only for semantic repair decisions, unresolved mechanical conflicts requiring an owner, provider invariant failure, or terminal required-CI failure. Healthy/waiting/success ticks do not wake caco-merger.
- Enforce the root invariant: the Caravan root targets current main and is up to date before merge eligibility; each descendant targets and descends from its exact parent. A stale root such as PR #1962 must be synchronously advanced or returned as a typed blocker, never left indefinitely without checks.
- Add fixtures for two concurrent authors, join conflict then same-PR retry, tail moving between preflight/mutation, root main advance, descendant rebuild, missing checks, CI failure wake, healthy no-wake tick, and crash/restart idempotency.
- Document the integration contract for the Cacophony companion implementation and return the exact landed SHA/version before cutover.

## Operator correction — 2026-07-19 10:00 BST

The consuming Cacophony repository must explicitly set `rebase_on_join: true` in checked-in `.caravan/config.yaml`. Deterministic Cara continues to own serialized topology and routine sync, but its agent-in-loop repair contract must allow an authorized caco-merger to edit arbitrary repository paths after a typed real CI/semantic/provider failure. Do not limit that repair role to textual `conflicting_paths` or pre-granted semantic paths. Keep exact repository/PR/head/base/session binding, same-PR non-force publication, reviewed diff, fresh CI, and audit receipts. The narrow grant mechanism may remain useful for deterministic automation, but it cannot block the broad authorized merger repair path.

Post-v0.0.4 board audit (2026-07-20): v0.0.4 includes major Caravan-side slices—atomic remote join receipt (`780ac5d`, bd-6e7179), deterministic sync scheduler/wake status (`ec3a4db`, bd-d38dbf), deterministic receipt hashing (`091abe6`, bd-0f8b68), and force-generation invalidation (`35c08e6`, bd-4342ee). The umbrella is not complete: its later operator correction requires broad session-level authorized merger edits (bd-17375b reopened; narrow grants alone are insufficient), plus the companion Cacophony `pr_cara_join`/event-driven cutover and live acceptance. Added bd-17375b as an explicit dependency; do not close umbrella from the landed slices alone.

Board administration follow-up: added `bd-6f463b` as the explicit sync-owned best-effort queue optimiser/auto-admission dependency alongside broad authorized repair `bd-17375b`. The umbrella remains blocked until both land and companion Cacophony cutover/live acceptance is complete.

title: Admission ordering elects a red candidate that check refuses
description:
Verified against live cacophony with read-only `cara status` / `cara check`, no merge authority needed.

Before this change, the two surfaces DISAGREED about the same pull request:

    cara check --pr 2276   -> eligible=false, "candidate PR has a failing required check"
    cara status            -> next_candidate: 2276

The CI refusal added for bd-fc2b96 lived in `validate_candidate`, which is on the `check` path only. `resolve_admission` computes admission ORDER with its own independent rejection list (draft, fork-only, external auto-merge, priority-label problems) and never consulted CI. So the red PR was correctly called ineligible by `check` and simultaneously elected as the next candidate by ordering.

The consequence was the full stall, measured live: 2276 held the front, and 2245/2259 then reported "explicit admission intent fails closed on PR #2276", so nothing could be admitted at all.

Fix: ordering applies the same rule, and SKIPS rather than order-blocks. Skipping is the operator's ruling: queueing behind red is guaranteed rework, because the failure must be fixed, fixing it rewrites the head, and everything stacked behind is rebased anyway. So the queue advances to a clean candidate instead of waiting on a red head. `caravan-force` remains the audited override; a pending check is not a failure.

VERIFIED LIVE, same command, after the fix:

    next_candidate: 2279
    skipped: 2245 (mechanically incompatible), 2259 (mechanically incompatible),
             2276 (failing required check)

This is the third instance tonight of one class: a rule applied at one site and not its sibling, with tests green because each site was tested alone. Pinned by a_red_candidate_is_skipped_so_the_queue_advances, which asserts BOTH that the red PR loses the front and that the clean follower gains it.
