title: Cara stacking emits a merge head that its own rebase_cousin_history guard then refuses
description:
Cara 0.0.60 produced a stacked candidate head that its own guard then refuses, so the first successful stack in this repository cannot converge. All facts below were measured from the GitHub API, not inferred from Cara receipts.

## Observed refusal

Cara sync reports for Cacophony PR2330:

```
rebase_cousin_history
affected_prs=[2330]  caravan_id=2331
candidate merge oid 6d9304953ecd1ee38a8f54a9167e0fda5b186703
references history outside candidate/target ancestry
```

## What Cara actually created

`6d9304953ecd1ee38a8f54a9167e0fda5b186703` is a MERGE commit and its committer is `Caravan`:

- parents: `61727d484cc2ca2d7223d1caf60b1367bd9aeadb` and `3753825bba3c87a95319e7b02c84a968baa2966c`
- subject: `Merge branch 'main' into agent/ms-mac/cacophony/msm-2-bd-4fa94b`
- `3753825b` is Cacophony PR2331's head, committer `Caravan`, and is NOT main
- `61727d48` is a Caravan-rewritten copy of the worker's fix commit, parented directly on `ef896674` which is the previous release commit, not current main

Ancestry:

- `3753825b...6d93049`: ahead 2, behind 0, merge base `3753825b`
- `main...6d93049`: DIVERGED, ahead 4, behind 1, merge base `a035d903`
- PR2330's pre-stack head `defed764` versus `61727d48`: diverged, merge base `ef896674`

So Cara replaced the candidate's lineage with a commit rooted at an older release commit, then merged the parent caravan member into it. Relative to the target branch that is exactly the cousin-history shape the guard rejects. The producer and the refuser are the same component.

The exact owner cannot repair this by editing their pull request: both offending commits are Caravan-authored, and the pre-stack head was already clean and green.

## Secondary defects observed in the same object

1. The merge subject claims `Merge branch 'main'` while the merged parent is a caravan generation branch. Provenance is misleading to every downstream reader.
2. Timestamps are not chronologically coherent. `6d93049` carries author and committer date `2026-07-31T12:00:47Z`, while its own parent `3753825b` has committer date `2026-07-31T14:05:45Z`. A merge cannot predate its parent, so Cara-written dates must not be used for ordering or forensics.

## Required behavior

- Stacking must produce a candidate whose history is a linear descendant of the target and the parent member, or the guard must accept the exact shape Cara itself emits. One of the two must change; today they contradict.
- Rewritten candidate commits must be rooted on the current target branch tip, not on a stale release commit.
- A merge Cara creates must name the branch it actually merged.
- Committer/author dates on Cara-created commits must be monotonic with respect to their parents.
- When a refusal is caused by Cara-authored history, the receipt must say so and must not route repair to the pull request owner, who cannot act on it.
- Tests: stack one clean child onto one pending parent and assert the emitted candidate passes the ancestry guard; assert rewritten commits are rooted at target tip; assert merge subject matches the merged ref; assert parent-monotonic commit dates.

## Provenance

First successful Cara stack in the Cacophony repository, 2026-07-31, after the post-rewrite budget fix landed as `5f6bc3a` for `bd-84f82d`. Cacophony-side evidence bead and owner routing accompany this record.

title: Gate GitHub Stack rollout with default-path parity
description:
Final bd-e3069d rollout: full absent/stack_type=caravan parity suite, unavailable-capability zero-write refusal, force/hold/merge-queue policy matrix, sandbox receipts, documentation, min reader version, and explicit repository allowlist before production opt-in.

## External safety block discovered by bd-67b62b

An audited allowlist is not sufficient for rollout. The 2026-07-31 sandbox proved that `merge-async` can merge a selected Stack after a lower entry rewinds to a different head while preserving linear ancestry; only the selected top SHA is leased. Keep executable native merge disabled until the provider exposes a preventive complete-group generation lease. Post-merge `indeterminate` detection is evidence, not safety authority.

## Rollout gate slice landed at 9b4c4e4

- `tests/default_stack_parity.rs` asserts the absent/default `stack_type: caravan` contract directly: caravan backend, no batch bound, legacy reader pin accepted, and no native-only field in serialized policy. It fails if a future rollout slice changes the default path.
- Native-mode upgrades are all explicit and individually asserted: bounded batch inside GitHub's 2..=100 Stack range, `rebase_on_join: false`, caravan-owned head merging, and a reader pin.
- New `min_cara_version >= 0.0.65` requirement for `stack_type: github`, so an older Cara can never silently read a provider Stack as an ordinary label/base-chain caravan. The default backend is unaffected.
- Unavailable/unknown capability now produces typed `github_stack_capability_unavailable` / `github_stack_capability_unknown` mutation blockers instead of the generic rollout fence, so a future rollout cannot open the gate against an unproven provider and cannot treat unavailability as absence.
- `docs/github-app-policy.json` records Administration(write) as a conditional, scope-limited upgrade for the Stack lock ruleset and removes it from `forbidden_permissions`; the contract test asserts it is never a baseline permission and that the guide keeps documenting it as opt-in.

Remaining before production opt-in (still open on this bead): thread the ruleset-locked orchestrator through executable Stack membership/reshape/merge workflows, add the explicit repository allowlist, and only then remove `github_stack_backend_read_only`.

## Operator correction on validation environment (2026-08-01)

"Sandbox" means a hermetic test environment, not a disposable GitHub repository. Caravan already dogfoods itself in this repository (`.caravan/config.yaml` live, `cara status` healthy), and that is the environment for routine validation; a dedicated `caravan-test` repository may follow. The two recorded provider proofs needed real GitHub Stack/ruleset behaviour that cannot be emulated locally, and no further disposable repositories will be created. Recorded in `docs/validation/github-native-stack-sandbox-2026-07-31.md`.

## Rollout allowlist landed at ff591fa

- `stack_rollout.mutations_opt_in` plus a recorded `reviewed_by` is now a required per-repository allowlist, validated to require `stack_type: github` and a non-empty reviewer. It is deliberately necessary but not sufficient.
- Fence precedence is explicit and tested: unavailable/unknown capability outranks everything (`github_stack_capability_unavailable` / `github_stack_capability_unknown`), then a repository without the opt-in reports `github_stack_repository_not_opted_in`, then an opted-in repository still reports `github_stack_backend_read_only` until the reviewed ruleset-locked orchestrator ships. Opening the fence therefore cannot silently enable every repository that merely selected the native backend.
- Parity contracts extended: the default policy carries no opt-in, and an opt-in on the default backend is refused.
- `cara help` and SPEC state the allowlist and precedence.

Also landed in the same reintegration: `docs/github-app-setup.md`, the operator click-path for creating the GitHub App, requested by the operator. It covers App creation, the exact baseline permissions plus the three conditional upgrades (including the scoped Administration(write) Stack-lock case), private-key handling, installation and installation-ID discovery, a working reference broker, config/environment wiring, verification, and troubleshooting.

Remaining on this bead: thread the ruleset-locked orchestrator through executable Stack membership/reshape/merge workflows, then remove `github_stack_backend_read_only`.

## Lock-fenced landing order landed at 4891106

`src/github/stack_land.rs` owns the one property no individual provider adapter can guarantee: the complete-group ruleset lock is released exactly once, only after terminal provider proof.

- Ordered phases `planned → locked → submitted → terminal → released`, hash-sealed, shape-validated, and persisting `provider_atomic: false`.
- `outstanding_lock()` names a lock the transaction still owns, so an interrupted run is always identifiable as lock-holding instead of silently leaving a repository ruleset behind.
- Submit requires an acquired lock; poll requires a durable UUID checkpoint; release requires terminal proof. Pending/submitted/enqueued states are refused at release rather than unlocking the selected refs mid-flight, which is exactly the lower-head race the lock prevents.
- Every terminal outcome releases, including sealed `indeterminate`, so a safety-ambiguous result never strands the ruleset.
- Completed steps are idempotent replays with no provider access; tampered, foreign-repository, and progress-claiming-without-evidence checkpoints are refused before any command runs.

Five focused tests cover pending-never-releases, all three terminal releases, out-of-order refusal before provider access, tampered/foreign checkpoint refusal, and idempotent replay. The workflow fence is unchanged and still closed.

## Fence coverage proof landed at 8572d15

- `every_mutating_domain_consults_the_rollout_fence` asserts at source level that force, force_intent, membership, pause, priority, repair, reshape, sync, and sync_plan all call `initialization::require_ready`, which is where the capability, repository opt-in, and read-only blockers live. The fence is only as strong as its weakest mutating entry point, and this fails if a future domain skips it.
- `every_native_stack_blocker_refuses_mutation_with_its_exact_code` asserts all four native blockers (`github_stack_capability_unavailable`, `github_stack_capability_unknown`, `github_stack_repository_not_opted_in`, `github_stack_backend_read_only`) refuse with their exact typed code and `mutation_blocked: true`, so no caller can mistake a capability failure for ordinary readiness.

Operational note: the first reintegration attempt was rejected before publish by the host disk safety floor (4.1 GiB free against a 5.4 GiB floor), not by any Caravan defect. `caco prune run --cargo-targets --current-agent` freed 10.5 GiB and the identical head landed; dead letter rdl-019fbe15 was discarded with that reason.

## Policy-to-provider bridge landed at 01aa4d8

`src/stack_policy.rs` is the narrow seam between Cara policy and the Stack adapters. It derives no new policy and performs no provider access.

- `StackPolicyFacts` deliberately takes only the exact facts it may consider (discovered PRs, compatibility reports, held members) rather than the whole status, so the seam cannot quietly start depending on scheduler state it does not own. CI authority stays in the sync lane and enters as a caller-supplied verdict.
- Maps to the provider planner's blocker vocabulary: closed Stack, non-open entry, absent-or-drifted discovery (`GraphInexact`), non-open/draft PR, hold, non-clean compatibility, and required checks not ready.
- Durable `caravan-force` intent maps to `ForceUnsupported`: GitHub's async Stack merge documents no administrator bypass, so refusing is the only honest outcome. Silently landing a forced entry would misrepresent what was proven.
- Every returned entry preserves its exact provider generation, so the planner still fails closed if the Stack it reads disagrees with this evidence.
- Unknown or absent compatibility evidence is not converted into a merge refusal; it surfaces through graph problems instead.

Five focused tests cover the clean case, discovery drift and absence, force refusal, the combined conflict/hold/draft/closed/CI mapping, and closed-Stack/non-open-entry positions.

## Fail-closed landing route landed at a43c811

`route_landing` decides which landing path one caravan must use, and every native gate fails closed:

- The default backend returns `CaravanOwned` immediately without consulting capability, rollout opt-in, or provider Stack state. A test routes it against deliberately hostile native state (unavailable capability, drifted Stack) to prove the stable path cannot be affected by any of this logic.
- Native routing requires, in order: a proven `Available` capability (`NotProbed`/`Unknown`/`Unavailable` all refuse as `github_stack_capability_not_proven`), a recorded repository opt-in, a complete inventory page, exactly one Stack mapped to the caravan, and an `Exact` consistency verdict.
- Ambiguity is never resolved by choosing one: zero or multiple mapped Stacks both refuse with `github_stack_caravan_mapping_ambiguous`.

Three tests cover the untouched default path, the exact native success case, and every gate refusing with its exact code.

With this, all three native layers exist and are fenced: policy bridge (`stack_policy::stack_merge_evidence`) → ready-prefix planner (`github::stack_merge`) → lock-ordered landing (`github::stack_land`), selected by `route_landing`. The remaining rollout step is calling them from the sync workflow and removing `github_stack_backend_read_only`, which is now one reviewed change rather than new untested wiring.

Host note: disk pressure recurred (7.7 GiB free); pruned this agent's cargo targets again. Agent checkouts and cargo targets remain the dominant fleet consumers.

title: Do not index empty physical chain set before root admission
description:

Zero-write plan correctly selected canonical PR #2101 for auto_admission_new. Root cause on current Caravan main: `(chains.len() == 1).then_some(chains[0].caravan.id)` eagerly evaluates chains[0] even when chains is empty inside apply_physical_chains. Use a non-indexing optional access for empty/single/multiple chains and preserve outcome.caravan_id only for exactly one chain. Add an execution regression with rebase_on_join=true, empty fleet, auto admission enabled, canonical clean candidate: physical selected set is empty, apply phase returns a valid empty outcome, then root admission executes and emits exact receipt. Also cover no candidates (healthy noop), multiple chains, plan/execute parity, JSON no panic, and lock cleanup. title: Map Caravan evict and split to native Stack rebuilds
description:
Phase 6 of bd-e3069d: for exact unqueued Stack generations, preflight complete replacement chains, unstack, run existing Cara reshape rules, recreate replacement Stacks, and converge interrupted phases. Never claim provider atomicity for unstack/rebuild.

## Landed on main at 5b611a9 (Cara 0.0.76 line)

`src/github/stack_reshape.rs` implements the phased, explicitly non-atomic rebuild:

- `GitHubStackReshapePlan` seals repository, operation id/actor, evict/split rule, selected PR, the exact open unqueued `before` generation, the complete replacement partition, and the derived per-PR postconditions under a stable FNV plan hash. Semantics are revalidated on every verify, so a tampered plan cannot be replayed.
- Partition rules: eviction yields zero or one surviving chain with every surviving exact PR/head generation preserved; split requires a non-head selected PR and exactly two chains divided immediately before it. Queued/merging/draft/closed entries are refused before any provider access.
- Postconditions express what the existing Cara reshape must establish: exact base/head, required/forbidden control labels (`caravan`, `caravan-evicted`, `caravan-force`), and disabled auto-merge. This adapter never reimplements or weakens reshape policy; it only proves it from fresh PR truth.
- Phases: `preflighted` → `unstacked` → `reshape_applied` → `rebuilding` → `rebuilt` → `verified`. Every checkpoint is self-contained, hash-sealed, shape-validated against its phase, and persists `provider_atomic: false`.
- Preflight is zero-write and binds the exact provider generation. Unstack reuses the CRUD adapter's exact absence proof, so a lost response or crash converges without a second unstack write. Replacement Stacks are created one at a time; an already-created exact topology is an `already_satisfied` zero-write retry.
- Final verification proves each multi-member chain exists exactly once, refuses truncated inventory, and proves singleton chains and fully dissolved caravans by exact inventory absence.

Seven hermetic tests cover eviction/split planning, queued refusal, zero-write preflight, full crash-recovery convergence with no repeated writes, partial-reshape refusal before replacement creation, tampered-checkpoint refusal, and a singleton-halves split that creates no provider Stack. `cara help`, README, SPEC, and the native Stack design doc now state the phase contract and that reshape is resumable but never provider-atomic. `github_stack_backend_read_only` remains closed.

title: Release both P0 engine fixes as v0.0.75
description:

title: Classify every provider and Git write behind a fenced runner seam
description:
Second child of bd-754d6b after protocol bead bd-53d3a2. Establish a complete machine-checkable mutation-intent seam before enabling remote_fenced/read_only modes.

Extend CommandSpec with a non-secret intent classification: read, provider_write, or git_write (default read). Mark every production GitHub/GraphQL/REST/gh mutation builder and every production git push/delete/update-ref writer; test/fixture-only commands are separately scoped. Add a FencedCommandRunner wrapper accepting a MutationFence trait. Before a marked write it must synchronously revalidate the exact RemoteLeaseGuard fencing token; read commands bypass without backend calls. Lost/expired/indeterminate fence returns a typed runner failure before child spawn. The wrapper must share operation deadline and telemetry without weakening existing request/mutation budgets or force-with-lease args.

Add source/contract guards that enumerate all gh write forms (`pr create/edit/merge/comment`, label create/edit, run rerun, POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE APIs, GraphQL mutation) and git writer forms (`push`, update-ref where provider-facing) and fail when any is unmarked. Conversely, GET/list/view/fetch/ls-remote remain read. Fake runner tests prove zero child calls on lost fence, exactly one fence revalidation per marked write, zero lease calls for reads/local_only, and no secret rendering.

Do not activate writer.mode remote_fenced/read_only yet. The following child must thread one operation-scoped guard into every runner and acquire it before operation.lock; this bead only makes omission detectable and centrally enforceable once wrapped.

title: cara new cannot flatten a squash-merged root, only sync can
description:
Live report from cacophony: `cara new` on PR 2271, with no existing caravans, refused with

    tree_mismatch: merge-preserving replay tree differs from the independently
    computed clean merge tree
    expected_tree af776f4e19062301e4def629ded5780a52aad3f3

The operator's reasonable reading was that `rebase_on_join` had not applied. It had — the refusal comes from inside the physical rebase. The real gap is which *kind* of rebase was authorized.

bd-85b71d established that a caravan ROOT squash-merged by cara has its history discarded at landing, so replaying its merge topology proves nothing; the root is flattened onto the independently proven merge tree instead. That reasoning was wired into `src/sync.rs` only. `src/membership.rs` builds its own `RebaseExecutionBudget` for `new`/`renew`/`join` and never set `flattening_squashed_root`, so a branch containing a merge commit could be flattened by a later sync but not by the `cara new` that creates the caravan.

Result: exactly the bd-85b71d shape (a branch that merged main into itself with hand-resolved conflicts) is admitted by sync but refused at creation, which is where an operator actually hits it first.

Fix: authorize flattening in the membership path under the same two conditions sync uses — the candidate is a root (no join target, so its base is the default branch) and `sync.head_merge_actor` is `caravan`. A member joining behind a tail is still never flattened, because its ancestry must physically follow the chain, and an unauthorized merge-preserving replay still fails closed.

title: auto_merge_invariant should re-arm a caravan head after a transient red; GitHub disarms automatically but never re-arms
description:
A caravan head that ever goes red permanently loses its auto-merge invariant, because the disarm is automatic and the re-arm is not. Nothing in the system notices. The queue then sits with a head that will never merge unattended, and the symptom reads as "the owner never armed auto-merge", which sends whoever investigates down the wrong path.

Observed live on cacophony PR #2210 on 2026-07-27, where it held a six-member caravan for roughly ninety minutes overnight.

## Sequence

    02:26:12Z  owner arms squash auto-merge on #2210 (with `gh pr edit --base main`, clearing a DanglingBase row)
    03:38:00Z  required check `Check & Lint` goes red on runner cacophony-ms-dev-2
               -> GitHub silently DISARMS auto-merge
    03:38-05:12 head sits unmergeable; nothing re-arms; caravan of six blocked
    05:12:47Z  owner manually re-arms after cross-agent investigation
               head 2e02a53116 unchanged, no new generation, Cara's own rebase intact

The red was not the owner's diff. It was `tests/source-guard-tooling-fixtures.sh` aborting silently when `nix print-dev-env .#ci-source` failed on the runner host — filed separately as cacophony bd-bcb813. A re-run of only the failed jobs went green, confirming it as transient.

## Why this is systemic rather than a one-off

The disarm is GitHub behaviour and will not change: any failing required check disables auto-merge, and GitHub never re-enables it. So the invariant Cara relies on for unattended landing is silently destroyed by any transient red on the head, and only a human restores it.

That matters much more when transient reds are common, which they currently are. Under cacophony bd-603883, every native runner unit on two nodes is in a `226/NAMESPACE` restart loop, leaving three surviving `x86_64-linux` runners — and the red above happened on `cacophony-ms-dev-2`, one of those three. So the survivors are flaky rather than healthy. Flaky runners produce transient reds; every transient red on a head permanently disarms it; each occurrence needs a human. Those compound, and the queue wedges repeatedly for a reason no single component reports as a fault.

It also mimics a different failure. `auto_merge_invariant` reporting "head is not armed" is indistinguishable to a reader from "owner never armed it", so investigation starts at the owner rather than at the check history. Both agents who looked at this initially assumed a Cara or lifecycle bug.

## Suggested change

`auto_merge_invariant` repair should **re-arm** the head when it finds the invariant broken but the head otherwise eligible, rather than only reporting it. Guard rails worth having, offered as suggestions rather than requirements:

- re-arm only for the exact current head OID that Cara already selected, never a moved head
- re-arm only when the disarm is attributable to a check transition, not to an owner explicitly disabling auto-merge
- bound it, so a head that is genuinely and repeatedly red does not get re-armed in a loop; a small retry ceiling with a reported give-up is better than unbounded
- record the re-arm in the receipt, so it is visible that Cara did it rather than the owner

Reporting-only is defensible if re-arming is judged too much authority for the scheduler. In that case the report should at least distinguish **"never armed"** from **"armed at T, disarmed by a failing required check at T+n"**, because those two states need completely different responses and currently look identical.

## Provenance

Root cause and sequence established by cacophony:8x5t4zp7luvs0a4q on ms-dev-3, who owns #2210 and re-armed it. Filed here at their explicit suggestion ("durable follow-up for whoever owns queue health") by cacophony:d23tqrb17ss3e6xo from ms-dev-6, who was queued behind the head and narrowed the failing fixture. Neither of us has modified Cara, any runner, any queue state, or another agent's PR.

Related: cacophony bd-bcb813 (silent fixture abort that produced the red), cacophony bd-603883 (runner restart loop leaving three flaky survivors).

## SUPERSEDED 2026-07-27 ~08:35 BST — do not implement the re-arm recommendation

The operator has decided to **disable native auto-merge on the cacophony repository entirely**, and to make Cara the sole landing mechanism: on each tick Cara should retarget the caravan root to `main`, verify CI, and then directly **squash-merge** the exact root. Rationale given: all lifecycle via Caravan rather than a mix of Caravan and provider auto-merge, which is slower but safer and easier to reason about.

That closes off this bead's central recommendation. **Do not implement auto-merge re-arming.** If auto-merge is disabled repository-wide there is nothing to arm, nothing to disarm, and a scheduler that re-armed it would be reintroducing exactly the hybrid this decision removes.

Tracking for the replacement behaviour is **caravan bd-f8cf99** (P0), which covers Cara performing the retarget-verify-squash-merge itself.

### What remains valid here, and worth carrying into bd-f8cf99

The diagnosis stands even though the fix has changed, and two parts are worth preserving rather than losing with this bead:

1. **The failure mode this documented is real and was live.** A caravan head that went transiently red silently lost its auto-merge invariant, GitHub never re-armed it, and the head sat unmergeable for ~90 minutes blocking six PRs while presenting as "the owner never armed it". Whatever replaces it should not be able to enter a state that is (a) load-bearing for landing, (b) silently cleared by an unrelated transient, and (c) indistinguishable from never having been set.

2. **The wrong-target merge it contributed to.** With auto-merge armed on a chained PR whose base was another member's generation branch, #2213 auto-merged into `agent/ms-dev-3/.../8x5t4zp7luvs0a4q-pr-gf9e8151...` at 2026-07-27T07:15:08Z instead of into `main`, leaving bd-282638 unlanded and riding inside the next member's PR. That is the concrete harm from mixing provider auto-merge with Cara-managed chain topology, and it is the strongest single argument for the operator's decision. Cara's own squash-merge path must retarget the root to `main` **before** merging, or it reproduces the same class of error under a different mechanism.

Superseding note recorded by cacophony:d23tqrb17ss3e6xo, who filed this bead. Not closing it, since that is the caravan owner's call — but it should not be worked as written.

title: Make shared remote lease guard heartbeat-renewable
description:
Child of bd-f9c239 after repair propagation d84482e. Make Arc-shared RemoteLeaseGuard safely heartbeat-renewable before remote mode activation.

title: Add opt-in GitHub App identity and hosted execution modes
description:
Add an opt-in GitHub App execution backend alongside the existing local/ambient-gh backend. This is a parallel supported mode, not a replacement: existing local Cara behavior remains default and unchanged.

WHY

Today all GitHub API calls and direct git pushes use the operator's shared credential, so GitHub attributes force-pushes, comments, labels, and merge actions to the human account. Caravan receipts can explain the mutation, but the provider event actor is still indistinguishable from an operator or ordinary agent.

A GitHub App installation token gives Caravan its own provider principal, so GitHub can render `caravan[bot] force-pushed ...` and `caravan[bot] commented ...`.

TWO SEPARATE MODES

1. APP-AUTHENTICATED LOCAL EXECUTION

   Keep the current local scheduler, repository checkout, physical-rebase implementation, and operation budgets. Replace only provider credentials with an installation-token provider. This is the minimum useful slice and immediately supplies bot attribution.

2. APP-HOSTED EXECUTION

   Add a webhook receiver and worker service that runs Cara outside the operator machine. This is optional and later. A GitHub App supplies identity, permissions, installation lifecycle, and webhooks; it does not execute Cara itself.

AUTHENTICATED LOCAL ACCEPTANCE

- Add an explicit config mode, defaulting to today's ambient/stored gh account behavior. App mode is opt-in per deployment/repository and cannot silently activate from ambient environment.
- Public, non-secret config may name app slug/ID and installation selection. Private key/token material never enters `.caravan/config.yaml`, git, plans, errors, receipts, command arguments, or process listings.
- Introduce a refreshable GitHub credential-provider abstraction rather than resolving one static token for a whole tick. Installation access tokens expire, while Cara ticks can be long; refresh before expiry and single-flight concurrent refreshes.
- Generate a short-lived App JWT from a protected key/KMS/credential command, discover or bind the exact repository installation, and exchange it for a repository-scoped installation token with least privilege.
- Inject the installation token into every `gh` API/GraphQL command through the existing secret environment path. Existing `GitHubMutationAdapter` behavior and request budgets remain unchanged.
- Inject the SAME installation principal into git fetch/push. Direct physical-rebase pushes currently bypass `gh`, so API-only App auth would still show force-pushes as the human. Use an askpass/in-memory credential helper or equivalent secret environment; never place the token in remote URLs, argv, logs, checkpoints, or errors.
- A mutation refuses before provider write if API and git transport principals do not resolve to the same exact app installation.
- Telemetry/receipts include auth mode, app slug, installation ID, token expiry, and expected provider actor, but no token or key material.
- Force-push and comment integration tests prove the provider actor is the App installation rather than the ambient user. Commit metadata identity is a separate concern: use a stable Caravan bot name/noreply address, and document whether commits are merely attributed or cryptographically verified.
- On 401/expiry, refresh once under the same request/write budget and exact lease. Never turn auth retry into an unbounded provider retry.
- Ambient/stored `gh` mode retains exact current behavior and tests.

MINIMUM APP PERMISSIONS

Document and test the narrow set rather than requesting broad administration:

- Metadata: read
- Contents: write (branch fetch/push and ref updates)
- Pull requests: write (base changes, auto-merge/merge operations, review-object mutation)
- Issues and/or Pull requests: write as required by PR comments/labels endpoints
- Checks/statuses and Actions: read; Actions write only if configured rerun behavior requires it
- Workflows: write only where Cara must push branches containing `.github/workflows/*`

Branch rules must explicitly permit the App to force-update only Caravan-managed source branches. Do not grant blanket default-branch bypass.

HOSTED MODE ACCEPTANCE

- Verify webhook `X-Hub-Signature-256`; persist/deduplicate `X-GitHub-Delivery`.
- Treat webhooks only as wake hints. Every job re-reads authoritative provider refs/checks/labels before deciding.
- Queue non-overlapping work per repository/installation and preserve current exact leases, budgets, mutation caps, result-tree checks, and manual-decision policy.
- Use isolated ephemeral worktrees over a bounded clone cache. Never share mutable worktrees between repositories/jobs.
- Store App keys in KMS/secret manager and audit installation/repository scope.
- Persist bounded event receipts and expose health/last-tick state without storing tokens.
- Installation created/deleted/repositories-added/removed events update tenancy safely.

LOCAL + HOSTED SINGLE-WRITER RULE

The current `operation.lock` is a local file and cannot coordinate separate hosts. Supporting both implementations does NOT mean both may write the same repository concurrently.

Initial safe contract: local and hosted modes coexist in the product, but repository config/deployment selects exactly one active writer. The other may read/plan.

If automatic cross-mode failover is desired, add a remote compare-and-swap lease keyed by exact repository identity, with owner, operation ID, expiry, heartbeat, and fencing token. Both local and hosted writers must acquire it before the existing local lock and re-check the fencing token before every provider/branch write. Service outage fails closed; break-glass takeover is explicit and audited.

NON-GOALS

- Do not replace or deprecate local Cara.
- Do not weaken exact branch leases, operation budgets, or manual merge authority.
- Do not infer mutation authority merely from App installation.
- Do not rely on webhook ordering or delivery for correctness.

PROGRESS (v0.0.67 BASELINE)

Completed local-mode slices:

- bd-03d863: refreshable exact-repository App installation auth for GitHub API calls.
- bd-c586b8: the same pinned principal for exact HTTPS Git transport, with secret-environment helper and transport hardening.
- bd-02242b: independent explicit auth-mode/slug/installation opt-in; broker environment alone remains ambient.
- bd-e811f3: machine-checked least-privilege permissions, branch, webhook, attribution, and single-writer deployment contract.

Operator-gated acceptance remains bd-71e444 (live API + force-push bot actor canary). The existing `cara web` receiver already verifies HMAC, binds installation/repository, durably deduplicates delivery IDs, treats events as wake hints, coalesces bursts, and keeps fallback polling; hosted work should reuse rather than duplicate it.

Hosted execution remains incomplete. Before any hosted writer may coexist with local operation, add a remote CAS lease/fencing implementation and recheck its monotonically fenced token before every provider or branch mutation. Until then, deployments must configure exactly one writer per repository as documented in docs/github-app.md.

HOSTED FENCING CHILD

bd-754d6b now tracks the mandatory remote CAS writer lease/fencing contract. Hosted workers must remain non-writing until it lands. This is intentionally separate from the operator-gated live App actor canary bd-71e444 and from the existing local signed-webhook receiver.

REMOTE FENCING CORE COMPLETE (v0.0.70)

bd-754d6b and integration parent bd-f9c239 are complete. v0.0.70 at 710816a ships local_only (default), read_only, and remote_fenced modes; strict external CAS broker protocol; remote-before-local acquisition; explicit provider/Git mutation intents; operation-wide fenced runners including physical and repair publication; single-flight heartbeat renewal; inherited repair-to-sync guard; bounded latest-grant checkpoints; and fail-closed read-only planning. This enables safe core coordination but does not deploy a hosted service or automatic failover.

Epic remains open for operator-gated live App actor proof bd-71e444 and optional hosted worker/tenancy/queue deployment. Hosted deployment must use the shipped remote_fenced mode and the documented one-writer contract.

title: Admission capacity still uses worst-case slot pricing and yields an impossible 0-member bound
description:
The bounded-prefix work fixed the physical-sync RESERVE but not the ADMISSION bound, and the admission bound now computes a self-contradictory 0-member capacity that closes the queue to all new work.

Read-only `cara status --json` from the canonical daemon checkout, Cara `0.0.11`, at main `7c0bb4158e13ce20673b3a62699fdfef827406dc`:

```json
"sync_budget": {
  "deadline_ms": 3600000,
  "command_timeout_ms": 600000,
  "deadline_command_slots": 6,
  "max_admissible_members": 0,
  "blocked_candidate": 2234,
  "safe_next_action": "every caravan holds the 0-member bound implied by the configured deadline; admission stays closed with caravan_budget_capacity_exhausted until a caravan drains"
}
```

Per caravan:

```json
{"caravan_id": 2215, "required_command_slots": 21, "required_ms": 315000, "retained_command_slots": 16, "retained_ms": 240000, "at_capacity": true,
 "safe_next_action": "let this caravan drain before admitting another member: 4 members already reach the 0-member bound implied by sync.max_duration_secs=3600s and command_timeout_secs=600s"}
{"caravan_id": 2233, "required_command_slots": 9, "required_ms": 135000, "retained_command_slots": 7, "retained_ms": 105000, "at_capacity": true,
 "safe_next_action": "let this caravan drain before admitting another member: 1 members already reach the 0-member bound implied by sync.max_duration_secs=3600s and command_timeout_secs=600s"}
```

Three problems, in increasing severity.

**1. Two different budget models are in use simultaneously.** `required_ms` is now computed from actual work: 315000ms for 21 slots and 135000ms for 9 slots, both exactly 15000ms per slot, independent of `command_timeout_ms`. That is the fixed model and it works. But `deadline_command_slots` is `3600000 / 600000 = 6`, which is the OLD worst-case model, pricing every slot at the full command timeout. So the reserve says a 21-slot chain costs 315000ms out of 3600000, under nine percent, while admission says only 6 slots fit at all.

**2. The bound is impossible, not merely tight.** It reports a "0-member bound". Caravan 2233 has exactly ONE member and is reported `at_capacity: true` with the text "1 members already reach the 0-member bound". A zero-member capacity cannot be satisfied by any caravan including an empty one, so no member can ever be admitted regardless of drain. The stated remedy, "until a caravan drains", cannot help: draining to zero members still leaves a 0-member bound.

**3. Raising `command_timeout_secs` silently closed the queue.** `command_timeout_secs` moved 120 to 600 in checked-in config. Under the worst-case admission arithmetic that cut `deadline_command_slots` from 30 to 6, which is what produced the 0-member bound. An observer on a stale checkout with `command_timeout_secs: 120` concurrently reads `max_admissible_members: 12` against the identical binary, caravans, and moment, so the divergence is fully explained by that one config field feeding the unfixed admission path.

Requested repair:

- Compute admissible capacity from the same actual-work model that now produces `required_ms`, not from `deadline / command_timeout`. The two must not disagree by two orders of magnitude on the same chain.
- A capacity bound of zero should be impossible to emit. If the arithmetic produces a non-positive bound, that is a defect condition and should be reported as one, not as ordinary at-capacity gating with a drain suggestion that cannot work.
- `at_capacity` on a one-member caravan should be treated as a self-evident contradiction and fail loudly rather than quietly closing admission.
- Guidance text must not recommend an action that cannot resolve the condition it describes.

Live impact at time of filing: `blocked_candidate: 2234`, and candidates have been accumulating since roughly 08:00 UTC behind an earlier operator-directed merge freeze. Existing caravans can still drain, so this presents as a slow silent stall rather than an outage, and it will look like a fresh incident to anyone who sees the queue drain to empty and then refuse everything.

Evidence provenance: measured on the mutable cargo-installed `0.0.11` at `/home/harry/.cargo/bin/cara`, not the reviewed store closure. The reserve-side fix is likewise confirmed only on that build. Cross-vantage comparison contributed by the helsinki profile worker, whose stale `command_timeout_secs: 120` checkout served as the control arm that isolated the config dependency.

## Merged duplicate: bd-e99fe6

Title: Guarantee forward progress when caravan physical-sync reserve exceeds tick budget

Cara's correct all-or-nothing apply-budget refusal becomes a monotonic deadlock once a live caravan grows larger than `sync.max_duration_secs` can ever process.

Live Cacophony evidence:

```
physical_sync_budget_insufficient
4560000ms required, 3430138ms remaining (38 command slots)
```

Config: `sync.max_duration_secs: 3600`, `command_timeout_secs: 120`, `max_mutations_per_tick: 64`, `max_candidates_per_tick: 8`. Caravan2208 grew from 4 to 7 members while blocked. At seven members, Cara requires 76 minutes against a 60-minute deadline. Because every pass refuses before mutation, no member drains; because nothing drains, accepting more members only increases the required reserve. Scheduled and manual drivers hit the same bound.

The safety refusal is correct—never start an apply that might overrun mid-chain—but the system must preserve bounded forward progress.

Required, in order:

1. Prefer a checkpointed/resumable bounded-prefix apply: plan/verify the complete graph, reserve enough for an exact prefix plus durable checkpoint, apply strictly root-to-descendant, persist completed-prefix receipts before return, and resume idempotently next tick without replaying completed provider mutations.
2. If complete-graph all-or-nothing is architecturally required, compute maximum admissible chain size from the configured deadline before admission and refuse further joins with typed `caravan_budget_capacity_exhausted` evidence while allowing the existing processable prefix to drain.
3. Required/remaining budget must model actual operations, concurrency and already-completed checkpoints rather than a permanently increasing whole-chain worst case.
4. Preserve force-with-lease, exact provider revalidation, no manual reorder/eviction/split, and fail closed on drift/unknown receipts.
5. Status must expose required budget, processable prefix, blocked candidate, configured deadline and safe next action before the cliff, not only after a sync refusal.
6. Add tests for 1..N members around the threshold, interrupted prefix/resume, provider drift, CI/head transitions, independent caravans, candidate admission at capacity and no duplicate mutations.
7. Validate against the seven-member Cacophony caravan2208 without manually reordering its members.

A temporary deadline increase is an operator-owned stopgap only; it moves the cliff and is not completion. Current manual sync loop is paused to avoid burning rate limit on guaranteed no-write passes.

## Ratchet changes geometry when new arrivals form separate caravans

Observed after the budget refusal: `caravans` went from 1 to 2 with no sync driver running. The second caravan is a single member, PR `#2228`, an ordinary new publication that formed its own caravan rather than joining the deadlocked chain.

That matters for how this is fixed. The original recording of this deadlock assumed a single chain growing without bound until `required_ms` exceeds the deadline. If new arrivals instead form separate caravans, the first chain stops growing, which is better, but drain is still zero and the NUMBER of stuck units now increases rather than the size of one unit. Same deadlock, different geometry.

Consequence for acceptance criteria: a fix that only caps or resumes a single chain would not address the multi-caravan accumulation case. Whatever forward-progress mechanism is chosen should make progress across the set of caravans, not merely within one, and should be measured by total units drained rather than by whether any single chain can be applied.

Credit: observed and reasoned by the helsinki profile worker while under an explicit read-only watch, and verified independently by cluster control, which confirmed caravan 2228 has exactly one member and is an ordinary admission rather than a second sync actor.

## Exact mechanism: required_ms is command_slots x command_timeout_secs, a pure worst-case projection

Three measured datapoints from live refusals, contributed by the helsinki profile worker under a read-only watch, establish the formula precisely:

- 7 members, 38 slots: `4560000ms required` vs `3430138ms remaining`, short by 1129862
- 6 members, 32 slots: `3840000ms required` vs `3455426ms remaining`, short by 384574
- 6 members, 33 slots: `3960000ms required` vs `3425694ms remaining`, short by 534306

In every case `required_ms` equals `slots x 120000` exactly, where 120000 is `command_timeout_secs: 120`. So the reserved apply budget assumes EVERY command consumes its full timeout, and is not informed by observed latency at all. That is the root of the deadlock: real commands complete far faster, but the reserve is computed as though none do.

Two consequences that sharpen the fix options recorded above:

- raising `sync.max_duration_secs` is even more clearly a stopgap than stated. At 120s per slot you need `max_duration >= slots x 120s + planning`, so roughly every five additional slots costs another ten minutes of deadline, permanently.
- lowering `command_timeout_secs` has more leverage than the remedy text suggests, because it divides `required_ms` directly. At 100s, the current 33 slots would need 3300000ms and would fit inside the 3425694ms remaining with no other change. That is a genuine same-night unblock, but it trades against real provider and Git latency, so it needs an owner's judgement rather than a guess.
- the durable ask already recorded, reserving budget per unit of work actually attempted, is exactly right, because the entire gap here is worst-case versus actual.

Also confirmed: a drain does NOT reliably relieve the deadlock. Losing the root cut required_ms by roughly 600000 but left it short, and the requirement then rose again from 3840000 to 3960000 as one slot was added. The ratchet keeps climbing across a successful merge.

Planning consumption is real and must be included in any sizing: the 3600000ms deadline had already dropped to ~3425694ms remaining before apply was reserved.

## Fourth datapoint: formula holds, and parallel caravans do NOT compound the deficit

Datapoint 4 from the helsinki read-only watch: `3960000ms required vs 3429503ms remaining, 33 command slots`. 33 x 120000 = 3960000 exactly, a fourth consecutive exact hit, so `required_ms = command_slots x command_timeout_secs` has still not been falsified.

Full trend:

| slots | required | remaining | short by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 38 | 4560000 | 3430138 | 1129862 |
| 32 | 3840000 | 3455426 | 384574 |
| 33 | 3960000 | 3425694 | 534306 |
| 33 | 3960000 | 3429503 | 530497 |

Remaining is stable across passes at roughly 3425000 to 3455000, so planning consistently consumes about 145000 to 175000ms before apply is reserved. The deficit is therefore driven almost entirely by slot count and not by variable planning cost, which is good news for a fix: slots is the only lever that moves.

Important correction to the multi-caravan concern recorded earlier in this bead: on this pass `caravans` went 1 to 2 again while the SELECTED caravan stayed at 33 slots. The new caravan did not add slots to the selected one. Cluster control verified the second caravan is `2232`, a single member, PR `#2232` "fix(android): bound chat memory and OOM classification", an ordinary new publication.

So parallel caravans are NOT compounding the selected-chain deficit, which is consistent with the per-chain-prefix model in `ad14f74` treating independent chains separately. Accumulation shows up as more units rather than a larger selected unit. That materially narrows the fix: forward progress across the set still matters for total drain, but the deadlock itself is a single-chain slot-count problem, not a cross-chain summation problem.

## Second ratchet driver ISOLATED by controlled comparison: base drift, not chain growth

A controlled quiet-interval test isolates a second and previously unrecorded driver of the deadlock. Slot count changes ONLY when `main` moves, and holds exactly steady when `main` is quiet.

Paired series of (main head, slots):

- `b464e1ae5cb`, 38
- (root #2208 merged), 32
- `b464e1ae5cb`, 33
- `b464e1ae5cb`, 33 — main quiet, slots steady
- `9d6278a10f0`, 36 — main MOVED (release v1.2.1575), slots jumped 33 to 36
- `9d6278a10f0`, 36 — main quiet, slots steady

The decisive pass: two samples roughly 35 minutes apart on an unchanged base produced byte-identical projections, 4320000 required with remaining differing by only 438ms. That rules out a time-based or spontaneous ratchet.

Mechanism confirmed: projected apply cost rises with BASE DRIFT. Mechanism disproven: members re-parenting and consuming slots. Cluster control verified per-member state independently and found the chain stacked on each other's branches with only the root targeting `main`, and the root had NOT re-parented, still at head `2e02a53116` last updated 02:25:35Z with `ahead 2, behind 2` against `main` after the 03:30 release cut. So nothing consumed slots by doing work; the planner is pricing rebase work it has not performed and cannot start.

Why this matters for the fix, and it is worse than pure chain growth:

- unrelated `main` traffic increases projected cost while the chain simultaneously grows staler, because nothing applies the rebases. One event does both.
- a quiet `main` is stable but still deadlocked; a busy `main` actively worsens it.
- there is a perverse loop: a queue that cannot drain forces manual lands, manual lands move `main`, and every such move makes the queue more expensive to drain.

Consequence for acceptance criteria: capping chain size is necessary but NOT sufficient. A fix must also ensure projected cost does not grow unboundedly with base drift on a chain that is not being applied, for example by pricing only the prefix it intends to apply this pass, or by applying rebases incrementally so drift is retired rather than accumulated.

Formula confirmation continues: 36 x 120000 = 4320000, a sixth consecutive exact hit, so `ad14f74` has not yet reached the runtime in use (`cara 0.0.10`, consistent with `bd-bbc981` pending).

Credit: isolation designed and executed by the helsinki profile worker under a read-only watch, with per-member base state verified independently by cluster control.

## RETRACTION: the base-drift isolation above is FALSIFIED — do not act on it

The "second ratchet driver isolated" section above is WRONG and must not be used for fix design or deployment verification. Retracted by its own author on the next pass, and verified by cluster control.

Falsifying observation: `main` head was UNCHANGED at `9d6278a10f0` across three consecutive passes, yet slots jumped 36 to 42 on the third, `5040000ms required vs 3376327ms remaining`. Slots moved while `main` was quiet, which is exactly the outcome that was predicted to break the finding. `caravans` also went 2 to 3 active across that interval.

Why the earlier test was underpowered: the two quiet passes with steady slots showed only that slots do not drift spontaneously with TIME on an unchanged base AND unchanged membership. Membership happened to be static across both, so the test never controlled for it. The single 33 to 36 jump coincided with the v1.2.1575 release cut and was attributed to base drift, but membership change is an equally plausible and unexcluded explanation for that same jump.

Corrected position, deliberately weaker than before:

- `required_ms = command_slots x command_timeout_secs` remains solid, now seven consecutive exact hits including 42 x 120000 = 5040000.
- Slot count is NOT stable, and at least two candidate drivers remain plausible: chain or membership growth, now directly evidenced by a quiet-main pass with slots +6 and caravans +1; and base drift, still consistent with the per-member read but NOT established, since its only supporting datapoint is confounded with membership change.
- The deadlock persists across every observed configuration regardless of which driver dominates.

Consequence for the fix: do NOT scope acceptance to "cost must not grow with base drift" as though that were established. The durable requirements already recorded above stand on their own, since they address worst-case reserve versus actual work whatever moves the slot count. Isolating the driver requires holding membership constant, which no observer here can control.

Improvement adopted for future evidence: capture caravan COUNT and selected-chain membership alongside `(main head, slots)` on every pass, so a future jump can be attributed rather than inferred.

Recorded because the falsified version was previously written up here as a controlled comparison and routed onward; anyone who read it should re-read this section.

## Negative result: slot count varies with every sampled field held constant

A same-instant capture recorded slots moving 41 to 42, `required_ms` 4920000 to 5040000, while every other tracked field was unchanged:

- `main` unchanged at `9d6278a10f0`
- caravans unchanged at 3
- cara `merge_candidates` unchanged at 8, identical PR set `[2233,2232,2227,2225,2223,2215,2213,2210]`
- cara compatibility entries unchanged at 14
- daemon `ordered_candidates` unchanged at 5, with its `observed` timestamp genuinely advancing from 05:08:11 to 05:43:05

Combined with the earlier 42 to 41 decrease, every mechanism proposed during this investigation is now excluded for at least one observed transition:

| proposed driver | excluded by |
|---|---|
| base drift | both the 42→41 and 41→42 transitions, main quiet for both |
| membership growth | the 42→41 transition, membership independently confirmed at six |
| caravan count | the 41→42 transition, steady at 3 |
| candidate set/ordering | the 41→42 transition, identical 8-PR set |
| daemon ordered_candidates | the 41→42 transition, steady at 5 across a real refresh |

The honest conclusion is that slot count varies for reasons not visible in any field sampled here. No sixth mechanism is proposed. Note that CI check state is one dimension neither observer sampled, and PR check transitions did occur during this window; that is offered only as an unsampled dimension, NOT as a proposed cause.

Directly actionable consequence for anyone sizing a stopgap: slots have been observed at 33, 36, 41 and 42, with `main` quiet for most of that range. Any `sync.max_duration_secs` or `command_timeout_secs` value sized against a single observed slot count will be wrong within about an hour. A stopgap must carry headroom above the observed range rather than tracking the current reading, and even then it only moves the cliff.

This also reinforces requirement 3 above: a reserve computed from a quantity that moves unpredictably, while assuming every command consumes its full timeout, cannot be made safe by tuning. It has to be replaced by a reserve tied to work actually attempted.

Formula status: twelfth consecutive exact hit, 42 x 120000 = 5040000, so `ad14f74` had still not reached the observed runtime at this point.

## Head-of-line handoff gap REPRODUCED: autonomous root merge twice, autonomous handoff zero times

The deadlock's user-visible signature has now been observed twice in one night with identical shape, which upgrades it from an incident to a reproduced defect.

Occurrence 1: root `#2208` merged natively once green; caravan re-formed as `2210`; the base retarget to `main` and the squash re-arm were then performed BY HAND by the member's owner after `cara sync` refused pre-mutation on the budget reserve.

Occurrence 2: root `#2210` merged natively at 06:03:38 with all checks green and no intervention; `main` advanced to `176fd149d37ecbcf7b7b90652dde277a80abb7ec`; the caravan re-formed as `2213` with five members `[2213, 2215, 2223, 2225, 2227]`. Canonical immediately went degraded with exactly two problems:

```
dangling_base: PR #2213 still targets merged predecessor #2210; sync must advance it to `main`
auto_merge_invariant: caravan head #2213 must have squash auto-merge enabled
```

Verified independently: `#2213` is OPEN and CLEAN with zero failing and zero pending checks, its base is still the agent branch of its predecessor rather than `main`, and it has no auto-merge armed.

What this establishes:

- Automatic ROOT MERGE works and is proven twice. Given an armed root and green required checks, the provider lands it with no operator or sync involvement.
- Automatic CHAIN HANDOFF has never once occurred. Both times, the two repairs that promote the next member to root, base retarget and root arming, were left undone because physical sync refuses before its mutation phase.
- The two failures are therefore not independent. The budget refusal is precisely what prevents the handoff, so every root merge produces a degraded queue that then requires manual repair to continue.

Consequence for acceptance: a canary or proof that only observes "the root merged" is measuring the half that already works. The falsifiable criterion is that after a root merges, the successor is advanced to `main` and armed WITHOUT manual intervention. That has zero successful observations to date.

Deliberately NOT repaired by hand on this occurrence, so the reproduction is preserved as evidence rather than overwritten.

## The deadline is never fully available: a chain sized exactly to max_duration_secs still cannot start

A later observation reduces this from a large structural gap to a marginal one, and in doing so exposes a clean off-by-planning defect in the admission arithmetic.

Measured: 30 slots, `required_ms = 3600000`, `remaining = 3416655`, short by only 183345. Every earlier pass was short by between 384574 and 1557755.

Two arithmetic consequences, both derived purely from observed numbers rather than any proposed mechanism:

1. At 30 slots the projection is EXACTLY 3600000ms, which is exactly the configured `sync.max_duration_secs: 3600`. So a chain sized precisely to the entire deadline still cannot begin, because planning has already consumed roughly 183000ms before the apply reserve is computed. The reserve is checked against REMAINING budget while the admissible chain size is implicitly reasoned about against TOTAL budget. The two are never equal, so the effective capacity is strictly less than the configured deadline and always will be. Any capacity calculation, cap, or stopgap that uses `max_duration_secs` directly is off by the planning cost.
2. At 28 slots the projection would be 3360000ms, which fits inside the observed 3416655ms remaining. So the chain is roughly two slots from being able to mutate unaided, and may simply begin working after another member or two drains, with no config change at all.

Point 1 should be treated as a durable requirement rather than an observation. Whatever replaces the current reserve must either compare like with like, by computing admissible size against budget actually remaining at reserve time, or must reserve planning explicitly so the comparison is honest. Otherwise the boundary condition is permanently unreachable and the system is guaranteed to refuse a chain it was configured to accept.

Point 2 is also a caution for interpreting any future success. If the queue starts moving after further drain, that is NOT evidence that a deployed fix worked. It would be the chain falling below the marginal threshold on its own. Distinguishing the two requires the behavioural check recorded elsewhere in this bead: a `required_ms` that is no longer an exact multiple of `command_timeout_secs`.

Successor criterion at this point, independently verified by cluster control across all five remaining members:

| PR | mergeStateStatus | armed | base |
|---|---|---|---|
| #2213 | CLEAN | false | `agent/ms-dev-3/...8x5t4` (predecessor #2210 MERGED) |
| #2215 | CLEAN | false | `agent/ms-dev-3/...h8e3r` |
| #2223 | CLEAN | false | `agent/ms-dev-6/...d23tq` |
| #2225 | CLEAN | false | `agent/ms-dev-6/...v2dom` |
| #2227 | UNSTABLE | false | `agent/ms-dev-5/...3ru8p` |

Four of five are CLEAN, unarmed, and dangling on a predecessor branch. Nothing advanced any base or armed anything autonomously in roughly the first hour after the root merged. Formula status at this point: fifteenth consecutive exact hit, 30 x 120000 = 3600000.

## RESOLVED IN BEHAVIOUR: the predicted discriminator fired positive on 0.0.11

The falsifiable test specified earlier in this bead has now run and returned the passing result.

Test as specified in advance: on `0.0.10` the reserve was `required_ms = command_slots x command_timeout_secs` exactly, sixteen consecutive exact hits. The agreed discriminator was that a `required_ms` which is NOT a flat multiple of `command_timeout_secs` proves the bounded-prefix work is live, while an exact multiple would mean the binary changed but the reserve logic did not.

Measured by cluster control via read-only `cara status --json` in the canonical daemon checkout, at main `7c0bb4158e13ce20673b3a62699fdfef827406dc`:

```
sync_budget.command_timeout_ms = 600000
sync_budget.deadline_ms        = 3600000
caravan 2215: required_ms = 315000, retained_ms = 240000, processable_prefix = [2215, 2223, 2225, 2227]
caravan 2233: required_ms = 135000, retained_ms = 105000, processable_prefix = [2233]
```

Neither 315000 nor 135000 is a multiple of 600000. Under the old model a four-member chain at a 600000ms command timeout would have reserved several million milliseconds against a 3600000ms deadline and refused before mutation, as it did all night at 120000ms per slot. Instead it reserves 315000ms, under nine percent of the deadline, and publishes an explicit processable prefix covering all four members.

This satisfies the substance of requirements 1, 3 and 5 recorded above: the reserve now models work actually attempted rather than a whole-chain worst case, a processable prefix is exposed in status rather than only after a refusal, and the deadlock condition no longer arises for these chains.

Three caveats deliberately attached:

- The runtime measured is the MUTABLE cargo-installed `0.0.11` at `/home/harry/.cargo/bin/cara`, not the reviewed store closure. This is evidence that the CODE behaves correctly. It is NOT evidence that the reviewed artifact is deployed; that claim belongs to the Cacophony-side deployment bead and remains unproven.
- Config changed underneath the measurement series. `command_timeout_secs` is now 600 on main and canonical while the sixteen-hit baseline was taken at 120, and `sync.max_duration_secs` was briefly 65525 before being corrected to 3600 at commit `7c0bb4158e13`. The discriminator survives this because it is stated as "not a flat multiple of `command_timeout_secs`, whatever that value is", rather than as a literal 120000.
- Admission remains closed: `max_admissible_members = 0` with at-capacity wording, so existing caravans can drain but new members cannot join. Whether that is intended gating or a second independent bound is not established here.

Credit: the discriminator was formulated by the helsinki profile worker from the original `required_ms = slots x command_timeout_secs` derivation, generalised by it to be independent of the literal timeout value, and specified before the fix was observable, which is what makes this a test rather than a post-hoc reading.

## Reopened: admission capacity still uses legacy full-timeout slots

Canonical Cacophony config now has `sync.max_duration_secs=3600`, `command_timeout_secs=600`; Cara0.0.11 proportional reserve defaults to 15 seconds per command. Read-only canonical status proves physical prefixes work: caravan2215 has 21 required slots but `required_ms=315000`, and 16 retained slots give `retained_ms=240000`, both exactly 15s/slot with the full four-member prefix processable.

However `max_admissible_members()` still calls `deadline_command_slots()`, which divides the deadline by the full child timeout: `3600/600=6`. The minimum ordinary chain-capacity shape exceeds six slots, so capacity is projected as zero and every nonempty caravan is `at_capacity`. `blocked_candidate=2234` and `caravan_budget_capacity_exhausted` close joins even though the same status proves the existing chain fits comfortably under the proportional reserve.

This is a mixed-model regression: apply/drain budgeting uses the landed proportional reserve while admission capacity retains the retired worst-case timeout arithmetic. With no caravans, one independent root may still start, but it cannot accept a second member; normal batching collapses to serial one-member caravans.

Required:

- derive `max_admissible_members` from the same proportional reserve/model used by `admit_physical_prefix`, or deterministically simulate the hardest one-pending-member shape through that model;
- retain worst-case timeout only as evidence, never as the admission bound;
- preserve fail-closed zero capacity only when the proportional model truly cannot process one member;
- tests for deadline3600/timeout600/reserve15 expecting positive multi-member capacity and consistency between projected capacity, processable prefix and typed refusal;
- status must not say a full processable prefix is simultaneously over a zero-member bound;
- preserve existing new-independent-caravan and real no-progress safeguards.

Runtime provenance caveat: measurement used mutable cargo Cara0.0.11, not reviewed store deployment, but source inspection independently confirms the mixed formulas in `src/sync/budget.rs`.

Caco-merger independently verified Caravan bd-9264d0 deployment before retrying PR #1962:

The longer timeout/resume work is functioning as designed, but a full cold SSH clone remains unusable under a persistent provider sideband disconnect. Repeating the same full clone is not a recovery strategy.

- Make the partial repository resumable in place after transport interruption. A same-session retry must reuse already received verified objects rather than deleting and retransferring the whole repository.

- Optionally seed from a canonical verified provider checkout or shared object cache/alternates, but re-read the configured provider remote and exact head/target before use; never trust daemon-internal refs as publication proof.
- Use bounded SSH keepalive/low-speed/progress settings where appropriate, with no unbounded loops and no global SSH/Git config mutation.

- Add fixtures where the first fetch disconnects mid-sideband and exact resume completes from partial objects, plus head/target drift refusal and repeated-disconnect bounded failure.

title: Prove live sync rebases the root, merges green, and promotes its child
description:
## Observed gap

The Cacophony repository explicitly configures `rebase_on_join: true` and `sync.head_merge_actor: caravan`, but the operator has never observed a live sync tick merge a green root or promote the second member.

At 2026-07-31T15:44Z, after `main` advanced at 15:19Z to `8d4bac65e679b8ddcbf6f1659bcb6b46f31679bb`, live provider facts were:

- root PR #2331: head `3753825bba3c87a95319e7b02c84a968baa2966c`, base `main`, compare status `diverged`, ahead 2 / behind 1, provider `MERGEABLE` but `BLOCKED`;
- required aggregate `Check & Lint` was FAILURE and `Rust Check & Lint work` was CANCELLED, so root merge was correctly not yet authorized;
- child PR #2330 already targeted #2331's branch.

The configured `cara-sync` cron runs on Helsinki every 15 minutes. Under strict physical mode, a completed tick should still plan/rebase the root and descendants onto the exact current default generation before waiting for fresh CI. If #2331 remains behind after a completed tick, preserve the tick's full structured stdout/stderr and fix the actual refusal rather than weakening safety on inference.

## Required work

1. Capture the latest complete `cara sync --all --json` success/refusal from the supervised Helsinki worktree, including exact Cara binary version and runtime commit/pin.
2. Determine whether the tick did not run, failed before physical planning, lacked apply reserve, rejected a generation/topology/lease precondition, or successfully no-op'd for a documented reason.
3. Fix the same-repository defect or route an exact operational dependency; do not guess from provider `mergeable` alone.
4. Demonstrate live progression on disposable/current authorized generations:
   - root physically follows the exact current default when strict mode is enabled;
   - fresh required CI binds that rewritten head;
   - a fully green root receives a sealed `root_merge` receipt and non-admin squash lands on main;
   - the child is retargeted/promoted to main with a sealed `root_promotion` receipt in the same bounded tick when allowance remains or the next tick otherwise.
5. Preserve the existing virtual mode boundary: `rebase_on_join: false` already avoids constant history rewrites. Any future hybrid that merges a behind root must bind checks to GitHub's exact current synthetic merge candidate and prove squash result/retained-patch safety; plain `MERGEABLE` is not sufficient.

## Acceptance

- One complete live receipt chain proves root update -> fresh CI -> root merge -> child promotion, or a typed refusal names the exact unresolved external condition.
- Regression fixtures pin the root-behind-main and post-merge child promotion shapes.
- The cron's spoken summary remains convenience only; full structured evidence stays in logs.
- GitHub native stacks audit `bd-e3069d` remains deferred until this fundamental path is proven.

## Exact supervised refusal captured

Helsinki runs `cara 0.0.60`. The 15:32 and 15:47 UTC scheduled ticks both started from Cacophony main `8d4bac65e679b8ddcbf6f1659bcb6b46f31679bb` and failed before writes with `rebase_cousin_history`, decision fingerprint `fnv1a64:3a5bdf677d643926`.

The root #2331 planned successfully from old head `3753825bba3c87a95319e7b02c84a968baa2966c` onto current main, yielding retained planned head `7fb30b3c40b238a677d9c13fe22622e0d57975ef`. Child #2330 head `6d9304953ecd1ee38a8f54a9167e0fda5b186703` is a two-parent merge with parents `61727d484cc2ca2d7223d1caf60b1367bd9aeadb` and the exact old root `3753825bba3c87a95319e7b02c84a968baa2966c`. Topology validation incorrectly treated that exact provider base as foreign because a physical rebase means the planned root no longer contains the old root commit by ancestry.

This is deterministic product behavior, not a missing tick or CI gate. The bounded fix maps only the exact old provider base to its retained same-batch simulated parent, verifies every other parent as before, independently proves the final merge tree, and seals old/new parent identity in the topology receipt.

## Live acceptance checkpoint — 2026-07-31 16:43 UTC

- `v0.0.61` release workflow `30645938021` completed successfully at landed `c376c1b`; all Darwin/Linux assets and SHA256 files are published.
- Helsinki has already advanced to `cara 0.0.62`, which contains the `v0.0.61` topology fix.
- The old deterministic `rebase_cousin_history` refusal disappeared. The supervised 16:40 sync owner reached `physical_rebase_applied` for the live chain, with exact receipts:
  - root #2331: `cce82efdf04a23a1f796a2dea3a86766f8976d03` on `main@2f7aa88389ac7d86cd535d01ba57fc62bb711ec9`;
  - child #2330: `a32f123946b667a18c72261ad949cb6bfb51353c` on the exact rewritten root `cce82efd...`;
  - #2332: `b4604b0c6e29d5df087d14b34d4b737c164b90b0` on #2330's exact rewritten head;
  - #2333: `e9ee4c1662d8f45d228b92d696c7c2c9c483c7ac` on #2332's exact rewritten head.
- GitHub independently reports those exact head/base relationships. Fresh CI runs are active on the rewritten generations.
- The cron invocation observed `operation_lock_contended` only because the prior bounded sync was still live and advancing (owner age 42s, non-indeterminate, phase `physical_rebase_applied`); no stale-lock intervention is authorized or needed.

Remaining acceptance: wait for exact-generation root CI to turn green, then require the sealed #2331 root merge and #2330 promotion/retarget receipt. The bug remains open until those provider facts are observed.

## Newly proven P1 liveness blocker — `bd-e500b0`

At 17:07 UTC, `main` had remained exactly `23a0b5cc79c865b9083fb45b45109d26b78237df` since 16:39, but root #2331 changed from `a2589ef...` to `44086280...`. Both are two commits ahead of that same main with identical ordered subjects and identical per-commit tree OIDs; only reset timestamps/OIDs differ. The second rewrite cancelled the prior exact-generation CI (`Check & Lint` and `Fast Tests` were cancelled/failed as superseded) and started a third run. This is not external main churn: strict sync is non-idempotently replacing an already-based root. `bd-e500b0` owns the exact no-op fix and now blocks final root-merge acceptance.

## Operator force contract correction — `bd-91e96a`

Harry confirmed that `cara force` is durable PR-scoped intent: when that PR reaches caravan head, if mechanically mergeable, ignore CI and merge it immediately. Existing exact-generation invalidation is contrary to the intended contract. Live #2331 also proved `cara force` incorrectly blocks on unrelated incompatible admission candidates (#2245, #2259, #2314). `bd-91e96a` owns rewrite preservation, non-head arming, selected-caravan problem scope, and immediate forced-root CI short-circuit. The correction was broadcast project-wide before implementation.

## Final live acceptance — cara 0.0.64, operation `019fb99d-8f9a-7a00-8004-82615da66ca3`

The complete requested root-update/force-merge/child-promotion path is now proven on the live Cacophony repository:

- Durable force was armed on root #2331 at exact head `26b87c8966cde39966862591be7edff5707d238e`, base `main@8b4bf4654fcc0553c984a8de18d3e68b9d1cd741`, actor `harryaskham`, reason `cargo.lock broken on main`. The audited arm receipt was `019fb995-e5f4-7360-8485-c9719d116689`.
- The next ordinary `cara 0.0.64` sync emitted `force_merge_attempted` with `ci_bypassed=true` while visible checks included `Rust Check & Lint work=FAILURE` and `Rust Fast Tests work=IN_PROGRESS`. No CI or required-run gate prevented consumption.
- The same operation emitted `force_merge_completed` and GitHub reports #2331 `MERGED` at 2026-07-31T19:19:11Z with squash/default commit `24300a1f0c7e7ad50902961f47dc5acf98e024e9`.
- The operation then emitted `root_promoted` for child #2330 with sealed `RootPromotionReceipt`:
  - base before: #2331 branch at `26b87c8...`;
  - base after: `main@24300a1...`;
  - child head unchanged: `ec3988c82c3131f07d8bb58b29f9bdcd86f30ee0`;
  - predecessor #2331 proved merged;
  - trigger `merged_predecessor_retarget`;
  - evidence hash `fnv1a64:448b411cc87c2031`;
  - confirmation reads: 1.
- GitHub independently reports #2330 OPEN directly on `main@24300a1...`.
- `force_merge_attempted`, `force_merge_completed`, `root_promoted`, and `head_advanced` share the same exact operation id. The force-completed and promotion hook deliveries succeeded; the attempted-event best-effort hook timed out but did not affect the completed provider transaction.

This closes the acceptance requested by the operator. The nonlinear old-parent mapping, unchanged-root idempotency, durable force semantics, direct admin squash, and child promotion are all proven in production with exact provider/journal evidence.

title: Add bounded event journal with cara log and cara log -f

title: Make semantic grant apply and revoke recover from partial persistence
description:
A bounded post-landing audit of `bd-17375b` found two partial-persistence states that the public grant/revoke commands cannot currently reconcile.

1. In `src/repair.rs:1099-1133`, `grant_paths` persists new receipts with `applied: false`, writes/stages each expected blob, then persists `applied: true`. If the second manifest write fails after `git add`, the next identical grant call observes `baseline_oid == expected_result_oid` and takes the idempotent `continue` branch without setting the existing receipt to `applied: true`. It can return `already_applied: true`, while `repair continue` remains permanently blocked by `repair_grant_incomplete`.

2. In `src/repair.rs:1218-1267`, `revoke_grants` validates and mutates one path at a time. A later actor/drift/write failure can leave earlier paths revoked, making an exact retry fail with `repair_grant_not_found`. A manifest-write failure after restoring/staging the baseline but before removing the receipt leaves the receipt expecting the semantic result, so retry fails with `repair_grant_result_drift`.

Make both commands resumable and receipt-driven across every persisted/index state, preferably by validating the whole requested set before mutation and explicitly reconciling `(receipt.applied, actual index OID)` states. Add fault-injection tests around manifest publication after staging and a multi-path revocation where a later path fails. Preserve the fail-closed scope and provider non-mutation guarantees.

2026-07-21 burn-down triage: promoted from draft for v0.0.6 because this is a concrete repair-session correctness hole with known persisted-state reproductions; implementation remains isolated from msm1's owned physical-rebase work.
