title: Cara admission: elect a canonical from diverged same-stream sets and repair-route a stuck canonical
description:
Two Cara admission improvements proven by the bd-0dec13 / bd-6e888a incident, filed so they are not lost now that the acute wedge is closed. Both are Cara-side (Caravan), not Cacophony source; sent to the Cara developer as `msg-019fa013-448a-77d1-85e8-3b56240f7c50`.

## 1. A diverged same-stream set has no owner exit

When successive generations of one agent/bead stream differ by **rebase** rather than by added commits, no exact source containment exists between them and Cara fails the whole stream closed:

`fail closed: same-stream open generations are divergent or unproved: 2196...2197=Diverged, 2196...2198=Diverged, 2197...2198=Diverged`

All candidates are then dropped from the FIFO order (`blocks_order=false`), so the newest one can never be reached however far the queue drains. The owner cannot recover: Cara never auto-closes generations, and no first-party surface lets an owner close or withdraw one. On this incident that state held a P0 Pages fix for roughly seven hours.

The mechanism itself works — it just needs the owner to hand-craft history. Publishing a containment merge (identical tree, previously published heads as parents) immediately produced:

- #2196/#2197/#2198 -> `superseded_generation`, `canonical_pr=2220`
- #2220 -> `current_generation`, "unique canonical generation for this exact Cacophony agent/bead/stack slot (exact source containment)"

Proposed: elect a canonical from a diverged set (newest head on the freshest base; the rest `superseded_generation`) exactly as the containment path does, or expose an explicit owner-side supersession declaration so an octopus merge is not the only exit.

## 2. An unrepairable elected canonical wedges every other candidate

PR #2117 held the canonical first-admission slot while untouched since 2026-07-23, conflicting with main in `crates/caco-cli/src/config_repository_validation.rs`, red on `Check & Lint`, `Fast Tests (unit)`, and `Public Fast Tests preparation`, and classified by Cara's own check as `next_action=repair`. Every clean candidate behind it received `candidate is not canonical first admission attempt; fail closed on PR #2117`, stalling at least three P0/P1 owners (#2198, #2206, and the #2201 class). The same shape recurred twelve hours earlier on #2113 (bd-5504c9), so it is a repeating class, not a one-off.

Proposed: when the elected canonical's own check returns `next_action=repair`, route it for repair and advance election instead of rejecting every candidate behind it.

## Cacophony-side counterpart

bd-220916 already tracks publish leaving predecessor generations open when the head moves. Note the interaction: this repository's retryable-rejection guidance tells owners to `caco agent rebase` and retry `complete`, which is precisely the head move that manufactures the unprovable divergence in (1).

## 3. `auto_merge_invariant` should re-arm the head, not only report it

Observed overnight on caravan head #2210 (owner `8x5t4zp7luvs0a4q`, evidence in their 06:13Z message):

- the owner armed squash auto-merge at 02:26:12Z, together with the `gh pr edit --base main` that cleared the DanglingBase row;
- GitHub then **silently disarmed** it when a required check went red (`Check & Lint` failed 03:38 on runner `cacophony-ms-dev-2`, from the unrelated `tests/source-guard-tooling-fixtures.sh` step-6 silent abort now tracked as bd-bcb813 / bd-603883);
- Cara subsequently reported `next_action=repair` for every enrolled member with the single problem `caravan head #2210 must have squash auto-merge enabled`, which reads exactly like "the owner never armed it";
- the caravan stayed parked for roughly three hours until the owner manually re-ran the failed jobs and re-armed at 05:12:47Z. Members behind it, including the P0 Pages fix #2225, could do nothing but wait.

The asymmetry is the defect: **disarm is automatic, re-arm is manual.** Any caravan head that ever goes transiently red loses the auto-merge invariant permanently until a human intervenes, so one flaky required check converts into an unbounded fleet-wide stall.

Proposed: when `auto_merge_invariant` detects a head whose auto-merge is off but which is otherwise an eligible enrolled head, re-arm squash auto-merge itself (idempotently, with a receipt naming the head, the prior disarm evidence, and the actor) instead of only emitting a repair problem. Failing that, the reported problem should distinguish "never armed" from "armed then disarmed by a red check at <time>", so the owner and any triaging agent can tell a missing action from provider behaviour.

Reported by agent 3ru8pp8fgdkebnq9 on behalf of the #2210 owner's suggested follow-up; the two admission fixes above came from the same incident chain.

## Item 3 superseded by operator decision (2026-07-27 08:30Z)

Harry announced that auto-merge will be disabled on the cacophony repo and Caravan will instead squash-merge a valid, compatible HEAD on each tick and advance the next member's target to `main`, so lifecycle stops being a mix of Caravan and GitHub auto-merge. That makes item 3 above moot in its literal form: there is no auto-merge flag left to re-arm. Do not build the re-arm.

What the item's evidence still argues for, and should carry over into the tick-owned design:

- The stall was invisible because the reported problem could not distinguish provider behaviour from owner inaction. Whatever replaces it should name the transition it is waiting on and who can perform it, so a member behind the head can tell 'head not yet processed by tick' from 'head needs an owner action'.
- The dangling-base half is now first-class work for the tick: the identical `still targets merged predecessor #NNNN; sync must advance it to main` pair appeared on three consecutive heads (#2210, #2213, #2215), because the chain is stacked and every merge orphans the next base.

Sequencing risk worth recording: moving all lifecycle onto the tick makes the tick a single point of failure while it is still failing. Every `cara-sync` run has exited 69 with 'queue mutation was skipped; provision a launchable system Cara for this runner' since at least 2026-07-26T16:07Z, and ms-dev-5's runner unit reports `tool=cara ... missing_source_pin` for CACO_CARA_BIN even though #2217 landed the `.#ci-runner` composition in-repo. Provision the Linux runner pool and confirm one green tick before disabling auto-merge, or the repository is left with no working merge path at all.

## Recurrence 2026-08-04 — PR #2415 / bd-804c7d

The same elected-canonical repair wedge recurred on a clean, mergeable current-base candidate:

- candidate PR: #2415
- owner: `7sypyuy6qjt2zfz8`
- bead: `bd-804c7d`
- exact head: `53f9cd371b51ca5205d48e97d874dc2c9eb4fbf9`
- expected main: `cd103ca2c2c9ad08cdc72b47fcf3fca829a800a3`
- dead letter: `rdl-019fca2c-c03d-7051-bb07-780560efd68f`
- idempotency key: `488da5c06b74f75d0fde55aaf069b8f21b761a3ecf37856c0d949cabb4e58d2f`
- Cara check returned `next_action=repair` before admission

title: Bind GitHub App runtime identity to strict repository config
description:
Child of bd-b15483 after bd-02242b. Add strict non-secret repository policy for GitHub auth identity and bind runtime deployment environment to it.

Mismatch fails closed with secret-free typed config/startup diagnostics. This ensures broker/environment alone cannot override repository policy and multi-repo web cannot mix installations accidentally.

Do not perform environment validation in pure `config validate` parsing, so policy can be reviewed without credentials. Add pure runtime-value validation tests plus AppContext/web coverage. title: Cut v0.0.82 for superseded-red parking and membership fixes
description:
## Why

Helsinki fleet queue runs Cara `0.0.81` while Caravan main contains three unreleased fixes:

```text
61950727 bd-e4955a: prove cancelled prerequisites never park
e9e9a482 bd-59f6d2: bind membership to rewritten head
468abd22 bd-42928c: publish releases to canonical GitHub
```

Live consequence: Cacophony chain `#2393 → #2386 → #2394 → #2395` is parked-red after #2395 advanced from genuinely red head `2f3a46c...` to repaired head `1f9bc351...`, whose current checks have no failure. The fix is landed but not deployed.

## Required

Cut exactly one repository-native Caravan `v0.0.82` release from reviewed current main using `scripts/release.sh`/canonical atomic branch+tag publication. Verify branch/tag commit identity and GitHub release assets. Do not use Cacophony release leases or manually move tags. Report exact tag, commit, workflow/assets and upgrade route for Helsinki. Do not mutate the Cacophony queue directly.

## Deployment blocker — Helsinki self-update cannot consume authenticated GitHub credential

`v0.0.82` is published at main/tag `91cc25797436` with four assets. Helsinki remains on Cara 0.0.81.

First-party deployment attempts from the canonical Caravan worktree:

```text
cara self-update check
cara self-update run
```

Both refused with GitHub releases/latest HTTP 403 and left version 0.0.81 unchanged. A single authenticated retry with ephemeral `GH_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)"` produced the same refusal; token value was neither printed nor persisted. The updater reports that its library must be configured with `with_github_token` or `with_gh_token_fallback`, indicating the CLI path is not consuming the normal authenticated environment.

Do not manually copy release assets or repeat unauthenticated retries. Complete this release task by providing a reviewed first-party authenticated self-update/deployment route, then update Helsinki and prove `cara --version == 0.0.82` plus the repaired head `1f9bc351...` is not parked by superseded red.

## Deployment completed — authenticated first-party self-update

Published release:

- canonical main/tag commit: `91cc25797436382de8280966e702f454509d5c14`
- tag: `v0.0.82`
- four assets published
- Helsinki installed path: `/home/harry/.local/bin/cara`
- installed version: `cara 0.0.82`
- installed SHA-256: `150c30d3e1cb26dbc61bab7ccc08d23bc4e0addb56d602b1183586491807fc26`

The initial deployment failures were authenticated GitHub API quota exhaustion, not missing updater auth support. Current Cara already reads explicit `GITHUB_TOKEN` and enables `gh auth token` fallback. Both configured github.com user tokens independently reported remaining quota 0. The authoritative reset was `2026-08-03T11:47:42Z`; no retries were made until after reset.

Exact successful reviewed route (executed remotely through first-party `caco ssh`, token never printed or persisted):

```bash
set -euo pipefail
token="$(gh auth token --user harryaskham)"
export GITHUB_TOKEN="$token"
unset GH_TOKEN
cara self-update check
cara self-update run
hash -r
installed="$(command -v cara)"
cara --version
sha256sum "$installed"
```

Post-reset `self-update check` resolved `v0.0.82` and all four expected assets. `self-update run` reported current/latest 0.0.82 with no further promotion needed, proving another first-party updater path had completed during the bounded quota wait; final path/version/hash were verified explicitly.

Cron guidance: use `GITHUB_TOKEN`, not `GH_TOKEN`, sourcing it at runtime from `gh auth token` without logging/persisting the bearer.

No Cacophony queue mutation occurred. No v0.0.83 was cut for closure; post-tag wrapper `f2f94e32` is separate source work.

title: Allow forced self-update into a user-owned PATH directory
description: Depends on updatable-cli/bd-e195f5 (install to an explicit target directory). Today self-update refuses with self_update_package_managed when the running binary is Nix or Homebrew managed. That is correct about never writing into the store, but leaves no escape hatch when the pin lags the release: an operator on a /nix/store caravan 0.0.7 binary had no first-party way to run a newer Cara without a full rebuild. Operator direction 2026-07-27: a forced update must NOT rewrite the store; it downloads into a user-owned directory that PATH already prefers, leaving the package-managed binary untouched underneath. Required: never write into /nix/store or a Homebrew cellar under any flag, since a store path whose contents no longer match its hash is a corrupted closure; install into a user-owned directory defaulting to ~/.local/bin and overridable explicitly; verify that directory actually PRECEDES the package-managed binary in the effective PATH before writing and refuse with exact evidence otherwise, because a silent no-op update is worse than a refusal; emit a loud typed receipt naming both resolved paths, both versions and the artifact hash recording that the new binary shadows a package-managed one; keep it trivially reversible so deleting the file restores the package-managed binary. Safety context: this is the shadowing behind the ms-dev-2 incident where a cargo-installed 0.0.10 sat ahead of the reviewed store 0.0.8, segfaulted under nix-ld with empty output, and looked like a quiet queue for hours. Runtime provenance shipped in v0.0.11 makes shadowing provable from any status receipt, so the forced path must surface that evidence rather than hide it. Document plainly that a forced install is a temporary local override and the durable fix is updating the package pin.

title: Ineligible candidates must not wedge automatic admission
description:

description:
Cacophony's Cara queue is stopped outright: `cara sync --all` fails in discovery, phase one, so no admission, no chain planning and no merges run.

The cause is entirely a version gap. Cacophony pins caravan `ab97f9e` = **v0.0.51**. Three fixes are on main and **no existing tag carries any of them**, latest tag being v0.0.54:

    9bff2d2  bd-54222d  a null check rollup means no checks, not a failed read
    8abb215  bd-35a9fd  stop an unknown journal record from killing a sync
    0a3d434  bd-4e0430  skip and name one unusable PR record instead of failing discovery

Built both runtimes and ran the same read-only command against the live Cacophony board from the daemon checkout, same repository and same minute:

    cara 0.0.51, built from cacophony's own flake.lock (ab97f9e)
      -> ERROR github_discovery_failed

      -> DISCOVERY OK
         caravans:       2300 [2300], 2311 [2311], 2313 [2313]
         next_candidate: 2276
         queue:          2276, 2301, 2305, 2306, 2309, 2315, 2316
         skipped:        2245, 2259  (mechanically incompatible; no rerun changes that)

So the queue is undamaged. Every symptom is the pin.

## Scope

Cut one release from current main. Version bump only — `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`, matching the shape of the v0.0.54 release commit. No code.

Deployment to Cacophony is a separate step: the hourly `just update-flake` advances the pin on its own, so this bead ends at a published release, not at a pin bump.

msm0 had validated and begun cutting v0.0.55 when the collision was spotted, and stood down rather than race version tags; its local release commit `0dffda2` was never published and no v0.0.55 tag exists. Three Cara versions are live against one repository — 0.0.22 on the cron, 0.0.51 in the pin, 0.0.54 on main — and the journal-variant crash is exactly that shape: an older reader refusing a record a newer writer emitted. The cron will keep meeting records it cannot parse until whatever pins it is advanced too.

description:

description:

title: A candidate-scoped conflict aborts a tick after its rebases have landed
description:
A tick rewrote two branch generations under exact leases, converged both caravans, reached final rediscovery, and then aborted with `invalid_graph` naming "the current default branch". Live, from an operator's run:

    initial_discovery: discovered 2 caravan(s), 12 unqueued PR(s)
    rebase_applied: rewrote 2 branch generation(s) under exact leases
    midpoint_rediscovery: revalidating every pushed generation
    provider_convergence: converged 2 caravan(s) with 0 completed provider mutation(s)
    final_rediscovery: reading the authoritative post-mutation graph
    cara invalid_graph: ... the current default branch

`first_blocking_completion_problem` decides whether the post-mutation graph converged. It never asks whether a problem gates the fleet:

    let Some(number) = force_head_auto_merge_gap(status, problem, force_merge) else {
        return true;
    };

Anything not of that one specific shape counts as blocking. A `CandidateIncompatible` problem describes an UNADMITTED pull request in no caravan, so it cannot describe a failure to converge, but it takes that branch and aborts the tick.

On the live fleet #2245 and #2259 have been permanently incompatible with main all day, so EVERY tick did its rebases and then aborted at the last step. Nothing has merged since 11:05 while the queue formed caravans and planned chains correctly throughout. The work was done and then discarded.

THIS IS A SITE I MISSED. bd-226a07 fixed exactly this class: the two admission gates were asking `is_candidate_scoped()`, which names one non-blocking category, and stopped seeing a second. I fixed those two gates, verified them, and reported the class closed. There are FOUR `decision_for_problem` call sites; the other two route through this function, and I never traced them. Tenth instance of a rule applied at one site and not its siblings, and the second time I have committed it in the act of fixing that very class.

WHAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: enumerating the call sites rather than the ones I had already found. `grep -n 'decision_for_problem('` returns four lines and takes seconds. I ran that grep tonight only because an operator pasted a log I could not explain.

title: Implement reviewed Cara force-intent preview/apply contract required by Caco
description:
## Live blocker

Cacophony's reviewed first-party exception surface (`caco cara force-preview|force-apply|force-revoke`, SPEC 17.2 / bd-2d33b0) invokes the configured pinned Cara wrapper as:

`cara --json force-intent preview|apply|revoke --pr ... --head ... --membership-generation ... --failure-fingerprint ... --reason ... --expires-at-ms ... --auto-merge squash`

Reviewed Cara v0.0.7 rejects `force-intent` as an unrecognized subcommand. Caravan true main `657fb201d1f426de5fcf16339e56a1f4250c3bad` still only exposes the older `force arm|revoke` label surface in `src/force.rs`; it has no membership generation, required-check/decision `fnv1a64` fingerprint, bounded expiry, preview, or atomic force-intent-plus-squash-auto-merge receipt. Therefore Caco's audited force path cannot preview or apply any exact PR, despite being published and specified.

## Exact incident

PR #2120 head `4b5ddd6a9f1d61599d68ccd05e5c831dba1fc239` is an operator/controller-classified CI/control-plane blocker. Fresh true main `6bf8d95128a4e69a5e8517b5b69dc490caa16da0`, clean merge-tree `be437cc6244c9caace9f62deb85a207beff38eb3`, focused 40/40, clippy/rustfmt/SPEC green, and provider failure isolated to merge-ref fetch disconnect. Standing bounded force authority requires the typed force-preview/apply lane, but the reviewed Cara command needed to obtain/validate membership generation and failure fingerprint does not exist. No provider mutation attempted.

## Required behavior

- Implement exact `force-intent preview|apply|revoke` CLI/JSON/MCP parity matching Caco's published arguments and evidence validator.
- Every action independently re-reads exact provider PR/head, current membership generation, required checks, and current decision; stale supplied values fail closed with typed current evidence.
- Preview never mutates and returns exact `membership`, `required_checks`, `current_decision`, shared `fnv1a64` failure fingerprint, and expiry.
- Apply performs one atomic reviewed provider transaction recording exact-head force intent plus squash auto-merge and returns proof fields required by Caco.
- Revoke is idempotent, exact-generation, and rollback-safe even after expiry.
- Add drift/race/replay/expiry/no-op tests and preserve normal queue ownership.
- Include this fix in the sole reviewed Cara successor release tracked by `caravan/bd-1a7201`; no mutable-head/source fallback.
creator: helsinki:cacophony:helsinki-cacophony-cluster-ctrl

title: cara check cannot recommend joining a caravan it can see
description:
Every caravan on the cacophony fleet has exactly one member. The cause is not a policy choice and not a caco defect: `cara check` cannot recommend a join unless the caller already names the tail, and the caller is asking cara to determine precisely that.

THE FULL CHAIN, traced end to end:

    caco  crates/caco-cli/src/lib.rs:72409
          runs `cara --json check --pr <n>`        NO --tail-pr, NO --head-pr
    caco  cara_admission_action_from_check
          reads data.next_action, "new" -> New, "join" -> Join, anything else -> error
    cara  read.rs:1722
          let explicit_join = input.tail_pr.is_some() || input.head_pr.is_some();
    cara  read.rs:1767
          if !explicit_join { check_new(..) }      evaluates against the DEFAULT BRANCH only
          -> next_action: New, mode: NewCaravan
    caco  runs `cara join --pr <n>`  only if it got "join"; otherwise `cara new`

So caco asks the right question, cara answers "new" without ever considering an existing caravan, and caco faithfully creates another single-member one. Confirmed against the live fleet: the control-label audit markers on #2300, #2308, #2295 and #2287 all read `:new:`, while #2215 from 27 July reads `:join:` and did stack.

REPRODUCED IN A TEST. Added to read.rs tests, it fails today with `left: New, right: Join`:

    let member    = pr(1, "one", "main", true);
    let candidate = pr(9, "nine", "main", false);
    let status    = status(candidate.clone(), vec![member, candidate]);
    let output    = check_analysis(&status, &CheckInput::default(), &clean_checker).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(output.next_action, CandidateNextAction::Join);

THE OTHER ADMISSION PATH ALREADY DOES IT RIGHT. `sync::evaluate_auto_candidate` builds `current_tail_generations`, tries each tail, returns `Join(tail)` on the first eligible, and returns `Skip` rather than `New` when none fits. Two admission paths, opposite answers, and the one caco consults is the one that cannot say join.

WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE CHANGE, which is why I am filing rather than landing it. Setting `next_action` to Join alone leaves the rest of the output describing the other evaluation: `mode: CheckMode::NewCaravan`, `caravan_id: Some(current_pr)`, `target_pr: None`, and compatibility reports computed against the default branch. caco only reads `next_action`, so that would work and would be incoherent for every human and every other consumer. The coherent fix resolves an implicit target BEFORE `explicit_join` is decided, so the join path produces the join output.

CONSUMERS ENUMERATED, since the risk is changing what `next_action` means:
    caravan  read.rs sets it; sync.rs uses it only for a diagnostic reason string
    cacophony  exactly one reader, cara_admission_action_from_check, which already
               handles "join" and dispatches `cara join --pr <n>` with no tail, so
               cara resolves the tail itself and no caco change is required

NOT CLAIMED. It is a structural change to target resolution in the most consequential path in the tool, and it wants a fresh pass rather than the tail of a very long session.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, worked out while tracing and recorded so the next person does not have to rediscover it. Not prescriptive.

The incoherence I was worried about disappears if the target is resolved ONCE, before `explicit_join` is decided, rather than by patching `next_action` afterwards. Roughly:

    let explicit_join = input.tail_pr.is_some() || input.head_pr.is_some();

    // NEW: when the caller named no target, offer the caravan it could join.
    let implicit_tail = (!explicit_join)
        .then(|| joinable_tail(status, pull_request, checker))
        .transpose()?
        .flatten();

    let effective = match implicit_tail {
        Some(tail) => Cow::Owned(CheckInput { tail_pr: Some(tail.0), ..input.clone() }),
        None => Cow::Borrowed(input),
    };
    // then use `effective` everywhere `input` is used below

Every existing path then produces a COHERENT join output: `mode`, `caravan_id`, `target_pr` and the compatibility reports all describe the join, because they are the same code that already handles an explicit `--tail-pr`.

`joinable_tail` should mirror `sync::evaluate_auto_candidate` rather than invent a second policy: enumerate `current_tail_generations`, skip held caravans, test each with the checker, return the FIRST eligible tail, and return None when none fits. Returning None must fall through to the existing `check_new` path, so a candidate that cannot join cleanly still gets its own caravan, which is the correct outcome and not a regression.

COST: one merge-tree check per live tail, on a checker that already caches by (branch, exact oid). caco calls `check` on every reintegration, so this is not free, but it is the same work sync already does per candidate.

VERIFICATION THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE UNIT TEST: the fleet currently has zero caravans, so `join` cannot be exercised live. Whoever takes this should confirm against a fleet with at least one live caravan that `cara check --pr N` returns `next_action: join` AND a coherent `target_pr`, before trusting it. A green unit test here proves the branch is reachable, not that the recommendation is right.

## Code trace confirming the diagnosis, and the one crux the shape has to resolve

Read-only trace by crvn-dev-msm-1, deliberately NOT claimed for the reason the author gives: this is target resolution on the most consequential path, and a wrong next_action makes caco run the wrong mutating command. Recording what I verified so the next pass starts further along.

CONFIRMED, and better than the bead states: resolve_target_caravan ALREADY implements implicit resolution. read.rs around line 2015:

    match status.analysis.fleet.caravans.as_slice() {
        [caravan] => Ok(caravan),
        [] => Err(caravan_tail_not_found "there is no caravan to join; use `cara new`"),
        caravans => Err(ambiguous_caravan_tail),
    }

So the single-caravan case needs no new resolution logic at all. The only reason it never runs is the gate one call earlier:

    let explicit_join = input.tail_pr.is_some() || input.head_pr.is_some();
    let target_caravan = explicit_join.then(|| resolve_target_caravan(status, input)).transpose()?;

CONFIRMED the join branch is coherent and self-contained. It computes compatibility against the tail, additionally proves every other caravan head still attaches after the proposed new tail, and sets mode, caravan_id, target_pr and eligible correctly. Nothing there assumes the caller named a target, so it does not need changing.

THE CRUX, which is where the care is needed. Simply taking the join branch whenever exactly one caravan exists changes behaviour for a candidate that CANNOT cleanly join. Today it evaluates as new and forms a second caravan, which is legitimate: parallel caravans are supported and cross-caravan compatibility is proven. After a naive change it would instead return an ineligible join, and a candidate that could have progressed independently would be blocked.

So the shape has to be prefer-join-else-new, not join-instead-of-new:

  1. resolve an implicit target when exactly one caravan exists
  2. evaluate the join
  3. if the join is clean, return the join output as the join branch already builds it
  4. if it is not, fall back to the new evaluation and return that, ideally recording why the join was rejected so the reader can see the queue tried to stack first

Two evaluations means two compatibility passes in the fallback case, which is worth measuring against the tick budget before landing. Note bd-750d37, filed alongside this, observes that a tick already discards its compatibility cache between rediscoveries; the same cache would make this fallback nearly free.

WORTH KNOWING for the multi-caravan case: resolve_target_caravan returns ambiguous_caravan_tail for more than one caravan. sync::evaluate_auto_candidate already does the right thing there, trying each tail in turn 
LIVE REPRODUCTION, observed 2026-07-31 04:16:26 during a read-only watch. This is no longer inferred from code plus markers on closed pull requests; it is the defect happening with the alternative plainly available:

    PR #2324 created 04:16:26
      caravan-control-label-audit:v2:NEW:2324:b6c5edd10
      labels: [caravan]
    queued at that moment, all clean:
      #2317 #2318 #2319 #2321 #2322 #2323 #2325
    result: caravan #2324, members=[2324]

Seven candidates were available to join. The reintegration path asked `cara check --pr 2324` with no tail, was told `next_action: new`, and caco did exactly what it was told.

Note what it was NOT: not a sync tick. A tick evaluates tails and joins, pinned by the passing test `greedy_planner_forms_empty_fleet_then_uses_first_compatible_tail`. The two admission paths give opposite answers on identical state, and the one caco consults is the one that cannot recommend a join. That is why the fix belongs in `check_analysis` and not in caco or in policy.

SECOND LIVE REPRODUCTION, 2026-07-31 07:19:52, four hours after the first and with MORE candidates available:

    PR #2328 created 07:19:52
      caravan-control-label-audit:v2:NEW:2328:2ce8b0e61
      labels: [caravan]
    queued at that moment, all clean: ELEVEN candidates
    result: caravan #2328, members=[2328]

The first reproduction (#2324, 04:16) had seven candidates available; this had eleven. Same path, same `intent: new`, same outcome. The behaviour is not occasional or state-dependent: every pull request arriving through caco reintegration forms a single-member caravan regardless of how many candidates are queued beside it.

This also bounds what the 07:02 merge of #2324 demonstrated. A tick CAN complete and land a caravan, but each caravan it lands holds exactly one pull request, so the queue currently behaves as a serialised merge gate rather than a batching one. The purpose of stacking is that CI runs once against a composed head; with one member per caravan that saving never occurs.

MEASURED COST, two complete tick cycles observed 2026-07-31:

    #2324  formed 04:16 (intent: new, SEVEN candidates queued)  ->  merged 07:02
    #2328  formed 07:19 (intent: new, ELEVEN candidates queued) ->  merged 09:32

Both merged cleanly with the `caravan` label intact, so the queue works end to end: it forms caravans, rebases under exact leases, converges, and merges without aborting. Both caravans contained exactly ONE pull request.

Eleven candidates were queued throughout both cycles and are still queued now. So the observed drain rate is one pull request per tick cycle, roughly one every two and a half hours, while eleven compatible candidates sit beside it that could have ridden the same CI run.

That is the batching saving stacking exists for, not being realised, and it is now measured rather than argued. The defect does not make the queue incorrect; it makes it a serialised merge gate. Every property one would want from a merge queue is present except the one that motivates having a chain at all.

title: Worktree setup is priced as an ordinary command and excludes macOS
description:
JUSTIFICATION REVISED. The original premise was RETRACTED and the fix was kept on different grounds. Recording both so this does not become load-bearing by accident.

WHAT WAS CLAIMED, AND WITHDRAWN
bd-1a4e28 measured `git worktree add` on ms-mac at 23620/15816/12333 ms against a 10176ms sub-deadline and concluded macOS was STRUCTURALLY unable to complete a physical rebase. I wrote that into this bead and shipped the floor on it.

Re-measured on the same node, same protocol, same repository shape (3823 tracked files vs 3801):

    clone runs:                 1046  1671  1164  2207  1950 ms
    live ~/cacophony checkout:                             4735 ms

1.0-4.7s, i.e. 3x to 22x faster and comfortably UNDER the deadline said to exclude the platform. The most likely explanation is that the original sample was taken while ms-mac was genuinely degraded (nix store dylibs failing code-signature validation, git/cargo being SIGKILLed) — that measures the sick node, not the platform. I cannot prove that; I can only show the number does not reproduce on a healthy one. A caravan has since formed on ms-mac, which is direct counter-evidence to the structural claim.

WHY THE FLOOR STAYS ANYWAY, on its own merits
The per-command timeout is sized for commands whose duration reflects the WORK REQUESTED. Worktree materialisation is not that: it scales with REPOSITORY SIZE and is identical whether the tick then replays one commit or forty. Tying the two to one number couples quantities that have nothing to do with each other, and the coupling only ever bites in the direction of a false timeout.

The concrete failure this guards is budget DIVISION, not slow platforms. `sync.reserve_secs_per_command` divides the tick budget across commands, and that mechanism has already produced an absurd per-command budget in production: a 285ms deadline for `git fetch` (bd-89e59f), which no real command could meet. A fixed setup cost must not shrink because the budget was divided more ways.

HONEST ACCOUNTING OF THE NUMBER
60s is HEADROOM, not a derived value. Observed healthy worst case is 4.7s, so the floor is ~13x that. Default `command_timeout_secs` is 30, so on a default config this floor DOUBLES the allowance for exactly one command. The cost of that is real and bounded: a genuinely hung worktree creation takes 60s rather than 30s to detect. The operation deadline still clamps every command, so it cannot overrun a tick.

If the number is ever questioned, the defensible alternatives are: drop it to the configured `command_timeout_secs` (protects against division only, never exceeds operator intent), or derive it from measured tree size. I did not do either, because the queue works and the cost of being wrong here is 30 extra seconds on a path that is already failing.

title: Budget and reduce authenticated GitHub API usage
description:
## Observed problem

During the post-v0.0.4 audit, authenticated GitHub requests exhausted the shared user-ID API quota. Cara does authenticate `gh` subprocesses: it validates ambient `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`, otherwise resolves a repository-accessible `gh auth` account token and injects it. The issue is query volume and many processes/agents sharing one user bucket, not anonymous access. A single Cacophony `cara status` took about 12.8 seconds and multiple separate `status`/`next-candidate`/`check` calls each rediscovered overlapping repository, open-PR, check, label, default-ref, merge-candidate, and history facts.

## Required outcome

- Add secret-free API budget telemetry to status/check/sync/loop receipts: auth kind/login or app installation identity (never token), GraphQL cost/remaining/reset, REST remaining/reset when available, calls by phase, cache hits, and bounded exhaustion continuation.
- Include GraphQL `rateLimit { cost remaining resetAt }` in existing queries without a separate probe; parse REST rate headers where practical.
- Reuse one exact discovery snapshot throughout a bounded sync/auto-admission tick. Batch repository/PR/check/merge-candidate/history facts and avoid repeated full discovery within one unchanged generation. Mutation boundaries must rediscover exact affected provider facts.
- Add bounded generation-aware caches for read-only snapshots and REST ETags/conditional requests where supported. Never use stale cache as mutation authority.
- Make loop back off adaptively near quota reset and prefer event-driven wakes. Rate exhaustion is a typed waiting/retry result, not an LLM repair decision and never authorizes mutation from stale state.
- Avoid spending an API call solely to validate auth on every short-lived Cara process when the first real request can provide exact access failure, while preserving safe multi-account repository selection.
- Support GitHub App installation-token operation for automation, using a token helper/environment rather than secrets in `.caravan/config.yaml`. Document GitHub Actions `actions/create-github-app-token` or equivalent, least-privilege permissions, installation-bucket behavior, and user-token fallback.
- Ensure one Cara loop/controller is the recommended polling owner; other agents consume its durable snapshot/journal rather than independently polling.

Test shared user quota exhaustion, app installation identity, GraphQL and REST budgets, cache generation invalidation, webhook wake coalescing, adaptive backoff, exact reread before mutation, and no secret leakage. A GitHub App is desirable for a separate least-privilege installation bucket and webhooks, but must not substitute for reducing API volume.

title: Use the GitHub App installation identity for git fetch and force-push
description:
Second child of bd-b15483, after bd-03d863: authenticate Caravan's direct Git fetch/push transport with the same exact GitHub App installation credential used for `gh` API calls. This turns local App mode from read/API-only into a usable mutation mode and makes provider force-push events show the App bot identity.

CURRENT SAFETY BOUNDARY

bd-03d863 intentionally returns `GithubAppGitTransportUnavailable` before every `git push` when App broker mode is active. Do not remove that refusal until this slice proves exact principal parity and secret handling.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOR

- Resolve the same exact repository-scoped cached `GithubAppCredential` used by `gh`; API and git transport may never select independently.
- Supply HTTPS git username `x-access-token` and installation token through a protected askpass/in-memory credential helper or equivalent environment-only mechanism.
- Never put token in remote URL, git config on disk, argv, process display, errors, receipts, checkpoints, reflogs, or logs.
- Support exact fetch, dry-run push preflight, force-with-lease push, clone/repair materialization, and branch deletion where Cara already authorizes them.
- Refuse non-GitHub remotes, repository identity mismatch, SSH transport unless a reviewed App-compatible transport exists, expired credential after one refresh, or API/git installation mismatch.
- Preserve all existing exact leases, request/mutation budgets, deadlines, branch ownership, and push diagnostics.
- Temporary helper files are mode 0700/0600, contain no token when possible, and are removed on success/error/panic/session shutdown. Prefer a static helper that reads secret environment over generating a token-bearing script.
- Telemetry/receipts name App slug, installation ID, and transport mode, never token.
- Local ambient-gh mode remains byte-for-byte behavior compatible.

PROVIDER IDENTITY ACCEPTANCE

A sandbox integration must create an App-authenticated branch update and prove the GitHub timeline actor is `<app-slug>[bot]`, while the exact commit/tree/lease receipt remains Cara's. API comment and force-push actor must resolve to the same App installation.

TESTS

- App push receives credentials only through secret environment/helper protocol.
- Command/display/error/debug/JSON never contains a sentinel token.
- Force-with-lease success retains exact old/new OIDs and App principal.
- Stale lease refuses without overwrite.
- Token expiry refreshes once under the same deadline; repeated auth failure stops.
- API App A plus git App B mismatch fails before push.
- SSH and local non-GitHub remotes fail closed in App mode.
- Ambient mode runs existing git commands unchanged and does not invoke App broker/helper.

IMPLEMENTATION / LIVE-PROOF SPLIT

The code and hermetic transport acceptance remain on this bead. The operator-approved live GitHub timeline actor canary is tracked separately as bd-71e444 because this checkout has no App installation/private-key authority and must not create or mutate sandbox provider state autonomously. Closing this implementation bead does not claim that external canary has run.

title: Make sync rebuild a real rebased chain after parent head changes
description:
Operator-directed live Cacophony gap after bd-49a809 closed. Harry expects one bounded `cara sync --all` to repair/rebase the whole active chain in parallel, rather than requiring the merger agent to inspect and update every PR manually.

Live reproduction with packaged Cara 0.0.2: Cacophony caravan `[1972,1962,1959,1958,1946]` was clean until merger repaired PR #1972 from `3f245f7066becbb6fec1d98fe9528c6c8a88fef6` to `e635eeb33ae78d9829b0f5c2a485b32681c860b6`. PR #1962 still represented the prior parent generation. `cara status` reported `incompatible` for `[1972,1962]`; `cara sync --all` returned `link_conflict` with conflicting paths `README.md` and `SPEC.md`, no provider receipts, and suggested manual checkout/repair. It did not rebuild descendants.

The deployed Cacophony `.caravan/config.yaml` has `force_merge: true` but no `rebase_on_join`; bd-49a809 defined that mode with safe default false. This creates an operator-visible rollout/behavior gap: sync silently falls back to manual link-conflict repair instead of making the requested whole-chain mode and remediation explicit.

Acceptance:
- When `rebase_on_join: true`, `sync --all` must build a complete root-to-tail rebase plan against exact current parent OIDs, preflight every edge/conflict and all force-with-lease ownership/permission guards before the first write, then rebuild eligible independent steps with bounded safe parallelism while preserving dependency order.
- Each rewritten PR emits old/new head, parent, lease, base, exact provider receipts, and invalidates prior CI; descendants are rediscovered after each generation and receive fresh exact-head CI.
- A conflict stops before mutating that edge or its descendants and returns exact files plus the retained successfully rebuilt prefix.
- When the mode is absent/false, `status`, `check`, and `sync` must explicitly report `rebase_on_join=disabled` and the exact project-config action rather than implying the agent should hand-rebase every edge.
- Add a Cacophony-shaped five-member fixture covering parent-head repair, whole-chain rebuild, no partial writes on preflight conflict, stale remote head, moved main, and rerun idempotency.
- Document the safe canary/rollback for enabling this mode in an existing project. Do not weaken fork, ownership, dirty-worktree, conflict, or force-with-lease guards.

This is distinct from bd-49a809's implementation slice: it tracks sync orchestration, bounded parallelism, explicit disabled-mode diagnostics, and live rollout behavior proven missing in Cacophony.

Additional operator acceptance 2026-07-18: handle merged-head promotion/retarget, not only in-place parent-head repair. Exact live target is merged #1972 -> active successor #1962 -> child #1959. Whole-chain planning must use a verified retained refs/pull/<merged>/head range boundary if the merged predecessor branch was deleted, rebuild #1962 onto exact main, rebuild #1959 onto planned #1962, then midpoint rediscovery and existing ensure_base(main) retarget must consume fresh facts. Verify this exact chain live after implementation/deploy; keep repair-workspace work in bd-cf44d1 separate.

Strict all-target clippy, 222 all-target tests, and Darwin flake check green before final apply-target guard; focused physical 5/5 green after guard.

Active caravan is [1962,1959,1958,1946]. #1962 is promoted/retargeted to main@cff967990a08e7fad3f78979616917018bd7c449 with head 05fe82fe80c692613463a888bd4df5bc34d4ddee; #1959 base is that exact #1962 branch/OID and head d95f2de64871549adcc72c3f8266cc11b478f3e4. title: Add Caravan-owned runtime wrapper for same-repo pr_cara_join integration
description:
## Parent chain

Required by:

- `cacophony:bd-071583` — run Caravan project reintegration through `pr_cara_join`
- `cacophony-config:bd-869abf` — typed same-repo Caravan pull-request/Cara integration

## Current state

Caravan main `9c7f9f3` contains `.caravan/config.yaml` with `rebase_on_join: true`, but has no checkout-owned `scripts/cara-runtime.sh`.

Cacophony production SPEC requires the queue runtime argv shape:

    scripts/cara-runtime.sh --source system --

Cacophony's wrapper is checkout-relative and cannot validly service a Caravan checkout. Config must reference a reviewed wrapper/runtime owned by the Caravan project, not a sibling Cacophony path.

## Required behavior

title: Treat candidates contained in an already-merged PR as superseded
description: Confirmed NOT fixed on main at 7e56547. Generation integrity is computed only from open PRs: github.rs open_generation_facts / pull_requests_with_generation build facts from the open-PR query, so generation::analyze never sees a merged predecessor. A candidate whose exact commits are strictly contained in an already-merged PR therefore stays a live ordered admission attempt instead of being structurally ineligible with blocks_order=false, exactly as open supersession already behaves. Required: extend containment evidence to merged same-stream PRs using exact merge commit/tree/patch evidence, classify the contained candidate superseded_generation with a precise reason and safe next action, exclude it from ordering rather than wedging the queue, and never auto-close it. title: Cara 0.0.83 first status exhausts budget before provider calls
description:
## Live 0.0.83 recurrence

Cara v0.0.83 release/tag/assets/updater are terminal green and Helsinki cron installed user-local 0.0.83. The release contains status-budget fix `65eef249` from closed `bd-4fe538`.

Acceptance still fails on the first read-only status when no last-good snapshot exists. Two independent bounded attempts—release owner and controller with the configured GitHub token—returned the same typed error:

```text
code=status_partial_unavailable
elapsed_ms≈38336–38644
deadline_ms=35000
phase=compatibility_analysis
provider_api.authenticated=false
provider_api.calls=0
status_partial=false
mutated=false
```

This is not provider latency/auth: the entire dedicated budget expires in local `compatibility_analysis` before the first provider call. Because there is no previous successful snapshot, the last-good partial path cannot recover. Caco therefore still projects canonical Cara as unavailable even though 0.0.83 sync succeeds.

## Required behavior

- bound/yield compatibility analysis itself so a first status can complete within its read-only deadline for the current >8-candidate graph
- reserve enough time for at least the minimal provider identity/status reads needed by the adapter
- when full compatibility analysis cannot finish, emit a useful typed `status_partial` even without a historical last-good snapshot, built from bounded local/current evidence with explicit unknown fields
- never report `authenticated=false` as an auth diagnosis when zero provider calls occurred solely because local analysis exhausted the budget
- preserve no-mutation semantics and the separate mutating-sync reserves/lock
- expose phase timings, candidate counts, completion reserve, skipped/deferred analyses, provider-call counts, and whether partial came from current bounded evidence versus historical last-good
- add fixtures for first-ever status with >8 candidates, slow compatibility analysis, zero provider calls, no last-good, later full snapshot, and Caco adapter degraded projection

## Acceptance

- current Cacophony fixture returns success/full or typed current-evidence partial under 35s on a first status call
- `caco agent merge-queue list` reports canonical Cara healthy/degraded, not unavailable
- no manual/competing sync and no mutation during status

Do not close release bead `bd-569151` until this source fix is released/deployed and the adapter proof is green.

title: A wildcard decision mapping gives any new graph problem a fleet-fatal decision by default
description:
`decision_for_problem` in `src/sync.rs` mapped `GraphProblemKind` to `DecisionKind` through a match ending in `_ => DecisionKind::InvalidGraph`.

That wildcard is the mechanism behind the whole bd-299d3e / bd-550b0e class, not another instance of it. When `CandidateIncompatible` was introduced, it silently fell into the wildcard and was given a fleet-fatal `InvalidGraph` decision by default. A single unqueued conflicting candidate then aborted every `cara sync` tick on a fleet with zero caravans, and no test failed, because nothing in the type system was asked to notice a new variant had appeared.

bd-604e38 was intended to close this class by making classification compiler-enforced, and it made `blocks_fleet`/`is_candidate_scoped` exhaustive. But an exhaustive classifier only protects call sites that *ask the classifier*. `decision_for_problem` never asked; it compared variants by hand and defaulted the rest. So the class was not closed: four of the five known sites were instances, and this one was the mechanism.

## Fix

Replace the wildcard with an exhaustive match over every `GraphProblemKind`, so adding a variant fails to compile until somebody chooses its decision. `CandidateIncompatible` is mapped explicitly rather than by default, with a comment recording that it should never reach a decision because every fleet gate skips it first.

## Verification

The guard was proved rather than asserted. Adding a probe variant to `GraphProblemKind`:

- before: compilation failed only at `src/model.rs:551` (`blocks_fleet`)
- after:  compilation also fails at `src/sync.rs:5239` (`decision_for_problem`)

        error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: `GraphProblemKind::ProbeOnlyVariant` not covered
            --> src/sync.rs:5239:22

Probe variant reverted; `cargo check` clean.

## Audit performed alongside

Every other `match` over a problem kind in non-test source was checked. The remaining wildcards (`src/sync/decision.rs:109`, `:255`, `:430`, `src/sync.rs:5345`, `:5381`, `src/next.rs:88`) are over `DecisionKind`, `HeadOfLineBlockKind` and `NextStatus`, not `GraphProblemKind`. The hand comparisons `bd-550b0e` left in `validate_graph` (`AutoMergeInvariant`, `DanglingBase`) select *correctable* cases after the classifier skip, so an unrecognised variant fails closed to fleet-fatal rather than being silently excused, which is the safe direction.

Found while auditing why Cacophony has never formed a caravan; credited to msm0's class hunt, which surfaced four sibling sites.

title: Cara reports repo-resolution failure as authenticated=false, misdirecting anyone who reads the diagnostic toward credentials that are fine
description:
Cara reports a repository-resolution failure as an authentication failure, sending anyone who reads the diagnostic toward a fix that is not the problem.

OBSERVED, 2026-07-30, by helsinki:unknown:harry on ms-mac, read-only:

  cara status from a managed agent checkout reports:
      provider_api: authenticated=false, auth_source=gh_default_or_unauthenticated

  BUT `gh auth status` from that same checkout, same moment, reports:
      logged in to github.com as harryaskham, via GH_TOKEN

AUTHENTICATION IS FINE. What actually failed is repository discovery - `gh repo view` could not infer the repo because the checkout's origin points at a local daemon mirror rather than GitHub (tracked separately). Cara collapses that into an auth state.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING SEPARATELY FROM THE UNDERLYING RESOLUTION BUG: the diagnostic actively misdirects. An operator or agent reading "authenticated=false, auth_source=gh_default_or_unauthenticated" will reasonably go and check tokens, re-run gh auth login, or suspect credential expiry - none of which can help, and one of which (re-authenticating) mutates real credential state for no reason. The reporting agent said explicitly that this "would send someone down a completely wrong path", and they only avoided it by independently running gh auth status.

SUGGESTED FIX SHAPE: distinguish "could not determine the repository" from "could not authenticate", and report the former with the actual gh error text rather than as an auth_source value. The underlying gh failure message is specific and useful - "none of the git remotes configured for this repository point to a known GitHub host" - and it is being discarded in favour of a misleading summary.

THIS IS AN INSTANCE OF A PATTERN SEEN REPEATEDLY ACROSS THE FLEET TODAY: a surface returning a well-formed, plausible, internally consistent answer that is about the wrong thing. Those are more expensive than errors, because nothing prompts the reader to doubt them.

Filed by helsinki-cacophony-caco-ctrl on behalf of the reporting agent, who characterised it and explicitly did not file. Dedup: caravan board scanned via --title-contains for auth, gh, repo and discovery; nearest neighbour bd-48610a (scope release backfill gh auth check) is CLOSED and concerns scoping an auth check rather than misclassifying a resolution failure as one.

title: A budget refusal recommends the change that makes it worse
description:
The post-rewrite budget refusal advised:

    rerun the same command with a fresh operation budget, or raise command_timeout_secs / the sync duration bound

Raising `command_timeout_secs` makes this refusal STRICTLY WORSE. The requirement is derived from that value:

    let timeout  = command_timeout_secs
    let required = timeout * POST_REWRITE_COMMAND_RESERVE      // 4

    60s  ->  required 240,000ms
    300s ->  required 1,200,000ms

`remaining` comes from the operation deadline and is unaffected by `command_timeout_secs`, so raising it increases the bar and never increases what is available. It cannot help, in any configuration.

MEASURED HARM, not hypothetical. An operator hit this refusal on the live fleet, read the remedy, and filed a P0 proposing exactly `60 -> 300`, reasoning by analogy with the hook `timeout_secs: 300` convention in the same config file. That would have taken the requirement from 240s to 1200s while leaving the deadline unchanged. The analogy is reasonable and the advice endorsed it: in a hook that key is a CEILING, here it is a MULTIPLICAND, and nothing in the message said so.

The other half of the old advice was correct: raising the sync duration bound does help, because `sync_operation_budget` is `min(max_duration_secs, 3600)` and that IS the operation deadline.

Now states all three real levers and the arithmetic behind them: rerun with a fresh budget, raise `sync.max_duration_secs` to enlarge the deadline, or LOWER `command_timeout_secs` because the reserve is 4x that value. The formula is also emitted as `required_formula` so a reader can compute the consequence of a change before making it.

This is the same class as several defects fixed here today, with one distinction worth keeping: those surfaces reported a condition inaccurately, while this one accurately reported the condition and then recommended an action that deepens it. A wrong diagnosis wastes time; wrong remediation spends it in the wrong direction and looks like progress.

description:

title: Provide a managed clean repair workspace for Cara sync decision recovery
description:
## Live Cacophony canary failure

On 2026-07-18, `cara status` correctly detected caravan `1962 -> 1959 -> 1958 -> 1946`, with PR 1962 still targeting merged predecessor 1972. `cara sync --all` could not advance it from either available Cacophony controller workspace:

1. The managed controller checkout was dirty with broad unrelated tracked/untracked state, so Cara returned `dirty_worktree`.
2. A first-party `caco project checkout` could not pass provider initialization (`gh repo view` reported that no configured remote pointed to a known GitHub host).
3. The controller therefore created a raw detached `.cara-clean` git worktree, manually fetched the exact PR head, manually updated the local branch ref after `local_branch_diverged`, and manually merged `origin/main` before resolving the typed `head_conflict` in README.md and SPEC.md.

This is the unsafe escape hatch the Cacophony merger contract forbids. Cara found the right decision but did not provide a first-party owned workspace/continue path in which the agent could repair it.

## Required outcome

- Add a Cara-owned isolated repair workspace for mutating `sync`, or integrate with a declared managed-checkout provider so ordinary dirty controller state is irrelevant.
- Fetch/check out the exact provider PR head using an expected-head receipt without requiring callers to run raw `git update-ref`.
- After the operator/agent resolves a typed conflict, provide an explicit verify-and-continue command that checks expected remote head, patch scope, conflict markers, and branch ancestry before non-force publication and resumes `sync --all`.
- Preserve the worktree and emit bounded recovery instructions on interruption; never leave an untracked nested worktree in the controller checkout.
- Add fixtures covering dirty caller checkout, daemon/internal remotes, locally divergent PR refs, and resume after a two-file head conflict.
- Keep semantic conflict resolution agent-owned; this bead is about safe workspace and resumability, not auto-guessing content.

Audit receipt from caco-ctrl replay: the controller did invoke Cara first (`cara status --json`, then `cara sync --all --json`) and respected typed stops for missing initialization, dirty worktree, local branch divergence, and `head_conflict`. The failure is end-to-end recovery: `caco project checkout` could not initialize because its internal remote was not GitHub-recognized, and Cara exposed no owned repair workspace/continue operation. caco-ctrl then crossed the safety boundary into `git worktree add --detach .cara-clean`, manual exact fetch/update-ref, raw merge/conflict edits/commit, branch push, and repeated Cara sync. Thus discovery/decision use was correct; repair execution was not Cara-owned and violated the intended no-raw-surgery contract. Current fix must make the post-decision path fully first-party, and controller guidance should stop rather than hand-roll when that path is unavailable.

Implementation checkpoint on branch commits 7d73574 + a0f38a7 + c2b6b9e (rebased onto eb77ec7): new CLI/JSON/MCP `repair start/status/continue/abort` surface. Start resolves explicit GitHub provider SSH URL by repository slug and creates an independent exact-head clone under caller Git common Caravan state, so dirty caller, daemon-internal origin, and local PR ref divergence are untouched. Atomic manifest records repository/PR/head/old-base/target/provider/config fingerprint/workspace/conflict paths/baseline index/state/timestamps/prepared or published head. Continue checks config/session/workspace/provider identity, exact merge target, no unresolved/unstaged/untracked/marker state, typed conflict-only index scope, exact parents, unchanged head+target refs; then commits and ordinary non-force pushes the explicit provider URL, verifies ref, and resumes sync-all while holding the caller repository operation lock. Committed/pushed interruption resumes idempotently; explicit confirmed abort deletes only local session state. Focused evidence green: 6 repair tests (dirty+internal origin, scope rejection, committed-before-manifest recovery, moved-head no overwrite, exact parents/non-force publication, confirmed abort no provider mutation), CLI parser, 3 CLI/MCP parity tests, rustfmt on new module, git diff check, strict library Clippy. Full-tree rustfmt is pre-existing red on eb77ec7 outside touched repair code; no unrelated formatting churn included. Awaiting bd-cacf7c orchestration land before final rebase/reintegration; no physical_rebase or checkout_for_decision overlap.

title: Treat newer running workflow generation as current for admission
description:
Live Cacophony PR #2358 was skipped as "candidate has a failing required check" after an operator removed skip/evict labels to progress it, even though its replacement workflow generation was running. Admission before final CI is intentional: joining rebases the PR and invalidates/reruns CI anyway. Only stable current terminal red should block.

Exact evidence from Cara status:

- old `Public Fast Tests preparation`: CANCELLED, completed 2026-08-02T09:49:02Z, workflow run 30742496352
- replacement same identity: IN_PROGRESS, started 09:50:30Z, provider `completed_at=0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`, workflow run 30742505941
- Cara incorrectly marked the newer IN_PROGRESS row `superseded=true` and the old CANCELLED row current
- old `Check & Lint`/`Fast Tests (unit)` failures from run 30742496352 remained decisive while newer run 30742505941 had started but had not yet materialized all downstream check identities

Root causes:

1. `CheckSnapshot::observed_at` uses `completed_at.or(started_at)`. GitHub's year-0001 unfinished sentinel is non-empty, so a running row is ordered at year 0001 rather than its real later start time.
2. Supersession is only per check identity. During a new workflow run's startup window, terminal downstream rows from the prior workflow generation remain "current" until matching downstream jobs appear, despite positive evidence that a newer workflow generation on the exact same head exists.

Required behavior:

- Normalize unusable provider timestamps (empty/year-0001) as absent.
- Order each observation by the latest valid `started_at`/`completed_at` timestamp.
- Parse workflow run identity from check details URLs (or carry it explicitly) and ensure rows from an older run of the same workflow on the exact head cannot remain terminal-current once a newer run is observed queued/in-progress/current.
- Preserve independent workflows: a newer `CI` run must not supersede `Android companion`, and a genuinely current failure in an independent workflow must still block.
- `Waiting` (Expected/Queued/InProgress, including a replacement workflow generation) remains eligible for automatic admission; only stable terminal red from the latest current generation is skipped/parked.
- Preserve fail-closed behavior when ordering/generation evidence is absent or ambiguous.
- CLI/web JSON must mark the same rows superseded that classification ignores.

Acceptance fixtures:

1. exact #2358 shape: old cancelled + newer in-progress same identity with year-0001 completed_at => newer current, disposition Waiting, candidate not skipped;
2. newer workflow run started but old downstream failure has no matching new row yet => old-run failure superseded for admission;
3. same-run sibling failure + pending remains Failed;
4. failure in a separate workflow remains Failed;
5. absent timestamps do not silently discard red;
6. pending candidate can form/join a caravan (no wait-for-green policy regression).

Broadcast sent to Cacophony before implementation per operator direction. Do not mutate live Cacophony PRs for testing.

title: Caravan membership does not follow a superseded generation, so republishing a member silently dissolves the caravan
description:
The first caravan ever formed on cacophony dissolved silently because its only member was superseded by a new generation, and membership did not follow to the successor PR.

TIMELINE, 2026-07-30

    ~04:31  CARAVAN #2287 forms. members=[2287]. First caravan on this repository.
            Verified read-only: healthy=true, next_candidate=2276, correctly
            skipping 2245/2259 as incompatible and 2282/2285 as failing checks.
    ~09:00  #2287 goes red: 5 jobs CANCELLED plus 2 aggregate FAILUREs (bd-c04d9b).
            Re-run advised rather than eviction. Nobody evicted it.
    ~10:5x  #2287 recovers to fully CLEAN with no intervention.
    11:13   #2287 CLOSED, not merged, no merge commit.
    now     #2300 is open with the SAME TITLE from the SAME AGENT
            (39g9gzpp6jejdw3x) on a NEW BRANCH, and carries NO caravan label.
            No open PR in the repository carries the caravan label.

So this was not an eviction and not a failure. The author republished its work as a new generation - normal Cacophony reintegration behaviour - and the caravan simply ceased to exist.

WHY THIS IS A REAL GAP RATHER THAN EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR

Generation supersession is routine and frequent on this fleet. Agents republish constantly. If every republication silently dissolves any caravan the PR belonged to, then a caravan can only survive as long as none of its members is revised - which for a queue whose purpose is to hold work while it converges is close to a contradiction.

It is also SILENT. Nothing reported that the caravan had dissolved. It was discovered by checking labels on open PRs and finding none. A queue that can lose its contents without saying so is hard to trust, and harder to debug.

Note this could only be found once a caravan actually existed. It had never formed before today, so no amount of prior analysis would have surfaced it.

QUESTIONS THAT NEED ANSWERING

1. Should membership follow a generation? When a member PR is superseded by a successor from the same agent, same bead, same logical work, should the successor inherit the caravan position? `cara rejoin` exists for evicted PRs; there appears to be no equivalent for superseded ones.
2. If it should NOT follow automatically - which is defensible, since the successor's patch may no longer be compatible with the chain - then the dissolution must at minimum be REPORTED, and ideally the successor should be offered as a candidate rather than dropped.
3. What happens with a multi-member caravan? If a middle member is superseded, does the chain re-stitch as it would on eviction, or does the whole caravan dissolve? The eviction path has `--cascade` with documented tail-first ordering; supersession appears to have nothing.

RELATED: bd-c04d9b (cancellations converted to failures - the reason this member went red in the first place), bd-1ac172 (cancellation must not auto-evict). The irony is worth recording: the caravan survived the red state that a naive eviction policy would have killed it for, and was then lost to an ordinary republication that nobody was watching for.

title: Navigate safely across Cara-rewritten stale local branches
description:
Live Cacophony `cara prev` from child fix-cara-timeouts refused `local_branch_diverged` because predecessor fix-slackiq-nodes had been physically rewritten by Cara/provider: discovered exact provider head 570e26e while the existing local predecessor branch remained c059bf1. This prevents all chain navigation precisely when a stack needs sync. The worktree was clean and the target provider branch existed locally/remotely; raw reset would be unsafe, but hard refusal is not a usable navigation policy.

Teach next/prev/van navigation to reconcile a non-current stale local destination after exact provider discovery without losing code. Fetch and reverify the exact provider branch OID. If the destination local ref differs, preserve its old OID under a deterministic bounded internal Cara backup ref/receipt, then update/create the named local branch at the exact provider OID and checkout it. Never delete the old object or silently reset a branch checked out in another worktree. Current worktree must be clean with no in-progress Git operation; provider movement during fetch/check fails closed. Dirty state, unsafe ref names, missing/deleted/fork-only provider heads, ambiguous PR mapping, or backup/ref transaction failure writes no branch switch.

Acceptance:
- Clean child→Cara-rewritten predecessor navigation succeeds at exact provider OID and records old local OID + backup ref + new OID.
- Already exact local branch is unchanged; absent local branch is created exact as today.
- Divergent local commits are retained by reachable backup ref; receipt tells operator how to inspect/recover them.
- Destination checked out in another worktree, current dirty worktree, ref race, and partial transaction fail safely.
- next/prev and fleet navigation share the same helper; historical merged-successor behavior remains exact.
- No provider mutation and no implicit sync/rebase; JSON/MCP/human output distinguish provider navigation reconciliation from destructive reset.
- Regression fixture covers c059bf1→570e26e and repeated Cara-owned rewrites.

title: x86_64-linux release build exceeds its timeout on a cold cache
description:
The v0.0.42 release was cancelled: `build x86_64-linux` ran 07:56:28 to 08:56:46, exactly 60:18, and was killed by `timeout_minutes: 60`. The darwin leg of the same run took 95 seconds.

That asymmetry is the diagnosis. x86_64-linux does not build the native package: it builds `caravan-static`, a full musl CROSS-COMPILE of the entire dependency tree. With a warm Nix cache that finishes in minutes, which is why the four preceding releases each completed end to end in 9-10 minutes. With a cold or unreachable cache it rebuilds everything from source, and an hour is not surprising.

Two independent observations, not one:

1. This timeout, at exactly the configured limit rather than at a random point, which is what distinguishes a budget problem from a hang.
2. The internal Nix binary cache was directly observed timing out earlier the same night: `unable to download 'http://100.78.63.1:38080/collective/...narinfo': Timeout was reached (28) Connection timed out after 15001 milliseconds`.

Raises the budget to 120 minutes, matching what the removed aarch64-linux entry already carried for exactly this reason. That entry's 120 was evidently sized for a cross-build; x86_64-linux does the same kind of work and was left at the native-build default.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX: a slow or unavailable binary cache. This only stops a cold-cache build being killed halfway. If the cache is persistently unreachable, releases will merely take an hour instead of failing, which is worth knowing but is infrastructure rather than caravan.

Not previously filed on purpose. One overrunning run is an anecdote and I had already been wrong three times tonight by treating a single observation as structural. It was filed once the run reached a terminal state and the elapsed time landed exactly on the configured limit, which turns a guess into a measurement.

v0.0.41 remains a complete, usable release with all four assets. The v0.0.42 tag exists with darwin assets only; its code is on main and ships in the next release.

title: Reconcile squash-equivalent pre-squash commits when attaching candidates to a caravan tail
description:
## Live Cacophony reproduction

PR2227 is the tail of caravan `[2215,2223,2225,2227]` at head `94373464efe68fcca5b4010c83b100c33e7469ff`. Main-based PR2245/PR2247 cannot attach because merge-tree reports conflicts in `crates/caco-cli/src/lib.rs` and `crates/caco-daemon/src/canonical_queue.rs`.

The conflict is inherited stack history, not bd-4640a7 source. Tail carries pre-squash commit `79abc31d4e` from PR2208; main carries its squash `1a09ceecef`. At the squash point both relevant blobs are byte-identical, but commit identities differ, so replaying the stacked pre-squash history conflicts against content already on main. Every squash-landed member can recreate this at the next tail.

## Required

- During promotion/rebase/attachment, detect pre-squash commits whose resulting content/tree is already represented on current main.
- Reconcile/drop only with exact cumulative tree/blob proof; commit-message/patch heuristics alone are insufficient.
- Preserve genuinely-new child content and fail closed on semantic difference.
- Emit receipt listing old commit, squash/main proof, affected paths, before/after cumulative tree and dropped/reconciled action.
- Tests for exact blob equality, disjoint later main movement, partial overlap, same patch/different tree, multiple squashes, conflict after equality point, and PR2215→2227 topology.
- Do not rewrite a live provider branch without reviewed owner/hold authority.

Near-term PR2227 disposition is operator-controlled under membership hold; this bead is the durable recurrence fix.

## Correction: PR2227 is not the causal live case

Owner re-measurement proved the initial PR2227 attribution was wrong. Blob equality existed only at ancestor `79abc31d4e` for caco-cli, and canonical_queue equality was vacuous because PR2208 did not touch that file. At current head `94373464ef`, merge base, main tip and PR head are three distinct blobs for both `crates/caco-cli/src/lib.rs` and `crates/caco-daemon/src/canonical_queue.rs`. PR2227's present incompatibility is an ordinary three-way semantic conflict, not safely droppable squash-equivalent history. Never use take-either or automatic commit dropping for this PR.

The general pre-squash duplicate hazard remains valid and needs controlled tests, but PR2227 must not be cited as proof of causality. Keep general structural acceptance separate from specific file-level conflict evidence.

title: [P0] Make Caravan the sole squash-merge actor with retarget-before-merge ordering
description:
Direct operator architecture decision: disable native GitHub auto-merge for Cacophony. Caravan becomes the sole leased merge actor. On each tick it must retarget the current caravan head to main when its predecessor merged, revalidate against the new base, squash-merge exact head into main, then promote the next member. Remove the existing `auto_merge_invariant` in the same release; otherwise repo-level auto-merge disable makes every caravan permanently degraded.

Strict operation order:
1. If caravan head base != main and predecessor is merged, retarget head base to main.
2. Wait for/recompute exact merge-base, compatibility, required contexts and zero-run diagnostics against the NEW base/head.
3. Only when exact head is valid/compatible/green, squash-merge it to main under Caravan lease.
4. Emit provider receipt and verify main contains the resulting tree before promoting next member.
5. Promote next member and repeat on a later tick; no native auto-merge actor.

Never merge before retarget/revalidation. Live failure receipt: PR2213 was CLEAN but still based on predecessor generation branch. Native auto-merge landed commit `3da6addbf0b1` into `agent/ms-dev-3/cacophony/8x5t4zp7luvs0a4q-pr-gf9e8151b76a9dae6b883c59a249700a7ca933540`, not main; compare against main is DIVERGED, behind_by=3, so content never reached main. Caravan then re-rooted to2215 with the same dangling-base condition. Fix must safely handle the whole remaining chain, not one head.

Safety/acceptance:
- single leased mutation actor; exact repository/head/base/required-check re-read and abort-on-drift;
- idempotent squash receipt, provider request IDs, main tree containment postflight;
- retry/indeterminate classification with no duplicate merge;
- atomic promotion plan integrated with bd-9ead1b realistic sync budgeting;
- tests for stale predecessor branch, wrong-target refusal, required checks becoming stale after retarget, concurrent main movement, provider timeout after merge, and multi-member drain;
- migration of existing caravans with no native auto-merge and no content loss;
- SPEC/config/status update: no `auto_merge_invariant`; report Caravan merge authority and next exact action.

Coordinate Cacophony removal of native arming/rearming and runner provisioning. Do not mutate Cacophony PRs in tests.

title: Release workflow schedules an aarch64-darwin job no runner can ever accept
description:
Every release since v0.0.11 has required a manual `just release-backfill-target <tag> aarch64-darwin`, nine consecutive times. The cause is not flaky infrastructure.

`.github/workflows/release.yml` pins the darwin leg to `runs-on: [self-hosted, nix, aarch64-darwin]`. Queried live, the repository has seven registered runners and every one of them is Linux X64:

    caravan-ms-dev, ms-dev-2..6, pocket4
    labels: self-hosted,nix,Linux,X64,x86_64-linux,nixos,<host>

No runner advertises `aarch64-darwin`. The job is therefore unschedulable by construction: it queues until the run is cancelled or times out, and the release run never reaches a terminal state. `fail-fast: false` hides it as a hang rather than a failure.

Second, smaller issue: the `aarch64-linux` leg pins `runs-on: [self-hosted, nix, ms-dev-2]`, a single host. When ms-dev-2 is busy (it was, at the time of filing) that leg queues behind unrelated work. It is slow rather than broken, and the pin is deliberate because only ms-dev-2 advertises aarch64 in Nix extra-platforms, so it should stay pinned unless another host gains that capability.

Remedy: stop scheduling a leg that cannot be scheduled. Either register a darwin runner, or drop the matrix entry and make the documented `just release-backfill-target` path the contract, so a release run concludes honestly instead of hanging on a job no machine can accept. A workflow that cannot succeed should not be presented as pending.
